# §STRUCTFIX-1 — Three fuzzer-evidenced false-validation cards: `pnc` ×2, `bmo_ca_business` ×1

STRUCTFIX-1, 2026-08-13. Branch `wave3-structfix-1`, base `cc3ab29`. Brief:
`docs/agent-handoffs/STRUCTFIX-1.md`. Baseline: run `6893a75b`. Live
reproducers: the wave scratch `repro.py` (cases P1-A, P1-C, P1-B), run first
and re-run against the fix.

These are not coverage cells. Each card is a document that publishes
**approved / clear with wrong numbers** — the failure mode where every printed
identity still closes because the error is applied uniformly, so no downstream
oracle can see it. The method is therefore the reverse of a coverage cell:
characterise what the archive ACTUALLY prints before choosing the rule, because
the whole risk is a fix that reads a fuzzer's document correctly and a real
one wrongly.

Both sweeps were run over the whole **source folder** rather than the claimed

## S2. Card P1 — `pnc`: a space-grouped thousands figure read as its tail

**Defect.** `_SUMMARY_MONEY_RE`'s integer part admitted only comma grouping, so
`1 000.00` could not match whole; the piece that DID fit was its `000.00` tail.
The Balance Summary is a flattened grid, so all four columns truncate together:
`beginning`, `ending` and the average balance are each wrong by the same
thousand, `beginning + activity == ending` still holds, and the statement
publishes approved/clear. Measured in the reproducer: beginning `1000.00 →
0.00`, ending `1200.00 → 200.00`, ADB `1243.33 → 243.33`, no flag.

**What the archive prints — measured before choosing the rule.** 54 of the 62
`PNC Bank` documents have a Balance Summary block. **27 of them contain a
`<digit><space><3 digits>.<dd>` sequence** — which is exactly the shape a
space-thousands reading would consume. **In 10 of the 27** the leading digit is
the **cents tail of a completed figure** and the space is a column gap:

```
balance 541.22 541.22            <- average ledger / average collected
Ending balance 232.79 10,321.82 8,358.20 2,196.41
```

**In the other 17 it is not**, and an earlier revision of this section claimed
otherwise — "in every one of the 27" — which was false and is corrected here.
In those 17 the token to the left is a bare item count or a date, printed in
the `Description Items Amount` index and the `Daily Balance` ladder that the
block capture happens to include:

```
Description Items Amount Debit Card Purchases 7 202.05    <- count 7, amount 202.05
Date Ledger balance 02/10 1,195.48 02/11 953.78           <- date 02/11, balance 953.78
Interest Earned this period 0.00% 29 165.59               <- rate, then 165.59
```

Read with a space-grouping integer part those fuse into **fabricated figures of
entirely plausible magnitude** — 7,202.05 and 11,953.78. §S2b is what removes
them.

So the naive rule ("a space between digit groups is a thousands separator")
would have glued real columns together, and the naive fail-closed rule ("refuse
a figure preceded by digit-space") would have refused the second column of
every summary line in the archive. Neither is admissible.

**The rule that is.** One space character does two jobs, and what separates
them is what stands to its left: **a complete `.dd` figure ENDS a column**, so a
space after one is a column gap; anywhere else a digit run adjoining a
`<space><3 digits>` group is the head of one figure. Both halves are needed and
they fail in opposite directions — without the grouped integer part the figure
cannot match whole; without the boundary guard the truncated tail is what
matches instead.

```python
_THOUSANDS_SPACE = "\u0020\u00a0\u202f"
_SUMMARY_MONEY_RE = re.compile(
    rf"(?<![\d.,])"
    rf"(?:(?<=\.\d\d[{_THOUSANDS_SPACE}])|(?<![\d][{_THOUSANDS_SPACE}]))"
    rf"(?:\d[\d,]*(?:[{_THOUSANDS_SPACE}]\d{{3}})*)?\.\d{{2}}-?"
)
```

The separators are the ones `analysis/money.py` already surveys — its format
axes list `1 234.56` (:17) and `EITHER_MINUS_SPACED` (:214) exists to strip
them. `_money` now removes them before `parse_money`, which strips `$ , *` but
not spaces and SEARCHES rather than anchors, and would otherwise read
`1 000.00` as one dollar by a second route. `_average_balance` reads the same
figure grammar: same block, same printed format, and a document whose columns
are read whole must not publish a truncated average beside them.

**Effect on the 54 real blocks.** For 23 of them the pattern returns a different
*list* of figures than the old one: **6 suppression only, 4 glue only, 13
both**, and **77 fabricated tokens** in total. Every difference sits at index 6
or later, past the four `_summary_amounts` consumes, so no document's reading
moves and the sweep is byte-identical. But "inert today" is not "correct", and
a reader standing over a region where a date fuses with a ledger balance is one
layout change away from taking one. That is what §S2b bounds away.

## S2b. Card P1, second finding: the reader was standing in the wrong region

Adversarial review (Ocean, 2026-08-13) returned two defects in the first commit
of this card. Both were real, both reproduced exactly, and both are the same
root cause — the region scanned, not the figure pattern.

1. **The glue above.** 77 fabricated tokens across 17 blocks, disclosed by the
   first revision of this section only in its suppression half.
2. **The fail-closed claim was false by construction.** `_SUMMARY_MONEY_RE`'s
   comment said a figure that cannot be read whole leaves the document failing
   closed. With a spare figure in the block it did not — it SHIFTED the window.
   On the reviewer's construction (`1 0000.00` in the grid, average pair
   below) the shipped reader returned `['500.00', '300.00', '1,200.00',
   '900.00']`: the average ledger pair read as summary columns, a silent
   approval standing exactly where the refusal belonged. Zero archive
   incidence, but the comment asserted a property the code did not have. The
   negative fixture passed only because its body happened to print exactly
   four figures — a fixture that agreed with the claim instead of testing it.

**The fix, which is §S6.5 of the first revision, now taken.** The summary is
read from the line that prints the grid, and nothing below it is read. On all
54 blocks the four columns are the first four figures of a single physical
line.

The row is **located** by a permissive figure count (`_ANY_FIGURE_RE` — the old
pattern, which still matches the fragments the strict one refuses) and **read**
with `_SUMMARY_MONEY_RE`. That split is what makes the fail-closed property
true: a refused figure still counts towards finding the row, so the row is
found a column short and the statement fails closed. Locating by the strict
count instead would skip the grid and settle on the next line carrying four
figures — the `Daily Balance` ladder read as a summary, which is the shift
again, worse.

Measured over the 54 blocks, after:

| | |
|---|---:|
| blocks where the permissive and strict locators pick the same line | **54 / 54** |
| blocks whose four read figures move | **0** |
| lines below the grid row, now never scanned | **722** |
| figures in that region, now out of reach | **581** |
| glued tokens inside the region still read | **0** |
| PNC sweep vs base | **byte-identical, 62 / 62** |

The reviewer's construction now returns `None`. Both the glue region and the
shift are gone, and the claim in the code is one the code has.

## S3. Card P2 — `pnc`: a dated row that moves no money published as a posting

**Defect.** PNC genuinely prints sub-dollar amounts with the leading zero
dropped, so the row grammar must accept `.dd`; a dated informational line
carrying `.00` then satisfies it exactly as a posting does. `04/30 .00
Overdraft fees assessed this statement period` published as a third
transaction at approved/clear.

Nothing downstream can catch it: the row adds zero to the ledger sum and zero
to the section total, so `beginning + activity == ending` still holds with it
in the ledger, and PNC discloses no per-direction count oracle
(`analysis/count_semantics.py` `SECTION_LEVEL_ORACLES`) that could see the
extra row. The refusal has to happen at the row or nowhere.

**What the archive prints.** Over the 62 documents the two section readers
accept **6,673 rows**:

| measured | count | consequence |
|---|---:|---|
| rows carrying a **zero amount** | **0** | the rule reaches no printed posting |
| rows using the bare `.dd` form | **54** | genuine postings — `02/02 .82 ACH Credit Acctverify …`; the concession must stay |
| rows with **no** trailing reference number | **3,822** | a "postings carry a Reference number" rule is not available |

So the reference-number column — the other candidate the brief names — is not a
reliable structural discriminator on this layout, and is not used. The rule
shipped is the one the measurement supports: **a posting moves money.**

```python
def _posts(amount: float) -> bool:
    ...
    return amount != 0
```

`_posts` never reads the description, so a furniture wording this parser has
never seen is refused on the same grounds, and no real posting is refused for
how it is worded. Applied to `_parse_checks` as well, where `.00` is equally
readable and a cheque that moves no money is not a cheque.

`Total Overdraft Fees .00 .00` is unaffected and pinned as such: it is printed
outside the Balance Summary body and carries no date, so it was never a row.

## S4. Card B — `bmo_ca_business` `_MONEY_EN`: STOP, premise refuted by the archive

The card asks for `_MONEY_EN` to be aligned with its `_MONEY_FR` sibling —
`1 000.00` being "the Canadian/SI convention, on a CANADIAN bank". **The
archive says this printed layout does not use it, and that the space-grouped
shape means something else entirely on these documents.**

**Measurement 1 — every space-grouped occurrence is a reference number.** On
the lines the parser actually reads (the summary row it selects and the ledger
grid), the EN population contains **441 occurrences of `<1-3 digits><space><3
digits>.<dd>` across 65 of 168 documents**. Every one of the 30 read verbatim
is a merchant, cheque or account number abutting the amount column — and
Measurement 2 below is what generalises that from a sample to the population:

```
Apr 27 Debit Card Purchase, DOLLARAMA # 95 122.44 1,303.25
   -> store #95, amount 122.44, balance 1,303.25
Business Account # 3849 1981-774 277.52 23,730.09 23,955.40 502.83
   -> account 3849 1981-774, then the four summary cells
ISN: 5716186693 Cheque #174 500.00
   -> cheque #174, amount 500.00
Dec 01 Online Transfer, TF 3849#8840-536 800.00 1,077.52
   -> reference 3849#8840-536, amount 800.00, balance 1,077.52
```

The same lines print their real thousands **with commas** — `1,303.25`,
`23,730.09`, `239,642.85`.

**Measurement 2 — the separator census.** Of the 168 EN-population documents
with markdown:

| | documents |
|---|---:|
| print comma-grouped thousands **and** a space-shaped sequence | 65 |
| print comma-grouped thousands only | 96 |
| print a space-shaped sequence and **no** comma-grouped figure | **0** |
| print neither (no grouped figure at all) | 7 |

**No document in the archive uses the space as its thousands convention.** The
space-shaped sequences never stand alone; they always coexist with comma
grouping, which is what identifies them as reference numbers rather than
separators.

**Measurement 3 — the proposed fix, swept.** The literal alignment (FR's
separator class AND FR's `-` lookbehind; the separator class alone is not even
self-consistent, since without excluding `-` an account number's trailing group
starts a money cell):

```python
_MONEY_EN = re.compile(r"(?<![\d.,-])-?\$?(?:\d{1,3}(?:[,\u0020\u00a0\u202f]\d{3})+|\d+)\.\d{2}(?!\d)")
```

It does fix the reproducer, and the `-` exclusion does rescue the account-number
and transfer-reference lines. Over the 169-document `BMO` sweep:

| | |
|---|---:|
| movers | **30** |
| `validated/approved` → `withheld/withheld_adb` | **30** |
| any document improved | **0** |

Named movers, with the row each loses (glued cell → `parse_grouped_float`
raises → the row is skipped → continuity breaks → withheld):

| document | txns | first row lost |
|---|---|---|
| `BMO/3b3a1a46_April 30_ 2026.pdf` | 115 → 114 | `-122.44 Debit Card Purchase, DOLLARAMA # 95` |
| `BMO/3dc6c574_December 31_ 2025.pdf` | 122 → 120 | `-126.44 Debit Card Purchase, MARSHALLS #723` |
| `BMO/3ecfcd90_April 30_ 2025.pdf` | 74 → 72 | `-938.04 Debit Card Purchase, BEST BUY #84` |
| `BMO/3ecfcd90_March 31_ 2025.pdf` | 122 → 121 | `-115.42 Debit Card Purchase, BEST BUY #84` |
| `BMO/548fa9bf_July 31_ 2025-1.pdf` | 59 → 58 | `-143.18 Debit Card Purchase, SWISS CHALET #1` |
| `BMO/7246d185_February 27_ 2026.pdf` | 206 → 205 | `-137.74 Debit Card Purchase, FOOD BASICS 63` |
| `BMO/8b7d99d9_April 30_ 2026.pdf` | 198 → 189 | 9 rows |
| `BMO/8b7d99d9_February 27_ 2026.pdf` | 153 → 148 | 5 rows |

…30 in total. The brief's stop condition — "any outcome-class regression is a
stop" — fires. **`analysis/bmo_ca_business.py` is unchanged on this branch.**

**What the truncation actually is.** At the token level `1 000.00` (a
space-grouped amount) and `# 95 122.44` (a store number beside an amount) are
the same string shape. No lookbehind separates them: the `-` exclusion handles
the `1981-774` and `8840-536` forms but not the `# <digits>` form, which is the
common one. And the mutant is self-consistent under truncation — every figure
truncates together, the balance-continuity rule this module relies on still
holds, `Closing totals` still agrees with the summary, `Number of items
processed` still matches — so there is no second printing to catch it either.

The one place the ambiguity resolves is **document level**: no archive document
mixes the two conventions (0 space-only, 161 comma-bearing). A rule of the form
"a document that prints comma-grouped thousands anywhere is a comma-grouping
document, so a space in it is not a separator" would be correct on 161/161 of
the documents that print any grouped figure, and would read the fuzzer's
document (which prints no comma anywhere) correctly. That is a real design with
archive support, but it is per-document state threaded through `_cells`, it is
materially more than the card scopes, and getting it wrong publishes wrong
numbers silently — the exact failure class being closed. **Carried to Ocean as
a proposal (§S6), not taken unilaterally.**

Two smaller findings from the same measurement:

* The FR-style `-` lookbehind, **alone**, removes **0** matches on the whole
  169-document population — it is free. It does not fix the card (without the
  separator class `1 000.00` still truncates), so it is not shipped as a change
  with no defect behind it; it is available to Ocean as a one-character
  hardening if the document-level rule is ever taken.
* `_MONEY_FR`'s lookbehind excluding `-` is load-bearing for exactly this
  reason, and the EN sibling's omission of it is only harmless because EN does
  not admit space groups. The two facts are coupled: **whoever adds the
  separator class must add the `-` exclusion in the same change.**

## BC1. What the bank actually prints

The account summary is TWO printed columns that the text layer flattens into
one interleaved run of lines. Verbatim from `D8FB3C2A…` (the first BofA
document in the run):

```
Account summary
Beginning balance on February 1, 2026 $6,644.32
# of deposits/credits: 24
Deposits and other credits 11,872.17
# of withdrawals/debits: 195
Withdrawals and other debits -13,952.65
# of items-previous cycle: 8
Checks -1,020.00
# of days in cycle: 28
Service fees -0.00
Average ledger balance: $3,024.88
Ending balance on February 28, 2026 $3,543.84
```

The left column is money (`Deposits and other credits`, `Withdrawals and
other debits`, `Checks`, `Service fees`); the right column is a STATISTICS BOX
(`# of deposits/credits`, `# of withdrawals/debits`, `# of items-previous
cycle`, `# of days in cycle`, `Average ledger balance`). They are independent
lists — which is why `# of days in cycle` lands next to `Service fees`. **No
printed figure scopes `# of withdrawals/debits` to the `Withdrawals and other
debits` money line**, and the apparent pairing is an artifact of the flatten.

The same document's Checks section, eleven pages later:

```
Checks
Date Check # Amount Date Check # Amount
02/24/26 1117 -800.00 02/25/26 1119 -60.00
02/24/26 1118 -60.00 02/27/26 1120 -100.00
Total checks -$1,020.00
Total # of checks 4
```

## BC2. The characterization, per layout

Measured over all **360 distinct claimed BofA documents** (362 rows, 2
duplicate hashes). "captured" is the payload's `direction == "debit"` row
count, which is exactly what `analysis/reconcile.py:253-257` compares against.

| layout | docs | prints `# of withdrawals/debits` | prints `Total # of checks` | raw == captured | raw + cheques == captured | baseline stored == captured |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** — native business summary | 344 | 344 | 107 | **344** | **0** | 237 |
| **B** — native consumer summary | 16 | 0 | 0 | — | — | — |
| **C** — HTML-table summary | **0** | — | — | — | — | — |
| **total** | **360** | 344 | 107 | **344** | **0** | 237 |

Four things that table settles.

1. **The raw printed figure is a whole-direction count, 344 of 344.** It
   reproduces every row in the debit column — withdrawals, cheques and service
   fees together.
2. **The cheques are inside it.** On the 107 documents that print a cheque
   count, that printed count equals the captured `Check` rows on **107 of
   107**, and the printed debit count still reproduces the whole debit column
   without adding it. Adding it counted them twice.
3. **The control.** The credit sibling in the same printed statistics box —
   same grammar, same box, no scope ambiguity — is **344 of 344**. The box is a
   whole-direction row counter; the debit line is not a different kind of
   thing from the credit line.
4. **Reader C is unreachable in this archive.** No BofA document contains a
   `<table>` at all (0 of 360), so the HTML-table reader's scope is inherited
   from the identical printed line rather than measured. Said out loud in the
   code comment and in the semantics entry, because it is the one part of the
   claim that rests on argument rather than on counting.

### BC2.1 Why the mapping looked right — the asymmetry, stated

The cheque MONEY genuinely is outside `Withdrawals and other debits`: the
summary prints `Checks` as its own line, and that line equals the Checks
section's own `Total checks` figure on **107 of 107**. `stated_total_debits`
therefore really does have to sum the printed lines — and
`repair_bofa_summary` was right to do that, and still does. The cheque COUNT
is not outside. **Money scope and count scope differ on this bank**, and the
defect was reading one off the other. That sentence is now in
`_SUMMARY_COUNT_SCOPE` and in a fixture
(`test_f9_the_cheque_money_still_sits_outside_the_withdrawals_total`).

### BC2.2 What this says about COUNTS-P1 §3.1

Phase 1 measured "raw ⇒ 237 match / 107 mismatch; `+ check_count` ⇒ 153 / 191"
and concluded neither form was safe. The 237/107 split is reproduced here
exactly — and it was never a property of the raw form. **The observer's "raw"
was the STORED value, which is already `+ check_count` on the 107 documents
where the repair fired.** The 237 that matched are the documents where the
repair added nothing; the 107 that missed are the documents where it did. The
`+ check_count` counterfactual is worse still: it added `metrics.check_count`
on top of an already-mapped stored value, i.e. it counted the cheques twice on
those 107. Phase 1's caution was right and its diagnosis was right (the three
readers disagree); the specific number that made the mapping look "WRONG on
more than half" was measuring the defect, not the mapping.

### BC2.3 The printed-only test that is NOT available, disclosed

The cleanest printed-evidence proof of scope would be a **cheques-only**
statement: printed outflow money consisting of the `Checks` line alone, where
`# of withdrawals/debits == Total # of checks` would settle the question from
two printed integers with no row anywhere in the argument. **The archive
contains zero such documents** (`N - M` ranges from 24 to 435 over the 107).
The necessary condition `N >= M` holds on 107 of 107, which is consistent with
inclusion and does not prove it alone. So the scope claim rests on §BC2 items
1-3 — a 344-of-344 agreement with a 344-of-344 control — not on a single
decisive printed identity. Recorded because the falsifier in the semantics
entry is what carries the residual risk.

## BC3. The change

`analysis/bofa.py`:

* **`_SUMMARY_COUNT_SCOPE`** (`:368-403`) — the printed-layout note, the

* **repair path** (`:623-632`, `:642`) — `Total # of checks` is no longer read;

`analysis/count_semantics.py`: `bank_of_america:debit` → `comparable=True`,
`scope="whole_direction"`, carrying the history, the measurement, the

an explicit FALSIFIER. The credit entry's `file:line` provenance is refreshed.

fields that moved, with document counts:

**Zero outcome movement, zero unlicensed field movement.** Three observations
on the three fields that did move:

* **Every movement is exactly that document's printed cheque count.** The

* **`reconciliation.captured_debit_count` did NOT move**, on any document. The

* **`metrics.effective_num_withdrawals` is the third mover, and it is the

  straight into it. So the inflated count was not merely internal — it was
  **published as the withdrawal count on 107 documents**, and it is now the
  printed figure. Declared rather than buried: it is a different third field
  from the one the card named, and it is a direct restatement of the same
  correction, not an independent movement.

Three cards. Two were carried out of §CHASE-LAYOUTS as fail-closed residuals
(A′ zero-activity, B1 savings); the third arrived mid-flight from Ocean, out
of the F-MONEYFMT fuzzer's finding.

**Revised after Ocean's adversarial review (verdict: SHIP with amendments).**
The review's strong findings held — card C moves nothing, the savings family
validates with row counts equal to the bank's stated instance counts, combined
statements route correctly, and every A′ admission is genuinely empty. Three
amendments landed in `4c15e88` and are recorded where they belong rather than
in a changelog: the A′ guard gained the posting-row clause and its stated rule
was **corrected** to what fires on the real population (§Z2); card C's
authorization is now in the repository (§Z3.3); three small corrections came
out of the same review (§Z6.4b). All proofs below are re-run on the amended
tree.

## Z0. Summary

|---|---|
| Cell worked | `folder_label == "Chase"` × `failed` × `chase` detected at ≥0.5 in `6893a75b`: **18 records / 18 distinct documents**, reproduced exactly. |

Fixed. **Zero archive movement** — no document in the 501-strong claimed population prints the shape — so the card's value is the class of defect closed, not a document count (§Z3.3). |
| Result over the cell | **0 → 14 claimed and 0 → 14 VALIDATED.** The other 4 fail closed with named diagnoses. |

## Z1. The cell reproduced, and the families re-separated

Selecting `folder_label == "Chase"` × `outcome_class == "failed"` × `chase`
scoring ≥0.5 in `candidates`/`near_miss` from `6893a75b`'s `rows.csv` gives
**18 records over 18 distinct content hashes** — the brief's 18 exactly, no
duplicates. Every one carries `chase:0.5` and `no_parser_matched`: detected by
`chase`, declined at parse.

All 18 were rendered read-only through the production ladder
(`ocr.pipeline.parse_statement`, offline rungs only, `allow_visual_ocr=False`,
so no model client is ever constructed), served from the MAIN checkout's D-3
artifact cache: **18 cache hits, 0 misses, `$0.00`.** The 501-document
claimed population likewise: **501 hits, 0 misses.**

The ANALYSIS stage is deliberately **not** cached in any instrument here. This
branch changes analysis output while `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` is still 8, so a
cached payload would answer the question the previous tree answered — and a
cached *write* would put this branch's output into the cache the main checkout
and every other worktree in the wave read. OCR artifacts are shared read-only;
analysis is computed fresh and discarded.

Grouping the 18 by printed structure gives a different split from the one
§CHASE-LAYOUTS assumed:

| Family | Printed signature | Volume |
|---|---|---|
| **A′-1** genuine zero-activity | `CHECKING SUMMARY`, instance count 0 in every section, **no** `*start*transaction detail` | **4** |
| **A′-2** checking on the savings grid | `CHECKING SUMMARY` **and** a single `*start*transaction detail` grid | **3** |
| **B1** savings | `SAVINGS SUMMARY`, single `*start*transaction detail`, grid `DATE DESCRIPTION AMOUNT BALANCE` | **10** |
| **B2** empty sentinel skeleton | all 14 `*start*…*end*` pairs present and empty | **1** |

§CHASE-LAYOUTS filed all 7 non-savings documents as A′ and predicted 4 would
validate. The prediction is right; this is **why** it is right. Only 4 of the 7
are zero-activity documents at all. The other **3 are Chase checking statements
printing the single transaction-detail grid instead of the six named
sections** — a third family, not a zero-activity variant. The conservative
guard refuses them because they state instances and their balances differ,
which is the correct outcome, but "the conservative rule correctly declines
them" (§C6.2) understates what they are. Recorded as a new fail-closed family
with its volume rather than folded into A′ (§Z6.1).

## Z2. Card A′ — a period in which nothing happened

`parse_chase_statement` ended
`if not txns or stmt.beginning_balance is None or stmt.ending_balance is None: return None`,
so Chase's own statement for a period with no activity was refused as
unreadable. Pre-authorized by Ocean under the §C6.1 conditions.

**(a) The minimal diff.**

```python
-    if not txns or stmt.beginning_balance is None or stmt.ending_balance is None:
+    if stmt.beginning_balance is None or stmt.ending_balance is None:
+        return None
+    # A period in which nothing happened is still a statement, and Chase prints
+    # one: an opening balance, a closing balance equal to it, and its own
+    # instance count of 0 against every section, with no detail section at all.
+    # An empty ledger is admissible ONLY on that evidence — the bank itself
+    # stating no instances and no movement, and the two balances agreeing.
+    # An empty ledger on any other document is this reader failing to read a
+    # section that is there, so it keeps refusing: the emptiness is never taken
+    # as its own proof that the period was empty.
+    # (W3 §CHASE-CLOSURE, from §CHASE-LAYOUTS C6.2.)
+    if not txns and not (
+        not stmt.stated_credit_count
+        and not stmt.stated_debit_count
+        and not stmt.stated_total_credits
+        and not stmt.stated_total_debits
+        and stmt.beginning_balance == stmt.ending_balance
+    ):
         return None
     stmt.transactions = txns
     return stmt
```

**One declared strengthening over the §C6.2 proposal.** That proposal tested
the two stated COUNTS and the two balances. This also tests the two stated
TOTALS. The reason is the `do NOT equate an empty ledger with a valid
statement` condition: a summary stating `Deposits and Additions 0 $250.00`
contradicts itself, and the counts alone would have admitted it. Measured both
ways over the 7 — the strengthening costs nothing (4/7 either way) and refuses
one more contradiction class, so it ships.
`test_an_empty_ledger_is_not_by_itself_a_zero_activity_statement[total_stated]`
pins it.

**AMENDED after Ocean's adversarial review — the clause that makes this safe,
and a correction to what the rule actually says.**

The review found the guard as first written could not tell "the bank printed
zero" from "**this reader failed to read the summary**", and built four shapes
that print real money yet were admitted with an empty ledger and
reconciliation green: summary rows carrying no instance count; section amounts
printed without cents; an HTML summary whose section rows are short; an HTML
summary whose section columns are shifted. Each leaves every stated field
unset while both balance rows still read, and each needs only
`beginning == ending` — which is a real shape, not a contrivance: a sweep
account or a net-zero month closes where it opened.

The required clause is added: the empty ledger is admissible only if the
document **also prints no posting row** (`and not _DATED_ROW_RE.search(text)`).
`_DATED_ROW_RE` reuses this module's own `MM/DD` row grammar, looked for
anywhere in the document and deliberately section-blind — a false positive
costs one refusal, a false negative publishes an empty ledger for a statement
that printed rows.

**And the rule is not what the first draft said it was.** Measured over every
distinct document in the archive with `chase` detection computed live:

```
distinct documents in the archive: 3380
rendered: cache hits=3367 misses=13
chase DETECTS: 515
admitted empty-ledger WITHOUT the clause: 4
admitted empty-ledger WITH the clause:    4
real admissions the clause newly refuses: 0
SHAPES (cr_none, db_none, tc_none, td_none, balances_equal, dated_row):
   x4: (True, True, True, True, True, False)
```

Every admitted document carries **`None` in all four stated fields, never
`0`** — the summary prints no section rows at all. So "the bank stating zero
instances" is **not** what fires on the real population and the rule must not
be read that way. The discriminator is: the two balances agree, no stated
evidence was recovered, and no posting row is printed. The guard comment and
the `ZERO_ACTIVITY` fixture description are corrected to say so, and
`ZERO_ACTIVITY_AS_PRINTED` is the fixture carrying the real shape.

Each of the four probes is pinned twice — once asserting it reaches the guard
in the dangerous state with the clause disabled in-process (so a fixture that
starts being refused for some other reason fails rather than passing
vacuously), and once asserting the shipped tree refuses it.

**A residual, still disclosed.** `_parse_native_summary` ends
`stmt.stated_debit_count = debit_count or None`, so a printed debit count of
**0** and **no debit row at all** are the same `None` here. Changing that line
is outside the authorized guard, so it is not done — and after this amendment
it no longer carries the safety argument, because the posting-row clause does.
All 501 currently-claimed documents have transactions and cannot reach the
branch at all (§Z4.1 measures this rather than arguing it).

**Population note.** The review reports 8 admissions over ~1,034 chase
documents; this scan finds **4 over 515**, asking `chase.detect` directly on
every one of the 3,380 distinct archive documents. The two populations are
built differently and I could not reconcile them from here — flagged for Ocean
rather than papered over. The clause refuses **zero** real admissions in the
population measured, which is the property the amendment requires.

**Result over the A′ family.**

| the 7 A′ documents | base `c5673d2` | shipped |
|---|---|---|
| validated | 0 | **4** |
| failed | 7 | 3 |

The 3 are family A′-2 (§Z1): they state instances and their balances differ.

## Z3. Cards B1 and C

### Z3.1 `chase_savings` — the registration

Chase's savings statement is a distinct printed product on the same native
template: `SAVINGS SUMMARY`, and ONE `*start*transaction detail` grid
`DATE DESCRIPTION AMOUNT BALANCE` in place of the six named checking sections.
`chase` detects all 10 on its own two markers and declines all 10 at parse,
because it hard-requires `CHECKING SUMMARY`.

**Markers — three required, all issuer furniture, no bank NAME.** `*start*summary`
(Chase's own text-layer sentinel, the marker R4-3 added to `chase` precisely
because a bank name is wire boilerplate), `SAVINGS SUMMARY`, and the printed
grid header. Plus one **excluding** marker on `CHECKING SUMMARY`.

**Band 10 + `supersedes` chase**, the established shape for a narrower document
class of the same institution (`chase_export`, `rbc_french`,
`td_canada_native`). Without the edge both registrations claim and the document
resolves **`ambiguous`** — a readable statement sent to review. The edge is safe
in the strong sense rather than the observed one: the excluding marker means
`chase_savings` **cannot** claim, and therefore cannot shadow `chase` on, any
document printing the checking product. A combined statement printing both
summaries stays with `chase`, which owns the checking sections.
`test_the_checking_product_is_positively_excluded` asserts the exclusion by
`excluded_by`, not by absence.

**Two structural rules carry the grid**, and neither reads vocabulary for
meaning:

* **The amount cell wraps onto the line ABOVE its row** — the mirror image of
  the F1 family — when the Description column is full. A bare money line is a
  wrapped AMOUNT when a row starts on the line after it, and a wrapped BALANCE
  when it stands inside one. The difference is the row-group boundary, so it is
  resolved after grouping (a group's trailing bare-money line is the next row's
  amount) rather than by pattern-matching the token. This is the
  `square_checking` footer lesson applied before the defect rather than after
  it: a claim about what a line *contains* is not a claim about where the row
  *ends*. `test_a_bare_money_line_inside_a_row_is_its_balance_not_the_next_amount`
  is the fixture that would fail under the naive rule.
* **The grid's Beginning/Ending Balance rows are bounds, not transactions.**
  One producer flattens the whole grid onto a single physical line, which puts
  the closing bound at the end of the last row — where its figure would be read
  as that row's Balance cell. It is split back off as furniture, reusing the
  bound marker the parser already declares.

`tables.group_rows` is consumed unmodified. It drops what precedes the first
row by contract, and the first row's wrapped amount lives exactly there, so
that leading run is restored by the caller — the case its docstring names.

### Z3.2 The B1 instrument, and why 10/10 rather than ~6/10

Five printings, none derived from the ledger being checked: the summary's two
balances, the grid's own two bound rows, every row's printed running balance,
the last printed balance against the stated ending balance, and the stated
instance counts against the rows read.

| the 10 B1 documents | base `c5673d2` | shipped |
|---|---|---|
| validated | 0 | **10** |
| running-balance walk clean | 0 | **10 / 10** |
| ledger identity holds | 0 | **10 / 10** |
| last printed balance == stated ending | 0 | **10 / 10** |
| grid bound rows agree with the summary | 0 | **10 / 10** |
| stated credit and debit counts == rows read | 0 | **10 / 10** |

§C6.3's rough reader reached 6 validated / 3 withheld / 1 failed and was
explicitly built "to size the family rather than to propose an
implementation" — it captured 1–3 rows on documents whose ledgers carry more.
The two structural rules above are the difference, and the count check is what
makes 10/10 a measurement rather than a hope: a dropped row would show up as a
stated-count mismatch and as a break in the walk, on documents that print
between 1 and 9 rows.

The first build of this reader scored **9/10**, and the one withheld document
was the flattened producer whose closing bound was absorbed into its last row.
That is the `square_checking` §C4-item-3 defect, found here by the instrument
instead of by review. Fixing it structurally took the family to 10/10.

### Z3.3 Card C — the money guard did not admit what the money finder finds

**Authorization.** Card C is not in the CHASE-CLOSURE handoff. It was
authorized by **Ocean's scope-extension directive of 2026-08-13**, issued
mid-flight on the F-MONEYFMT fuzzer's evidence, and scoped there to
guard/finder alignment only — explicitly not a widening of `_SUMMARY_AMOUNT`.
Recorded here so the authorization is in the repository rather than in message
history; the adversarial review was right to refuse to infer it from the
handoff.

`_AMOUNT_RE` guards what `_money` may scrub; `_SUMMARY_AMOUNT` finds the money
in a summary row. W3 F10 widened the finder to allow a gap between the sign and
the figure; the guard was not widened with it.

```python
-_AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(r"\(?-?\$?\s*[0-9][0-9,]*(?:\.[0-9]{2})?-?\)?")
+_AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(r"\(?(?:-\s*)?\$?\s*[0-9][0-9,]*(?:\.[0-9]{2})?-?\)?")
```

A row printing the two attested conventions together — the sign outside the
currency symbol, the column's padding between them, `- $530,178.70` — matched
the finder, failed the guard's `fullmatch`, and `abs(_money(...) or 0.0)`
published **0.00** for a figure the bank had plainly printed.

**It was silent, which is the point.** With a small fee the error sits inside
reconcile's ±1.00 summary tolerance:
`test_the_misread_fee_hid_inside_the_reconciliation_tolerance` reproduces a
document that ships `summary_ok=True`, `ok=True`, `issues=[]` with a residual
of **+0.75** and both `stated_service_charge` and `stated_total_debits` wrong.
The fix does not move the tolerance; it removes what was hiding under it.

**The gap is bound to the sign** (`(?:-\s*)?`) rather than floated across the
prefix, so the guard widened by exactly one printed spelling: an unclosed
`( $X` is still refused, as it was before. `_SUMMARY_AMOUNT` is **not** widened;
the deletion-variant shapes (`($X)`, `$-X`, U+2212) are unattested and stay
backlog. `test_the_guard_admits_every_shape_the_finder_finds` pins the
alignment as a property over the sign × symbol × spacing product rather than as
examples, so the two cannot drift apart again.

**Archive movement: zero.** No document in the 501-strong claimed population
prints the shape (§Z4.1 is 0 diffs with card C in the reverted set). The card's
value is the defect class closed and the invariant now pinned, and the honest
figure is zero documents moved — not a number.

# §COMMSEC-GEN — the `community_section` core-processor template, generalized

COMMSEC-GEN, 2026-08-13. Branch `wave3-community-section`, base `c5673d2`,
worktree `.claude/worktrees/mt-commsec`, brief
`docs/agent-handoffs/COMMSEC-GEN.md`. Baseline: run `6893a75b`.

The cell as handed over: Mission Valley product variants (19 documents detected
at 0.5 and declined at parse) plus First Carolina Bank (2 unclaimed documents on
the same template). §C6.4 had characterized the 19 as "the same customer's other
products … the parser reads one product's section shape" and requested a ruling.

## G0. The characterization contradicts the cell's own premise

**The account product was never the discriminator.** §C6.4 attributed the 19
declines to `Business Analyzed Checking` / `Business Interest Checking` /
`Business Checking` being products the reader does not handle. They are not:
`mission_valley`'s entry point passes `account_heading=None`, so the reader
never restricts itself to a product section in the first place, and the product
literal it does carry (`Business Checking\s*-\s*([X0-9]+)`) only ever populated
`account_number`.

The decisive counter-example is inside the baseline's own validated set:
`85F9F7E7…` is a **`Business Analyzed Checking`** statement and it validates,
while `C7AE0ADA…` is also **`Business Analyzed Checking`** and is declined.
Same issuer, same product, opposite outcomes. Whatever separates them is not the
product name.

What separates them is which **credit section** the statement happens to print.

## G1. Populations, derived from the run rather than quoted

| Population | Distinct hashes | Rows | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mission_valley` detected ≥0.5, `failed`/`no_parser_matched` | **19** | 21 | 17 `Chase/`, 2 `Mission Valley Bank/` |
| `mission_valley` validated (must not move) | **17** | 18 | 16 `Chase/`, 1 `Mission Valley Bank/` |
| `dakota_west` validated (must not move) | **3** | 3 | `Unidentified/` |
| First Carolina (`fcbcarolinas.com`), unclaimed | **2** | 2 | `Chase/` |

The row/hash gap is deduplication: two of the declined Mission Valley documents
and one of the validated ones are filed twice under different customer prefixes.
(Dakota West has no gap; its November statement is a single row marked
`pinned_corpus_duplicate`, which is how the pinned corpus shows through.)

A fortieth document is reachable and was **not** in the run: `CD7E104D…`,
`Misc/Checking Account Statements - 1_30_2026 - 4001245.pdf`, the pinned-corpus
Mission Valley statement. It is covered by `corpus_gate.py`, field for field.
Complete reachable set = 39 + 1 = **40**, and §G6 proves that enumeration
exhaustively rather than by sample.

## G2. The section grammar this platform actually prints

Every transaction section is introduced by its own name followed by the printed
column header `Date Description Amount`. Over the 41 documents of §G1 — the 39
this template claims plus the 2 First Carolina — the set of names is exactly
six:

| Printed name | Occurrences | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `Electronic Credits` | 79 | credits |
| `Other Debits` | 50 | debits |
| `Account Summary` | 44 | **not a transaction section** — same grid header |
| `Electronic Debits` | 38 | debits |
| `Deposits` | 23 | credits |
| `Other Credits` | 7 | credits |

The reader's credit headers were `Deposits` and `Other Credits`. **The commonest
credit section on the whole platform, `Electronic Credits`, was not a credit
section at all.**

It nonetheless read correctly on 17 documents, by accident. `Electronic Credits`
was absent from the *credit stop list* as well, so a `Deposits` section's lazy
body ran straight through the `Electronic Credits` header and swallowed its
rows. A statement that prints no `Deposits` section has nothing to run past, and
reads **zero credits** — which the reconciliation gate then declines, correctly,
because the ledger does not match the printed count.

That is the whole of families C and (with §G4) the sign case. Per-document
instrument over the 19:

| Decline stage | Documents |
|---|---|
| reconciliation gate, credits read **0** of N | 14 |
| reconciliation gate, credits read only the `Other Credits` section (1, 3 and 5 rows of 96, 27 and 36) | 3 |
| summary did not match at all (overdrawn balance, §G4) | 2 |

On all 17 gate declines the **debit** side was already exact — count and total,
delta `0.00` on both — which is what makes the diagnosis unambiguous rather than
a guess: one side of the ledger was perfect and the other was empty.

## G3. The fix is the grammar, not a longer list

Enumerating `Electronic Credits` into the header list would have closed the 19
and left the next qualifier this core processor invents to a future cell. The
platform's rule is that **the head noun of a section's name carries its
direction** — `<qualifier> Credits` / `<qualifier> Debits`, plus the unqualified
`Deposits` — so that is what the reader now reads:

```python
_SECTION_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?<![A-Za-z])(?:[A-Za-z]+ )?(Credits|Debits|Deposits)"
    r"(?:\s+\(continued\))?\s+Date Description Amount",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
```

Three properties follow structurally rather than by enumeration:

* an unseen qualifier (`ATM Credits`, `Wire Debits`) is read on its shape —
  pinned by `test_a_qualifier_the_reader_has_never_seen_is_still_read_by_its_head_noun`;
* `Account Summary`, which prints the **identical** grid header, is excluded
  because "Summary" is not a direction noun — not by being named in a stop list;
* a section runs to the **next section's header**, so rows land in the section
  that printed them and no section can absorb the next one's rows. The
  swallow that used to do the work by accident is gone.

## G4. The second defect: an overdrawn period is still a period

Two of the 19 never reached the gate — their summary did not match at all. The
summary's money pattern was unsigned, and an overdrawn statement prints
`Beginning Statement Balance -$1,363.27`. Identical defect class to §C6.1's
Chase fix, in a different parser.

Widened to `-?\$[\d,]+\.\d{2}` for the two **balance** slots only, parsed with
`STRICT_LEADING_SIGN`. The period's credit and debit **totals** deliberately keep
the unsigned pattern: they are magnitudes whose direction is the row they sit on,
and widening them would let a stray minus become a negative period total.
`test_the_totals_are_magnitudes_and_a_signed_total_is_not_invented` pins that the
reader declines rather than invents.

**What was deliberately not widened.** `_daily_balances` uses the same unsigned
pattern, so an overdrawn *day* silently drops its running balance. Widening it is
a one-character change and it is **not made here**: two currently-validated
documents (`EB13FC00…`, `6EDE6313…`) print a negative daily balance, so the
change would move their `running_balance` output and break the byte-identity this
cell is required to preserve. Reported as a card in §G8.

## G5. First Carolina Bank — FAIL CLOSED, routed to the geometry queue

The two `fcbcarolinas.com` documents share this platform's *furniture* and its
*summary grammar* exactly — `Statement Ending`, `Customer Number`,
`Managing Your Accounts`, `Summary of Accounts`, and an
`Account Summary Date Description Amount` block the existing `_summary` regex
already matches unmodified. What they do not share is the activity grid. Instead
of named credit and debit sections they print one `Account Activity` table:

```
Post Date Description Debits Credits Balance
```

**Which of the two money columns a cell stood in is destroyed by flattening.**
Rows carry one money cell and, on the larger document, no balance. That is the
§C6.5 American Savings Bank criterion, and it was measured rather than assumed.

The only recovery signal printed is the Daily Balances ladder. Instrumented per
day — given a day's money cells and that day's balance delta, how many sign
assignments reproduce the delta?

| Document | Rows | Days unique | Days ambiguous | Ledgers fitting the ladder | …also fitting the printed counts and totals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `FA0B3967…` (4 pp) | 6 of 6 parsed | 4 | 0 | **1** | **1** — determined |
| `EA62440C…` (6 pp) | 107 of 117 parsed | 16 | 4 | **100** | **0** — no consistent ledger |

On the larger document 14 of 121 parsed rows carry no single money cell: the
row-to-money association is itself unreliable, and **no** assignment reproduces
what the bank printed. It is unreadable from the text layer, full stop.

The smaller document *is* determined — but only by enumerating sign assignments
and keeping the one that matches the printed totals. That is the decisive
architectural objection, and it is worth stating plainly because it is not an
argument about effort:

> For every other statement on this platform, **direction is printed** — the
> section name says `Credits` or `Debits` — and the reconciliation gate is an
> *independent* check on a reading made without it. For First Carolina the
> direction would be *derived from* the reconciliation, so the gate stops being
> evidence and becomes a tautology: the ledger balances because balancing is
> how it was constructed. A reader with no instrument left cannot be validated,
> only asserted.

**Ruling: FAIL CLOSED, volume 2, routed to the geometry queue** alongside §C6.5.
No `first_carolina` registration is added. A detect-only registration would
convert `no_parser_matched` into `attempted`, which §C6.6 rightly values, but it
would also be a claim that can never validate, and requirement 3 is explicit that
claimed-but-not-validated is not success. The fix belongs upstream, where the
column geometry still exists.

# §SCOTIA-REBUILD — Cell 11: `scotiabank`, 80 documents, and a reconciliation that could not fail

## S0. Summary

`analysis/scotia.py` published the balance movement as every row's amount and
discarded the printed money cell. `:113` computed
`amount = round(balance - prev_balance, 2)`; `:114-118` read like a guard on
the printed cell but its body re-assigned the identical expression, so the
branch was dead and `values[-2]` was never used for anything.

That alone would be a value defect. What made it a *gate* defect is that the
same loop published `running_balance = balance` and the parser took its
ending balance from the last row. `analysis/reconcile.py` checks
`beginning + sum(amounts) == ending` and `prev + pending == running_balance` —
both of which the parser had just constructed to be true. **`sum_delta` was
0.0 and `continuity_breaks` was 0 on all 80 scotiabank documents by
construction**, so the fail-closed path had nothing left to check on this
parser and its 75 validated documents were certified by a check that
re-derived their own arithmetic.

The rebuild makes the printed cell the amount of record and leaves the
balance column supplying only the direction, which is all it can supply: this
layout flattens `Withdrawals/Debits ($)` and `Deposits/Credits ($)` into one
printed value. Result over the cell: **validated 75 -> 78, withheld 5 -> 3,
failed 4 -> 3, and zero documents moved down.**

## S1. The pinned-corpus question, answered before any production edit

The corpus pins exactly one scotiabank document, `ScotiaBank/Scotiabank
-2.pdf` (`B64A0764...`, 417 transactions, PASS on both oracles). The row loop
was replayed on it through the audits' own markdown path
(`adb_forensic_audit.source_markdown`, as `corpus_gate` resolves it) before
`analysis/scotia.py` was touched.

The first replay found 20 rows where the printed cell disagreed with the
walk. **All 20 were an artifact of the tokeniser, not a disagreement.** This
document's text layer prints the amount column with its trailing zeros
stripped — `34.9` for $34.90, `403.5` for $403.50, `25` for $25.00 — and both
the parser's own `_MONEY_RE` and `analysis.money.parse_money` require two or
three decimal places, so `34.9` was read as the two numbers `34` and `9`.
Padding the printed form first, the printed cell agrees with the balance walk
on **all 417 rows**.

Field-level, against the module as it stood at `b95595f`:

| field | differences | audited? |
|---|---|---|
| `transaction.date` | 0 | yes (ADB posting days) |
| `transaction.amount` | 0 | yes (ledger sum) |
| `transaction.running_balance` | 0 | yes (balance oracle) |
| `transaction.direction` | 0 | published |
| `transaction.description` | **38** | published, not audited |
| every `Statement` scalar | 0 | — |

No audited value moves, so the formal ceremony is not engaged. The 38
descriptions all move the same way: the shipped parser located the
description's cut with `rfind` on the money token as a *substring*, so rows
kept a fragment of their own money cell (`...ONCA 34.9 3,`, `...MB-TRANSFER 2
52`). The rebuild cuts at the token index and the fragments are gone. This is
the one published-field change on a pinned PASS document and it is recorded
here rather than buried: `docs/*-audit-results.csv` carries no description
column, and `tests/data/parser_expectations.json` pins only `parser_id` and
`chain_declined_ids`.

`corpus_gate.py` returns GREEN (S7), which is the empirical half of the same
claim.

## S2. The cell reproduced independently

Run `6893a75b`, the newest full archive run. The scotiabank *detector* claims
84 documents (`scotiabank:0.5` in `candidates`); the other 28 documents where
the id appears at all sit at `0.166667`, a single marker, below the claim
threshold. Detection is untouched by this cell, so those 84 are the complete
blast radius and every one of them was swept.

Of the 84: 80 parsed (75 validated, 5 withheld on `withheld_adb`) and 4
declined. Replaying the archive markdown through the real pipeline
(`analyze_markdown` + `telemetry.record.classify_outcome`) reproduced
`75 / 5 / 4` exactly.

**One scout figure did not reproduce.** The brief carried "615 rows divergent
from the printed cell, 512 of them in validated documents". That measurement
compared `abs(delta)` with `abs(values[-2])` under the broken tokeniser, and
it is the same artifact §S1 found on the pinned document. Under correct
tokenisation the census over the cohort is **10 divergent rows out of 11,138,
and 0 of them in a validated document** — all 10 sit in three documents that
were already withheld. The brief's "~29 recoverable F1-class declines" did
not reproduce either: the cohort holds 4 declines, of which 1 is recoverable
and 3 are the geometry class.

The tautology was real and is exactly as described; what was not real is the
volume of wrong amounts it was hiding. The shipped amounts were mostly
*right* — because the delta equals the printed cell whenever the walk is
sound — but they were right underneath a check that could not fail.

## S3. The four defects, and the structural rule that replaces each

**1. The tautology.** The printed cell now ships as the magnitude and the
balance movement supplies only the sign. Where they disagree the
disagreement is published rather than resolved: the printed magnitude ships,
the printed balance ships, and `reconcile` sees a continuity break and a
ledger-sum mismatch. No new schema field — the platform already had the
check; it had been given nothing to check.

**2. Merchant-ref-as-balance.** A balance cell is now a currency value
printed to two decimals with optional grouping and an optional trailing
overdraft minus. An 11-digit `MRCH FIRST DATA CANADA(K)` reference on a
continuation line is not that shape and can no longer become a balance. The
amount is then the money token immediately preceding that balance, with bare
unseparated integers longer than three digits refused as reference numbers,
account fragments and years.

**3. Section discipline.** Rows are read only from inside an `Account
Details` posting table, bounded by the table's own printed column header
(`Date Description Withdrawals/Debits ($) Deposits/Credits ($) Balance ($)`)
and the section close. A Scotiabank PDF bundles several statements for one
account; the `Deposit Interest` sheet is a daily-yield ledger with one dated
row per calendar day and it declares a *different* grid, so it falls outside
every span by construction rather than by a blocklist of section names.

**4. Zero activity.** Admitted per the Chase A-prime rule: zero instances AND
zero totals in both directions, plus an opening balance, and then the closing
balance is the opening balance on the bank's own evidence. An empty ledger on
any other document still refuses — four negatives pin the ways a document can
fail to prove that nothing happened.

## S6. Carried findings and questions for Ocean

1. **`parse_money` cannot read a one-decimal amount.** `_TOKEN_RE` accepts
   two or three decimal places, so `34.9` returns `34.0` — silently, and
   $0.90 low. This cell pads the token at its own call site, which is the
   division `analysis/money.py` documents (engine shared, format with the
   bank), and money.py is out of scope here. But the shape "money printed
   with trailing zeros stripped" is unlikely to be Scotiabank's alone, and a
   parser that hands `34.9` straight to `parse_money` gets a wrong number
   with no signal. Worth a sweep on the money integration card.
2. **The scout's 615/512 figures should not be carried forward** into any
   roll-up; §S2 has the corrected census (10 / 0).
3. **Direction on a divergent row is the walk's sign**, since the flattened
   layout leaves no column evidence. On a row where printed and walk
   disagree, the magnitude is printed and the sign is inferred — the row is
   published *with* the contradiction rather than dropped, and `reconcile`
   withholds the document. Recorded as a deliberate choice.
4. **`possible_document_issue` fires at `continuity_breaks >= 3`.** Two of
   the three value-corrected documents now sit at 3 and 5; `D0056217` sits at
   2 and is withheld on other grounds. No action needed, noted so the
   threshold's new sensitivity on this parser is not a surprise.

## S9. Amendments from adversarial review

Ocean's review returned SHIP with two required amendments. Both are the same
class: a rule that was correct about what it looked at, and silent about what
it did not look at.

**1. Zero-activity was not checking that the posting tables were empty.**
The guard fired on `not txns`, which cannot distinguish "the bank printed no
activity" from "activity was printed and every row of it was refused". The
reviewer's probe prints 0/0 counts, $0.00/$0.00 totals, an opening balance
*and* two posting rows whose cells the shape rules reject — and the parser
published `transactions=[]` as validated/approved, which is exactly the
"empty captured ledger equated with a valid statement" the four negatives
were written to prevent. They all happened to carry no rows at all, so none
of them caught it.

The clause added: zero-activity is admissible only if the posting tables
contain no dated row, `BALANCE FORWARD` excluded as the table's opening
bound rather than a posting. This mirrors the Chase A′ no-MM/DD-row
discipline, scoped to the structural spans. `90D94C41`, the genuine
zero-activity mover, still validates.

**2. Spans were bounded at one end only.** `_posting_tables` ended a span at
`_TABLE_CLOSE` or the end of the document, so a section that never printed a
closing token ran on. Two consequences, both proven by the reviewer: a
trailing posting table absorbed a following `Deposit Interest` sheet that did
not open with a close token (2 fabricated rows), and — because every header
opens a span independently — an unclosed span ran THROUGH the next header, so
the following table's rows were read by both spans and published twice
(`03/02` duplicated).

Each span is now additionally bounded by the point at which the next table
declares its own columns. Every Scotiabank grid announces itself as a
`Date`-led run of column labels reaching a `($)` money column, so one bound
closes both holes.

**Re-proof after the span change** (span construction changed, so
byte-identity had to be re-established): the 84-document cohort sweep is
**identical on all 84 documents** — 0 differing on any of the 21 compared
fields against the pre-amendment run — and still 3 up / 0 down against the
baseline, the same three movers. The pinned document re-compared field by
field against `b95595f` is still 0 on every audited field.

### Residuals recorded, deliberately not fixed

* **Tail truncation with no summary grid.** When a document's final posting
  table is cut off and the layout prints no summary block, `ending_balance`
  is taken from the last row actually read, so a truncated tail yields a
  closing balance that is real but early. This is inherent to a layout that
  prints no closing figure to check against — there is no second source on
  the page to detect it. Recorded as the honest limit of this parser rather
  than papered over.
* **`$0.00` rows carry the debit label.** Five rows across the cohort print a
  zero amount — every one of them a `LOAN INTEREST` posting, in `6F78F153`
  (1) and `B616BF47` (4). With `delta == 0` the direction rule yields
  `debit`. This matches the behaviour at `b95595f`, and loan interest is
  genuinely a debit-column item, so nothing is misstated.
* **The `count_semantics` citation** (`analysis/scotia.py:80-82`) now points
  at shifted line numbers. Ocean's at merge.
# §FILENAME-BOUNDARY — the provenance admissibility boundary, applied to parsing

Platform cell, not a layout cell. The unit of work is one seam, and the
deliverable is an invariant: **a rename cannot change a published answer.**

## FB0. Summary

The OCR/native layer prefixes every document with
`<!-- source: <file> | pages: … -->`. R-4b made DETECTION blind to it
(`parser_registry.admissible_text`) and wrote the carve-out into that
function's own docstring — *"Parsing is unaffected: `parse` still receives the
whole document."* That sentence was the vulnerability.

F-PROVENANCE measured what came through the hole: 7 of 10 sampled parsers read
financial evidence out of the filename. The fix is one line at one seam —
`analyze_markdown` applies `admissible_text` at stage entry — plus the crash it
exposed, the cache key it obsoleted, and the test that keeps it closed.

`ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` is deliberately NOT bumped here; it is Ocean's at
merge.

## FB1. The defect, reproduced independently

Two reproducers, run against this branch's code before any change:

* **R1 — same bytes, different answers.** Corpus document `09BAFBBC`
  (`wells_fargo`). Under a neutral filename it publishes period
  `2026-05-01 … 2026-05-31`. Renamed to
  `January 1, 2020 through December 31, 2020.pdf` it publishes
  `2020-05-01 … 2020-05-31` — a six-year error in the period a human reads,
  from a rename alone. `wells._infer_year` takes the FIRST word-bounded year
  token in the document, and the comment line is above the statement.
  Post-fix, the same document under 5 filenames yields **1 distinct answer**,
  and it is the correct 2026 one.
* **R2 — the crash.** `date_tokens.period_from_long_dates` raised `KeyError`
  on 4 of 5 probe phrases: any abbreviated month, and any capitalized
  non-month word, because `([A-Z][a-z]+)` matches both. Post-fix: 0 raise,
  genuine long dates unchanged.

## FB2. Cards

1. **The boundary.** `analyze_markdown` rebinds `markdown = admissible_text(markdown)`
   as its first act. A REBIND, not a second local: one line makes the property
   total and checkable by reading the function, where a new local would leave
   the guarantee to every present and future call site remembering which
   variable is the admissible one.
2. **The crash.** `_MONTH_NAMES[sm]` → `.get`, and a miss returns `None`. The
   docstring's own contract is that None means "try another period format";
   the escaping `KeyError` was a `ParserCrashError` in deterministic mode and,
   in the webapp's auto mode, a silent fall-through to LLM extraction — an
   engine swap decided by an abbreviated month.
3. **The cache key.** The analysis stage hashed the raw markdown, and the
   filename is printed into the markdown header, so the filename was key
   material by the back door. Now `text_sha256(admissible_text(markdown))`.
   The `report` stage still keys on the whole markdown: a rendered artifact
   may legitimately show provenance.
4. **The test.** `tests/test_filename_boundary.py`, default suite.

## FB3. Why the seam is at stage entry, not at the parser call site

`parse` is not the only consumer of the document text. `analyze_markdown`
hands the same string to:

| Consumer | What it reads it for | Exposure |
|---|---|---|
| `resolve` → `registration.parse` | the ledger | periods, ADB, year inference |
| `apply_statement_repairs` | BofA / Regions substring gates | can overwrite ANOTHER bank's published balances |
| `assess_document_integrity` | the `Page N of M` declaration set | can FABRICATE or SUPPRESS `missing_declared_statement_page` |
| `compute_metrics(source_markdown=)` | the ADB posting-date check | ADB denominator |
| `extract_statement` | the LLM prompt | everything |

One rebind at stage entry covers all five. Each is pinned by its own test
rather than by inspection — see FB5.

## FB4. Scope discipline — what was NOT changed

No parser was edited. `wells._infer_year` still takes the first year token in
the document; it is simply no longer reachable from provenance, because the
provenance is gone before it runs. The repair stage still gates on substrings.
Those are separate cards. **One fix, one seam: no stop condition fired — every
measured case is neutralized by the boundary alone.**

## FB5. The invariance test — `tests/test_filename_boundary.py`

Default suite (no pinned PDFs, no OCR cache, no network, ~27s). 133 tests.

| Group | Cases | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| primary invariance | 4 parsers x 26 hostile filenames = 104 | identical bytes -> byte-identical FULL serialized report |
| vacuity guards | 4 | each fixture is still CLAIMED by its parser and still parses transactions |
| sentinel | 4 | no filename byte appears anywhere in the published report |
| seam idempotency | 4 | `analyze(md) == analyze(admissible_text(md))` — fuzz5's property, permanently |
| repair gate | 4 | a `BANK OF AMERICA` / `REGIONS` filename cannot fire that bank's repair |
| page declarations | 2 | a `Page N of M` filename can neither FABRICATE nor SUPPRESS `missing_declared_statement_page` |
| `date_tokens` | 8 | non-month long-date phrases are non-matches; genuine long dates unchanged |
| cache key | 2 | renames share one analysis entry; different bodies still do not |

The comparison is the whole serialized report, not a watched field list, so a
parser that starts reading provenance for any reason fails here rather than
being caught later by whichever field somebody remembered to check.

**Verified as a regression test, not a tautology.** With the seam line removed
and everything else intact: **23 failures across all four parsers**; the
Ocean-requested subset alone gives **9 failures**, including the Regions repair
firing on the Chase fixture from the filename alone, page-declaration
fabrication on all four fixtures, and suppression of the missing-page flag on
wells. Restored byte-exact and green.

## FB6. Proofs

Harnesses run from the wave scratchpad with `sys.path` pointed at THIS
worktree and the D-3 cache + `rows.csv` read from the main checkout read-only.
The adaptation is one line in a private copy (`wt_filename/fuzz2.py`:
`sys.path.insert(0, CODE)` instead of `REPO`) plus a hard assertion that
`analysis.pipeline` and `analysis.parser_registry` resolve under the worktree —
a worker that loaded main's code raises instead of silently proving nothing.

| Proof | Pre-fix | Post-fix | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| fuzz2 — 200 docs x 20 mutations (4,200 analyses) | **140 violated docs**, 420 violated pairs, 60 crash-mutations | **0 / 0 / 0** | 0 |
| fuzz3 — silent calendar-year widening, 200 docs x 9 | **120 violated docs**, 240 pairs, 20 crash-mutations | **0 / 0 / 0** | 0 |
| fuzz5 — parity `analyse(md)` vs `analyse(admissible_text(md))`, 200 docs | 0 changed | **0 changed** | 0 |
| fuzz4 — LIVE census, all validated archive docs | **0 / 1,615 contaminated** | (see FB7) | — |
| full default suite | — | 2,699 passed, 18 deselected (197s) | 0 |
| `tests/test_stated_counts.py` (incl. the new join tests) | — | 58 passed | 0 |
| `pytest -m corpus` | — | 14 passed, 2,700 deselected (1,803s) | 0 |
| `python corpus_gate.py` | — | **GREEN, 106 PASS / 3 WITHHELD** (883.6s) | 0 |
| conformance cross-product | — | 468 tests, inside the green default suite | 0 |

Pre-fix figures are F-PROVENANCE's own committed artifacts (`full.json`,
`wide.json`, `safe.json`, `live.json`), re-counted rather than quoted, over the
identical sample and mutation set — the reruns use the same `--per-parser 20`
and the same ordering, so the two columns are like-for-like.

## FB7. Zero outcome movement — the preview Ocean's instrument should confirm

**Predicted: zero.** Two independent measurements, both pre-fix, which is where
this question can actually be answered:

* fuzz4's live census compared every validated archive document's real
  filename against a neutral one: **0 of 1,615 contaminated**. Nothing the
  platform publishes today depends on a filename — naming-convention luck, not
  design.
* fuzz5 measured the change directly: applying `admissible_text` to the parse
  path altered **0 of 200** published reports across 10 parsers.

Honest limitation: **post-fix fuzz5 is a tautology** (both sides now go through
the boundary), so it is a no-crash regression check, not evidence of
invariance. The load-bearing evidence for zero movement is the pre-fix pair
above, plus the gate reproducing all 109 audited documents byte-identically.

## FB8. Carried findings and questions for Ocean

1. **The brief's line-index claim is wrong, and it does not matter.**
   `admissible_text` does NOT "substitute an empty line" on a real document.
   `to_markdown` emits `header\n\n\n\n--- Page 1 ---`, and the pattern's greedy
   `\s*$` consumes the header plus three newlines, so an 8-line document
   becomes 5: **a uniform 3-line prefix shift**, all of it above any content.
   Nothing downstream keys off an absolute markdown line index — the
   structurer derives its own from the text it is handed, and
   `DocumentGeometry` is built from OCR word boxes and is `None` for every
   production caller. Empirically confirmed by fuzz5 (0/200) and the gate.
   Flagged because the handoff asserted the opposite as verified.
2. **`period_from_long_dates` still raises `ValueError`** on an in-range-looking
   but impossible date — `"January 99, 2026 through February 4, 2026"`,
   `"February 31, 2026 through March 1, 2026"`. Same call sites, same crash
   class as the `KeyError` just fixed. **Deliberately not patched**: card 2 was
   scoped to the month lookup, and
   `test_shared_parser_utils.PERIOD_DOCS` currently PINS the `ValueError` as
   matching the frozen R-2 oracle, so changing it is a contract decision, not a
   cleanup. No longer reachable from a filename; still reachable from a garbled
   document body. Recommend a follow-up card.
3. **`admissible_text` strips EVERY matching line, not just line 1.** A body
   line shaped like `<!-- SOURCE: … -->` is now also removed from the parse
   text. New for parsing (detection always behaved this way). Almost certainly
   a hardening bonus — it defeats an injected fake provenance line — but it is
   a behaviour change, so it is stated rather than assumed benign.
4. **Two non-production callers still parse raw markdown**:
   `experiments/w3_3a/evaluate.py:158` and `tools/measure_structurer.py:153`
   call `resolve(markdown)` directly, below the boundary. Neither publishes an
   answer, and `tests/test_experiments_are_not_wired.py` structurally forbids
   `experiments/` from reaching production. Left alone — moving the boundary
   into `resolve` would create a SECOND boundary and still not cover the
   repairs, metrics and integrity consumers, which is exactly why the seam is
   at stage entry. Worth a decision if those tools ever gain a publishing path.
5. **Cache re-key cost is subsumed by the stage bump.** Card 3 re-keys every
   cached analysis on its own — an estimated **~13,300 artifacts** (256 shards,
   8 sampled, avg 52/shard). But `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` is in the same key
   and Ocean is bumping it at merge, which invalidates the same set. The
   incremental operational cost of card 3 is therefore **zero**: one full
   recompute happens either way, and results are expected identical.

6. **The cache key had a SECOND implementation, and this cell missed it**
   (caught by Ocean's adversarial review, fixed under an authorised scope
   extension). `telemetry/stated_counts.py`'s `_ArtifactJoin.payload_for`
   recomputes the analysis key to join a discovery run to its cached payloads,
   and it hashed the RAW reconstructed markdown. Once the cache moved to
   `admissible_text`, that join missed **every** document: `payload_for`
   returns None for all of them and `observe_run` emits `payload_absent` on
   100% of rows — the counts instrument goes blind while staying green, which
   is the worst failure mode available to a measurement tool. It had zero test
   coverage. Now fixed, pinned by three tests, and a repo-wide sweep confirms
   these are the only two computations of the analysis key
   (`webapp/artifact_cache.py:622`, `telemetry/stated_counts.py:777`); the
   `report` stage at :646 correctly still hashes the whole markdown.
   **Process lesson for the next platform cell: changing a cache key means
   grepping the repo for every reimplementation of that key, not just editing
   the module that owns it.**

# §DISPATCH-REPORTING — the declined queue, made visible

DISPATCH-REPORTING, 2026-08-13. Branch `wave3-dispatch-reporting`, base
`b95595f` (current main). Brief: `docs/agent-handoffs/DISPATCH-REPORTING.md`.

**Reporting only.** No dispatch, parsing, analysis or caching behaviour
changes; no outcome class moves; `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` untouched, because
no analysis payload differs by a single byte.

## D0. Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| The defect | `analysis/parser_registry.py:544-573` has recorded `Dispatch.attempted` ("declined, rather than broke") since W3-1 and `telemetry/record.py:210` has written it since H-3. `discovery/runner.py` never read it: `:592-595` mapped **every** statement-less unclaimed to `no_parser_matched`. |
| Why it matters | That one name carried two findings needing opposite work — a bank we have no parser for (build one) and a parser that recognises the document and returns None (widen it). 175 archive documents are the second kind. §CHASE-LAYOUTS C0 independently found 126 of its 176 documents were `Dispatch.attempted == ('chase',)` and the resulting fix validated 106 of them: the declined class is where the cheap validated gain lives, and it was filed at the bottom of the expensive list. |
| Changes | Three, all in `discovery/`: the row carries `attempted`; `_failure_reason` splits `parser_declined` from `no_parser_matched`; `summarize` ranks `parser_declined × parser` as `declined_clusters`. |
| `discovery/compare.py` | **Not changed, and proven not to need changing** (§D3). |
| Files | `discovery/runner.py`, `discovery/report.py`, `tests/test_discovery.py`, this log. Nothing else — `parser_registry.py` and `telemetry/` already did their part. |
| Tests | 5 added, all in the fast default suite. |
| Dry run | The pinned 109 reproduce exactly, with the new column present (§D4). |

## D1. The split

`no_parser_matched` now means what it says — nothing even claimed the
document. An unclaimed dispatch whose `attempted` is non-empty is
`parser_declined`. A crash still outranks both: "detected, then broke" is a
defect of ours and must never be filed as "detected, then declined", which is
the same argument W3-1 made one level up.

```python
    if dispatch is not None and dispatch.outcome == "unclaimed":
        return "parser_declined" if dispatch.attempted else "no_parser_matched"
```

The row's `attempted` column is bare ids, not `id:score` pairs: the declining
parser's detection score is already in `candidates`, and what the new column
adds is that it got as far as `parse` and returned None. It sits between
`candidates` and `near_miss` in `ROW_FIELDS`.

Note the column is populated for **claimed** documents too, when a claimant
declined before the winner was reached. The `declined_clusters` rollup counts
only documents that ended unclaimed — a document that was ultimately served is
not a work item — so the row and the rollup answer deliberately different
questions.

## D2. Why no outcome class can move

`telemetry.record.classify_outcome` reaches the reason only through
`if payload is None: return "failed", error_reason or ...`. The reason is a
pass-through label on an already-decided class. Both names are `failed`, both
are `unclaimed`, and `deterministic_coverage` is computed from
`dispatch_outcome`, never from the reason. The rename cannot move a document,
a coverage percentage, or a gate.

## D3. W3-4 compatibility, proven rather than asserted

`discovery/compare.py` keys movement on `outcome_class` and on the W3-2
`diagnostics.primary_class`. It loads `outcome.reason` into
`evidence.Document` and **never ranks by it**. So a baseline row saying
`no_parser_matched` and a candidate row saying `parser_declined` for the same
document is `unchanged`, contributes no transition, and cannot trip
`--fail-on-regression`. `test_the_rename_is_not_movement_between_two_runs`
builds both runs and asserts `identical is True`,
`movement == {"unchanged": 1}`, and empty transitions — so if compare ever
starts ranking by reason, that test fails rather than a merge gate
mis-reporting a reporting change as a regression.

Both surviving reason aggregators — `discovery.report.summarize`'s `reasons`
Counter and `telemetry/report.py:50` — are open-vocabulary Counters. A new
reason name flows through them with no code change.
