## T1. The measurement instrument, and what it was allowed to touch

Everything measured below comes from scratch scripts outside the repo, reading:

* `discovery_reports/2026-08-13T163911.518386-0000-6893a75b/rows.csv` — the two
  populations and their baseline outcomes (40 documents whose `candidates`
  name `td_us`: 28 validated, 2 withheld, 10 unclaimed; 73 naming
  `td_canada_native`: 63 validated, 10 withheld);
* the D-3 artifact cache at `webapp_data/artifacts/ocr/`, **by direct file
  path only** — the sqlite index was never opened, because a full archive
  discovery run was executing on the machine throughout. The markdown was
  reconstructed through `StatementMarkdown(...).to_markdown()`, the same
  reconstruction `webapp/artifact_cache.cached_ocr` performs on a hit, from
  the artifact whose `document.model` matches the run's recorded
  `source_model`.

**Zero OCR, zero model calls, `$0.00`, no write of any kind to the archive or
the cache.** `analyze_markdown` is called directly, never through
`cached_analysis`, so no artifact is stored.

**The instrument reproduces the run of record.** Before any edit, the sweep
over all 113 reconstructed documents returns the recorded outcome class for
every one, and the recorded reason for 103. The other 10 are the td_us
declines, recorded `no_parser_matched` by a run that predates `c476f1d`
(§DISPATCH-REPORTING) and reproduced as `parser_declined` — the rename, not a
drift, and it is the same 10 documents.

Before/after is measured **in one process**: the base-commit copy of each
changed file is loaded from its git blob as its own module and swapped into
`parser_registry._REGISTRY`, so the only variable is the file under test.
Compared per document: outcome class and reason, dispatch outcome, parser id,
candidate vector, attempted list, exceptions, 15 statement fields, transaction
count and signed sums, the reconciliation object, ADB and its validity,
coverage, quality and the integrity flags.

**The population is provably the whole of it, and nothing outside it can
move.** `resolve` builds `candidates` from every surviving claimant *before any
parse runs*, and returns `ambiguous` immediately when there is more than one.
So a document where `td_us` claims is a document whose `candidates` name
`td_us` — the 40 — and on every one of them `td_us` was the sole survivor
(`len(survivors) > 1` would have made it `ambiguous`, and none is). A parser
that starts returning a statement where it used to return `None` therefore
cannot displace another parser anywhere in the archive: on a multi-claimant
document the verdict was already decided before either parse. The same
argument covers C1's 73. `analysis/td_can.py`'s HTML-table path is untouched
either way — `_native_credit_like` has two callers, both inside the native
balance resolution; the table path reads `_credit_like`, which is unchanged.

## T2. U1 — an overdrawn opening balance is a balance (6 documents)

`_summary` reads four summary fields with four patterns. Three of the four are
balances; only the closing one could stand next to TD's minus sign.

```python
-        "beginning_balance": r"Beginning Balance\s+([\d,]+\.\d{2})",
-        "stated_average_balance": r"Average Collected Balance\s+([\d,]+\.\d{2})",
+        "beginning_balance": r"Beginning Balance\s+(-?[\d,]+\.\d{2})",
+        "stated_average_balance": r"Average Collected Balance\s+(-?[\d,]+\.\d{2})",
         "days_in_period": r"Days in Period\s+(\d+)",
         "ending_balance": r"Ending Balance\s+(-?[\d,]+\.\d{2})",
```

A pattern that cannot match the sign does not read a smaller number: it reads
nothing, `beginning_balance` stays `None`, and `:196` returns `None` for the
whole document — which is why an extraction defect arrived filed as an
unclaimed layout. `_money` already parsed a leading minus
(`PARENS_OR_LEADING_MINUS`), so only the capture pattern was ever at fault.
Identical defect class to §C6.1, which is where the shape of this card comes
from.

**The six movers, each verified against the figure the statement prints.**

| Document | printed `Beginning Balance` | closes at | rows | `sum_delta` | `summary_ok` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `1E175E596948` | `-8.32` | 124.07 | 76 | 0.00 | True |
| `9AB8FB6C0B20` | `-128.60` | -8.32 | 99 | 0.00 | True |
| `523A6816FA49` | `-16.04` | 9,317.95 | 53 | 0.00 | True |
| `CEA1C7496377` | `-335.39` | -921.58 | 99 | 0.00 | True |
| `3B228A49B3B4` | `-921.58` | 21.23 | 93 | 0.00 | True |
| `B839AE3942A4` | `-722.51` | 29,225.28 | 51 | 0.00 | True |

All six are `validated` / `approved` with no integrity flags. Two independent
corroborations that the sign is read correctly rather than merely accepted:
each document's ledger closes on its own arithmetic (`sum_delta 0.00`, a
mis-signed opening would break that identity rather than close it), and **two
pairs chain across consecutive months** — `9AB8FB6C0B20` ends at `-8.32` where
`1E175E596948` begins, and `CEA1C7496377` ends at `-921.58` where
`3B228A49B3B4` begins.

**The one value mover on a document that already validated.** `:39` was
silently dropping a printed negative average. Exactly one document in the
validated population prints one:

```
  B5AEDEB7E9C9  stated_average_balance: None -> -78.54
```

verified against its ACCOUNT SUMMARY, which prints
`Average Collected Balance -78.54` under a positive `Beginning Balance 163.90`.
Nothing else about that document moves — the field is not a required ADB
check (`analysis/adb.py:486-500` records `agrees_with_bank_stated_average` as

are identical before and after.

**The four documents that still decline are correctly declining**, and neither
card touches them: `7645F0A8583C` prints `Beginning Balance �,017.43` (Tesseract
lost the leading digit — an unreadable figure, not an unread one),
`A7E4B895E2A9` has no readable `Statement Period:` line at all, and the other

## T3. U2 — a short section is a short section, not a void document

```python
-        if abs(sum(abs(t.amount) for t in txns) - total) > 0.02:
-            return None
         all_txns.extend(txns)
```

Two scanned documents hit this, and on both the statement is not
self-contradictory — Tesseract lost rows out of a 40-row section while the
summary, the balances and the other sections came through exactly. Discarding
the document threw away 43 and 58 good rows and filed an OCR defect as an
unclaimed layout.

The rows that were read are kept and the shortfall is left where the platform
can see it. Both documents now reach the fail-closed gate and are refused
there:

| Document | rows | `sum_delta` | `summary_ok` | debit coverage | ADB | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2A0B516B2C7D` | 43 | +394.71 | True | 93% | refused | `withheld` / `withheld_adb` |
| `1A8B92DC6167` | 58 | +307.18 | True | 97% | refused | `withheld` / `withheld_adb` |

with the gap named in the reconciliation issues ("captured $5,193.88 of the
bank's stated $5,588.59 in debits (93%) — line-item detail is inconsistent or
incomplete; do not use it for daily-balance reconstruction"). Both carry the
same four integrity flags:

```
['debit_detail_coverage_mismatch', 'ledger_sum_mismatch',
 'missing_declared_statement_page', 'transaction_detail_not_corporate_reliable']
```

`missing_declared_statement_page` is pre-existing and independent of this card
— both are scans whose page declaration outruns the pages that survived — but
it belongs in the record: these documents arrive at review carrying it too.
**Claimed is not published: neither validates**, and they join `D3396D14BA8A` /
`BDA1DE2F3481`, the two documents of the same scanned batch that were already
withheld for the same reason.

**What removing the check costs — corrected after adversarial review.** This
section first claimed the discarded test "was a second, harsher copy of a gate
that already exists downstream." **That is false, and the reviewer disproved it
by construction.** `reconcile` compares DIRECTION-LEVEL totals — captured
credits against `stated_total_credits`, captured debits against
`stated_total_debits` — so it is structurally blind to two misreads of equal
and opposite size *within* one direction. The removed check saw both, because
it looked at one section at a time. It had a capability the coverage gate does
not have.

Reproduced independently before rewriting this paragraph, on a two-section
synthetic where `Electronic Payments` reads 100.00 short of its printed
subtotal and `Other Withdrawals` reads 100.00 over its own:

```
base parse    -> None                      (the old check caught it)
shipped parse -> 3 txns
recon.ok = True   summary_ok = True   sum_delta = 0.0
debit_coverage = 1.0   credit_coverage = 1.0   integrity.flags = []
quality = approved     ADB = 234.68
OUTCOME = ('validated', 'approved')
```

So the honest statement of the trade is this. The check was **destructive**: it
discarded the document, every correct row in it, and the diagnosis, and on
`2A0B516B2C7D` it did so over a comma in a subtotal line while capturing all 43
rows correctly. It was also **load-bearing** in exactly one case the platform
cannot otherwise see: two equal-and-opposite intra-direction OCR errors in one
statement. **Nothing in the 113-document population exercises that case** — it
is reachable only by construction — and the trade taken here is 45 recovered
rows and two honest withheld diagnoses against a residual that requires a
coincidence. The right home for the lost capability is an integrity check
registered for `td_us`, where a failure reports instead of discarding; that is
the §T7.1 card, and it needs a file this cycle does not own. Recorded as a
known, accepted, non-zero residual rather than as a free move.

One document's second mismatch is worth recording, because it inverts the
card's framing: on `2A0B516B2C7D` the `Other Withdrawals` section reads 18.00
against a subtotal of 3.00, which looks like the worse defect of the two. It is
not a defect in the rows at all. Tesseract read that section's own subtotal
line as `Subtotal: 15,00` — a comma where the decimal point is — so the money
pattern skipped it, the section body ran on into `Service Charges`, and the
section was compared against the *next* section's printed 3.00:

```
 12/08 WIRE TRANSFER FEE 15.00 Subtotal: 15,00 eee A180
 Service Charges POSTING DATE ?- DESCRIPTION AMOUNT 12/31 PAPER STATEMENT FEE 3.00
```

Both rows are captured exactly once, both are debits the ACCOUNT SUMMARY prints
(`Other Withdrawals 15.00`, `Service Charges 3.00`), and the stated total
corroborates them: 5,570.59 + 15.00 + 3.00 = 5,588.59, against a captured
5,175.88 + 18.00 = 5,193.88. **The whole remaining gap is the 394.71 Tesseract
lost from `Electronic Payments`, and nothing else.** The old check was
discarding a document, and 43 correct rows with it, over a comma in a subtotal
line — a figure it was trusting more than the rows it was testing.

## T4. C1 — three more of TD's own structural codes (4 documents)

`_native_credit_like` recovers direction from TD's transaction codes wherever
the printed BALANCE column leaves a group underdetermined. Three of TD's own
codes were missing, and each has a **sibling printed in the same position by
the same channel meaning the opposite** — which is what makes the code, and not
the wording around it, the evidence (R-1 item 8).

| Code | Meaning | Sibling that must not match |
|---|---|---|
| `E-TFR <ref>` | an incoming e-transfer | `SEND E-TFR <ref>` (outgoing) |
| `TD ATM DEP <n>` | deposit at TD's own machine | `TD ATM W/D <n>` |
| `GC <n>-DEPOSIT` | deposit through TD's deposit channel | `GC <n>-CASH WITHDRA` |

Only the spelled-out `E-TRANSFER` was read, so every incoming transfer printed
in TD's abbreviated form was taken for a debit — 90-odd rows across the
population. `CANCEL E-TFR` and `RECLAIM E-TFR` lead with their own verb, do not
match, and are left to the printed balances exactly as before. The `GC` unit
number is statement data, so the marker keys on the printed `-DEPOSIT` suffix
rather than on `GC`.

**The four movers**, each closing to `sum_delta 0.00` with no integrity flags
and ADB restored:

| Document | rows flipped | code |
|---|---|---|
| `D76F2467889F` | 1 (`TD ATM DEP 005218`, 200.00) | ATM |
| `D42B4023ECDA` | 1 (`E-TFR ***wG8 EPAY`, 4,201.00) | E-TFR |
| `7F19A3E37AAD` | 2 (`E-TFR`, 850.00 + 100.00) | E-TFR |
| `230E0915D1C7` | 4 `E-TFR` rows, **and one uncoded row the other way** | E-TFR |

The fifth flip on `230E0915D1C7` is the documented equal-amount tie-break, not
a second rule: `ENTEGRUS R2Y6X2` and `E-TFR ***2uN EPAY` are both 200.00 in a
group the arithmetic says contains exactly one 200.00 deposit, and
`_directions_from_credit_counts` now hands it to the coded row. The document
reconciles to 0.00 with that assignment and did not before, so the printed
balances confirm the swap.

**The ablation, all eight subsets over all 73 documents in one process:**

```
(none: base vocabulary)      validated= 63/73
etfr                         validated= 66/73     E-TFR      alone +3, removed from the full set -3
atmdep                       validated= 64/73     TD ATM DEP alone +1, removed from the full set -1
gcdep                        validated= 63/73     GC-DEPOSIT alone +0, removed from the full set +0
atmdep+etfr                  validated= 67/73
atmdep+etfr+gcdep            validated= 67/73
```

`GC <n>-DEPOSIT` earns no validation on this population, alone or in
combination — the brief's "+0 but needed" is not what the ablation says, and
this corrects it. It is not inert, though: with only that rule removed, two
documents that stay withheld either way move materially the wrong way —
`477E2FD610A1` from `sum_delta -19.90` to `-6,019.90`, **re-raising both
coverage flags it otherwise clears**, and `5E682B9B2C69` by 6,040.00 (credit
coverage 83% → 76%). A 3,000.00 deposit read as a 3,000.00 withdrawal is a
6,000.00 error, and the arithmetic moving toward the bank's own printed
balances is the evidence for the code. It ships with the other two.

**The caveat the brief flagged, verified.** `EA5C61862BB8` drifts from
`sum_delta +600.72` to `+1,000.72` — its one flipped row is
`E-TFR ***53t EPAY 200.00`, correctly a credit by TD's code, and the document
does not reconcile either way. Its remaining 600.72 is a different, unrelated
defect and it stays `withheld` before and after.

`PAY` was left in `_NATIVE_CREDIT_CODES`. It is unsound as a trailing-token
code (it is also the tail of `EPAY`, `BPY` and others) but net-neutral on this
population; removing it is a separate card, recorded in §T7.

### T4.1 The fixtures did not constrain the rule — four surviving mutants, four new tests

Adversarial review found that the first pass of C1's fixtures pinned the
*answer* on real shapes but not the *rule*: the negative test
`test_an_outgoing_e_transfer_is_still_a_debit` is satisfied by the
**pre-existing `SEND E-TFR` guard**, not by the new anchor, so a mutated anchor
kept the whole file green. Reproduced here before fixing, and the weakness was
broader than the two mutants reported — all four survived:

```
etfr_no_space    startswith("E-TFR") without the trailing space   35 passed  SURVIVED
etfr_substring   "E-TFR " matched anywhere in the description     35 passed  SURVIVED
atm_substring    "TD ATM DEP" matched anywhere                    35 passed  SURVIVED
gc_search        _GC_DEPOSIT_RE.search instead of .match          35 passed  SURVIVED
```

Four negative fixtures now pin the property the codes actually have — **each is
a whole leading token of the description, because that is where TD prints the
channel** — and each mutant dies to exactly one of them:

| Mutant | Killed by | Fixture row |
|---|---|---|
| `startswith("E-TFR")` | `test_a_longer_token_that_merely_begins_with_the_code_is_not_a_transfer` | `E-TFRFEE ***a1B` |
| `"E-TFR " in text` | `test_the_transfer_code_must_open_the_description` | `ACME E-TFR CORP` |
| `"TD ATM DEP" in text` | `test_the_atm_code_must_open_the_description` | `REVERSAL TD ATM DEP 000000` |
| `_GC_DEPOSIT_RE.search` | `test_the_deposit_channel_code_must_open_the_description` | `REVERSAL GC 0000-DEPOSIT` |

```
shipped          39 passed                 (control)
etfr_no_space    1 failed, 38 passed       KILLED
etfr_substring   1 failed, 38 passed       KILLED
atm_substring    1 failed, 38 passed       KILLED
gc_search        1 failed, 38 passed       KILLED
```

`E-TFRFEE` is the one worth reading twice: this parser exists because the
native text layer collapses column gaps, so a joined token is its standing
failure mode, and the trailing space in `startswith("E-TFR ")` is what keeps a
joined token from being read as the code. Nothing in the population prints it —
it is a fixture for the rule, not a shape from the corpus, and it is labelled as
such in the test file.

## T7. Carried findings and questions for Ocean

1. **U2's residual — demonstrated, not hypothetical.** With the per-section
   check gone, a document whose sections mis-read in *exactly compensating*
   directions within one direction reconciles on wrong rows and **validates
   with zero flags**. This was written here first as a possibility; adversarial
   review built it, and §T3 now carries the reproduction. Nothing in either
   population does it, and it needs two OCR errors of equal size in opposite
   directions within one statement, but the discarded check caught that case
   and the downstream coverage gate (direction-level, ±2% against the stated
   totals) is structurally incapable of catching it.
   The concrete mechanism to watch is the one §T3 documents: when a section's
   subtotal line is unreadable, `_section` runs on into the next section and
   swallows its rows. On `2A0B516B2C7D` the swallowed section then failed to
   parse on its own, so nothing was double-counted — but a document where both
   parse would count a row twice, and only the coverage gate would notice. If
   Ocean wants the protection back without the destruction, the parser-local
   way is an integrity check registered for `td_us`, which needs
   `parser_registry_entries.py` — TD-FRENCH's file this cycle. **Recorded as a
   card, not attempted.** The narrower fix for the mechanism itself (bound a
   section body at the next section heading, not merely at the next
   `Subtotal:`) is a second card, also not attempted: it changes what every
   td_us section captures and deserves its own measurement.
2. **The UNCAPTURED alternative for U2, considered and not taken.** The
   pipeline already has a convention for "activity the bank totals but we could
   not read as postings" (`Quality.aggregate_rows` / `summary_only`). Emitting
   the shortfall as an UNCAPTURED row would make both documents reconcile at
   100% coverage and land in `review` rather than `withheld`. That is a
   different, larger claim — it asserts the gap is real activity — and it is
   not what the card measured. Ocean's call.
3. **`PAY` in `_NATIVE_CREDIT_CODES`.** Kept per the brief. It is a trailing
   *token* test, so it fires only on a description ending in the bare word
   `PAY`; the population's `EPAY`/`BPY` tails do not reach it. Unsound as
   written, net-neutral as measured, worth its own measured card.
4. **`CANCEL E-TFR` / `RECLAIM E-TFR` are unread.** Six rows in the population.
   A cancelled outgoing transfer is a credit back, and both leave the direction
   to the printed balances today. Not in the card, not measured, not added.
5. **The rest of the unread native vocabulary, enumerated.** Named here so the
   next TD card starts from a list rather than a search. Counted over the 73
   documents; none is in the code vocabulary, all leave direction to the
   printed balances:

   | Printed form | Rows | Documents | Direction it implies |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `GC <n>-TRANSFER` | 2 | 2 | undetermined — the channel prints both ways |
   | `GC <n>-DEBIT MEMO` | 1 | 1 | debit (found as `-DEBIT MEMO`, not bare `-DEBIT`) |
   | `MOBILE DEPOSIT` | 2 | — | credit |
   | bare `DEPOSIT` | 2 | — | credit |

   The two `GC` forms were surfaced by adversarial review; the exact printed
   suffix is recorded because `_GC_DEPOSIT_RE` keys on it, and `-DEBIT MEMO` is
   what the population actually prints. **None added** — R-1 item 8 permits the
   codes, but this card measured three, and a fourth belongs to whoever
   measures it.
6. **D5 (`td_can` never populates `running_balance`)** was not touched, per the
   brief.

# §TD-FRENCH — the Quebec issue of the TD Canada printed grid

TD-FRENCH, 2026-08-13. Branch `wave3-td-french`, base `cce8ac1`. Brief:
`docs/agent-handoffs/TD-FRENCH.md`. Scout evidence: SC-TDCAN.

**Additive only.** A new parser module and a new registration. No existing
parser, marker, band or `supersedes` edge is touched, and the archive-wide
differential in §TF7 shows the claimant set of all 3,396 other documents is
unchanged.

## TF0. Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| The gap | 13 documents print exactly one physical grid the platform already validates 74 of, issued in French, and **nothing claimed them at any score**. Not a near-miss: `candidates == ()`, outcome `unclaimed`, `failed / no deterministic parser matched`. |
| The family | Confirmed independently of the scout by a marker scan over every OCR artifact in the archive: **exactly 13 of 3,409** documents (§TF1), 2,227 rows, 320 date groups. |
| What is new | Three things, and only three: FR-CA space-thousands money against descriptions that end in digits (§TF3), a `DC` overdrawn suffix where the English grid prints a minus, and TD's French transaction codes (§TF4). Everything else is the English layout. |
| What is reused | `td_can._credit_counts_from_balances` and `_directions_from_credit_counts`, imported and consumed unchanged. `analysis/td_can.py` is not modified — TDFIX-1 owns it this cycle. |
| Result over the family | **13 claimed / 9 validated / 4 withheld**, from 0 / 0 / 0. Every one of the 13 stated summaries reconciles to 0.00 and every printed row is captured; the 4 are the antisymmetric wrong-side class and are named in §TF6. |
| Movement outside the family | **None.** `td_canada_native` 74/74 and `td_us` 44/44 byte-identical before and after; 0 of 3,396 non-family documents changed claimant set; 0 ambiguous documents anywhere. |
| Files | `analysis/td_canada_french.py` (new), `analysis/parser_registry_entries.py` (one entry), `tests/test_td_french_layouts.py` (new, 66 tests), the conformance fixture, two count pins, one private-import allowlist entry, this log. |
| `count_semantics` | Deliberately **no entry**. The new id is UNSURVEYED, so its printed counts are `comparable=False` and the count check emits nothing — verified, not assumed. The table is Ocean's. |
| `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` | Must be bumped at merge (`webapp/` protected here): 13 documents produce an analysis payload where they previously produced none. |

## TF2. What is the same, and why that is the whole design

    DESCRIPTION        RETRAITS       DEPOTS           DATE    SOLDE

Five columns, one printed row per physical line, and a running balance at the
end of each date group — the English grid `td_can`'s native path reads, with
the column headings translated. It therefore loses exactly what the English one
loses: the text layer collapses the two money columns into one token, so
*which* column an amount was printed in does not survive.

The answer is the same too, so the arithmetic is the same code. The module
imports `_credit_counts_from_balances` and `_directions_from_credit_counts` and
consumes them unchanged. Copying them was not an option — it would fail
`test_no_two_functions_in_analysis_share_a_body` — and re-deriving them
differently would put two answers to one question in the tree. The debt is
recorded as two `ALLOWED_PRIVATE_IMPORTS` entries carrying the argument for the
end state (promote the pair into a shared module; `td_can.py` is another
cell's this cycle).

Registration carries **no band and no `supersedes` edge**, because this is a
disjoint document class rather than a narrower one. What holds the two apart is
the R-4 cross product (52 × 51 detection-negative assertions, all green) and
§TF7's archive-wide differential, not a precedence rule.

## TF3. Space thousands against description digits — pinned both ways

FR-CA money separates thousands with a space, so one printed amount arrives as
several tokens: `1 640,44` is `["1", "640,44"]`. TD's descriptions also end in
digits — `CHQ#00083-1149169334`, `UO342 TFR-A 5347895` — and the two collide.

The rule: **absorb a token to the left only when the decimal group's integer
part is exactly three digits.** That is the only case a French thousands group
can be, because such a group is always padded to three. `40,00` and `5,00`
cannot continue anything, so `UO342 TFR-A 5347895 40,00` keeps its seven-digit
account number in the description.

It is still a real ambiguity when the group *is* three digits.
`PETRO-CANADA 30 145,55` is both "30 145,55" and "145,55, posted by
PETRO-CANADA 30", and no rule reading one line can separate them. The parser
takes the French reading — what the bank's own money format says — and the
balance chain is what makes that safe rather than a guess. Both halves are
fixtured, on the same printed line under two different printed balances:

| fixture | printed balances | result |
|---|---|---|
| `test_the_joined_reading_is_taken_and_the_balance_confirms_it` | `40 000,00 → 9 844,45` | joined; group solves; `reconcile().ok` |
| `test_the_split_reading_is_not_rescued_it_fails_closed` | `500,00 → 344,45` | still joined; group unsolved; **`not reconcile().ok`** |

The second is the important one: the parser does not quietly switch readings to
make a document balance. It keeps the grammatical reading, the group goes
undetermined, the printed summary disagrees, and the document is withheld. Over
the real family the absorbing branch fires on 173 rows and costs nothing — all
13 summaries still reconcile to 0.00.

## TF4. The direction codes — derived from the printed balances, then ablated

Where the balances determine a group, they decide, and the codes cannot
override them. Where they do not, something has to read the row, and
`td_can._native_credit_like` is the English vocabulary — inert on French text,
which is why a balances-only build validates only 6 of 13.

The vocabulary was **not** written by reading descriptions. It was derived from
what the printed balance column says, over the 229 determined date groups whose
amounts are all distinct — where a group repeats an amount the arithmetic
cannot say which row is the deposit, so a label taken from one would be an
artifact of the tie-break rather than evidence:

| code | meaning | credits | debits |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DEP ` / `DEPOT ` | depot | 200 | 0 |
| `TP<nnnn>` | terminal settlement posting | 82 | 0 |
| `RECEPT - VFC` | reception d'un virement Interac | 80 | 0 |
| `TFR-DE` | transfert DE un autre compte | 24 | 0 |
| `CREDIT D'INTERET` | interet porte au credit | 3 | 0 |
| `ENVOI` | envoi d'un virement Interac | 0 | 119 |
| `TFR-A ` | transfert A un autre compte | 0 | 28 |

Structural codes only, never a counterparty name (R-1 item 8). The merchant
settlement codes are exactly why: over the same groups the balances make
`MRCH…` **53 credits against 42 debits** and `ELAVON` 7 against 14, so a rule
keyed on either name would be wrong about half the time. They are left out, and
the documents that need them are withheld (§TF6).

Ablation, one rule removed at a time, measured end to end over the 13:

| rule dropped | validated | documents lost |
|---|---|---|
| *(none — shipped)* | **9** | — |
| `DEP`/`DEPOT` → credit | 6 | `1131B891`, `699846B0`, `811D6591` |
| `TP<nnnn>` → credit | 6 | `1131B891`, `699846B0`, `811D6591` |
| `TFR-DE` → credit | 7 | `1131B891`, `699846B0` |
| `RECEPT - VFC` → credit | 8 | `1131B891` |
| `TFR-A` → debit | 9 | none |
| `ENVOI` → debit | 9 | none |
| `CREDIT D'INTERET` → credit | 9 | none |
| *no vocabulary at all* | 6 | `1131B891`, `699846B0`, `811D6591` |

The last three rows are recorded as residuals rather than removed. `TFR-A` and
`ENVOI` restate the default and so **cannot** move an outcome; they are written
down because TD prints each as one half of a pair, and a reader checking
`TFR-DE` should find `TFR-A` beside it. `CREDIT D'INTERET` is sound (3 credits,
0 debits) but its rows happen to fall inside determined groups today. All three
carry direct unit fixtures, so none of them is untested code.

Three instruments, all green on all 13 where they are checks rather than

1. **Page-footer counts.** The per-page `Credits`/`Debits` footers accumulate to

## TF6. The fail-closed remainder — 4 documents, named

All four are the **antisymmetric wrong-side class**: the credit total is short
by exactly what the debit total is long, so no money is invented or lost, and
all four are `withheld / withheld_adb` — never a published number.

| document | rows | side error | rows on the wrong side | what they are |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `4DE22E685A04` | 204 | ±462.75 | 1 | `MRCH22940680010 DIV 462,75` |
| `59BD662C0D4F` | 126 | ±1945.51 | 2 | `MRCH22940680010 DIV 1 320,51`, `COMPETITION DIV 625,00` |
| `654AB29A910A` | 126 | ±1945.51 | 2 | same statement, second PDF |
| `A3A50C108B7F` | 226 | ±2284.24 | 6 | `MERCH PAD PLAC`, `ELAVON MRCH SVC DIV`, `MRCH…` |

Every one is a merchant-settlement row sitting inside a date group whose
printed balances admit more than one split. They are precisely the codes the
evidence in §TF4 refuses to guess at: `MRCH…` is 53/42 and `ELAVON` is 7/14
over the determined groups. Forcing them would publish a wrong direction on
about half the population the rule touched.

The 4 are not a parser defect and there is no code change that closes them
honestly. What would close them is the same card §TD.T6 raised for the English
grid: **the column identity is in the PDF and the extractor discards it.**
`ocr/native_text.py` already recovers word geometry for two other banks, and
these amounts sit in one or the other printed money column with no ambiguity at
all. `ocr/` is protected for this agent: **raised, not attempted**, and it is
one card for both TD layouts rather than two.

folder-free: the **entire** archive, before and after, stratified by claiming

Both sweeps run the same script over the same 3,409 documents, read from

Two notes on the populations. They are defined by detection over the current

13 of the 3,409 documents are unreadable by the sweep script's page extractor.

## TF11. Amendments from adversarial review

Ocean's review returned SHIP with two tightenings and one optional. All three
are applied. Every number in TF0-TF10 above is unchanged: the 13-document
instrument is byte-identical before and after these edits, 9 validated / 4
withheld, and detection is untouched so the archive-wide differential of §TF7
cannot move.

**1. A zero-padded token cannot open a number.** Only the groups AFTER the
first are padded to three digits, so `FACTURE 007 100,00DC` is an invoice
number printed beside an amount and not 7 100,00.

The review prescribed one condition on `_LEADING_GROUP_RE`. Reproduced against
the code, that is **necessary but not sufficient for the review's own
example**: `007` is three digits, so the thousands-group loop takes it and it
never reaches the leading-group test. Narrowing that pattern alone leaves
`FACTURE 007 100,00DC` reading 7100.0. Both halves were therefore needed, and
both are in:

- `_LEADING_GROUP_RE` narrowed to `[1-9]\d{0,2}` — closes `FACTURE 07 100,00`,
  the shape that does reach the leader test;
- a stop condition after the absorption — whatever the two rules took, the
  group the number now opens with must not be padded. Absorption stops rather
  than the amount being rejected: `100,00` is still an amount, it just starts
  one token later.

Differential, the pre-review module loaded from `a29a848` beside the current
one in the same process:

```
line                     before         after          verdict
FACTURE 007 100,00DC     7100.0         100.0          FIXED
FACTURE 07 100,00        7100.0         100.0          FIXED
X 0 100,00               100.0          100.0          kept
FACTURE 1 007 100,00     1007100.0      1007100.0      kept
VENDEUR 30 145,55        30145.55       30145.55       kept
DEPOT 1 640,44           1640.44        1640.44        kept
```

The `1 007 100,00` line is the contrast half and is fixtured: a padded MIDDLE
group is correct French and must still read whole. Three fixtures added.

**2. The accent-folding docstring over-promised.** The review proved that
mixed-content mojibake does not detect: where only some characters are
double-encoded, `td_can.normalize_mojibake`'s whole-text reversal fails and the
fallback `_MOJIBAKE_TABLE` has no entry for an upper-case O-circumflex, so a
double-encoded `DEPOTS` beside one clean accent folds to text the markers miss.
Pre-existing, fails closed to a decline rather than a wrong parse, and
unreachable on this family, whose headers print unaccented. `_fold`'s docstring
now states what is actually guaranteed — unaccented, accented, and uniformly
double-encoded forms — and names the table gap as the cause of the limit.
`td_can.py` not touched; Ocean is queuing the table gap as its own card.

**3. Optional, taken:** `TFR-DE` now carries a word boundary, matching the
discipline of its sibling `TFR-A `. 0 occurrences affected in the corpus;
`TFR-DEX` no longer matches where it did before.

# §RBCCIBC-LAYOUTS — the RBC/CIBC tranche: 66 documents, and a money grammar that could not read a minus

## RC0. Summary

Five cards on one ownership, sequenced behind a gate. **66 of the 84 unclaimed
RBC/CIBC archive documents move `failed` -> `validated`, zero documents move
down, and the 160 already-claimed documents are byte-identical.** The four
documents with a broken character map are refused structurally and can no
longer be claimed by any registration this cell touches.

| card | family | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| D | the shared money grammar (the gate) | — | 160 claimed documents byte-identical |
| B | RBC English personal | 12 failed | **12 validated** |
| C | RBC French business (`rbc_french`, which saw only its other product) | 19 failed, 0 archive claims | **19 validated** |
| A | CIBC English (`cibc`, new registration) | 35 failed | **35 validated** |
| F1 | broken character map | 4 failed | 4 refused, structurally |

All 66 are instrumented per document, not merely claimed: the balance walk
closes, every stated total the bank prints equals the published ledger, every
printed count equals the published count, and `continuity_breaks` is 0.
**4,273 transactions** are published across the 66. Over the whole cohort,
**220 validated documents instrument sound and 0 unsound.**

The remaining 18 unclaimed documents were each identified, and none is a
statement of a layout this cell covers:

| n | what they are | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | broken character map (`85259525_*`) | refused by card F1 |
| 3 | French CIBC (`..._Account Statement 3`) | `cibc_french` detects, parses, declines |
| 4 | online-banking screen captures | `no_parser_matched` — not statements |
| 2 | void cheques | `no_parser_matched` |
| 2 | zero-money scans (`CTS*`) | `no_parser_matched` |
| 1 | an online transaction export (`...0672 2026-05-31`) | `no_parser_matched` |
| 1 | an online statement (`78ec8e63_onlineStatement (15)`) | `no_parser_matched` |
| 1 | a ZERO-ACTIVITY statement (`...0672 2025-09-09`) | `parser_declined` — see RC8.5 |

The last one is the only recoverable document left in the cohort.

## RC1. The instrument, and the scout's numbers

Every figure below comes from replaying the archive markdown through the real
pipeline (`analyze_markdown` + `telemetry.record.classify_outcome` +
`discovery.runner._failure_reason`), resolved from the D-3 OCR artifact store
by direct file path — the sqlite index was being written by a live discovery
run and was never read.

Before any production edit the harness was checked against run `6893a75b`: over
all 244 cohort documents (160 claimed, 84 unclaimed) it reproduced the run's
`parser_id` and `outcome_class` **exactly, 244/244, 0 disagreements**. Zero
OCR-cache misses.

The scout's per-family counts reproduced, and two were beaten:

| family | scout | measured |
|---|---|---|
| A CIBC English | 34 | **35** |
| B RBC English personal | 12 | **12** |
| C RBC French business | 18–19 | **19** |
| F1 broken CMap | 4 | **4** |

The scout's cohort of "153 rbc + 2 cibc_french = 155 claimed" is really **156
rbc + 4 cibc_french = 160**; the byte-identity sweep covers all 160, a superset.

## RC2. Card D — the gate, and the 160-document byte-identity sweep

Six defects in the shared money grammar, each with a named printed shape.

**1. `_SUMMARY_MONEY` could not read `- $2.55`.** It admitted `-$2.55` and
`$-2.55` and stopped, because the minus is set in the summary grid's *label*
column while the symbol belongs to the figure. A personal statement closing
overdrawn published `+2.55`, so the summary identity balanced against a
sign-flipped closing balance instead of failing. Six of the twelve card-B
documents open or close overdrawn and print it this way.

**2. A bare minus between two cells did not sign the balance.**
`194.82 - 192.33` published a POSITIVE 192.33 and broke the chain. The fix is
NOT in the money pattern, and that matters: the shipped `_MONEY_RE` widened to
`-?\s?` was dry-run against all 160 claimed documents first and **changed the
payload of 156 of them** — because `Interac purchase - 0184 B001 LITTLE KABUL -
180.59` is a merchant name that ends in a hyphen followed by a WITHDRAWAL. The
sign is now read in `read_grid_rows`, where the column is known: the Balance
column is the only column that prints a sign, so a bare minus is a sign only
between a row's amount and the cell that follows it. Both readings are pinned,
the adversary taken from a claimed document.

**3. The opening-balance row consumed its whole physical line.** Everything
printed after its own cell was discarded. In the CIBC layout that is a real
transaction, because the column header, the opening row and the first posting
share one line. Card A depends on this.

**4. `_grid_cells` read two rate operands as money** — the numerator of
`2.25/1,000` and the foreign amount in `450000.00 PKR @.005`. Both are now
recognised by the mark printed beside them (the `/`, and the same `@` the
existing rule uses, read *through* the currency code), so `403.50 SCD 09502`
stays a cell. Keying on the mark rather than on a list of currency codes is
what makes that true: the three-letter tokens that follow an amount in the
claimed population are `VSA`, `ATM`, `AMX`, `NSF`, `MON`, `INT`, `MIN`, `PAD`,
`GST` and `TIM` — not one is a currency.

**5. `_FR_MONEY_RE` could not span `(1 066,25 )`.** The bracket is the French
layout's only negative marker and it is set in its own column, so every
overdrawn balance in that family was sign-flipped. Its lookbehind also admitted
`+`, letting `ARCHIVE+8 129,14` glue a reference digit onto the amount.

**6. The French summary matched almost nothing.** Its two total wordings occur
in no document of the family, so both stated totals were silently `None` and
`reconcile.summary_ok` had nothing to check; the opening-balance pattern was
unanchored and began the space-grouped alternative inside the printed YEAR
(`... 2025 801,53 $` -> 2 025 801,53). Rewritten to the real wording, anchored,
read off the collapsed line, and it now assigns the two printed COUNTS.

### The sweep

Card D alone, over the full cohort:

```
byte-identical payloads : 244 / 244
payload changed         : 0
moved UP                : 0
moved DOWN              : 0
```

The argument was also made in advance, by census: of the shapes card D changes
the reading of, **every one occurs zero times in the 160 claimed documents**
(`summary_minus_space_dollar` 0, `grid_minus_space_amount` 0,
`grid_label_minus_space` 0, `fr_paren_space_close` 0, `fr_plus_glued_digit` 0,
`rate_slash` 0, glued-symbol tariff 0). The two probes that DID fire in the
claimed population were both investigated and neither is reachable: every
`Total cheques & debits (121) - 12,410.01` hit is in the summary block, which
the grid pattern never sees, and every `+`-glued digit is an `@ RBP+05.00`
rate already excluded by two existing guards.

## RC3. Card B — the English personal product, on one registration

RBC issues its English statement under two product names: the business one
heads its table `Account Activity Details` / `Cheques & Debits`, the personal
one `Details of your account activity` / `Withdrawals`. Same institution, same
three-column grid, same opening and closing rows — one registration, not two.
The conjunction with `ROYAL BANK OF CANADA` is unchanged and is what keeps
either heading from reaching another issuer; CIBC prints the identical column
header over its own grid, and a negative fixture pins that it still does not
claim.

The personal summary prints **no instance count** beside either total, so both
stated counts stay `None`. Deriving them from the ledger would manufacture the
oracle the platform checks itself against.

Result: **12/12 validated**, 1,180 transactions, all instrumented sound. Both
overdrawn documents carry the right sign (one opens at -2.55, one closes at
-2.55).

## RC4. Card C — a registration that could see only one of its two products

`rbc_french` claimed **zero documents in the 3,506-document archive**. Its
activity marker required `DATE DESCRIPTION RETRAITS` and nothing else, so the
nineteen BUSINESS statements — which head the same grid `Chèques et débits` —
went unclaimed corpus-wide. Its two summary total wordings were the personal
product's, so on every business statement both stated totals were silently
`None` and `reconcile.summary_ok` had nothing to check.

**A correction, and the gate is what forced it.** This cell first concluded
that `RETRAITS` was CIBC's header and matched no RBC document at all, and
narrowed the marker to the business wording alone. That was measured over the
archive only. The PINNED corpus holds one RBC French document —
`RBC French/12 - Relevé Royale Décembre 2025` — and it is the PERSONAL product,
which really does print `Date Description Retraits ($) Dépôts ($) Solde ($)`.
Narrowing the marker un-claimed it and `corpus_gate.py` went RED with
`no deterministic parser matched this statement`. The archive and the pinned
corpus are different populations and a census of one is not a census of the
other; that is the lesson worth carrying out of this cell.

The marker now accepts BOTH products, exactly as card B does on the English
side, and the summary reads both sets of wordings. The conjunction with
`BANQUE ROYALE` is what keeps `Retraits` — which IS also CIBC's French header —
from reaching a CIBC statement, and a negative fixture pins it. The
`ALTERNATE_FIXTURES` entry pins the personal branch so neither can be dropped
again.

Accents reach this parser as U+FFFD — this text layer loses them outright
rather than double-encoding them, so `normalize_mojibake` has nothing to repair
— and every accent is matched as `.`, the tolerance `analysis/cibc.py` already
uses.

### The cheque-serial ambiguity, resolved from the document

French thousands are spaced, so `Chèque - 253 127,40` is indistinguishable from
253,127.40. One row booked a quarter of a million dollars against an account
holding four thousand, and the document failed closed at `withheld_adb` with
`db 1,292,217.31` against a stated `19,118.73`.

Nothing inside the row settles it. The statement settles it elsewhere: these
documents append cheque-image pages declaring every serial the period cleared
(`No de série: 253 Montant: 127,40 $`). A statement that declares serials gets
a money pattern that refuses to BEGIN an amount at the number printed straight
after `Chèque - `; a statement that declares none keeps the plain pattern, and
a mis-read row fails the bank's own totals rather than being split on a guess.
Both halves are pinned.

A first attempt split the entry in two and was **rejected on measurement**: it
changed the row-boundary semantics of the shared reader, so a cheque row with
no printed balance handed its amount to the previous row as a balance. The
document went from one wrong number to fifteen continuity breaks. The pattern
form has no such effect.

Result: **19/19 validated**, all with both stated totals equal to the published
ledger and — for the first time — **both printed counts assigned, 19/19**.

## RC5. Card A — a new registration for the English CIBC statement

No English CIBC parser existed. It lives in `analysis/cibc.py` beside the
French layout, which is the convention `rbc.py`, `td_can.py` and
`bmo_ca_business.py` already follow for a second layout of one institution: its
own markers, its own normalization, its own registration (`cibc`, band 0, no
`supersedes`). The two share nothing but the bank word.

`read_grid_rows` is **shared, not copied**: `rbc._read_grid_rows` and its two
collaborators were promoted to `analysis/tables.py` in their own commit, proven
byte-neutral over all 244 documents. That is the option the brief preferred —
importing another parser's private helper is the dependency inversion the
no-parser-helper-clones guard exists to stop. `tables.py` imports no parser, so
the leaf property the guard tests still holds.

Four things are CIBC's own:

* **the grid is compressed horizontally.** The column header, the opening row
  and the first posting arrive on one physical line. So the Date column is
  consumed wherever it is printed, and a date token opens a row only where the
  grid can print one — at the start of the table's text, or right after a
  completed money cell, which is the previous row's Balance column. A `May`
  inside a merchant name has no printed balance before it and is pinned not to
  split a row.
* **`Balance forward`** is the opening row again after a page break, matched by
  the same label argument, and (thanks to card D) no longer swallowing the
  description printed after it.
* **bare `Withdrawals -` / `Deposits +` totals**, no counts.
* **a foreign-currency account states its currency on the closing-balance row**
  and nowhere else. 3 documents are USD, 32 CAD.

### The tariff quoted inside a description

Nine documents were off by exactly 16.95. `SERVICE CHARGE CAPPED MONTHLY
FEE$16.95 RECORD-KEEPING N/A` names the fee and the row's own cell then prints
it again, so it was booked twice. A printed cell stands in a column, so a
currency symbol welded to the word before it is part of the sentence, not the
start of a column — zero occurrences in the claimed population, nine in exactly
those nine documents. Fixing it took the family from 26 validated + 9 withheld
to **35 validated**.

Result: **35/35 validated**, 2,449 transactions, all instrumented sound.

## RC6. Card F1 — a broken character map is refused, not read

Four documents carry a PDF font whose character map is broken: the glyphs are
right, the codepoints are not. The text layer prints `ROYAL BANK OF CANADA`
perfectly, renders "Business Account Statement" as `Bu-in0-- A11ount
4t5t060nt`, and renders seventeen thousand dollars as `17J000-00` — while
*other* money on the same page survives intact. That mixture is what makes them
dangerous rather than merely useless.

`tables.glyph_damaged` asserts admissibility on the damage itself rather than
on any parser's markers, and is wired as an **EXCLUDING** marker on `rbc`,
`rbc_french` and `cibc`, so it returns 0.0 before any other marker is scored.
A test widens the marker set with an always-true marker and pins that the
document still cannot be claimed.

The threshold is measured, and the obvious metric was **rejected on the
measurement**: damaged MONEY tokens do not separate the populations — one of
the four targets has zero of them, and a healthy document scores 0.24 against
a target's 0.14. The metric that does separate is the share of words with
digits welded between their letters:

| population | documents | max ratio |
|---|---|---|
| the four targets | 4 | 0.45 (min 0.30) |
| claimed RBC/CIBC | 160 | 0.031 |
| unclaimed RBC/CIBC that must stay claimable | 80 | 0.036 |
| stratified sample, every other issuer | 618 | 0.033 |

Limit 0.15 — an order of magnitude clear of both. It fires on 4 of 858
documents, exactly the four. Re-checked against the population the archive
census does NOT cover: over the **109 pinned corpus documents** it refuses
zero, and the worst pinned ratio is 0.025.

**Scope, stated honestly.** The predicate is issuer-neutral; the WIRING is
three registrations out of 52. A scan of all 3,493 archive documents at the
shipped threshold returns **exactly five** over it — the four `85259525_*`
behind this guard, and `Unidentified/125ead7e_Gulf Coast Bank - June 2026.pdf`
at **0.261**, another issuer's, unclaimed today and behind nothing. Ocean's
adversarial review found that fifth document independently. Nothing claims it,
so there is no live exposure; but a guard whose whole purpose is to survive a
later widening is doing that job on three registrations and not on 49. Wiring
it platform-wide is RC8.7.

**Zero cross-claims.** The conformance cross-product is now 52 x 51 = 2,652

**The stratified probe.** 619 documents sampled across all 67 non-RBC/CIBC
folder labels (609 resolved): **zero claims by any registration this cell

**`count_semantics` — the one item that needs Ocean's table review.**
`analysis/count_semantics.py` is untouched. What changed is the data reaching

* `rbc` is COMPARABLE in both directions and stays so. Card B's personal

* **`rbc_french` already carries a COMPARABLE entry — for counts the parser

* Measured: all 19 report `stated_credit_count_matches` and
  `stated_debit_count_matches` TRUE, and **zero count-related integrity flags

  now load-bearing where it previously could not fire.
* Both `rbc` and `rbc_french` entries carry `file:line` provenance into
  `analysis/rbc.py` that this cell has made stale.
* `cibc` is a new registration and therefore UNSURVEYED, which is correct; it

   count, and the natural seam — a registry `integrity_check` — would need

3. **The archive is not the pinned corpus.** Card C's first design was

4. **`fb677033_5085287_2026_01_12_2026_01_12.pdf`** validates on a single
   transaction. It is a genuine one-day statement, instrumented sound, but it
   is the thinnest evidence in the cell.
5. **One zero-activity RBC statement is recoverable and was left alone.**
   `RBC/b9225462_Chequing Statement-0672 2025-09-09.pdf` prints
   `No activity for this statement period.`, an opening and closing balance of
   $0.00, and both totals as `(0) + 0.00` / `(0) - 0.00`. It satisfies the

   §SCOTIA-REBUILD S3.4 — four negatives, all present here. It declines today,
   which is the correct fail-closed behaviour in the absence of that rule for

6. **`ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` needs a bump on merge, and this cell did not

   payload for them is stale; `webapp/artifact_cache.py` documents that a code

   The brief reserves the bump to Ocean, so `webapp/` is untouched here —

7. **FOLLOW-UP CARD — wire `glyph_damaged` platform-wide.** The predicate is

   `Unidentified/125ead7e_Gulf Coast Bank - June 2026.pdf` at **0.261**, which

8. **FOLLOW-UP CARD — consult the declared serials per row.** The
   cheque-serial fix uses the declared-serial set as a document-wide BOOLEAN
   only: it selects `_FR_MONEY_SERIAL_RE`, whose lookbehind is positional and

9. **The negative cross-product does not cover `ALTERNATE_FIXTURES`.**
   `tests/test_parser_conformance.py`'s 52 x 51 = 2,652 negative assertions run
   over `FIXTURES` only. This branch put the RISKIER of `rbc_french`'s two
   wordings — `Date Description Retraits`, which is also CIBC's French header —
   into `ALTERNATE_FIXTURES`, so the branch that most needs cross-checking is
   the one the harness does not cross-check. Ocean's reviewer verified by hand
   that it cross-claims nothing today, and `test_c_negative_the_personal_
   header_alone_does_not_reach_a_cibc_statement` pins the specific pair.
   Extending the harness to run the cross-product over alternates as well is a
   follow-up card and would benefit every disjunctive marker in the registry,
   not just this one.
10. **A latent double sign in `read_grid_rows`.** The balance-sign rule reads a
   bare `-` between two cells as the sign of the second, and the money patterns
   also match a minus welded to the figure. A line printing BOTH — `194.82 -
   -192.33` — negates twice and publishes `+192.33`. No document in the
   surveyed populations prints it, and the balance walk fails closed if one
   ever does; recorded because the two rules were added in the same cell and
   neither comment mentions the other.

# §FIRSTCIT — a reconciliation that could not fail, and the guard that never looked

## FI0. Summary

`analysis/first_citizens.py` derived its opening balance from its own
transaction sums (`beginning = ending - credits + debits`) and lifted its
closing balance out of a grid position. `beginning + credits - debits ==
ending` was therefore true by construction: the document's reconciliation was
an identity restated, not a test, and it would have passed whatever the parser
had read. The balance oracle could not see this either, because
`balance_forensic_audit.independent_balances` takes `result.opening =
money(statement.beginning_balance)` straight off the parser
(`balance_forensic_audit.py:315-317`) — so `source_opening`,
`expected_opening` and `production_opening` were three renderings of one
number.

Both balances now come off the printed `Your Account(s) At A Glance` control
record, which also prints a count and a total for each of the four posting
sections and the monthly service charge, and which closes on its own
arithmetic before any figure in it is believed. The same block replaced four
memorized section totals, two memorized section terminators and a statement
MONTH pinned into two row regexes.

Sequencing: the pinned-corpus exposure check ran first and cleared. Five
pinned documents are in scope (1 `first-citizens-bank-deterministic`, 4
`citizens-bank-deterministic`) and every audited field on all five is
unmoved; `corpus_gate.py` is GREEN 106/3. No truth-set ceremony is required.

## FI1. The exposure check, first and in full

`Others/First Citizen/First Citizens Bank.pdf` (SHA `57058C69…A5CFAE`,
verified against its pin on disk) prints in its At-A-Glance box:

```
Statement Period Days Average Ledger Balance
- 10 + 9 44,862.06+ 11 9,800.18- 86 74,263.31- 0.00
31
1,145.55
Beginning Balance
Deposits Other Credits Checks Other Debits Monthly Service Charge
55,049.85
8,117.14+
+
14,702.87
Ending  Balance
```

Beginning is `1,145.55` carrying the leading `-` of the control row, i.e.
**-1145.55**; ending is **14,702.87**. Both equal the values the old parser
produced by derivation, so reading them off the page is value-neutral on this
document and the audited `*_opening` / `*_ending` columns cannot move. That is
what made the rebuild safe to do rather than a truth-set movement to escalate.

The printed block also closes on itself, which is what licenses trusting it:

```
-1,145.55 + 55,049.85 + 44,862.06 - 9,800.18 - 74,263.31 - 0.00 = 14,702.87
```

## FI2. One field deliberately NOT populated

`analysis/adb.py:264-291` overrides the reconstructed daily carry with any
`stated_daily_balances` snapshot it is given. The Daily Balance Summary on
this layout is readable and month-generic, and populating it would very likely
move `backend_adb` — a pinned audited field, currently `8116.50` against a
printed `8117.14`. `stated_daily_balances` is therefore left empty exactly as
before. It is a real improvement available to a later cell, and it needs the
ceremony this cell was told not to perform.

| Finding | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| FC-A | statement MONTH as literal `03` in two row regexes (`:99`, `:117`) | month read from the row and resolved against the printed period (`_resolve`) |
| FC-B | parse gated on a memorized four-section count/total fingerprint (`:235-243`) | gated on the counts and totals the document itself prints |
| FC-B′ | section terminators `"Total\n44,862.06"` (`:138`) and `"Total\n74,263.31"` (`:176`) — not in the scout's list | `_BOUNDARY_RE`, a structural boundary set |
| FC-C | `Other Debits` and `Daily Balance Summary` required to be present (`:209-210`) | every section optional; a month with no deposits prints none and its printed count is 0 |

## FI4. What the layout actually does, measured over 39 documents

The signature Ocean named — `Central Bank Operations - DAC02` +
`Your Account(s) At A Glance` — yields **39** documents corpus-wide when
scanned over every row of the run of record (21 + 1 pinned in `Unidentified`,
9 in `Citizens Bank`, 4 in `Bluevine`, 4 in `Synchrony Bank`). The folder
labels are wrong; the layout is one family.

Three traps, all confirmed:

- The **summary box prints out of order.** `days` precedes the beginning
  balance on 14 documents and follows it on 4. The ending amount precedes its
  own sign on some and follows it on others. The block is therefore read by
  token SHAPE, not offset: a bare integer is `days`, the signed-money line is
  the average ledger balance, and the three unsigned money cells are
  beginning, deposits and ending in printed order.
- The **Daily Balance Summary** prints `MM <bal>+` with the `-DD` day suffixes
  on the FOLLOWING line. (The audit's own `first_citizens_daily` was already
  month-generic; only the parser had pinned the month.)
- The **description column is flattened** by the generic native-text
  extractor: every description in a section arrives concatenated on one line
  while dates and amounts arrive as separate positional runs.

Two further variants the prototype's notes did not carry, both found by
failing loudly against the printed counts:

- The checks grid prints a `*` / `* * *` continuation marker ABOVE its rows on
  some documents and below them on others, and a cheque whose serial the bank
  could not read prints with an EMPTY number column (`06-11 8,000.00`; its own
  check-image list shows a bare `Chk#`). Requiring the serial lost exactly one
  cheque worth 8,000.00 on `fdfad302__06_30_2026`.
- When a service charge is billed, the debits section is RENAMED
  `Other Debits And Monthly Service Charge`, and the charge itself is itemised
  outside the four section totals — either in a `Monthly Service Charge
  Description` table or as a `<Month> Service Charge` line. It carries its own
  posting date in both, so it is recovered rather than dated by guesswork.

## FI6. The cost, stated plainly

The previous parser recovered real merchant text by splitting the flattened
description run on a regex of ~25 remembered merchant names
(`_DEBIT_START_RE`, `_CREDIT_START_RE`). That list is a statement-specific
constant, it generalises to zero other documents, and it is the reason this
parser covered exactly one file. It is gone. Descriptions across the family:

```
postings total            2606
section label (flattened) 2317   88.9%
cheque serial recovered    271   10.4%
full printed text           18    0.7%
```

On the pinned document this is a real regression: 95 of its 116 postings now
read `Other Credit` / `Other Debit` instead of merchant text. Descriptions are
in neither audit (`docs/balance-metrics-audit-results.csv`,
`docs/adb-audit-results.csv`), so the gate does not see it — which is exactly
why it is named here rather than left to be discovered. Against it: 34
documents that previously produced nothing now produce complete, reconciled
financial detail.

**This is recoverable, and cheaply.** `pdfplumber` reads the same PDF as
`03-02 POS Sig 02/27 Visa #8269 Cucina 100 864-6019606 SC 92.61` — one posting
per line, date first, amount last. The flattening is an artifact of the
generic `fitz` path in `ocr/native_text.py`, which already carries
bank-specific layout extractors (`+desjardins-layout`, `+wells`) for precisely
this problem. A `+first-citizens-layout` extractor would restore per-posting
descriptions for all 35 documents. It is NOT done here because
`ocr/native_text.py` feeds both forensic oracles, so changing it would move
`raw_daily_balance_snapshots` and `daily_balance_sum` on the pinned document —
audited fields, and someone else's ceremony.

## FI7. CIT-A — the same defect, twice, in citizens.py

`Debits` is a CONTAINER the bank subdivides into `ATM/Purchases` and
`Other Debits`, each repeating under `(Continued)` on every page it spills
onto. `citizens.py:161` sliced from `Other Debits` — a SUB-section heading —
to `Deposits & Credits`, so it began after any `ATM/Purchases` rows and
dropped them silently. The cheque grid had the same shape of bug: it was
closed by `Please See Additional Information on Next Page`, page furniture, so
a grid continuing under `Checks (Cont.)` was cut off at the page break.

Measured against each statement's own printed `Checks -` / `Debits -` control
totals:

## FI8. Why the hardcode guard missed a month literal — both causes

Asked for explicitly, and the fix is test-side, so it is included.

**Cause 1 — scope.** `test_no_literal_years_outside_date_parsing`,
`test_no_literal_account_numbers`, `test_no_exact_amount_constants` and
`test_no_raw_mojibake_sequences` were all `parametrize("filename",
GUARDED_FILES)` over a hardcoded 7-file list that never contained
`first_citizens.py`. Its four memorized totals (`55049.85`, `44862.06`,
`9800.18`, `74263.31`) each match `AMOUNT_RE` exactly. The rule that would
have caught them existed the whole time and was never pointed at the file.
The irony is on the record: the docstring of
`test_removed_literals_stay_removed_anywhere_in_analysis` states the R-4b
lesson that list-scoping fails, and that lesson was applied to the literal
scan and never carried across to the pattern-class scans.

**Cause 2 — no such class.** A bare `03` is too short for `ACCOUNT_RE`
(6+ digits), carries no decimal for `AMOUNT_RE`, and is not a year for
`YEAR_RE`. Even with the file in scope, the month literal would still have
passed. There was no calendar-literal rule at all.

Fix, with blast radius measured before each move:

| Scan | Scope now | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| year | layer-wide | 0 offenders |
| amount | layer-wide, 3 exempt | only `metrics.py`/`pipeline.py`/`reconcile.py`, whose constants are tolerances (`1.00`, `0.98`, `1.02`), read individually and named in `PATTERN_SCAN_EXEMPT` |
| calendar (NEW) | layer-wide, 1 baseline | `CALENDAR_RE` flags a 2-digit literal sitting before a regex date separator. Across all 68 modules it produces 2 hits, both in `first_community.py`. **Corrected in FI14:** only ONE is a calendar literal (`10/31 Ending Balance`, a memorized posting date); the other is `70` from a product-code suffix `(\d+-70)` — a false positive — and the `--- Page 12 ---` page marker beside it is invisible to the scan |
| account | still list-scoped | widening lights up `consumers.py` (`0836327000`) and `ibc.py` (`00000165`) |
| mojibake | still list-scoped | widening lights up `cibc.py`, `columbia_bank.py`, `navigant.py`, `truist.py` |

The account and mojibake backlog is 6 modules owned by other cells; turning
another cell's work red mid-wave is not this guard's call, so it is named in
the module docstring instead of acted on.

Run against the pre-rebuild `first_citizens.py`, `CALENDAR_RE` flags exactly
`:99` and `:117` — the two literals the handoff asked about — and nothing
else. That is pinned as a regression proof, along with one test asserting the
SCOPE itself, since scope was the defect. `_code_lines` also renumbered every
line below a docstring (it collapsed multi-line docstrings to `""`), so
offender reports pointed at the wrong code; it now blanks them line for line.

SC-CAPONE scout reports. Six cards, two production files, three commits.
`ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` NOT bumped — published output moves on 68 documents,
so the bump is Ocean's to compose with the rest of the wave.

## DB1. The measurement instrument, and what it was allowed to touch

Baseline run of record
`discovery_reports/2026-08-14T060822.665646-0000-88be9dd3` (v10), read from
the MAIN checkout. Parser identity for the cache-served rows enriched from
`…-6893a75b`, `…-89bb6185` and `…-52b4b2b2` — necessary, not optional:
capital_one has **zero** rows carrying a `parser_id` in the run of record
(all twelve of its claims were analysis-cache hits), so an unenriched
population is empty.

Markdown came from the D-3 OCR artifacts, addressed **arithmetically** —
`cache_key(STAGE_OCR, content_sha256, ocr_settings_key(...))` →
`webapp_data/artifacts/ocr/<key[:2]>/<key>.json` — across the three settings
partitions. The sqlite index was never opened. `analyze_markdown` was called
directly rather than through `cached_analysis`, so no artifact was written.
Zero OCR, zero model calls, **$0.00**.

**Fidelity first.** Before believing any output, the instrument replayed the
96-document family and reproduced the run of record's `parser_id`,
`outcome_class` and `outcome_reason` on **96 of 96 — zero mismatches**. Two
consecutive sweeps were byte-identical.

Before/after in one process: the base-commit copy of each changed parser was
loaded from its git blob as its own module and swapped into
`analysis.parser_registry._REGISTRY`, so both readings ran against identical
text through identical downstream code.

## DB2. us_bank — four refusals, one summary grid

The parser read the Account Summary through a memorized six-name category
vocabulary, mapped each name to exactly one detail heading, and required a
`Number of Days in Statement Period` line. All four cards are that one
assumption failing in four places.

**US-DAYS (11 documents).** The days line is optional — the layouts that print
no `# Items` column print no days line either. The printed period already
states the figure and `parse_us_bank_statement` already had that fallback
(`int(summary.get("days") or period_days)`), so the requirement refused 11
complete documents over nothing. The printed line still outranks the period
where it exists: the two disagree as a matter of course on this bank (the
cycle closes on a business day, the count is calendar), and **15 already
validated documents** carry that disagreement, so nothing new was introduced.

**US-CONSUMER (5 documents).** The consumer grid prints a different category
vocabulary — one `Deposits / Credits` for every inflow — and **no count column
at all**. The memorized six names matched nothing, so `_summary` read zero
categories and declined. The category NAME is now read. Measured across all 59
documents the generic reader finds exactly the six business categories (with
counts) and the three consumer ones (without), and **no spurious category at
all**; a spurious one would fail its own section-total check anyway.

**US-ECHECK (1 document).** Cheques are presented by MANNER — `Checks
Presented Conventionally` and `Checks Presented Electronically`, each with its
own subtotal — both rolling up to the summary's single `Checks Paid` figure
and a printed `Total Checks Paid`. A one-heading-per-category map read the
conventional block only and the category's section-total check then refused
the whole document. Sections are now keyed by CATEGORY, and any `Checks
Presented …` heading feeds the cheque category; the manner is matched, not
enumerated.

**US-PERIOD (1 document).** `Statement Period:`, the start date and `through
<end>` are one column of the page header, and flattening interleaves the
neighbouring columns between them. A multi-page statement reprints the header
on every page and somewhere in those repeats the halves land adjacent; this
one is `Page 1 of 1` and got a single printing to be lucky in. The period is
now read from the bank's own label. The bare adjacent pair is still read when
no label sits above one, so the reading is strictly the older one plus the
interleaved case — a point the `tests/test_parser_crash_shapes.py` fixture
caught when the first attempt replaced it instead of extending it.

## DB3. us_bank — the published product name (R-1 class)

The parser published `account_name="Platinum Business Money Market"` on every
document it read. Measured over the 40 it had validated:

| printed product line | documents |
|---|---|
| `U.S. BANK SILVER - BUSINESS CHECKING` | 26 |
| `U.S. BANK GOLD - BUSINESS CHECKING` | 10 |
| `PLATINUM BUSINESS MONEY MARKET` | 4 |

— wrong on **36 of 40**. The name is now read from the block the bank prints
above every Account Summary (product / `Member FDIC` / association line /
account number, the last two in either order). Anchoring on the whole block is
load bearing: `Member FDIC` is also printed as the footer of the credit-bureau
disclosure page, where the nearest line above is prose — and three documents in
the fix population print exactly that. A document printing no such block
publishes `None` rather than a guess.

## DB4. capital_one — a bracket is a sign marker (CO-FEES, 10 documents)

The native cycle-summary reader required literal brackets around
`Checks/Debits` and `Service Charges`. Capital One brackets a cell to mark it
**negative**, so the bracket is present exactly when there is a sign to mark.
Measured over every `Service Charges` cell the folder prints:

| printed cell | documents |
|---|---|
| `$0.00` | 10 |
| `($15.00)` / `($35.00)` / `($10.00)` / `($12.00)` / `($4.00)` | 12 |

The ten zero-charge documents are exactly the ten declines. Both cells now
admit the printed shape either way and `_money` reads the bracket as the sign
it is — `parse_digit_scrubbed(parens=True)`, which already did.

## DB5. capital_one — the cycle charge the summary states (CO-ADB, 1 of 2)

The bank posts its cycle charge on the day the charge falls, which can be
after the cycle it belongs to has closed. One such row puts the document
outside `adb.py`'s `transactions_within_period` check and the ADB engine fails
closed on all of it — correctly; its own warning says such rows "were excluded
rather than moved to a boundary day".

The existing normalizer already moved such a row onto the final cycle day but
identified it by ledger wording alone (`maintenance` / `cycle service
charge`). The remaining document prints the same charge as `Cash deposit limit
exceeded`. The charge is now also identified by the bank's own arithmetic: a
debit of exactly the figure printed under `Service Charges`, posted at the
boundary. Two independent readings agree on that row — the amount matches the
printed total exactly, and the printed debit COUNT is short by exactly one on
that document, which is the bank saying it does not count that row among its
`Checks/Debits` (DB8).

**No ADB oracle exists here and I did not pretend one did.** Capital One's
printed `Average Collected Balance` is a collected-funds average, not a daily
balance average: measured against our ADB on the documents where both exist it
differs by 0.01% to 25.6% (and by four orders of magnitude on a near-zero
account). It cannot validate a date treatment, so the second CO-ADB document
was left withheld (DB7).

## DB8. The capital_one debit count-scope — a promotion PROPOSED, with a fresh counterfactual

`count_semantics` records `capital_one:debit` as INCOMPARABLE, with
COUNTS-P1 §3.2's note that `stated_debit_count + 1 where a service charge is
printed` "is the mapping a parser card should encode". COUNTS-P1 measured 12
of 12 documents disagreeing by exactly +1 — **and every one of those 12 printed
a non-zero charge**, because the zero-charge documents were all declining.
"+1 always" and "+1 iff charged" were indistinguishable on that population.

CO-FEES supplies the control arm. Measured over all 22 documents capital_one
now reads:

| printed `Service Charges` | documents | captured debits − `stated_debit_count` |
|---|---|---|
| non-zero | 12 | **+1 on every one** |
| zero | 10 | **0 on every one** |

Credit direction: **0 mismatches on all 22**. Coverage 1.0 and `sum_delta`
0.0 throughout, so the rows are right and only the scopes differ.

Mechanism, not just correlation: on 8 of the 12 charged documents the extra
row is named `Service charge` or `Maintenance charge` outright; on the other
4 it is the fee whose amount equals the printed total exactly. The bank's
`N Checks/Debits` counts every debit row except the one its `Service Charges`
total covers.

**Proposal for Ocean** (the table is yours): promote `capital_one:debit` to
comparable with scope `service_charge_excluded_from_printed_debit_count` and
the mapping `stated_debit_count + (1 if stated_service_charge else 0)`.
Caveat I could not close: every charged document in the archive has exactly
ONE fee row, so what is strictly proven is "the rows the `Service Charges`
total covers are excluded" — a cycle aggregating two fees into that total
would want +2, and no such document exists here to measure.
