## UB1. The instrument, and the scout's numbers

Every measurement in this record was taken with a harness that reproduces the
production native-text rung exactly (`ocr.pipeline.parse_statement`, visual OCR
disabled), reading the archive PDFs from the MAIN checkout read-only. Nothing
was written to the archive or to the D-3 cache; `analyze_markdown` is called
directly, never through `cached_analysis`. **Zero OCR, zero model calls, $0.00.**

Harness fidelity was established before any production edit: over the 26
documents of the `Desjardins` folder the harness reproduced run `88be9dd3`'s
dispatch exactly — the same 5 rows claimed by `desjardins` plus the one
`pinned_corpus_duplicate` the run excludes, and the same 20 unclaimed.

The scout's populations, re-derived rather than repeated:

| family | scout | measured | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fifth Third | 13 docs, 12 rec | **13 docs, 13 validated** | all 13 in `Unidentified`, none in the folder named `Fifth Third Bank` |
| Fiserv | 56 in-folder, 30 rec, +10 other folders | **84 docs carrying the furniture**; 62 in `Unidentified`, 22 across 5 other labels | 18 of the 84 are already claimed (§UB4.1) |
| Desjardins FR | 10 docs, 6 rec, 4 chain-broken | **16 docs, 6 reconcile, 10 chain-broken** | the scout's 10 is the `Unidentified` slice; 6 more are filed under `Desjardins` |

**The folder named `Fifth Third Bank` contains no Fifth Third statement.** All
16 of its PDFs are Shopify Balance statements — a Stripe-issued product whose
disclosure names Fifth Third as one of two custodians. The 13 real Fifth Third
documents are filed under `Unidentified`. This is the §CHASE-LAYOUTS lesson
again, in a sharper form: the folder label was not merely unhelpful here, it
pointed at a different product entirely.

## UB2. Card 5 — three debit components, and what a bare label means

The account summary flattens to one line (shape reproduced with synthetic
figures throughout this record — no archive amount, date or name appears here):

```
02/01 Beginning Balance $(100.00) Number of Days in Period 28
300 Checks $(1,000.00) 150 Withdrawals / Debits $(2,000.00)
70 Deposits / Credits $4,000.00 02/28 Ending Balance $900.00
```

`Checks` is a debit-side total **separate from** `Withdrawals / Debits`. The
identity is `beginning + deposits − checks − withdrawals == ending`, and the
two-component reading fails on the 8 of 13 documents that print a cheque
total — the other 5 print the bare label discussed below. The
fixture `test_folding_the_cheque_total_away_would_break_the_closing_identity`
pins the reading rather than the result: it asserts that the two-component walk
does *not* reach the printed closing balance and the three-component walk does.

**The grammar the scout's trap sits inside.** Each component prints as
`[count] LABEL [amount]`, and *both* optional parts really are optional:

```
... Period 28 Checks 30 Withdrawals / Debits $(2,000.00) 25 Deposits / Credits ...
... Period 31 3 Checks $(1,000.00) Withdrawals / Debits 7 Deposits / Credits ...
```

In the first, `Checks` carries neither count nor amount and the `30` belongs to
`Withdrawals / Debits`; in the second, `Withdrawals / Debits` is the bare one.
A bare label means the component is **absent**, and the parser only accepts that
reading because the document says it twice: the matching detail section is
absent too. Where the two printings disagree the document is refused
(`test_a_bare_label_with_its_section_still_present_is_refused`).

**Where this cell disagrees with the scout.** The scout recorded "1 doc missing
the withdrawals clause — fail closed". That document (bare `Withdrawals /
Debits`) is not defective: its closing identity closes exactly with the
component at zero, it prints no `Withdrawals / Debits` detail section, and its
daily-balance walk completes. Refusing it would be fail-closed on a document
that proves itself. It validates, and the family is 13/13.

**Four instruments, all required to agree.** Measured over all 13 before any
parser existed, then again through the parser:

```
summary identity holds                : 13 / 13
section headings agree with summary   : 13 / 13
rows match their section's count+total: 13 / 13
daily balance walk holds              : 13 / 13
```

The cheque grid is a three-up `Number Date Paid Amount` layout with independent
`*` / `i` / `s` flags, and the three detail sections interleave across pages —
a page ends mid-grid and the next resumes it under `- continued` after
reprinting the whole address block. Sections are therefore gathered globally: a
page boundary closes whatever section was open, and every continuing page
reprints its own heading, so the reprinted furniture is *structurally* unable to
leak into a section without the parser needing to know what furniture looks like.

Detection keys on the print stream's own header
(`FTCSTMT### ### ######## UDSPDFSTMT ################### DDA`, uniform across
all 13), the issuer domain the page footers carry, and the summary heading. The
issuer matters in both directions, and the archive supplies the proof of each.

**A name-based marker would have missed twelve of the thirteen.** The words
"Fifth Third" appear on exactly one of the 13 real statements. The domain
appears on all 13.

**A name-based marker would also have claimed sixteen documents that are not
Fifth Third statements at all.** The 16 Shopify Balance documents filed under
the folder named `Fifth Third Bank` each name Fifth Third Bank in their
page-one custodian disclosure — a third-party product naming the bank that
holds the funds. Detection claims none of them:

```
Shopify Balance documents filed as 'Fifth Third Bank': 16
mentions of 'Fifth Third' in them                    : 16
claimed by fifth_third or fiserv_premier             :  0
```

This is R4-3's invariant meeting a real document rather than a hypothetical
one, and it is pinned as a fixture
(`test_a_custodian_disclosure_naming_the_bank_is_not_a_claim`).

## UB4. Card 2 — a platform, three parsers already on it, and one issue taken

### UB4.1 The collision surface is not only Wells Fargo

Fiserv Premier is a core banking platform. Censusing the whole extracted corpus
for its summary furniture found **84 documents**, and 18 of them are already
claimed:

```
unclaimed                66
claimed: capital_one     11
claimed: linkbank         4
claimed: farmers_merchants 3
```

`analysis/linkbank.py` is, in substance, already a Fiserv Premier parser — it is
simply gated on one bank's domain. Capital One's business checking and Farmers &
Merchants run on the same template. A registration written to "the Fiserv
summary" would make all 18 **ambiguous**, which routes 18 currently-resolved
documents to review. That is a regression, and no amount of downstream care
prevents it, because ambiguity is decided before any parse runs.

**That 18 is a floor, not the population.** It counts only the documents this
cell extracted; Ocean's review re-derived the same coexistence over a superset
and found **40**, every one of them byte-identical with and without this
registration. The larger number strengthens the claim rather than weakening it —
the disjointness holds over more than twice the evidence used to design it — and
the figure to quote going forward is 40.

The three parsers involved also hold **6 documents of the pinned corpus**
between them (`capital_one` 4, `linkbank` 1, `farmers_merchants` 1), so a
broader registration would have to clear the gate as well as the archive — the
RC8.3 lesson, and the reason §UB9 checks all 109 pinned documents directly
rather than inferring their safety from an archive census.

The 84 split into three printed issues:

| issue | n | already claimed |
|---|---|---|
| leading counts (`26 Deposits/Credits 9,999.99`) | 58 | 18 |
| parenthesised counts (`Deposits/Credits (28) $9,999.99`) | 14 | 0 |
| one-sided | 12 | 0 |

**This cell takes the parenthesised-counts issue only**, because it is the one
that is provably disjoint from every registration already on the platform: none
of the 18 already-claimed documents prints it. That disjointness is what lets
this registration be purely additive — no `excluding` marker naming another
bank, no `supersedes` edge, no change to an existing entry.

### UB4.2 The issuer is read off the page, not off the folder

The template prints a domain in its customer-service block and no bank name at
all. The name is recovered structurally: the statement's own return address is
reprinted in the group's disclosure directory beside the division that owns it,
so the return address selects the row and the name is the text in front of it.
Repeated-glyph page furniture is filtered; a directory that resolves to more
than one division, or to none, refuses the document.

This is what leaves the 4 fourth-family documents unnamed: their disclosure page
carries no directory, so there is no printed evidence of the issuer's name, and
this parser will not name a bank the page does not.

They are **not** named here either. An earlier draft of this section called them
"Coastal States Bank" — read off the same unverified furniture the section is
about, which is precisely the standard §UB5 applies to card 8. Struck.

Their refusal is in any case **over-determined**: all 4 also lack the
`Statement Dates … (N days)` period line this layout requires, so they are
refused on the period before the issuer is ever consulted.

```
d8ddb4db_April.pdf          REFUSED  period=N  issuer=None
d8ddb4db_Checking_…_6_3     REFUSED  period=N  issuer=None
d8ddb4db_Checking_…_7_3     REFUSED  period=N  issuer=None
d8ddb4db_May.pdf            REFUSED  period=N  issuer=None
```

### UB4.3 Result over the Fiserv family

```
detected by fiserv_premier : 14
parsed                     : 10
outcomes: {'validated': 6, 'review': 4}
declined (no printed issuer): 4      -> parser_declined, named below
```

| n | what they are | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | two divisions, both ledger shapes | validated |
| 4 | same two divisions | **claimed, withheld from validation by `missing_declared_statement_page`** — see below |
| 4 | a fourth family, not named here | refused: no period line, and no printed issuer (UB4.2) |

**One reading in this parser is uncorroborated, and is named as such.** The
summary carries `Service Charge` and `Interest Paid` clauses, and the closing
identity treats both as sitting *outside* the two transaction totals. Every
document of this family in the archive prints both as `$0.00`, so the corpus
does not test that reading either way. It is kept because it fails closed: a
charge that is in fact already inside the debit total would be subtracted twice,
the identity would miss, and the document would be refused rather than published
with a wrong balance. Recorded in the module at the point of use.

The 4 in the middle row are a **platform finding, not a parser defect**. Each
declares `Page N of M` footers on the statement pages and then appends the GLBA
privacy notice as unnumbered inserts — so a 6-page statement footered `1 of 8`
through `6 of 8` is followed by two pages carrying no footer at all. The
pipeline's page-declaration check reads that as two missing pages. The parser's
own four gates (summary identity, both counts, both totals, and either the
running-balance chain or the section totals) all pass on these documents. Raised
as carried finding UB8.2; `analysis/pipeline.py` is not this cell's to change.

## UB5. Card 8 — the family is real, the bank is not on the page

The card asked for a French-language extension of `analysis/desjardins.py`,
with three structural hints. All three point unambiguously at one family, and
that family is not identifiable as Desjardins.

**The family.** 16 documents printing `Relevé de compte` over a
`MM JJ DESCRIPTION DÉBIT ($) CRÉDIT ($) SOLDE ($)` grid, opening on
`SOLDE PRECEDENT`, running into a `FACTURATION DÉTAILLÉE` fee table. Every one
of the card's hints matches it and only it: the fee table is the structural
terminator; the money grammar is space-thousands with a comma decimal mark and a
**detached** minus printed as its own token before the balance; and the `MM JJ`
date pair collides with a space-thousands amount exactly as described — both are
a digit group, a space and another digit group, so a row-start matcher fires
inside `9 999,99` as readily as on a real `05 01`. Anchoring the row start on a
**following capital** separates them, because a date pair is always followed by
the description's first word and an amount never is. The known-Desjardins
layouts in the same folder match none of the three hints.

**The measurement.** With that grammar, over all 16:

```
family size                                     : 16
reconcile against the printed counts AND totals :  6
chain-broken                                    : 10
```

The 6 reconcile against a genuine in-document oracle — the fee table prints
`TRANSACTIONS DÉBIT <n> <total> CRÉDIT <n> <total>`, so the count *and* the
total of each side are checkable, on top of a zero-break balance chain. This
reproduces the scout's "10 docs, 6 rec, 4 chain-broken" exactly on the slice the
scout surveyed.

**Why nothing was built.** The registration would have to assert a bank. No
document in the family names one:

```
institution words in any document's header block: NONE
```

The only evidence for "Desjardins" is the archive folder label on 6 of the 16 —
and folder labels are established in this record as filing conventions rather
than truth (§CHASE-LAYOUTS: one parser's 28 documents were filed across five
different labels; and in this very cell, §UB1, the folder named `Fifth Third
Bank` holds no Fifth Third statement). Three independent lines of evidence point
away from Desjardins:

1. **There is a French Desjardins layout in the archive, and it is a different
   document.** 13 documents print `CAISSE DESJARDINS <caisse name>` in the
   header of every page over an `EOP ÉPARGNE AVEC OPÉRATIONS` grid. They name
   their institution; this family never does.
2. **The two share no ledger vocabulary.** `Solde reporté` / `Virement Interac`
   / `Paiement facture - AccèsD Internet` against `SOLDE PRECEDENT` /
   `COMPTE DIVERS` / `DPA ENTREPRISE` / `PERCEPTION DE CPTE`.
3. **They do not even print money the same way.** The Desjardins layouts use a
   **dot** decimal mark; this family uses a **comma**. And their PDFs are
   produced by `TargetStream StreamA2P for Visa Desjardins` with author
   `AccesD`, where this family's are `OpenText Exstream`.

Registering these as `Desjardins` would put a bank name into published
underwriting output on the strength of a folder name, which is the failure mode
`tests/test_parser_detection_markers.py` exists to prevent. **The card's gate
was met regardless**: `analysis/desjardins.py` is untouched, all 6 documents it
claims still parse and validate, and the archive-wide differential in §UB7 shows
no document outside the two new families changed claimant at all.

**What Ocean needs to rule.** Whether a registration may carry a `bank` label
its documents do not print, and if so what that label is. The template furniture
is unmistakable and the arithmetic is already proven on 6 documents, so the
answer to that one question is the whole of the remaining work.

## UB6. The Fiserv anti-collision proof

The brief made this clause binding, and it is the finding this cell would most
want re-checked, so it is measured three ways.

### UB6.1 The collision is real, and it is the counts clause alone

A Wells Fargo account summary prints the opening balance immediately to the left
of the `Deposits/Credits` label, and PDF flattening puts them on one line:

```
Statement period activity summary
Beginning balance on 1/1 $1,234.56 Deposits/Credits 9,999.99 Withdrawals/Debits ...
                                ^^
```

The obvious counts clause, `\d+\s+Deposits/Credits`, therefore matches the
**cents of the opening balance** and reads them as a transaction count. (The
shape is quoted with synthetic figures; the real ones stay in the archive.)
Over the 236 Wells Fargo documents of the stratified probe:

```
== single clauses, hits in the wells stratum (236 documents) ==
   counts clause, one side  (\d+\s+Deposits/Credits)     216 / 236
   counts clause, both sides                               0 / 236
   parenthesised counts (both sides)                       0 / 236
   opening balance ("Previous Balance")                    0 / 236
   "Statement of Account"                                 17 / 236
   the shipped conjunction (all three)                     0 / 236
```

Two of those lines are worth pausing on. **The template's own heading is not
sufficient either** — 17 Wells Fargo documents print "Statement of Account"
somewhere. Neither the heading nor the counts clause can carry this
registration on its own, which is precisely why the opening-balance clause is
required rather than corroborating: it is the only one of the three that is
zero on its own.

216 of 236, and 229 of those 236 are `validated` in the run of record. The
scout's figure of 197 is the same finding measured over a different slice; the
mechanism is confirmed.

### UB6.2 The clause shipped

`DETECTION_MARKERS` is a conjunction of three `required` markers — the template
heading, **the opening-balance clause**, and the parenthesised counts clause.
`required` rather than corroborating is the load-bearing choice: `score_markers`
carries a `+1` in the denominator when any required marker misses, so one
missing marker caps the score below `CLAIM_THRESHOLD` no matter how much else
fires. Each of the three is proven load-bearing by ablation in
`tests/test_fiserv_premier.py::test_every_marker_is_load_bearing`, and the
collision shape itself is pinned as a fixture
(`test_the_wells_shaped_summary_is_not_claimed`).

### UB6.3 The stratified probe, with the wells-heavy stratum

Deterministic (documents taken in `rows.csv` order, no sampling randomness):
every folder label, validated documents first, up to 12 each — **plus the whole
of the Wells Fargo labels**, which is the binding stratum. The run of record
holds 243 Wells Fargo rows, 236 of them digital; the probe took all 236, so the
wells stratum is not a sample of that population but the whole of its readable
part. (The archive's second `WellsFargo` folder contributes no row of its own to
the run — its files are deduplicated against the main label.)

```
== stratified non-target probe ==
documents probed : 679
strata           : 65 folder labels
wells stratum    : 236 documents (229 validated in the run of record)

claims by fifth_third or fiserv_premier            : 0
   of those, in the wells_fargo strata             : 0
documents whose OTHER claimants changed            : 0
ambiguous dispatches after                         : 0
```

Every probe document is resolved twice — once with the two new registrations
present and once with them removed from the registry — so "nothing changed" is a
differential rather than an assertion about a single run.

## UB7. Non-interference, measured over everything extracted

The same differential over every document this cell extracted (the whole
`Unidentified`, `Desjardins` and `Fifth Third Bank` folders plus the probe
cohort), deduplicated:

```
distinct extracted documents: 1563
documents whose claimant set changed: 27
   (none)  -> fiserv_premier   14
   (none)  -> fifth_third      13
documents OUTSIDE the two families whose claimants changed: 0
multi-claimant (ambiguous) documents after: 0
```

Every change is a document nothing claimed before. No document lost a claimant,
no document gained a second one. The counts here are *claimant sets*, so
`fiserv_premier` shows 14 rather than the 10 it parses: the other 4 are claimed
and then declined for want of a printed issuer, which is the `parser_declined`
outcome and exactly the fail-closed behaviour §UB4.2 describes — not a crash and
not a silent pass.

## UB8. Carried findings for Ocean

1. **`ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` needs a bump** (`webapp/artifact_cache.py`,
   currently 10). Both registrations change analysis output for documents whose
   cached payloads predate them. Not this cell's file.
2. **The page-declaration check does not tolerate unnumbered inserts.** Four
   otherwise-clean Fiserv statements are withheld because the GLBA privacy
   notice appended after the statement carries no `Page N of M` footer while the
   footers count it in their denominator. The signal is doing exactly what it
   was written to do; the question is whether "declared pages with no footer at
   the end of the document" should be distinguishable from "a page is missing
   from the middle". Four documents here; likely more across the archive.
3. **The Fiserv leading-counts issue is 40 unclaimed documents** and is reachable
   without touching an existing entry, by giving a second registration
   `excluding` markers for the three issuers already on the platform — which is
   a property of the new entry, not a change to theirs. It was not attempted
   here: it needs a generic issuer reader across roughly twenty banks, and the
   sub-vocabularies of its detail sections are genuinely various (14 distinct
   section-heading signatures among the 66 unclaimed documents of the family).
   It is the single largest remaining block this cell surveyed.
4. **`analysis/linkbank.py` is a Fiserv Premier parser under a bank's name.** If
   UB8.3 is taken up, the honest end state is one platform parser with the
   issuer read from the document, and `linkbank`/`capital_one`/`farmers_merchants`
   reconsidered against it. That is a change to existing registrations and
   therefore a ruling, not a cell decision.
5. **Card 8 is one ruling away from 6 validated documents** — see §UB5.
6. **The Fiserv fee terms are an uncorroborated reading** (§UB4.3). Every
   document of the family prints a zero service charge and zero interest, so
   whether they sit inside or outside the two transaction totals is untested.
   Both mistakes fail closed, so nothing wrong can be published; but the first
   document of this family with a real service charge will either validate or
   be refused, and which of those happens is the answer to the question.

## UA9. Amendments from adversarial review

Ocean's review reproduced all eight claims independently and returned SHIP with
one BLOCK-grade fix and three closures. All are applied below. **No outcome
moves: all 45 family documents are byte-identical to the reviewed branch.**

### UA9.1 The L-1 guard failed OPEN (the blocker)

`woodforest._accounts` collected summary rows only while they were
CONSECUTIVE and stopped at the first line that did not match. A summary block
whose rows straddle a page break prints `--- Page 2 ---` and the page's own
header between them — so a **two-account document would have been read as
one account and published**. That is the exact inversion of what the guard
exists for: a control designed to fail closed must not fail open, and this one
did.

The fix is structural rather than a wider tolerance. The summary region is now
bounded by **its own printed close** — the `Transactions` label or the activity
grid's column header, both of which the document prints to open the
per-account sections — and every summary row inside that region is collected
while anything else in it is skipped. Line adjacency is no longer load-bearing.

The reviewer's exact construction is pinned as
`test_a_second_account_split_by_a_page_break_still_fails_closed`, and a second
fixture pins that collecting across the region does NOT run past its close
(the account section that follows prints the same product name and number, and
the postings below it print money of their own).

**Why no document moves:** all 20 archive Woodforest documents are
single-account, so the defect was latent rather than live. It would have gone
live on the first genuinely multi-account Woodforest statement — which is
precisely the document the guard was written for.

### UA9.2 Symitar's silent row drop, aligned to the refuse convention

A posting whose `MM/DD` could not be resolved was `continue`d — dropped from
the ledger without a word — while this cell's own `woodforest._postings`
returns None and refuses the document for the same condition. Two readers, two
conventions, in one cell. Symitar now refuses: a row the grid printed but the
reader cannot resolve is a hole in the ledger, and a hole must refuse the
document rather than shrink it silently. Pinned with an unresolvable `02/30`.

### UA9.3 The `$`-blind `_ROW_RE`, recorded

`symitar._ROW_RE`'s money alternatives do not admit a currency symbol, while
the opening and closing rows this layout prints DO carry one
(`05/01/26 $ 1,000.00 Beginning Balance`). A posting row that ever printed `$`
would not open a row and would be swallowed into the previous row's
description. **Censused: across all 7 family documents the number of dated `$`
amounts that are not a Beginning/Ending Balance row is zero.** Left as-is
deliberately — widening the pattern to admit `$` would make the opening row
itself match as a posting, which is the more dangerous of the two errors — and
recorded at the pattern.

### UA9.4 The ±0.01 tolerance is a rounding allowance, not a repair budget

Inherited verbatim from `cibc._en_sign_from_balances`. Where it admits the
balance movement, the published amount becomes the MOVEMENT rather than the
bank's printed magnitude, which is a silent preference worth stating.
Measured over the whole Woodforest family:

```
rows total                          : 1,887
delta == printed magnitude exactly  : 1,871
NON-TRIVIAL repairs (0 < gap <= 0.01):     0
outside tolerance (kept as a debit) :    16   (all of them Royalty2's)
```

So every amount this parser publishes is the bank's own printed cell, and the
convention has never once altered one. Recorded at the function, because that
stays true only while the census stays at zero.

### UA9.5 The wealthsimple furniture claim is conditional

"The page furniture printed after the final row is never swallowed into it"
holds **only while the final row closes**. Two constructions break it, and
both are now stated at the module docstring and in the fixture:

* a wrapped description that happens to END in something the tail pattern
  reads as an amount/balance pair closes the row early, and the rest of the
  description becomes furniture;
* if the final row never closes, the boilerplate after it is accumulated into
  that row until something completes the pair.

Neither occurs in the family — all 16 documents read with zero unread rows —
and both fail closed downstream, because a row published with the wrong amount
breaks the balance walk the summary block is checked against. Recorded rather
than guarded, so the claim is not read as unconditional.

### UA9.6 The normalization commit was not detection-only

`0e84758`'s subject says "detection", and that overstates what it touched.
Dropping the whole-document normalization also required rewriting two `symitar`
**parse-path** regexes — `_ACCOUNT_SUMMARY_RE` and `_SECTION_RE` — to tolerate
the leading and trailing spaces the collapsing pass had been stripping. Both
are used by `_sections` and `_account_summary_balances` during parsing, not
only during detection. Detection equivalence was proven at the time (3,367
documents, 0 disagreements); **parse equivalence is proven here**, in the
sweep below.

## UB-RC. Review closures

Ocean's adversarial review returned **SHIP** — every headline survived
re-derivation over larger populations than this cell used (0/229 Wells; 40/40
coexistence byte-identity; the 27 movers re-derived from source PDFs) — with
three closures required before merge.

### RC-D1 A capitalized run in front of an address is not an identity

**Finding.** `_issuer` published whatever capitalized run preceded the return
address. The reviewer constructed `Statement.bank = "Member FDIC Equal Housing
Lender"` and `"Notices to Smith and Jones LLP"` from ordinary boilerplate, and
the docstring's "will not name a bank the page does not" was an overclaim. This
registration is slated to generalize across ~20 issuers, so a blocklist was
explicitly not an acceptable close.

**Close.** The name is published only when the document's **own web address
spells it** — `_spells(label, name)`: the domain's letters appear in the name in
order and both begin with the same letter. That is one structural rule covering
all three ways this platform's issuers name themselves, none of them enumerated:

| printed as | domain | name | why it passes |
|---|---|---|---|
| directory row | `altabank.com` | Altabank | the name written out |
| Regulation E notice | `ches.bank` | Chesapeake Bank | the name shortened |
| directory row | `fsbmsla.com` | First Security Bank of Missoula | the name abbreviated |

The shared first letter is load-bearing: `ches` is a subsequence of "Notices to
Smith and Jones LLP" *as letters*, and is rejected because that phrase does not
begin with a `c`. Otherwise, and when two names are corroborated at once,
`bank=None` — the capital_one precedent, None over a guess.

**An unnamed issuer no longer refuses the document.** The arithmetic does not
depend on the label, so refusing would have discarded a provable statement and
mis-reported the guard as a parse failure in telemetry. Over the whole extracted
archive **0 documents actually take that path** — every document this parser
publishes still carries a corroborated issuer — so `bank=None` is a safety net,
not a new class of unlabelled output.

Fixtures: the reviewer's three constructions publish None; three synthetic
issuers, one per row of the table above, still publish
(`tests/test_fiserv_premier.py`, D1 block).

### RC-D2 A zero-amount row has no sign to read a direction from

**Finding.** The count gate partitioned by `amount > 0` / `amount < 0`, so a
`$0.00` row fell out of both counts while still riding in `transactions` — a
four-row document passing a three-row count check, with the row published as a
zero-amount credit. The platform's rule is direction-not-sign.

**Close.** The gate now partitions by `Transaction.direction`. In the split
sections the heading fixes the direction, so a zero row is kept and counted. In
the running grid the direction lives in a Debits/Credits column the flattened
text layer has destroyed, so there is nothing to derive it from and the row is
refused outright rather than filed under a guessed side. Both halves fixtured on
the reviewer's four-row shape.

* **The 18-document coexistence figure is a floor**, covering only what this
  cell extracted; the reviewer's superset puts it at **40**, byte-identical

# §JHA-CELL — a core processor's template, read without naming a bank

## J0. Summary

`analysis/community_section.py` already read this template for two issuers.
It is not a bank's layout: it is a **core processor's**, and the archive
prints it under **22 different issuers**. Registering it per issuer would mean
a new registration, a new marker pair and a new fixture for every community
bank and credit union that ever buys this product, and would leave every
issuer nobody has met yet unread.

So it is registered once, on the **template's own furniture**, with the
**issuer read out of each document**. That is the mission_valley product-label
lesson applied one level up: publish what the document prints.

**56 documents claimed; 47 move `failed` → `validated`; nothing moves down.**

| | before (run `88be9dd3`) | after |
|---|---|---|
| validated | 45 | **92** |
| withheld | 0 | 7 |
| review | 0 | 2 |
| failed | 70 | **14** |

All 47 are instrumented per document rather than merely claimed: the summary
identity closes, the sum check closes, both printed totals equal the published
ledger, both printed counts equal the published counts, and — where the
document prints one — every per-section `N item(s) totaling $X` trailer agrees.
**5,370 transactions** published across the 56. Over the whole cohort,
**56 of 56 instrument sound and 0 unsound.**

The four issuer-specific readers that already existed are **46/46
byte-identical**, and the pinned corpus holds one document of each.

## J1. The instrument

Every figure below comes from replaying the archive markdown through the real
pipeline (`analyze_markdown(parse_mode="deterministic")` +
`telemetry.record.classify_outcome` + `discovery.runner._failure_reason`),
resolved from the D-3 OCR artifact store **by direct file path** — the sqlite
index was never opened. The `content_sha256 → artifact` index was built by
reading each payload envelope's own `input_sha256`, so it does not depend on
this process's environment reproducing the run's cache key.

Population re-derived from the run of record rather than taken from the scout:
`rows.csv` of `2026-08-14T060822.665646-0000-88be9dd3`, 3,506 rows / 3,380
distinct `content_sha256`, of which **3,367 have offline text** (the 13 without
are exactly the `deferred_visual_ocr` documents). Zero cache misses.

## J2. The cohort, characterized before any code was written

The scout's signature was `Statement Ending` + `Summary of Accounts` +
`N Credit(s)/Debit(s) This Period`. Measured, the discriminating member of that
conjunction is the **grid header**:

| probe | documents, archive-wide |
|---|---|
| `Account Summary Date Description Amount` | **115** |
| `N Credit(s) This Period` | 120 |
| `Statement Ending <date>` | 120 |
| `Summary of Accounts` | **193** |

`Summary of Accounts` is *not* exclusive — 17 Wells Fargo documents print it,
and narrowing on it alone would have reached them. The grid header appears in
115 documents and **every one is this platform: zero near misses.** The
registration therefore requires the grid header **and** a printed period-count
row, which also satisfies the two-required-marker invariant (R4-3).

Of the 115: **45 already claimed** (mission_valley 36, dakota_west 3,
midflorida 3, first_community 3 — `first_community` is a fourth issuer on this
template that the handoff did not name) and **70 `failed`, every one
`no_parser_matched` with an EMPTY `attempted`.** Nothing had ever claimed them.

Folders of the 70: Unidentified 51, Bluevine 5, R Bank 4, Rogue CU 4,
Columbia 3, Chase 2, SouthStar 1. The folder labels are operator guesses; the
template is what they have in common.

Sub-layouts: 47 J-A (per-direction sections), 23 J-B (`Account Activity`

## J3. Reading the issuer out of the document

| issuer evidence | coverage of the 115 |
|---|---|
| a **labelled** domain (`Online`/`Website`/`Internet Banking` + domain) | **110**, and UNIQUE in every one |
| any bare domain | 114 |
| a `Thank you for … <Bank>` sentence | 37 (mission_valley 36 + dakota_west 1) |
| `<Bank> … Member FDIC` | 1 |

The label is what makes this safe. Of the five documents printing no labelled
domain, **four print merchant domains** — `walmart.com`, `apple.com`,
`gosq.com` — inside their own transaction descriptions. "The first domain in
the document" would have published a merchant as the issuer on exactly those.

The read is scoped to the **masthead** (everything before the document starts
listing accounts), because R Bank prints its state regulator in the fine print
below the ledger (`Website: www.dob.texas.gov`) and a whole-document read saw
two labelled domains and could not say which was the bank.

Published as `Statement.bank`, lower-cased with `www.` removed — a domain is
case-insensitive and `www.` is not part of the name, and the same issuer prints
it both ways. Nothing else is transformed. Turning `falconbank.com` into a bank
NAME would be an invention, and a wrong one (it is Falcon International Bank).

## J4. Five defects the measurement found

Each was found by measuring, not by reading the code, and each is pinned.

**1. The section trailer was being read as a row.** `N item(s) totaling $X`
carries no date, so it lands in the final dated row's chunk, and this reader
takes the LAST money in a chunk. On a section of 18 items totaling $40,458.87
that publishes the section total as the last row's amount — a four-figure error
that leaves the row COUNT right, which is exactly what a count check cannot
see. Now cut at the money seam, and separately checked as the oracle it is.

**2. The trailer check mis-aligned on page breaks.** A section broken across
pages reprints its header as `(continued)` and `_sections` rightly treats each
run separately, but the trailer is printed once and counts the whole section.
Comparing it against the tail run reported every page-broken section as a
disagreement. Rows are now accumulated across runs until the trailer appears.

**3. The claim gate counted by SIGN.** The platform posts genuine `$0.00` rows
(a returned ACH) and the bank counts them in the column it printed them in. A
zero-amount row is on neither side of a sign test, so the gate rejected
documents whose ledgers were complete — three archive documents measurably so.
The gate now counts by `Transaction.direction`, the rule `reconcile` already
documents. Its cost is disclosed in `count_semantics` (J9.1).

**4. One cheque row masked a whole J-B ledger.** The body reader was chosen by
"did the first reading return anything", and both arrangements print
`Checks Cleared`. A single cheque made `txns` non-empty and the
`Account Activity` ledger was never read — **11 documents**. The arrangement is
now chosen by whether the document printed per-direction SECTIONS, and the J-B
branch does not add `_check_rows`, because that ledger already carries the
cheques and adding them would publish each twice.

**5. The account heading swallowed the page furniture, twice.** A regex matches
leftmost-first and this heading is preceded on the page by figures. A character
class admitting `/` and long digit runs let four documents publish an account
name of `tal Statement Ending 01/31/2026 Business Checking`; allowing a NUMBER
to open the name then let it begin inside the amount printed just before it
(`$1,034.78 BASIC BUSINESS CHECKING` → `78 BASIC BUSINESS CHECKING`). The name
is now a token sequence that must START with a word, so no token can be a date,
a masked account number, or the tail of an amount. All 56 published names are
clean; 16 distinct product names, all as printed.

## J9. Carried findings and questions for Ocean

**J9.1 — `count_semantics`: three ids are now immune by construction.** The
table recorded mission_valley and dakota_west as "parser-gated, **sign-keyed**"
and argued they were NOT immune to the stated-count check, because the gate
keyed on sign while the check keys on `Transaction.direction`. Defect 3 above
made the gate key on direction too, so a `match` for these three ids is now a
tautology. The entry says so in those words rather than leaving it to be
inferred from a run of passes. Their independent evidence is the per-section
trailer, which no summary figure can reproduce. **Ruling wanted:** accept the
disclosure, or hold the direction key to `community_section` alone and leave
the two older ids sign-keyed (which would re-break the three $0.00 documents).

**J9.2 — five reconciling documents declined only because we cannot name the
bank.** Their ledgers reconcile against every printed figure; they print no
labelled issuer domain. `Statement.bank` is `str | None`, so publishing them
unattributed is *possible*. Whether an underwriting product should publish a
bank-statement analysis that cannot name the bank is a product decision, not a
parser one, so this cell fails closed and asks. **+5 validated available on a
one-word ruling.**

**J9.3 — geometry card.** 2 documents print a J-B ledger whose balance column
is empty on every row; direction is column position and flattened text does not
carry it. A real customer for the geometry rung.

**J9.4 — L-1 is now costing 7 documents on this template alone**, all credit
unions printing share + checking + savings. A multi-account schema would
recover them; picking the busiest would not be honest.

**J9.5 — the registration's `bank` label is `"Core Statement Platform"`, not a
bank.** It is used only by `by_bank_label` (unclaimed documents) and by
folder-agreement aliasing. Consequence, deliberate: the 56 claims will read as
folder-label disagreements in 6 folders, which is TRUE — a JHA statement filed
under `Chase/` is misfiled — but it will show up in the agreement rollup and
should not be mistaken for a regression.

**J9.6 — one document is refused by a rule this cell chose to keep.** A signed
CREDIT total still fails the summary match outright, because a credit total
that reduced the balance contradicts the row it is printed on. Measured: 0 of
115 credit totals carry a sign, 1 debit total does. No document is lost to
this today; it is recorded so the asymmetry is a decision and not an accident.

**J9.7 — `midflorida` reads the J-B arrangement with its own bespoke reader**
in `analysis/midflorida.py`, gated on one product name. It is now the only
issuer on this template with a private copy of a body reader the shared module
also has. Out of this cell's ownership; worth a consolidation card, and its
3 documents are byte-identical either way.

**J9.8 — a DATED statistic after the closing balance would be read as the
closing balance.** `_summary` takes the first and last dated balance rows. The
two-column arrangement prints `Minimum Balance` / `Average Ledger Balance`
undated, which is what excludes them; an issuer that dates one of those rows
and prints it after the closing row would have it read as the closing balance.
Downstream this withholds rather than publishes (the ledger would not close
against it), but **the reader's own gate never checks the summary identity** —
`beginning + credits - debits == ending` — so it would claim and hand a wrong
closing balance to the pipeline. No archive document does this. Card: add the
printed identity as a parser-side gate, where it is cheap and local.

**J9.9 — the J-B $0.00 row is published as a credit.** In `_activity_rows` the
sign rule is `balance >= previous`, so a zero-amount row (the balance does not
move) takes `direction="credit"`. On the J-A side the direction is the column
the bank printed the row in, which is the platform's own rule and the one this
cell adopted for the count gate; the J-B branch cannot see a column. No
archive document has a $0.00 row in a J-B ledger, so nothing is measurably
wrong today. Card: derive J-B direction from the printed column where geometry
makes it available, and until then record that this one row class is signed by
convention rather than by evidence.

**J9.10 — the `posting_date_coverage` withholds (3 documents).** One posting
day in the source is not covered by the parsed ledger, while both printed
counts match exactly. A dropped transaction would break the counts, so the
uncovered date is most likely printed outside the transaction sections. Worth
one look before the ADB engine is asked to relax anything.

## J11. Amendments from adversarial review

Verdict SHIP, with four closures. The review also proved the byte-identity
claim one document larger than this cell had (J11.5) and confirmed the edges
are structural rather than observed: each sibling's markers are independent of
the template furniture, so no mangling of the template can flip a document
from a sibling to the general reader.

**J11.1 — the issuer comment overstated the label, and the reviewer built the
document that proved it.** The comment said "a domain printed under a label
that says it is the bank's own — the LABEL is the whole point". The code
required only that a label WORD appear immediately before a domain *in the
collapsed masthead*, and `Online`/`Visit` are ordinary words that occur in the
holder's own address block. The reviewer got `bank='walmart.com'` published.

Taken as a **structural tightening**, not just a comment fix, because the gap
had a clean cause: `_clean` collapses newlines, so a label ending one printed
line and an unrelated domain beginning the next became adjacent. The issuer's
real contact block prints both on ONE line. `_issuer` now reads the masthead
line by line (`_masthead_lines`, deliberately un-collapsed) and the separator
class is `[: \t]+` rather than `[:\s]+`. The comment is also corrected to say
what is actually true: **the masthead SCOPE is the guard, the label is
corroborating.** Reproduced and pinned both ways — the construction now
declines, and a document carrying that same line break *plus* a real contact
line still reads its issuer.

Cost on the archive: none. 56 claims, 47 validated, 5,370 transactions,
56/56 instrument sound — unchanged to the document.

**J11.2 — the trailer-oracle docstring was false, and the code with it.**
"Sections that print no trailer are simply not checked" did not hold when a
trailer-less section preceded a trailer-printing one: the accumulator that
lets a page-broken section be compared as one section folded section A's rows
into section B's comparison. A **false refusal** — fail-closed, but a bug, and
it made the only per-section oracle unusable on mixed layouts.

`_sections` now yields each section's printed name with the `(continued)`
marker removed, and the accumulator resets on a change of name. A trailer-less
section is now genuinely unchecked. Pinned with the reviewer's construction
(A no-trailer + B trailer → B compares only B's rows) **and its control** (a
row missing from B is still caught), so the reset cannot be mistaken for
turning the oracle off.

**J11.3 — clean once per document, not once per marker.** Both markers called
`_clean`, which rewrites the whole document, so this registration paid for two
full rewrites on every document of a 3,500-document sweep. The normalization
is now registry data (`detection_text`, passed to both `make_detector` and the
`Registration`), which is exactly the seam `make_detector` documents.

Measured over 300 sampled archive documents, one process, best of three:

```
52 other registrations                       10.628s
community_section, once-per-marker (before)   1.744s   share 14.1%
community_section, once-per-document (now)    1.010s   share  8.7%
speedup 1.73x · 5.9 percentage points of a whole sweep removed
claim disagreements between the two forms: 0
```

**J11.4 — records.** J9.8 (dated-statistic-as-closing-balance, and the
parser-side identity check it argues for), J9.9 (the J-B $0.00 direction
convention) and J9.10 + the two-class table in J5 (the 3
`posting_date_coverage` withholds, now named apart from the 4 bounced-cheque
walks) are added above.

**J11.5 — the sibling population is 46, not 45.** The review found one more
mission_valley document. It is in the D-3 store but NOT in run `88be9dd3`'s
population: the run's OCR settings key holds a NULL document for it, and its
text exists only under the other settings key — so a sweep derived from
`rows.csv`, as this cell's was, cannot see it. Swept explicitly:

```
content_sha256 CD7E104D7474…      claimants before: ['mission_valley']
                                  claimants after : ['community_section',
                                                     'mission_valley']
dispatch  claimed -> claimed, parser mission_valley -> mission_valley
payload   0BE7D98471CB18DF… -> 0BE7D98471CB18DF…   IDENTICAL
```

**46/46 byte-identical.** The lesson is the same one card C of §RBCCIBC
recorded in a different costume: a population derived from one artifact is not
the population. Re-derive from the artifact STORE, not from the run's rows,
when the claim is "nothing moved".
# §PIPEFIX — two orchestrator defects: a repair that reads a counterparty, and a page that was never missing

Protected-module cell. The unit of work is `analysis/pipeline.py`, the
deliverable is two minimal hunks, and the argument that matters is
containment: what else in the archive moves, and why every mover is the same
defect rather than a new one.

## P0. Summary

Both cards were raised by HUNT-CELL, which measured them counterfactually and
declined to patch modules it did not own. Neither pays out on this branch: the
+5 and the +3 are Huntington and Burke & Herbert documents that no
registration claims until `wave3-hunt` lands, so today they are
`failed / no_parser_matched` and never reach either code path. **These are
enabling fixes.** What they pay out here is the defect they remove from
documents that do publish.

| card | the defect | movers on this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | bank-summary repairs gated on a document substring, so another bank's name as a COUNTERPARTY fires them | **3** statements whose `ending_balance` is rewritten by a foreign repair |
| 2 | `missing_declared_statement_page` reads an absent page LABEL as an absent PAGE | **0 at merge — ships INERT.** Once wired: 114 documents lose a false flag, of which **13** publish (+2 pinned, ceremony) |
| 3 | `wells._infer_year` reads the first year token by position | **0** — measured, latent, not shipped (P4) |

Card 2 was extended mid-cell by Ocean with UNID-PACK-B's Fiserv finding. It
needed **no code change**: the rule keys on the presence of an unlabelled
sheet, not on what is printed on it, so a GLBA disclosure insert and a
deposit-image sheet are the same fact to it (P3.3). Enabling totals across the
wave: 5 Huntington (card 1) + 3 Burke + 4 Fiserv (card 2) = **12** documents
that stop being blocked by an orchestrator defect once their own registrations

Card 2's blast radius is materially wider than its carded +3. It is measured
exactly, every publishing mover is named, and it is put to Ocean rather than
quietly shipped (P3.5). After adversarial review it ships **inert** — the
mechanism is corrected and pinned by tests, but no production caller supplies
the page structure it needs, so nothing moves at merge. Activation is a
ceremony-gated follow-up card (P4b.5, P7.6).

`analysis/regions.py` and `analysis/bofa.py` carry a **zero-line diff**. The
change is `analysis/pipeline.py` and `tests/test_analysis.py`, nothing else.
`ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` is deliberately NOT bumped; it is Ocean's at merge.

## P1. The instrument

Every figure below comes from the archive markdown resolved out of the D-3
artifact store **by direct file path** — the sqlite index was never opened —
and replayed through this branch's real `analysis.pipeline`. The store
resolves 3,367 of the run-of-record documents; the rest have no OCR artifact
under any settings key and are excluded rather than assumed.

Baseline run of record: `88be9dd3`. Base commit: `625c41d`.

## P2. Card 1 — a repair fires for the registration that claimed the document

### P2.1 The defect

`apply_statement_repairs` gated two repairs on substrings of the document:
`"REGIONS" in markdown.upper() and "SUMMARY" in ...` (`analysis/regions.py`)
and `"BANK OF AMERICA" ... "ACCOUNT SUMMARY"` (`analysis/bofa.py`). Both
rewrite PUBLISHED figures — `beginning_balance`, `ending_balance`, the stated
totals, `stated_service_charge`.

A bank's name in a statement is as often a fact about a counterparty as about
the issuer. This is R4-3 applied to a repair instead of to a detection marker,
and a repair is the worse place for it: detection competes and can be
adjudicated, a repair simply overwrites.

### P2.2 The fix

The gate is the **claiming registration**, held as data next to the calls:

```python
_SUMMARY_REPAIRS: dict[str, Callable[[str, Statement], Statement]] = {
    "bank_of_america": repair_bofa_summary,
    "regions": repair_regions_summary,
}
```

resolved through `_registration_for` — the same R-3 resolution
`assess_quality` and `assess_document_integrity` already use, so an LLM
extraction naming a bank we have a parser for still gets that parser's repair
(the R-3 ruling), and one naming a bank we do not gets nothing. `dispatch` is
threaded to the three call sites; it was already in scope at all three.

At most one bank-summary repair can now fire, since a document has one owner.

These are registration IDs, not bank labels: `test_pipeline_names_no_bank`
stays green, and a new test holds every id in the table to a live registration
so a renamed parser cannot silently switch its repair off.

### P2.3 Why the sweep is complete rather than a sample

Old behaviour is `gate(markdown)`. New behaviour is `owner ∈ {bank_of_america,
regions}` **and** `gate(markdown)` — because each repair keeps its own internal
guard, which is why both modules have a zero-line diff. The two can therefore
differ in exactly one direction:

* `gate` true, owner is not the owner → the repair stops. Measurable, and
  swept exhaustively below.
* `gate` false, owner is the owner → the repair is called and its own guard
  returns the statement unchanged. A no-op by construction.

There is no third case, which makes the substring-gate candidate set a
complete enumeration of everything that could move.

### P2.4 The sweep, and the named movers

```
documents with an OCR artifact                  3,367
satisfy either substring gate                     456
  ...of which a parser claimed                    424
  ...whose OWNER is the repair's owner            384   (360 bank_of_america, 24 regions)
  ...claimed by some OTHER registration            40
       bmo_ca_business 19, american_express 9, td_us 4,
       chase 3, wells_fargo 3, mission_valley 1, us_bank 1
documents whose published statement CHANGES         3
```

The full claimed populations of `regions` (24) and `bank_of_america` (360) are
**byte-identical**. Of the 40 documents exposed to a foreign bank's repair, 37
were already no-ops — the gate was satisfied but the labels the repair reads
were absent — and 3 were genuinely corrupted:

| document | owner | fields the foreign repair was rewriting | outcome today |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Chase/1bfe70c4_20260430-statements-7933- (1).pdf` | `chase` | `ending_balance`, `stated_service_charge`, `stated_total_credits`, `stated_total_debits` | `withheld` |
| `Chase/abe3b3ef_20260331-statements-8658- (1).pdf` | `chase` | `ending_balance`, `stated_total_debits` | `withheld` |
| `Chase/d25571c6_20260331-statements-7871-.pdf` | `chase` | `ending_balance`, `stated_total_debits`, `stated_service_charge` | `withheld` |

Each has a correctly-parsed `ending_balance` overwritten today by a repair
belonging to a bank that appears in it only as a counterparty.

**ADJUDICATED — ACCEPTED (Ocean, adversarial review).** The review established
what the corruption actually is: on these three the base is publishing a
transaction COUNT where an ending balance belongs. With the repair keyed on the
claiming registration their ledgers reconcile exactly, and all three move
`withheld` → **VALIDATED**. They are carried here as three accepted publishing
movers, not as an open question.

### P2.5 The carded +5, counterfactually

The five Huntington documents are unclaimed on this branch, so the proof runs
with HUNT's registration constructed in memory as the claimant, against each
document's real archive markdown and a statement carrying the issuer's own

## P3. Card 2 — an unlabelled sheet is not a missing page

### P3.1 Characterization first, and it corrected the card

The handoff proposed restricting the DECLARATION SET, on the FIXUPS-1
lookbehind precedent. The three documents say that cannot be the fix. Their
printed shape, read off the archive markdown:

| document | declares | labels printed | sheets with text | unlabelled sheets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `6768-2026-Mar` | 6 | 1–5 | 7 | 2 |
| `6768-2026-Apr` | 8 | 1–7 | 9 | 2 |
| `6768-2026-May` | 6 | 1–5 | 7 | 2 |

Every declaration on these documents reads `of 6` / `of 8`. Removing
declarations from the set can only shrink `present` and therefore GROW
`missing`; it cannot withdraw this flag. The defect is not in what counts as a
declaration — it is in the inference from a missing label to a missing page.

The bank's own last page is physically present as an unlabelled deposit-image
sheet. On `6768-2026-Mar` it lists `2/13 $18,245.24`, `2/23 $8,000.00`,
`2/13 $1,525.00`, `2/20 $1,200.00` — exactly the two deposit and two
withdrawal rows of the published ledger. The "missing" page corroborates the
parse it was being used to impeach.

### P3.2 The fix

An unlabelled sheet is counted as what it is: a sheet that could be any one of
the pages whose label was not found. Where there are at least as many of them
as there are missing labels, nothing has been shown to be absent:

```python
        unlabelled_sheets = sum(
            1
            for sheet in _SHEET_SEPARATOR_RE.split(markdown)[1:]
            if sheet.strip() and not _PAGE_DECLARATION_RE.search(sheet)
        )
        if missing and len(missing) > unlabelled_sheets:
```

The sheet separator is the intake layer's own (`ocr.document.
StatementMarkdown.to_markdown`), read here for the same reason
`analysis/navigant.py` already splits on it: it is the one structural record of
how many sheets the supplied PDF actually has. No issuer literal is involved.

`[1:]` drops the intake preamble, which is not a sheet. It is load-bearing
twice: a caller passing raw (non-admissible) markdown would otherwise
contribute a phantom unlabelled sheet and weaken the check by one, and a
document with no separators at all — every hand-written fixture — yields no
sheets rather than one. The first draft omitted it and two new tests caught it.

**The check is not blunted.** The discriminating case is real and pinned: the
Columbia statement declares 5 pages, supplies 4 sheets and prints a label on
every one of them. Zero unlabelled sheets, so a page really is absent, and its
flag stands byte-identical — as does the synthetic Wells fixture behind the
FILENAME-BOUNDARY suppression test.

A tightening was considered and rejected on measurement: additionally
requiring `sheets_with_text >= declared_total`. It changes **nothing** over
3,367 documents, and it is close to implied — if each printed label sits on its
own sheet, `unlabelled >= missing` already entails it.

four Fiserv Premier statements are held out of validation by this same flag
because the GLBA privacy notice is appended as sheets carrying no footer while

**No code change was needed, and that is the result worth recording.** The rule

## P4b. Adversarial review: the separator-injection defect, and the records it asked for

Ocean's review returned SHIP-conditional. Card 1 was accepted outright (P2.4).
Card 2 carried a defect of my own making, and it is the more interesting half
of this cell.

### P4b.1 The defect: page content could forge a sheet

The first form of the card-2 hunk recovered the sheet structure by re-splitting
the RENDERED markdown on the `--- Page N ---` separators. That is a text
convention `ocr.document.StatementMarkdown.to_markdown` writes BETWEEN pages —
unescaped — and page content is OCR output of whatever the document printed. A
statement carrying the literal line `--- Page 9 ---` therefore manufactures a
sheet that does not exist, and manufacturing one unlabelled sheet is exactly
what it takes to withdraw a genuine missing-page finding.

This is the FILENAME-BOUNDARY principle one layer down, on the same
fraud-relevant flag: I replaced one untrusted-input channel (the filename) with
another (page body text), and did not notice because both were *our own*
rendering conventions. Validating the separator STREAM does not close it —
appending the forged marker inside the LAST page leaves the 1..K sequence
intact — so the count has to come from the object that knows how many sheets
were rasterised.

### P4b.2 The fix

`assess_document_integrity` takes `sheets: Sequence[str] | None`, the intake
object's own page list, threaded through `analyze_markdown`. The check is now
two conjuncts, and Ocean's free tightening is the second:

```python
        printed_sheets = [sheet for sheet in (sheets or ()) if sheet.strip()]
        unlabelled_sheets = sum(
            1 for sheet in printed_sheets if not _PAGE_DECLARATION_RE.search(sheet)
        )
        accounted_for = (
            len(printed_sheets) >= declared_total and len(missing) <= unlabelled_sheets
        )
        if missing and not accounted_for:
```

`_SHEET_SEPARATOR_RE` is deleted; nothing re-derives page structure from the
string any more.

**Fail-closed on silence.** A caller that supplies no sheet list gets the
pre-cell behaviour exactly: `printed_sheets` is empty, `accounted_for` is
False, the flag stands. A caller can only ever weaken this check by PROVING
structure, never by staying silent — which is the property that makes the
optional parameter safe to add ahead of its callers.

**What the combined rule now refuses**, stated exactly because the padding
vector is the obvious next attack:

* a short PDF padded with blank or whitespace-only sheets — they are excluded
  from `printed_sheets`, so they raise neither conjunct;
* any document supplying fewer text-bearing sheets than it declares pages,
  however many unlabelled sheets it has;
* any forged separator in page content, which no longer participates at all.

**The honest residual**, recorded rather than papered over: padding a short PDF
with a sheet that carries real text still withdraws the flag, and ONE CHARACTER
is enough to make a sheet text-bearing. Such a sheet is indistinguishable from
a genuine unlabelled insert without reading the page, and this cell does not
read pages; closing it needs a reader that can tell a statement page from a
filler page, which is a different capability from counting them. The in-code
comment states this limit at the point of use rather than claiming the two
conjuncts defeat padding.

**One call-site footgun, refused loudly.** `str` is itself a `Sequence[str]`,
so `sheets=markdown` type-checks and then iterates one CHARACTER per sheet —
thousands of unlabelled sheets, and this flag cleared on every document that
carries it. `assess_document_integrity` raises `TypeError` on a `str` rather
than coercing it to `None`: passing the document text is a caller defect, and a
caller that believes it is supplying page structure while supplying none would
otherwise run the check in its weakest mode indefinitely with nothing to show
for it. No document's content can reach this path — only a call site can — so
raising costs nothing at runtime and fails the wiring card loudly if it is
mis-wired. Pinned by
`test_passing_the_document_text_as_the_sheet_list_is_refused`.

### P4b.3 Re-verification after the fix

outcome         CARRY  WITHDRAWN   KEPT
failed            137        101     36
review              9          3      6
withheld           11         10      1
TOTAL             157        114     43

flags RAISED on any document                                              0
documents whose PAGE BODY contains a separator line (forgery in the wild) 0
documents where the intake-object rule disagrees with the string-split rule 0
publishing movers (card 2)                                               13
publishing movers (card 1)                                                3
```

The census reproduces to the document, and the intake-object count is
**behaviour-identical on every real document in the archive** — the forgery
vector is a live hole in the string-split form, but nothing in the corpus
exercises it, which is why the first form's sweeps looked clean. The 16 movers
are unchanged. The Burke three and the Fiserv four still clear
(`flags=[]` on all seven).

### P4b.4 Records the review asked for

1. **P3.5 TD-Mar row corrected.** `01 Mar TD Statement.pdf` declares **5**,
   missing **[2, 4]**, **3** unlabelled sheets (the table said 6 / 2 / 2). The
   verdict is unchanged; the row was mistranscribed.
2. **The CONTINUED-footer composition.** FIXUPS-1's `(?<!NEXT )` lookbehind
   means a sheet whose only page-number text is a continuation footer matches
   no declaration — so it counts as UNLABELLED here and can excuse a missing
   page. The two restrictions compose in a direction neither intended.
   **Measured: 0 of the 157 flag-carrying documents have such a sheet**, so it
   is synthetic-only today. Carried finding, not patched: the fix belongs with
   whoever next owns the declaration pattern.
3. **The denominator asymmetry**, now documented at the point of use:
   `declared_total` is the largest denominator in the document, but a sheet
   counts as labelled if it carries ANY declaration whatever its denominator.
   A sheet printing `Page 1 of 2` in a document declaring 8 is treated as
   labelled rather than as a candidate. Conservative — it only ever keeps the
   flag — so it cannot clear a document.
4. **`tests/test_structurer_pipeline.py`** quoted the pre-cell
   `apply_statement_repairs(markdown, normalize_statement(deterministic_stmt))`
   in its illustrative diff. Updated to the shipped call.
5. **The LLM-path label-parity gap**, carried as a card and NOT fixed here.
   `by_bank_label` is an exact casefold match on the registration's bank label,
   so an extraction naming `Bank of America, N.A.` resolves to nothing and gets
   no repair where the retired substring gate fired. Twenty unclaimed documents
   satisfy the BofA gate; **four are genuine Bank of America statements**:
   `927b5806_July_Statement_2026-07-07.pdf`, `94445b3f_Bank letter.pdf`,
   `b0e2e2e9_eStmt_2026-01-30.pdf`, `b4d1c344_March 2026 Bank of America .pdf`.
   All four are `failed / no_parser_matched` in the deterministic run of

   exposure is on the auto path only. This is a label-normalization card
   against `by_bank_label`, not a change to this branch.

### P4b.5 The wiring this fix still needs, which is not this cell's to write

The parameter is threaded but no production caller passes it yet, and the three
that can are all outside this cell's ownership. Until they do, card 2 is
fail-closed inert in production — no document is wrongly cleared, and none is
newly accused, but the 13 publishing movers do not move either:

| file | site | change |
|---|---|---|
| `discovery/runner.py` | `_analyse` (called from the intake result) | thread `document.pages` in and pass `sheets=` |
| `webapp/worker.py` | `analyze_markdown(markdown, parse_mode=...)` | `sheets=doc.pages` — `doc` is already in scope one line above |
| `webapp/artifact_cache.py` | `cached_analysis` compute lambda | pass the document's pages alongside `md` |
| `webapp/artifact_cache.py` | `analysis_settings_key` / `cached_analysis` key material | **add the sheet count** — see below, this is not optional |

**The wiring card MUST also add the sheet count to the analysis-stage cache
key material.** An earlier draft of this section claimed the opposite — "no
cache-key change is needed, the sheet list is a function of the same document
that produced the markdown". That was FALSE, and it was the most dangerous
sentence in this cell's output, because it would have been read as clearance.

The analysis key is built at `webapp/artifact_cache.py:638` as

```python
    input_sha = text_sha256(admissible_text(markdown))
```

— the ADMISSIBLE text, which is precisely the text with the
`<!-- source: … | pages: N | … -->` header removed. The page count is
therefore not in the key material at all. And `to_markdown` is not injective
over that text: a genuine three-sheet document and a forged one-sheet document
whose single page prints the separators render to the SAME admissible string,
so they take the same analysis cache key while having DIFFERENT correct
answers under this check. The reviewer demonstrated the collision (key
`EB23C6B1C971…`). Cache the first, serve it for the second.

The header is stripped for a good reason — FILENAME-BOUNDARY, since it also
carries the filename — so the fix is not to re-admit it but to add the sheet
count to the key material explicitly, alongside `stage_version` and
`parse_mode`.

**Ceremony gate.** Activating the wiring legitimately moves two PINNED corpus
documents, so it is Gustavo's formal ceremony, not a merge-time decision.
Measured with each document's authentic page list, over all five pinned
`page_coverage` documents:

| pinned document | declares | missing | sheets | when wired |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Regions/Regions.pdf` | 3 | 1, 2 | 3 | **flag withdrawn → validated** |
| `Misc/Texas Bank.pdf` | 4 | 1, 2, 3 | 4 | **flag withdrawn → validated** |
| `Misc/Builder June 2026.pdf` | 5 | 1, 2, 3 | 4 | flag stands |
| `Misc/Columbia May 26 complete.pdf` | 5 | 5 | 4 | flag stands |
| `Misc/Link Bank April statement.pdf` | 20 | 20 | 20 | flag stands |

Both movers are review→validated on a withdrawn false flag, which is exactly
the movement `corpus_gate.py` cannot see: the gate's partition is
106 PASS / 3 WITHHELD, and review and validated are both PASS. That is why
this branch was BLOCKED at `b8013d5`, where the string-split form made those
two moves with every gate check still green, and why the corpus-marked slice
(`test_telemetry_reproduces_the_gate_outcome_split`,
`test_withheld_diagnostics_reproduce_the_documented_diagnosis`) is the proof
that caught it. Both pass at this HEAD, because card 2 is inert.

`webapp/` is Ocean's and `discovery/runner.py` is outside this cell's
ownership, so all four items — three call sites plus the cache key — are
specified here rather than edited.

# §COUNTSP3 — five stated-count candidates, re-measured; three promoted, one split, one refused

| | |
|---|---|
| Cell | COUNTS-P3 (batch 4, card 4) — `wave4-countsp3`, base `707ba9e` |
| Cells worked | `analysis/count_semantics.py` (new entries only), `tests/test_count_semantics.py` |
| Candidates | `chase_savings`, `td_canada_french`, `burke_herbert`, `first_citizens`, `capital_one:debit` |
| Result | 3 registrations promoted in both directions · 1 split (credit comparable, debit incomparable with the mapping) · 1 REFUSED, with the measured cost of the alternative |
