| Table integrity | all 54 pre-existing direction entries field-identical; `UNSURVEYED`, `SECTION_LEVEL_ORACLES`, `DIRECTIONS` untouched; the check stays advisory |

## CP0. Summary

Five candidates arrived with evidence from batches 2 and 3. Every one was
re-measured from scratch against the current archive before anything was
written into the table, and the re-measurement changed two of the five
answers — not because the old evidence was wrong, but because **three of the
five family populations were being under-counted by the instrument that
produced the old numbers.**

That is the finding worth reading first.

## CP1. The instrument, and the population defect it had to fix first

Run of record `discovery_reports/2026-08-14T214345.671986-0000-d5c75ff6`
(v11), read from the MAIN checkout. Cached OCR and analysis artifacts were
addressed **arithmetically** — `cache_key(stage, input_sha, settings_key)` →
`webapp_data/artifacts/<stage>/<key[:2]>/<key>.json`
(`webapp/artifact_cache.py:295`, `:410`) — across the three OCR settings
partitions. **The sqlite index was never opened.** Zero OCR, zero model calls,
**$0.00**.

**The population defect.** The run's `rows.csv` leaves `parser_id` EMPTY on
every analysis-cache hit — 119 distinct documents (110 `validated`, 6
`review`, 3 `withheld`). This is the known H-3 cache-hit hole, already named
in §DB1 and in the batch-2 coverage-metric note; what this cell adds is that
it silently shortens FAMILY POPULATIONS, which is exactly what a
counterfactual's denominator is made of. Three of the five candidate families
were short:

| family | population from `rows.csv` | true population |
|---|---|---|
| `capital_one` | 18 | **22** |
| `first_citizens` | 34 | **35** |
| `td_canada_french` | 12 | **13** |
| `chase_savings` | 10 | 10 |
| `burke_herbert` | 3 | 3 |

**`model_used` cannot recover the identity** and the attempt is recorded so
nobody repeats it: it is the slugged BANK LABEL, not the parser id, so it
disagrees with `parser_id` on 1,590 of 2,329 documents and collapses three
BMO registrations onto one string.

Identity was recovered instead by **replaying `parser_registry.resolve` over
the reconstructed markdown**. Fidelity was proven before the results were
believed: on all 77 documents of the five families that DO carry a
`parser_id`, the replay reproduced it, **77 of 77**. Enriched, all three short
families land exactly on their historical figures — `capital_one` 22 (§DB8's
22), `first_citizens` 35 (§FI14.3's 35), `td_canada_french` 13 (TD-FRENCH's
"13 claimed / 9 validated / 4 withheld"). The agreement is the proof that the
enrichment recovered the right documents rather than merely more of them.

## CP2. The five candidates, measured fresh

Per direction: the bank's printed count against the rows we captured, keyed on
`Transaction.direction`, exactly as `analysis/reconcile.py:242-257` computes
it.

| candidate | credit | debit | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chase_savings` | 10/10 match | 6/6 match, 4 `not_printed` | **PROMOTED** both |
| `td_canada_french` | 9 of 13 match, 4 mismatch | 9 of 13 match, 4 mismatch | **PROMOTED** both |
| `burke_herbert` | 3/3 match | 3/3 match | **PROMOTED** both, disclosed tautological |
| `first_citizens` | 35/35 match | 26 exact + 9 off by +1 | **SPLIT** — credit comparable, debit incomparable |
| `capital_one:debit` | (already comparable) | 10 exact + 12 off by +1 | **REFUSED** — see CP4 |

### CP2.1 `chase_savings` — promoted, with the denominator stated honestly

The handoff's pointer read "10/10 exact both directions". The underlying
record (CHASE-CLOSURE) says "chase_savings 10/10 with counts equal to printed
instance counts", which is a statement about ten DOCUMENTS. Measured per
direction, the debit side has **six** comparisons, not ten: four of the ten
savings statements posted no debit category at all and
`stated_debit_count = debit_count or None` (`analysis/chase_savings.py:216`)
maps that to absent, so they report `not_printed`. Six of six agree, zero
disagree.

Six is still a counterfactual, which is what separates this from
`chase_export:debit` — held incomparable precisely because 4 of 4 print
nothing. The entry records the denominator rather than inheriting the
compressed one.

The credit figure is a printed whole-direction count (`:198-203`); the debit
figure is a SUM over a closed label list (`:130-137`, summed `:207-216`), the
`chase:debit` construction, and carries the `chase:debit` caveat unchanged.
`Fees` is INSIDE the summed labels (`:214-215`), which is what keeps this bank
out of the capital_one class.

### CP2.2 `td_canada_french` — the one promotion that buys information

On this layout the PDF text layer collapses the RETRAITS and DEPOTS columns
into a single token, so **which column a row was printed in does not survive
extraction**; the parser solves it back out of the running balance the bank
prints at the end of each date group (`_resolve_directions`,
`analysis/td_canada_french.py:468`, direction assigned `:474`). The printed
per-page `CREDITS <n>` / `DEBITS <n>` footers (`:92`, accumulated `:401-408`)
are therefore an ORACLE ON THAT SOLVE, read off the page. Independence is
strict: the solver takes the rows, the groups and the opening balance, and
never reads `stated_credit_count` — the module writes those two fields and
reads them nowhere.

All 13 documents, per direction:

```
  9 documents  credit +0 / debit +0   all `validated`
  1 document   credit -1 / debit +1   withheld  4DE22E685A04...
  1 document   credit -2 / debit +2   withheld  59BD662C0D4F...
  1 document   credit -2 / debit +2   withheld  654AB29A910A...   [recovered]
  1 document   credit -6 / debit +6   withheld  A3A50C108B7F...
```

The four disagreements are **SYMMETRIC** — the credit direction is short by
exactly what the debit direction is long by — which is the solver putting n
rows in the wrong column, and is precisely the defect class this check exists
to name. All four are already `withheld/withheld_adb` and already carry
`ledger_sum_mismatch`; `withheld` is decided before flags are read
(`telemetry/record.py:296-297`), so promotion adds two flags to four withheld
documents and moves no outcome. The handoff asked whether "the withheld 4 stay
inert": they do, in OUTCOME. They are not inert in FLAGS, and that is the
promotion working rather than failing — one of the four (`4DE22E685A04...`,
-1/+1) carries no coverage flag at all, so its misplaced row is currently
invisible.

### CP2.3 `burke_herbert` — promoted, and the entry says the agreement is a tautology

3 of 3 agree in both directions, and the entry's main job is to say out loud
that this carries no information: `_validate` refuses any document whose row
count in either direction differs from the printed count
(`analysis/burke_herbert.py:200-203`), so a CLAIMED burke_herbert document has
matching counts by construction. §H8.5 asked for the entry on the grounds that
"the stated-count check fires on it from its first day" — that premise is
wrong (UNSURVEYED emits nothing), but the conclusion is right for a different
reason: "examined and structurally silent" and "not yet examined" are
different facts, and the table is where the difference is recorded.

Two things are written into the entry rather than left for a future reader:

1. **The control arm does not exist.** The printed label is the capital_one /
   texas_bank label — `<N> CHECKS/DEBITS` beside a SEPARATE `SERVICE CHARGE`
   line (`:61-62`) — and all 3 archive documents bill a ZERO charge. The
   archive therefore cannot distinguish "whole direction" from "service-charge
   excluded" here, the same indistinguishability §DB8 found in COUNTS-P1's 12
   all-charged capital_one documents. What closes it is not evidence but the
   gate: the parser also requires the negative rows to SUM to the printed
   `CHECKS/DEBITS` total (`:194-195`), so a Burke statement whose billed charge
   sat outside that figure goes UNCLAIMED rather than mis-flagged. Fail-closed,
   not proven-absent.
2. **A `$0.00` row would make this direction lie.** The gate counts `a > 0` /
   `a < 0` — the SIGN — while this check counts `Transaction.direction`, which
   the parser sets at `amount > 0` (`:277`). A genuine zero-amount row is
   counted by NEITHER side of the gate and as a DEBIT by this check: the exact
   divergence §JHA-CELL found on `community_section`. No document of this
   family has one (0 zero-amount rows over 3 documents). If one appears, the
   remedy is the gate, not the entry.

### CP2.4 `first_citizens` — the split, and why the credit side is worth little

§FI14.3 corrected its own §FI10 recommendation from COMPARABLE to "a
capital_one-class MAPPING entry" and left the table untouched for this cell.
The fresh measurement reproduces §FI14.3 exactly on the current archive, over
all 35 documents:

```
  counts agree exactly : 26   every one with a ZERO service charge
  counts off by +1     :  9   every one with a BILLED service charge
  credit direction     : 35/35
```

**The debit direction is the capital_one class and stays incomparable.** The
expected side is `checks + other debits` — the two GATED sections
(`analysis/first_citizens.py:611`) — while the published debit rows are those
two sections PLUS `billed`, the monthly service charge, which the bank prints
outside the four section totals and the parser recovers from its own
itemisation (`:476-479`, `:486-523`) and appends at `:597`, `:614`.

The mapping this bank wants is **`stated_debit_count + 1 where the billed
service charge was RECOVERED AS A POSTING`**. Note the second clause, which
the capital_one entry does not need: `_service_charge_posting` returns nothing
when the itemisation cannot be located (`:523`; the module docstring names it
as the one path that can still fail reconciliation), so a charged document
whose charge was not found is `+0`, and a naive "+1 iff charged" mapping would
manufacture a mismatch on it. All 9 charged documents in the archive were
located.

**The credit direction IS promoted, and the entry discloses that its 35/35 is
also a tautology**: `_matches` refuses the document unless each section's
parsed posting count equals the printed one (`:526-531`, applied `:584-589`),
and both credit sections publish `direction='credit'` uniformly (`:417`,
`:444`). Its falsifier is the debit direction's own shape — an interest credit
recovered outside the gated sections the way `billed` is would make the credit
direction disagree by +1 on correct rows.

## CP4. `capital_one:debit` — REFUSED, on four independent grounds

The fresh measurement **confirms §DB8 exactly** on the enriched population of
22: 12 charged documents at `+1`, 10 zero-charge documents at `0`, credit
22/22. The mapping `stated_debit_count + (1 if stated_service_charge else 0)`
is 22 of 22. The disagreement is therefore NOT with the evidence. It is with
what the table can express and what this cell may touch:

1. **The schema has no mapping.** `CountSemantics` is
   `(comparable, scope, reason)`. The shipped check compares
   `stated_debit_count` by EQUALITY (`analysis/reconcile.py:253-257`). There is
   no field, and no code path, that could apply "+1 iff charged". Flipping
   `comparable` to `True` does not install the mapping — it installs the
   equality test the mapping exists to avoid, and CP3 measures the result: 11
   regressions.
2. **Installing it needs modules this cell does not own.** A mapping needs
   `reconcile.py` or `pipeline.py`, both outside the handoff's ownership list,
   and the existing entry's own argument is that the mapping belongs to a
   parser card because "asserting it at the platform level would change the
   expected side, which is a parser's job and not this table's."
3. **`capital_one:debit` is an EXISTING entry** and the handoff's ownership
   line is "new entries + their pins ONLY — no existing entry may flip."
4. **It would move four PINNED corpus documents** from `validated` to `review`
   with `corpus_gate.py` still GREEN over the move — see CP7.

The candidate as written and the ownership rule are in direct conflict; the
rule wins, and the conflict is reported rather than resolved unilaterally.

### CP4.1 One stale sentence in the existing `capital_one:debit` entry — NOT edited

The entry reads: *"Measured: 12 of 12 capital_one documents disagree by
EXACTLY +1 with a non-zero stated_service_charge on every one."* On the
current archive the family is 22, of which 12 are charged and disagree by +1

## CP7. The pinned corpus — and the fourth ground for refusing `capital_one:debit`

The 109-path manifest was hashed and joined to the run. **Five of the 83
candidate-family documents are pinned corpus documents, and all five are
PASS** — and every one of the five is a document the identity replay
recovered, invisible in `rows.csv`:

```
393547C0407F...  capital_one     PASS  validated  service charge 15.00  debit +1
4FC7799B53D7...  capital_one     PASS  validated  service charge 15.00  debit +1
C5C39D466437...  capital_one     PASS  validated  service charge 15.00  debit +1
C6D4DAC2278D...  capital_one     PASS  validated  service charge 15.00  debit +1
57058C69B871...  first_citizens  PASS  validated  service charge  0.00  debit +0
```

Read that twice. **Four of the pinned 109 are charged capital_one documents**,
and a plain COMPARABLE `capital_one:debit` moves all four from
`validated/approved` to `review/integrity_flags`. `corpus_gate.py` would report
GREEN over it: validated and review both sit inside the gate's PASS bucket, so
its 106/3 partition cannot see the move. That is precisely the blindness
§PIPEFIX P4b proved and the reason the corpus-marked slice is now mandatory —
and here it arrives as a live, pinned-document consequence rather than a
hypothetical.

`first_citizens`'s single pinned document bills a zero service charge, sits in
the 26-document exact arm, and is unaffected in either direction.

**None of the three promoted registrations touches a pinned document at all** —
no `chase_savings`, `td_canada_french` or `burke_herbert` `content_sha256`
appears in the manifest — so the committed table cannot move a pinned document,
and the gate plus the corpus-marked slice are run as the proof of that rather
than as its argument.

The enrichment is what made this visible: unenriched, the counterfactual would
have missed four PINNED documents.

### The pinned-set edit, both sides

`tests/test_count_semantics.py::test_the_comparable_set_is_pinned_so_a_promotion_is_never_incidental`
pins BOTH sets by equality and asserts they cover the table exactly, so an
entry cannot be moved from one to the other without two deliberate edits. Both
were made: seven keys added to `comparable`, one added to `incomparable`, and
the `len(comparable) + len(incomparable) == 2 * len(SEMANTICS)` invariant still
holds at 62.

Seven tests were added beside the pins (the last two closing review findings
D2 and D5):

| test | the job it does |
|---|---|
| `test_a_tautological_entry_says_so_rather_than_reading_as_evidence` | the three gate-immune directions must SAY they are immune |
| `test_the_countsp3_promotions_each_carry_a_falsifier` | the `first_community` / BofA idiom, now standing for this cell too — and it ENUMERATES all seven promoted directions with one NAMED exemption, rather than sampling a list it can silently fall out of (D1) |
| `test_a_service_charge_entry_says_whether_its_control_arm_was_exercised` | D2 — both `Checks/Debits`-shaped debit entries must disclose that no charged document exists to test the scope against |
| `test_the_first_citizens_debit_entry_carries_the_mapping_and_its_cost` | the mapping, the 26/9 split, the `RECOVERED AS A POSTING` clause, and the measured price of promoting anyway |
| `test_the_td_canada_french_promotion_argues_its_own_independence` | the solver must not be able to read the count it is checked against |
| `test_the_observer_version_moves_when_the_table_does` | D5 — pins `OBSERVER_VERSION` against the table's SHAPE, so the observer's own bump-on-change contract stops depending on someone remembering it |
| `test_an_incomparable_direction_can_never_flag[first_citizens-debit]` | the structural prohibition, on the new incomparable direction |

Suite **3,769 → 3,780**. The +11 is fully accounted: 6 new test functions, 1
new `incomparable` parametrization, and 4 new parser parametrizations in
`tests/test_stated_counts.py::test_an_incomparable_direction_can_never_emit_mismatch`,
which iterates the table.

## CP12. Adversarial review — the six findings and their closures

Verdict: **SHIP**, conditional on the `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` bump, which is
Ocean's at merge.

**D1 — the falsifier test sampled a list instead of enumerating the set.**
Its docstring claimed every promoted direction states a falsifier while
`chase_savings:credit` and `burke_herbert:credit` were silently absent from
its iteration. The docstring was the thing that was wrong, and the reason it
could be wrong is that the list was hand-written.

Closed two ways. `chase_savings:credit` **now carries a falsifier** — it is a
plain printed-figure entry with no gate behind it, so it can genuinely be
wrong, and the way you would find out is a savings layout printing a COUNT
beside a second credit category (the parser already reads `Interest Paid This
Period` for its amount and no count, `analysis/chase_savings.py:219-222`); the
tell is a captured credit count exceeding the printed one by exactly the rows
of the unnamed category. `burke_herbert:credit` stays exempt because it cannot
be wrong — the gate counts `a > 0` and the parser sets `direction='credit'` on
exactly `amount > 0`, so the two sets are provably identical — but the
exemption is now **named in code** (`FALSIFIER_EXEMPT`) with its argument
attached, and the test asserts the exemption list is exactly that one key. The
iteration list is now the enumerated set of all seven promoted directions, so
a future promotion cannot fall out of it by omission.

**D2 — the cell's own standard, applied asymmetrically. The one that matters.**
`chase_savings:debit` asserted flatly that this bank "folds its service charge
INSIDE the printed debit count, which is what keeps it out of the capital_one
class", while `burke_herbert:debit` disclosed at length that its equivalent
claim had no control arm. Re-measured: **0 of the 10 archive documents print a
`Fees` row at all** — `stated_service_charge` is unset on every one — so the
folded-charge arm is exactly as unexercised as burke's, and the entry was
stating a construction as though it were a measurement.

The entry now says so, in burke's own idiom: `Fees` IS one of the summed
labels (`:135`, `:207-216`) so the fold holds BY CONSTRUCTION, the control arm
is empty, construction is the stronger of the two here because the count and
the money come off the same printed line and the parser cannot take one
without the other — and it is still not evidence. The falsifier was widened
with it: any debit category the label list does not name, *including a fee
line spelled anything other than `Fees`*, under-counts the expected side, and
if that category proves to be a charge printed outside the summed labels this
bank joins the capital_one class.

`test_a_service_charge_entry_says_whether_its_control_arm_was_exercised` pins
the disclosure on **both** `Checks/Debits`-shaped entries, so the asymmetry
cannot come back.

**D3 — an over-general sentence about the burke gate.**
`burke_herbert:credit` said the gate "refuses any document whose row count in
either direction differs from the printed count". Exactly true for credit,
FALSE in general for debit: the gate counts by SIGN (`a > 0` / `a < 0`) and
this check counts `Transaction.direction`. The credit sentence is now precise
— it names the `a > 0` set, names `direction='credit'` on `amount > 0`, says
the two are the same set, and points at the debit entry for where they
diverge. The debit entry was already right and is untouched.

**D4 — `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION`.** Noted and left alone: without the bump the
four `td_canada_french` flags are silently inert, because their payloads are
served from a cache keyed on a stage version that did not move. The composed
bump at merge covers it. `webapp/` untouched here.

**D5 — `OBSERVER_VERSION` was stale by its own contract** (scope granted).
Bumped **2 → 3**, with the comment extended to enumerate what a v3 rollup
reports differently from a v2 one over the same archive: the three both-
direction promotions, the `first_citizens` split, the `capital_one:debit`
refusal and its measured cost, and the concrete consequence — 61 documents
across the four families leave `unsurveyed_parser`, and four
`td_canada_french` documents start reporting `mismatch` where v2 reported them

The contract itself was the deeper problem — "bump when the table changes" was

# §WIRING — the activation that stopped: a sixth pinned document, and a ceremony half the harness cannot execute

Ceremony-gated cell (PIPELINE-FIX-2's follow-up card). Four cards were carded:
A the three call sites, B the analysis cache-key material, C the approved
Regions/Texas-Bank truth-set ceremony, D gate hardening. **A, B and C are NOT
landed.** The activation trips the card's own stop rule — it moves a pinned
document nobody had counted — and one half of the approved ceremony turns out
not to be executable in the pinned harness at all. D is landed, because it is
the instrument that makes both facts visible and it moves nothing.

## W0. Summary

| card | disposition | why |
|---|---|---|
| A — the three call sites | **STOPPED, not written** | activating them moves a SIXTH pinned document (W1) |
| B — sheet evidence in the cache key | **STOPPED, respecified** | ships with A; and the carded "sheet count" is *insufficient* — demonstrated collision (W3) |
| C — the two-document ceremony | **HALF-BLOCKED, not executed** | Texas Bank moves as approved; Regions cannot move offline at all (W2) |
| D — gate hardening | **LANDED** | moves nothing; closes both blind spots, proven by mutation (W4) |

Nothing in this cell changes a published value, an audit CSV, a pinned
expectation, or `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION`. The corpus gate gains one check.

## W1. The stop: a sixth pinned document carries the flag, and loses it

The card's scope is *exactly two* pinned documents. §PIPEFIX P4b.5 measured the
five pinned documents diagnosed `page_coverage` and concluded two move. That
table enumerated the documents by their DIAGNOSIS, not by the flag, and a sixth
pinned document carries `missing_declared_statement_page` without being
diagnosed `page_coverage` — because it is `withheld`, and its primary diagnosis
is `source_contradiction`:

```
declarations printed  [(2, 2)] declared_total     2

=> accounted_for      True  -> flag WITHDRAWN when the wiring activates
```

It is one of the **three pinned WITHHELD statements**. Its outcome class does

The withdrawal is *honest* — the page is present and simply unlabelled, exactly

## W2. The other half of the ceremony cannot be executed offline

`Regions/Regions.pdf` is one of the **six image-only pinned statements**. The

So in every offline harness Regions is analysed with `sheets=None`, the check

keep them for the wrong reason — silence rather than a genuinely absent page.

This is a property of the harness, not of the document. Read by direct file
path out of the D-3 archive store, the same bytes DO carry their page list, and

(Independently pre-measured by SCAN-SCOUT and reproduced here from the artifact

## W3. Card B respecified: the sheet COUNT is not enough key material

§PIPEFIX P4b.5 prescribes adding "the sheet count" to the analysis key
material, because `to_markdown` is not injective over `admissible_text` and a
forged one-sheet document can take an honest three-sheet document's cache
entry. The prescription is directionally right and **quantitatively wrong**:
the answer depends on the sheet PARTITION, not on its cardinality, so a
count-carrying key still collides. Demonstrated, not argued:

```python
SEP = "--- Page 2 ---"
A = ["Page 2 of 2\nalpha", f"Page 2 of 2\nbeta\n\n{SEP}\n\ngamma"]
B = [f"Page 2 of 2\nalpha\n\n{SEP}\n\nPage 2 of 2\nbeta", "gamma"]
```
```
same admissible text            True
same sheet COUNT                True  (2)
legacy input_sha equal          True  (3E57530980D6D53D...)
A: missing_declared_statement_page = PRESENT
B: missing_declared_statement_page = WITHDRAWN
```

Two sheet lists, the same length, rendering to the same admissible markdown,
with opposite answers on the fraud-relevant flag. `sheet_count` in the key
material maps them to one entry. The key must therefore carry the partition —
a digest over the sheet list itself — and it should live in the analysis
stage's **input hash**, not in `analysis_settings_key`: the settings key is a
per-RUN constant and `telemetry/stated_counts.py::_ArtifactJoin` indexes the
whole artifact table on one value of it (`stated_counts.py:707,720`). Making it
per-document would silently blind that join.

**Consumers of the derivation to re-point when B lands** (repo-wide grep for
`admissible_text` / `text_sha256` / `analysis_settings_key`):

1. `webapp/artifact_cache.py:653` — the derivation itself.
2. `telemetry/stated_counts.py:774-779` — the second copy the FILENAME-BOUNDARY
   lesson warned about; it reconstructs `pages` already, so it can supply the
   same evidence, but it must be changed in the same commit or the instrument
   goes blind while reporting nothing wrong.
3. The module docstring's `input` table (`artifact_cache.py:45-48`) and the
   `cached_analysis` usage example (`:156-160`).

B invalidates the whole v11 analysis cache by construction. That is expected;
Ocean's composed stage bump covers the re-measurement.

## W4. Card D, landed: the gate now checks the product's own verdict

`corpus_gate.check_outcomes` proves 106 PASS / 3 WITHHELD out of the two
committed audit CSVs. **Neither CSV has a `flags`, `notes`, `risk_level` or
`possible_document_issue` column**, so both oracles are blind to three kinds of
truth-set movement:

* review to validated inside the audits' single PASS class — the `b8013d5`
  regression;
* a published integrity flag appearing or disappearing with **no class change
  at all** — the BMO statement of W1. The carded outcome-CLASS check would not
  have caught it;
* **`risk_level` and `possible_document_issue` moving independently of the flag
  list** (Ocean's review, D1). `possible_document_issue` keys on
  `recon.continuity_breaks >= 3` while the `running_balance_breaks` flag keys on
  the same counter being non-zero, so 2 breaks → 3 leaves class, reason and
  flags byte-identical while `risk_level` goes review → high. It is served to
  users, and the approved Texas Bank ceremony moves it review → clear.

So the pinned expectation is the outcome class plus **the whole published
integrity block** — `_Verdict(outcome, flags, notes, risk_level,
possible_document_issue)`, flags and notes in published order. Measured
justification for the widening: over the 109, the earlier
`(class, reason, flags)` triple **failed to determine
`(risk_level, possible_document_issue, notes)` on 4 documents** — the five
page_coverage documents share one triple while their notes name different page
numbers.

**The `reason` leg was dropped**, and the finding recorded rather than the field
silently removed: over every state the pinned corpus reaches (6 distinct
`(class, flags)` pairs, **0 collisions**) the reason is a total function of
`(class, flags)`, which `classify_outcome`'s structure explains — `withheld`
here is always `withheld_adb`, `validated` always `approved`, and each `review`
reason is selected by a named flag or by the flag list being empty. It added
zero discrimination. `test_the_outcome_reason_adds_no_discrimination_over_class_
and_flags` keeps that true, so a future reason which is NOT so determined
surfaces as a red test.

`PINNED_OUTCOMES` is total over 109 without listing 109: it enumerates the nine
documents that are not plainly published, and every pinned path absent from it
must equal `PUBLISHED_OUTCOME`. Measured: **all 100 validated documents share
exactly one published state** — `('', (), 'clear', False)` — so "absent" is a
real expectation rather than a gap. Recorded from the current tree,
PRE-ceremony.

**The harness-drift trap, closed.** A gate harness that analyses differently
from production pins a verdict production never publishes. This cell's own
evidence is the trap in both directions: had `production_verdict` passed
`sheets=` it would have been RED at a HEAD where production is inert; had it
hardcoded `sheets=None` it would have stayed GREEN forever after the wiring
landed — blind again, on the one flag it was added to watch.
`PRODUCTION_SUPPLIES_SHEETS` therefore declares what the call sites actually do,
and an AST test holds that declaration to them. Wiring production without
flipping it is a red test; flipping it moves pinned verdicts and so demands the
ceremony. Two deliberate steps, neither skippable.

**The declaration's three escapes, closed (Ocean's review, D2).** A declaration
is only as good as its coverage, and the first form had three holes: a helper
extracted out of a listed function would leave it GREEN while production was
wired; `ANALYSIS_CALL_SITES` had no exhaustiveness check; and `**kwargs` or a
literal `sheets=None` mis-classified. Now
`test_every_production_caller_of_the_analysis_is_classified` sweeps the whole
repository by AST and requires every module calling `analyze_markdown` or
`cached_analysis` to be either a declared call site or an explicitly excused
one — **11 modules, 0 unclassified**. A literal `sheets=None` counts as NOT
supplying (it is the fail-closed default written out); a `**kwargs` splat is
unreadable statically and is therefore refused in an excused module, so it must
be declared. Every declared site must agree, so a sibling call that still
passes `sheets=` cannot mask an extracted helper that does not.

**`batch.py` is the third production caller, and P4b.5 missed it.** Decided and
declared: it holds the intake object in scope (`_read_source` returns it),
`webapp/artifact_cache.py`'s docstring already names it a CLI consumer of the
cache, and although its own `needs_review` column keys on quality rather than
integrity, `_emit` serialises the report and hands it to `build_record`, which
runs `classify_outcome` — so **batch.py publishes an outcome class derived from
these flags into its telemetry JSONL**. It must be wired at activation.
Excused, each with its reason in `EXCLUDED_ANALYSIS_CALLERS`: the two forensic
oracles (wiring them would couple the oracles to the change under test, and
neither audits any of these fields), `benchmark/ourside.py` (its resolver yields
no page list), `analyze.py` / `adb_debug.py` / the two coverage scripts (no
intake object exists on their paths), and `corpus_gate.py` itself.

(For the record, P4b.5's "three call sites" are two of the three real ones: its
third entry, `webapp/artifact_cache.py`'s `cached_analysis` compute lambda, is
that module's docstring usage example rather than a caller; its fourth entry,
the key material, is card B; and `batch.py` is absent from the table.)

**Proven by mutation, not by assertion** — expectation flipped in memory, gate
RED, restored, GREEN:

| mutation | gate |
|---|---|
| committed expectation | GREEN |
| `review` to `validated` (the `b8013d5` shape) | RED, names the class move |
| expectation gains a flag the document no longer publishes (the BMO shape) | RED |
| expectation loses a flag the document does publish | RED, "newly publishes" |
| a note's text changes (the page_coverage shape the old triple could not see) | RED, both directions named |
| `risk_level` moved (D1's counterexample) | RED |
| `possible_document_issue` moved | RED |
| document unreadable | RED — a verdict we cannot compute is never a pass |
| restored | GREEN |

Cost: +222s on the gate (109 production-ladder resolutions plus one analysis
each), on top of the base ~430s. See W5 for the contended wall-clock figure.

Red on base, and this branch is FASTER than base. The constant was not raised.

The gate's 1246.0s is a contended number — batch 4 ran eight cells and a second
`corpus_gate.py` on the same box. The new check's own cost, measured alone, is
**+222s** (109 production-ladder resolutions plus one analysis each).

Both figures above are from the post-review re-run at `HEAD`, after the whole
published integrity block replaced the (class, reason, flags) triple.

The forge-fixture family (`test_page_content_cannot_forge_a_sheet_boundary`,
`test_padding_the_pdf_with_a_blank_sheet_does_not_clear_the_flag`,
`test_no_sheet_list_leaves_the_check_exactly_as_it_was`,
`test_passing_the_document_text_as_the_sheet_list_is_refused`) is green at every
commit — untouched, since no production behaviour changed.

## W6. Carried findings

1. **The stop (W1).** `Others/BMO/BMO_Statement_January_2026 Final-1-2 (1).pdf`
   is pinned movement outside the approved scope. Gustavo's ceremony needs
   re-scoping to three documents, or the activation needs to leave this one
   alone — which cannot be done without an issuer or shape literal.
2. **Regions cannot move offline (W2).** Either the ceremony lands as one
   document (Texas Bank, 101/5/3) with Regions deferred, or the committed
   corpus artifacts gain their page list first. The D-3 store already holds it;
   no live OCR is needed.
3. **Card B is under-specified (W3).** Sheet count is not sufficient key
   material; the partition is. And it belongs in the input hash, not the
   settings key.
4. **Tesseract-mangled page declarations (SCAN-SCOUT, recorded, not patched).**
   23 of 179 scanned archive documents print declarations `_PAGE_DECLARATION_RE`
   cannot read (`1of5`, `4 o0f6`). A tolerant pattern moves **zero** documents
   today, so the regex is deliberately NOT widened here — a latent for whoever
   next owns the declaration pattern, alongside §PIPEFIX P4b.4's
   CONTINUED-footer composition.
5. **A third copy of the key derivation exists outside the repo**, in the
   scan-scout scratchpad instrument (`keys.py`). Not repo code and not this
   cell's to fix, but it will go stale the moment card B lands.
6. **`production_verdict`'s first justification was measured wrong.** It said
   `balance_forensic_audit.source_markdown` "silently produces different
   markdown for the four layout-aware banks". Measured over the pinned
   manifest: **0 of 109 differ**. The resolver choice is still right, for a
   different and stronger reason — `source_markdown` returns text and nothing
   else, while `parse_statement` returns the intake object whose `pages` a
   wired caller must supply, so only it can still be correct after the wiring
   lands. Sentence corrected in place.
7. **A green `pytest -q` is not a verified truth set.** The 109-entry map is
   compared against the product only by `python corpus_gate.py` (or
   `pytest -m corpus`); the unmarked tests check the map's shape and prove the
   mechanism by mutation on one document. Recorded in both module docstrings so
   green CI is not mistaken for a verified map.
8. **A flagless `review` is reachable and must stay recordable.** The first form
   of the shape test asserted every non-validated entry carries a flag, which
   would have made a legitimate `quality_needs_review` expectation
   unrecordable — the gate would have gone RED with the only correct remedy
   blocked by a test. It now asserts each entry is a state `classify_outcome`
   can actually reach, including the internal consistency of `risk_level` with
   `flags` and `possible_document_issue`.

# §SCANA — the Fifth Third statement, photographed

SCAN-A, 2026-08-15. Branch `wave4-scana`, base `ba13ec3` (main `ea8d8e8`, two handoff
commits on). Batch 4 refill, SCAN-SCOUT card A.

## SA0. Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| Population | 4 distinct shas, all `scanned` / `failed` / unclaimed, named in the handoff |
| Result | **4 / 4 validated**, from 0 / 4. Improved 4, regressed 0 |
| Registrations added | none — `fifth_third` already existed; one detection marker and three readings widened |
| Marker blast radius | the final markers claim **17 of 3,380** archive shas: the 13 `fifth_third` already claimed + these 4, and nothing else |
| Family sweep | the 13 already-claimed documents are **byte-identical**, payload for payload |
| Statement-specific constants added | none |
| Protected modules touched | none |
| Files changed | `analysis/fifth_third.py`, `tests/test_fifth_third.py`, `tests/data/parser_conformance_fixtures.py`, this log |
| Truth-set movement | none — no pinned corpus document is in this family |

The four documents are four consecutive months of one account, and that is
worth saying first because it gives the cohort a fifth instrument the parser
does not have: **each month's printed closing balance is the next month's
printed opening balance**, across all four, with no gaps.

```
Jan  6F57BE08   5,745.44  ->  -1,159.85
Feb  64A49584  -1,159.85  ->     502.89
Mar  53906D0E     502.89  ->     213.65
Apr  CDB8A6CC     213.65  ->   4,214.58
```

Nothing in the reader chains statements together. Three independent readings
per document plus this chain across them is the reason the cohort is published
rather than reviewed.

## SA1. What was actually wrong

Nothing about the *statement*. The `fifth_third` reader shipped in batch 3
against thirteen electronic PDFs, and three of its assumptions turned out to be
assumptions about the PDF rather than about the layout the bank prints.

**1 — the print stream is furniture the FILE carries.** Detection required
`FTCSTMT044 044 20260228 UDSPDFSTMT …`, described in the module as "the one
piece of evidence no other issuer's document carries". True, and still true —
but it is a print-stream header, not ink on the page, so a photograph of the
identical statement has no trace of it. What the page itself prints is the
product the statement names in its own `Account Type:` field. The census over
all seventeen documents:

```
                                 print stream   Account Type: 5/3
13 electronic (already claimed)        13              9
 4 scanned (this cohort)                0              4
```

Both branches are load-bearing. The four electronic documents that do not name
a `5/3` product print `COMM'L 53 ANALYZED` instead and are held by the print
stream; the four scans have no print stream and are held by the product line.
Replacing the marker rather than widening it would have lost four documents.

`issuer_domain` (`53.COM`) and `summary_block` (`ACCOUNT SUMMARY`) were **not**
touched. Every one of the seventeen documents prints the domain in its page-one
footer, so widening the issuer marker to accept the bank's *name* — which the
prototype handed over did — would have bought nothing and spent the one thing
this parser's detection is built to resist. The archive measures the cost:

```
documents naming FIFTH THIRD anywhere in their text ........... 60   (of the 3,367 with OCR text)
  ... carrying 53.com too (the real family) ...................  5
  ... naming the bank WITHOUT its domain ...................... 55
      ... of which also print 'Account Summary' ...............  9
          8 Bank of America statements (all validated as bank_of_america)
          1 Bluevine statement
```

Those nine are one marker away from a wrong-parser claim, and a wrong parse
that happens to reconcile is precisely what the conformance cross product
exists to prevent. Only five of the seventeen real documents spell the bank's
name out at all, so the name buys nothing even for the family it belongs to.
**The marker set shipped here is strictly tighter than the prototype's**, and
the fixture that isolates it carries both other markers, so the domain is the
only thing withholding the claim (SA6).

**2 — the summary's middle span could not cross a printed line.** The
electronic PDF flattens the whole account summary onto one line; the scan
prints one component per line:

```
03/01 Beginning Balance $502.89 Number of Days in Period 31
9 Checks $(20,634.00)
38 Withdrawals / Debits $(14,452.62)
10 Deposits / Credits $34,797.38
03/31 Ending Balance $213.65
```

`_SUMMARY_RE`'s middle group was `(.*?)` without `DOTALL`, so on a scan it
never matched and `_summary` returned None. It now spans lines, **bounded at
400 characters**. The bound is the point: an unbounded `[\s\S]*?` would let a
beginning balance pair with an ending balance printed further down the
document — a different account's, or a different period's. Measured, the widest
summary the archive prints is 140 characters (13 electronic: 110–140; 4
scanned: 114–133), so 400 is roughly three times the observed need and far
short of the distance to any second summary block.

**Correction, from the adversarial review (SA10.1): the duplicate-label
refusal is NOT what fences a foreign close, and this section said it was.** A
scan can lose the statement's own ending-balance line, and the span then
reaches a later block's close in 188 characters — inside the bound, every
component printed exactly once, no label repeated. `_summary` pairs this
beginning balance with someone else's ending balance and returns it happily.
The fence is **instrument 1**, the walked closing identity: 100 + 150 − 30 − 20
is 200, not 77,777. Instrument 4's terminal check reads the same close a second
way, and measured on that fixture either one alone refuses the document —
deleting BOTH is what lets the foreign pairing publish, with `ending_balance`
77,777.00. Widening this bound therefore does not open a door the
duplicate-label refusal guards; it leans harder on the closing identity, which
is what anyone arguing for a wider bound is really arguing about. Pinned by
`test_a_foreign_ending_balance_is_refused_by_the_closing_identity`.

**3 — OCR speckle welds itself to printed numbers.** Two shapes, one per
document:

* `13. Deposits / Credits $23,960.46` (Feb). The full stop broke `(\d+)\s+`,
  the count read as absent, and an amount with no count beside it is — by this
  parser's deliberate rule — a summary it will not read. The count is now read
  through the speck.
* `1229%i 04/20 400.00` (Apr). A sequence-gap asterisk photographed as a
  percent sign. `(?:\s*\*)?(?:\s*[is])?` did not admit it, the row was dropped,
  and the cheque section then failed its own printed count.

Both tolerances are absorbed **only where a second, independent printing of the
same figure has to agree**, which is what makes them safe rather than
convenient:

* the component count read through the speck is still checked against the count
  the section heading prints on its own line (`Deposits / Credits 13 items
  totaling $23,960.46`) — instrument 2. A misread count refuses the document;
  the tolerance never completes the summary from the heading. Pinned both ways:
  `test_a_full_stop_welded_to_a_component_count_is_absorbed` and
  `test_the_absorbed_count_is_still_read_off_the_summary_not_the_heading`.
* the cheque row admitted through the glyph is still checked against the
  section's printed count, the section's printed total (instrument 3) and the
  printed daily-balance walk (instrument 4). April's own arithmetic is the
  proof that the dropped row was real: without cheque 1229 the walk to
  `04/20 (64.02)` is short by exactly 400.00.

The glyph tolerance is written as a **shape** — up to two glyphs that are
neither digits nor the date's own separator — not as a list of the
substitutions one OCR engine happens to make. Two is the flag cluster the
layout prints (`*i`, `*s`); a longer run is not a flag and is not admitted,
which `test_the_glyph_tolerance_is_a_bounded_shape_not_an_open_gap` pins by
making the section's printed count refuse the document when it is tried.

Four newly reached, and they are exactly the four named in the handoff. No
existing claim was lost (all 13 still claimed) and no registration outside this

**Nothing is left behind, either.** The other direction of the same sweep: 60
documents in the archive contain the words FIFTH THIRD, and every one that is
not in the seventeen is a counterparty mention in someone else's ledger —
16 Shopify Balance statements filed under a folder labelled "Fifth Third Bank"
and claimed by `shopify_balance` (the custodian-disclosure family, exactly as
the parser's own test warns), 10 Bank of America, 7 Chase, 7 Huntington, 5
American Express, 2 Bluevine, and 8 unidentified. Of the ten `failed`
documents that name the bank, four are this cohort; the other six are payroll
cards and statements with a Fifth Third ACH debit or ATM fee in their rows. And
**no document that carries `53.com` is left unclaimed** — the domain marker
partitions this archive perfectly.

**Why the detection sweep plus the family sweep is the whole argument here.**
`git diff --stat ba13ec3..HEAD -- analysis/` reports **one file changed, 63
insertions and 7 deletions**, and all seven deleted lines are inside
`fifth_third.py`'s own four regexes and one marker. No shared module was
touched, so no other parser's code path can have moved, and the only documents
whose payload can differ are the ones `fifth_third` detects. The sweep
enumerates those exhaustively at 17: 13 proven byte-identical below, and 4 that
had no result at all before.

## SA5. The review point — `53906D0E` publishes ADB −53.54

The handoff flagged this for corroboration against the printed daily balances
before shipping. Corroborated, exactly.

March runs overdrawn for most of the month. The document prints fifteen daily
closes and the parser publishes all fifteen. Walking them with each close held
until the next printed date, over the 31 days the summary itself states:

```
03/01   502.89 × 1        03/13  -2,676.28 × 3      03/23      10.09 × 3
03/02    49.45 × 1        03/16    -989.41 × 1      03/26  -7,489.91 × 1
03/03  -557.85 × 1        03/17    -406.89 × 2      03/27   3,855.46 × 3
03/04  -594.85 × 2        03/19     950.77 × 1      03/30    -994.92 × 1
03/06     8.59 × 5        03/20   1,684.40 × 3      03/31     213.65 × 1
03/11    -2.41 × 2                                  ————————————————————
                                                    31 days, sum -1,659.67
                                                    -1,659.67 / 31 = -53.54
```

`daily_balance_sum` in the published payload is `-1659.67` and
`average_daily_balance` is `-53.54`. The figure is the arithmetic of the
bank's own printed closes, to the cent, and the parser had already been
required to reproduce every one of those closes by walking its transactions
(instrument 4) before it would publish anything. `min_balance -7,489.91` and
`max_balance 3,855.46` are both printed on the page too.

A negative average daily balance on an account that opened at 502.89 and closed
at 213.65 looks wrong at a glance, which is exactly why it was flagged. It is
right: the account spent most of March overdrawn, including one day at
−7,489.91, and the printed balances say so.
`test_an_overdrawn_scan_publishes_the_printed_daily_balances_it_averages` pins
the shape.

## SA6. Fixtures, and the mutation pass that rewrote two of them

`tests/test_fifth_third.py` gains a scanned-layout section: a synthetic
photograph of the same statement — no print stream, the summary broken one
component per line, `1002%i` in the cheque grid — and one adversarial twin for
every tolerance introduced. 36 tests in the file, up from 24. Plus the scanned
branch's entry in `ALTERNATE_FIXTURES`, which the conformance suite runs as a
detection-positive for the disjunctive marker.

Then every change was mutated and the suite re-run. **Nine mutants, nine
killed** — but only after two of them survived the first pass and the fixtures
that should have caught them were rewritten:

| mutant | verdict |
|---|---|
| drop the product-line branch of `print_product` | KILLED (7 failures) |
| drop the print-stream branch of `print_product` | KILLED (14 failures) |
| widen `issuer_domain` to the bank's NAME (the prototype's version) | **survived → fixture rewritten → KILLED** |
| summary span back to single-line `(.*?)` | KILLED (5 failures) |
| summary span unbounded `[\s\S]*?` | KILLED |
| drop the component full-stop tolerance | KILLED |
| cheque row back to the literal `(?:\s*\*)?(?:\s*[is])?` list | KILLED (5 failures) |
| cheque glyph run unbounded `*` | **survived → fixture rewritten → KILLED** |
| cheque glyph run widened to `{0,3}` | KILLED |

The two survivors are worth recording because both were tests that *looked*
like they pinned the rule:

* **the glyph bound.** The fixture printed the over-long-gap cheque on `03/06`,
  a day the daily summary does not print — so instrument 4 refused it and the
  bound was never consulted. Rewritten so that every other instrument agrees
  with the row (the summary closes, both printings say three cheques totalling
  $35.00, the walk lands on every printed close): the shape of the gap is now
  the only thing that can refuse it. A twin asserts the same document IS read
  when the gap is a real two-glyph flag cluster, so a quietly widened bound
  cannot look tested either.
* **the issuer marker.** The counter-example fixture carried neither of the
  other two markers, so loosening `issuer_domain` changed nothing about it.
  Rewritten to carry both — and renamed
  `test_the_issuers_domain_is_what_holds_the_widened_marker_set_together`,
  because that is what it now tests — leaving the domain as the single
  withholding piece of evidence.

Neither defect would have shown up in any other proof. Recording it because
the general lesson is the one this wave keeps re-learning: a test that only
demonstrates the rule working cannot fail when someone simplifies it away.

## SA9. Carried findings for Ocean

1. **Three cheque descriptions carry an OCR-degraded number.** On `53906D0E`,
   `Check 11943` and `Check 11971` are the printed `1194 s` and `1197 i` with
   the flag glyph welded onto the number; on `CDB8A6CC`, `Check 12271` is
   `1227 i` and `Check 0000` is a cheque number the scan could not resolve at
   all. **No financial field is affected** — the counts, the per-section totals
   and the daily walk are exact on all four documents, which is how we know
   these are real cheques and not phantoms. It is the *description* that is
   degraded. Widening the flag tolerance to strip a trailing digit would be
   guessing at which digit is the flag, and this cell will not guess. Named
   because a reviewer reading the transaction list will see it.
2. **A scanned `COMM'L 53 ANALYZED` statement would still not be reached.**
   The product-line branch keys on the `5/3` shorthand. The four documents that
   print the other product name are all electronic and are held by the print
   stream. No such scan exists in the archive; if one appears it fails closed,
   which is correct, and the fix is a one-line widening with its own blast
   radius measured.

Ocean's verdict SHIP, with three required closures. All three landed in

The reviewer paired a real beginning balance with a FOREIGN ending balance at
under 200 characters with no duplicate label anywhere in the span, which is the
counter-example to the reasoning this cell recorded. The code was right and the
justification was wrong — a bad combination to leave behind, because the next
person widening the bound would have checked the wrong guard and concluded they
were safe. Reproduced here at **188 characters** on a fixture built from the
scanned document with its own ending-balance line lost, which is exactly what a
scan does to it.

Corrected in both places, naming instrument 1. One honest addition the review
did not ask for: instrument 4's terminal check reads the same close a second

```
instrument 1 deleted             -> REFUSED
instrument 4 terminal deleted    -> REFUSED
BOTH closing-identity checks off -> PUBLISHED ending=77777.0 begin=100.0 txns=5
```

Either reading alone holds; the foreign pairing only escapes when both are
gone. `test_a_foreign_ending_balance_is_refused_by_the_closing_identity` pins
the corrected reasoning in three falsifiable pieces: the pairing IS read (so
the bound is not the fence), every component appears exactly once (so the

bound was never consulted) — and the document is refused anyway. Narrowing

```
uniqueness guard deleted     -> PUBLISHED 5 printed days instead of 4:
```

`by_day` is a `dict`, so the LAST copy wins the walk and the walk still reaches

## FCX1. Characterisation — where the batch-3 reader lost it

FI6 called the description column "flattened by the generic native-text
extractor" and FI11.2 said `ocr/native_text.py` "shreds this layout". Both are
true and neither is the mechanism. The mechanism is one line:

```python
# ocr/native_text.py::_native_pages
text = " ".join(part.strip() for part in str(block[4]).splitlines() if part.strip())
```

MuPDF returns page 2 of the pinned statement as ten blocks. Block 2 is the
whole description column — **74 lines inside one block**: `Date`,
`Description`, `Amount`, and 71 printed descriptions. Blocks 3 and 5 and 7 are
the date column (61 + 3 + 5 lines); blocks 4, 6 and 8 are the amounts. The
generic reader emits each block as ONE line, so the dates and amounts survive
as parallel runs and the descriptions arrive as

```
Date Description Amount POS Sig 02/27 Visa #8269 Cucina 100 864-6019606 SC POS
Sig 02/28 Visa #8269 Companycam Companycam.Co NE Overdraft Charge Coast Payment
9392 Barcotrucks Web Pay Rc*****7-004 ACH Same Day Originated Credit ...
```

— 69 postings welded end to end with nothing between them. That string cannot
be split structurally: there is no separator, no repeated prefix, no length
rule. It is why the previous parser needed ~25 remembered merchant names to cut
it, and why the batch-3 rebuild, which correctly refused to remember them,
could only label the postings by section.

**But nothing was ever missing.** `block[4]` carries the newlines; `" ".join`
throws them away. Read the same page with line boxes and the table is intact:

```
y=  83.8 n=3 [37]03-02 || [79]POS Sig 02/27 Visa #8269 Cucina 100 ... SC || [439]92.61
y=  92.8 n=3 [37]03-02 || [79]POS Sig 02/28 Visa #8269 Companycam ... NE || [439]159.43
y= 101.8 n=3 [37]03-02 || [79]Overdraft Charge                          || [439]36.00
```

Description baselines sit ~1.3pt above the date and amount they belong to and
rows are 9pt apart, so a 3pt band recovers ownership exactly. On the pinned
document that yields 95 rows against the printed counts of 9 other credits and
86 other debits — 9 + 86 = 95, the control record's own figures.

## FCX2. The recovery, and why it is structural

`parse_native_first_citizens` (`ocr/native_text.py`). Every rule is read off
the page; nothing is remembered:

| Rule | Read from |
|---|---|
| where a described table starts | the band whose three cells say `Date`, `Description`, `Amount` |
| which section it is | the band immediately above that ruler (a table the page does not name is **not read** — nothing guesses) |
| where the columns are | that same ruler: the x of `Date`, the x of `Description`, the right edge of `Amount` |
| what a row is | a `MM-DD` in the date column plus money ending at the amount column's right edge |
| what a wrapped line is | a LONE cell in the description column, within one row pitch of the row above |
| where the table ends | the first band that is neither |

Three traps fall out of this rather than being special-cased:

- **`ACH Batch         03-13 Seq #  5041  Track Id# 104869791`.** A description
  containing a date cannot be mistaken for the date cell, because the date is
  identified by its COLUMN, not by its shape.
- **`Total` / `44,862.06`.** The printed total prints a money cell of its own,
  so it is not a lone cell and cannot be swallowed as a continuation. The next
  section's heading prints at the DATE column's x, not the description's, so it
  cannot be either.
- **The deposits, cheque and daily-balance grids are never read at all** — they
  print `Date Amount Date Amount …`, `Check No. Date Amount …` and
  `Date Balance …`, so they are not `Date/Description/Amount` tables and the
  extractor never enters them. That is also why the daily chain, an ADB input,
  is untouchable by this code path.

**Additive by construction.** The pages are `parse_native_pdf_text`'s own list,
so the generic text is preserved byte for byte and the SAME volume gate decides
whether a document has usable native text (a rasterised body still falls
through to OCR, FC-D unchanged). The recovered rows are appended after the last
printed page — past `An updated`, past every `--- Page` marker, past anything a
section-bounded reader can reach. A document from which no row is recovered is
not claimed, and the ladder returns exactly today's bytes.

Wired into all six copies of the native rung order (`ocr/pipeline.py`,
`balance_forensic_audit.py`, `adb_forensic_audit.py`,
`deterministic_coverage_audit.py`, `build_corpus_cache.py`, `adb_debug.py`),
below every other bank-specific extractor and above the generic one.

**The continuation window, fixed after review.** It was seeded from the
header-to-first-row gap, which is a header height and not a row pitch: measured
13.33-13.98pt against a 9.00-9.18pt pitch, so the first row of every table
carried a window of ~1.6 pitches and would swallow a stray printed a whole line
low. Unreachable in this population only because every real table ends with
`Total` + money, which is not a lone cell — an accident, not a rule. The window
now comes from the table's OWN row pitch once two rows have set it
(`pitch + 1.0`), and until then from the row's own printed line box (measured
10.00-12.30pt here: taller than the pitch, short of the header gap). Both are
read off the page. Against the measured extremes it admits every wrapped line
in the family (8.82-8.97pt) and clears the header gap by ~1.0pt either side.
Re-extracted family-wide after the change, pre-fix module and post-fix module
in one process: **2,120 rows, 0 documents whose rows changed**. Fixtured at
`test_a_lone_line_below_the_last_row_is_not_joined`, whose `[13.0-1]`
parametrisation — a stray wider than the pitch but narrower than the header gap,
on a ONE-row table — is red against the old rule.

## FCX3. The overlay is a second reading, not a shortcut

`_described` (`analysis/first_citizens.py`) lays the reported rows over the
postings the parser already read. It publishes a section's printed text **only
when the extractor's rows reproduce that section's parsed dates and amounts
exactly, in order, one for one.** The extractor read the table by geometry; the
parser read it positionally out of the flattened column. Two independent
readings of the same table have to agree before a single description is
published, and any disagreement — a count that differs, a date that resolves
elsewhere, a cent out — returns the whole section to its label.

This is worth naming against FI14.2, which established that
`analysis.reconcile` is NOT an independent test of the detail for this bank
because `_matches` plus the summary's own closure force the walk. The overlay
does not fix that (it moves no money, so it cannot). What it does add is a
genuine second reading of the two described sections, checked cell by cell.

Everything the batch-3 gate does still runs, and runs BEFORE the overlay: the
control record, the summary closure, the four per-section count+total checks,
the daily walk. The overlay changes text and only text.

### The report is cut OUT of the document, not read around it

Found while reviewing the first working version, and fixed at `b71fc07`.

Every reported row repeats the section heading it was printed under. Left in
the text, a report is a second printing of `Other Debits From Your Account`
inside the very string `_section_blocks` splits on and
`_service_charge_posting` scans with `[A-Z][a-z]+ Service Charge\s*$`.

Measured on all 39 documents, that cost nothing: the spurious section blocks
contribute no posting (a `FC_TX|…` line matches neither the date run nor the
amount run), and no recovered description happens to end in
`<Word> Service Charge`. Both are luck. The second one would have dated a
billed service charge off a merchant name — a published fact, silently wrong,
on a document that still reconciles because `_matches` never sees the charge.

`_report` now returns the rows AND the document with the block excised, and
the parse seam rebinds `markdown` to the document immediately after detection
(which still runs on exactly the bytes dispatch scored). A malformed report is
excised too: it is not statement text whether or not it parses. The excision is
EXACT — asserted as string equality against the same fixture built without a
report — so a reader below sees the document it would have seen had the intake
never reported anything.

Re-running the whole family sweep after the change produced a byte-identical
result file, which is the point: the fix removes a hazard, not a symptom.

**Correction — the first trap fixture was a FALSE GUARD.** Adversarial review
found that `test_a_recovered_description_cannot_redate_the_billed_service_charge`
passed at the pre-fix commit and with the excision monkeypatched out. Its trap
row sat AFTER a genuine printed `April Service Charge` itemisation, and
`_service_charge_posting` returns on the first pattern match, so the trap could
never be reached. A test that cannot fail is worse than no test, because it is
counted.

It is replaced by the reviewer's construction, at
`test_a_recovered_description_cannot_invent_the_billed_service_charge`: a
charge the summary BILLS (400.00) and the document itemises NOWHERE, with the
report appended where intake appends it and one row whose printed memo ends

```
E  AssertionError: assert not [Transaction(date='2026-04-22',
E     description='Monthly Service Charge', amount=-400.0, direction='debit')]
```

— a charge the bank never itemised, invented from the report, dated off a
merchant name, on a document whose four section totals still agree because
`_matches` never sees it. Its floor is pinned beside it
(`test_a_billed_charge_with_no_itemisation_is_omitted_not_invented`: the charge
is omitted and `reconcile` correctly does NOT close).

The excision's own guards are the two that were always real and are also red at

(the document after excision equals the same fixture built without a report,
and `_section_blocks` finds one debits block rather than four) and
`test_a_malformed_report_is_still_cut_out`.

### What `_described` does and does not guarantee

Stated precisely, because the gate cannot see the difference. `_described`'s
check is over DATES and AMOUNTS only: it requires the extractor's rows to
reproduce the section's parsed date and amount sequence exactly, in order. It
does not, and cannot, verify that the description attached to a row is the
description the bank printed on that row — a permuted set of descriptions over
the same date/amount sequence would pass it unchanged.

Description attribution rests on two other things instead, both measured:

1. **The second engine.** All 2,118 published descriptions were confirmed
   against `pdfplumber` (FCX5), which resolves layout independently of PyMuPDF.
   That is the attribution proof, and it is a MEASUREMENT, not an invariant.
2. **Geometric headroom.** Row ownership is a 3.0pt band on the y-centre. Over
   the 2,286 multi-cell bands INSIDE a described table across all 39 documents,
   the largest intra-band spread is **0.42pt** (p99 0.42, median 0.18) —
   **2.58pt of headroom**. Reconciling the reviewer's 2.14pt/0.86pt figure:
   that is drawn from the whole-page population, whose true maximum is
   **2.92pt** (0.08pt headroom) — but every band above 2.0pt is page furniture
   (the `FOLLOW THESE EASY STEPS TO BALANCE YOUR CHECKING ACCOUNT` worksheet,
   the address block, the `14,702.87 || +` pair), **0 of them inside any
   described table**, and none can become a row or a continuation. The number
   that governs attribution is the in-table 0.42pt.

**Therefore: any new sub-family joining this population must be re-confirmed
against the second engine.** A green corpus gate is not evidence about
descriptions — the audits contain none — and neither is a passing `_described`.
The confirmation is the pdfplumber sweep and it must be re-run, not assumed.

**Latent permutation blindness, recorded.** Two postings sharing a date AND an
amount inside one section are interchangeable to `_described`, so a reordering
between the two readings would swap their descriptions silently. There is no
reachable reordering today: `_fc_bands` sorts by `(y-centre, x0)` and the
parser reads the flattened runs in printed order, so both readings are in
printed order by construction. It is the sort that is load-bearing here, and it
is named so a future change to it is not mistaken for a refactor.

### Zero movement outside the family, over the whole archive

The extractor can only change a document it CLAIMS, and it claims nothing whose
text carries neither the issuer marker nor the printed control record. So the
blast radius is decidable rather than sampled. Every one of the 3,506 archive
rows had its cached OCR artifact read by direct path (the sqlite index never
opened, no PDF re-read needed — all 3,506 resolved from artifacts) and both
gates applied to exactly the text the run of record analysed:

```
archive rows swept               : 3506
documents the extractor can gate :   39
  inside the named family        :   38
  OUTSIDE the named family       :    1
```

The one outside is `Unidentified/fdfad302_3-31-2026 DFSBS.pdf`, and it is the
pinned statement: `dedup_status: pinned_corpus_duplicate`, `duplicate_of:
Others/First Citizen/First Citizens Bank.pdf`, content_sha256
`57058C69…A5CFAE` — the same bytes, already measured, reaching the same answer.
Its `parser_id` is blank in the run of record because it is a dedup skip, which
is why the family list built from parser mentions did not contain it.

38 archive documents + the pinned file = 39 distinct shas, which is FI4's 39.
No document outside them can be reached by any line of this branch.

### The forensic oracles' own daily chain, read off both texts

FI6 named one specific risk for a layout extractor in this module: it "moves
pinned ADB evidence", `raw_daily_balance_snapshots` and `daily_balance_sum`.
That is a claim about the ORACLES, not about `analysis.metrics`, so it is
answered where it was made — `adb_forensic_audit.raw_daily_balances` and
`balance_forensic_audit.raw_daily_balances`, called directly on the base
markdown and the new markdown for every document in the family:

```
documents                        : 39
adb oracle daily-chain movers    :  0
balance oracle daily-chain movers:  0
```

Structurally, not just observably: `first_citizens_daily` bounds its body
between `^Daily Balance Summary$` and `^An updated`, the report is appended
after the LAST printed page, and `An updated` (where the bank prints it at all)
is on the Daily Balance page. There is no arrangement of these two markers that
puts the report inside that body.

## FCX5. The descriptions are confirmed by a second PDF engine

The extractor reads line boxes with PyMuPDF. `pdfplumber` is a different
engine with a different layout model, and FI6 recorded that it reads these rows
one posting per line. Every published description was matched to the pdfplumber
line carrying the same date and amount:

```
descriptions checked   2118
confirmed              2118   (100.0%)
conflicting               0
```

2,094 are character-for-character identical after whitespace normalisation. The
other 24 are the wrapped rows: pdfplumber emits the first printed line only, and
our reading is that line plus the continuation it drops — a strict superset,
never a different answer. Counted independently on the extractor side: **2,120
rows recovered, 24 carrying exactly one wrapped continuation line**, the same
24. Both engines agree on which rows exist; they differ only in that one of
them gives up at the line break.

(2,120 rows recovered vs 2,118 descriptions published: the two spare rows are
on `3df19105_May2026_1301.pdf`, which the parser DECLINES. It publishes
nothing, before and after — a document you cannot prove publishes nothing, and
recovering text from it changes that not at all.)

Description coverage over the family's 2,606 postings:

```
                                  before          after
  section label (flattened)   2109  80.9%       0   0.0%
  full printed text              9   0.3%    2118  81.3%
  deposits grid (no column)    208   8.0%     208   8.0%
  cheque serial recovered      271  10.4%     271  10.4%
  monthly service charge         9   0.3%       9   0.3%
```

The 208 and the 271 are not a shortfall. The deposits grid prints `Date` and
`Amount` and no description column at all, and a cheque's printed identity IS
its serial. There is nothing left on the page that this does not read.

### The affordability red, A/B'd rather than asserted away

the 109 pinned sources, against a 250 ms constant. This branch adds NO

```
first_citizens DETECTION_MARKERS, AST compared base 707ba9e vs branch: IDENTICAL
detect = make_detector(DETECTION_MARKERS)                            : IDENTICAL
```

so base and branch are the same computation, and the paired measurement then
confirms it. First, arms built from the base marker set and the branch marker

```
  trial 2:  BRANCH 274.6   BASE 243.2      BASE    median 244.5

  trial 6:  BRANCH 263.6   BASE 244.5
  trial 7:  BRANCH 296.7   BASE 256.1
```

Then with the arm ORDER alternated, which is what the +16 ms median above
actually was — both arms running the identical registry:

```
overall min 250.9   median 279.9   max 298.6   threshold 250.0
```

Pre-existing at 68 registrations under load, reproducible with the base marker

## FCX7. Carried for Ocean

1. **`OCR_STAGE_VERSION` MUST be bumped at merge, and this is a blocker for the
   measurement, not a nicety.** The OCR artifact cache is keyed on
   `(content_sha256, ocr_settings_key)` and `OCR_STAGE_VERSION` is inside that
   fingerprint (`webapp/artifact_cache.py:336`). This branch changes what the
   OCR stage produces for 35 documents WITHOUT changing the key, so a cached
   run serves the pre-change markdown and the parser correctly falls back to
   labels. In the run of record all 34 archive rows are `cache_ocr: hit`, so
   the next archive run would show **zero movement** for this family unless the
   OCR stage version moves. `webapp/artifact_cache.py` is WIRING-1's file this
   batch (its Card B owns the key-material hunk), so this cell did not touch
   it.
   **Correction (adversarial review): something else in the wave DOES bump it.**
   `wave4-geom` moves `OCR_STAGE_VERSION` 2 -> 3 and updates its pin at
   `tests/test_artifact_cache.py:723` (`assert OCR_STAGE_VERSION == 2`, present
   in this tree). So the merge composition is explicit: Ocean resolves this to
   ONE 2 -> 3 at the train and that single bump covers this cell too. A solo
   merge of either branch that bumps the constant without touching that pin
   reds the suite. WIRING-1's Card B does not help here — it invalidates the
   ANALYSIS cache, a different key.
   Cost of the bump: the digital rung re-extracts natively for free; the
   scanned documents re-run the offline rungs. It is wall clock, not vendor
   spend. Everything proven above is proven by running the ladder directly on
   the PDFs — the path `corpus_gate.py` and both forensic audits already take —
   so the change itself is proven independently of the cache.
2. **`stated_daily_balances` is still deliberately empty** (FI2, FI11.5) and
   this cell did not touch it. Unchanged: it would move `backend_adb` on a
   pinned document and needs the ceremony.
3. **FI14.5's two carried cards are unaffected and still open.** D2 (the
   service-charge date contradicting the printed daily chain on 4 of 9) and D5
   (the dropped ending-balance sign line) live in the summary and daily-balance
   readers, neither of which this cell goes near.
4. **FI14.3's MAPPING recommendation is unchanged.** The overlay adds and
   removes no posting, so the 26 exact / 9 off-by-one split against the printed
   per-direction counts is exactly as measured. COUNTS-P3 material still.
5. **`count_semantics` untouched**, counts still inert (`UNSURVEYED`,
   `comparable=False`).
6. **The four dormant declines still publish nothing** and are unchanged.
   `3df19105_May2026_1301.pdf` now has 2 recoverable rows and is still refused,
   which is the right answer: the recovery is text, and text is not evidence of
   a balance.
7. **The affordability assertion is red on BASE too**, measured, at 68
   registrations under load — 16 of 16 trials over the 250 ms constant with the
   base marker set. Named here for the record only; DETECT-BUDGET owns it and
   this cell neither touched the test nor raised the constant.
8. **THE SEAM CARD — the excision lives in one parser, not the intake seam.**
   `_report` cuts the block out inside `analysis/first_citizens.py`, so the
   property "the intake's report is never read as printing" holds for this
   parser and for no other. That is a property of today's population (this is
   the only reader of an `FC_*` block), not of the design. The moment a second
   parser consumes an intake report — or this family's documents reach a
   generic reader — the excision has to move to the admissibility seam beside
   `admissible_text`, where it would be total instead of promised. Note the
   precedent already in the tree: `+navy-federal` wraps its rows in an HTML
   comment and `+wells` does not, so there is no shared convention to inherit
   yet. Card it before the third producer, not after.
9. **`_described` is a date/amount check, not a description check** (FCX3).
   Description attribution is proven by the pdfplumber sweep, which must be
   re-run for any new sub-family; a green gate says nothing about it.

# GEOM-1 — geometry, evidence-ranked (batch 4, card 7)

Branch `wave4-geom`, base `ea8d8e8`. Run of record
`discovery_reports/2026-08-14T214345.671986-0000-d5c75ff6`.

Gustavo's ruling is the whole shape of this cell: **geometry only where word
boxes restore information the flattened text PROVABLY destroyed**, and every
geometry-read value through the existing gates unchanged. So the deliverable is
two things — one family closed, and a ranking of the rest with the proof
attached to each rather than the impression.

## GEOM1.1 What already existed, characterized before anything was built

| Fact | Anchor |
|---|---|
| A word-geometry producer exists and works | `analysis/structurer/geometry.py:135` |
| Nothing in production computes it | its only caller is `tools/measure_structurer.py` |
| Per-bank geometry readers are precedented in the intake layer | `ocr/native_text.py::_navy_transaction_rows`, `::_wells_rows` |
| `ocr/` does not import `analysis/` | verified; `geometry.py`'s own docstring calls the separation deliberate |
| A full design for the wiring already exists | `DESIGN_GEOMETRY_INTEGRATION.md` (PLATFORM-PROPOSALS, DESIGN status, no code) |

That design's §3.3 recommends the per-bank `ocr/` route for the class where
rows are intact and column identity was discarded, and defers the
`analysis/`-side wiring (`document_geometry` through the pipeline, the
registry, and `analysis_settings_key`) to its own card. This cell took the
first and did not touch the second: no protected-module change, no new
registration, detect-sweep budget untouched at 68.

**`_wells_rows` is the anti-pattern the new module is built against.** It reads
its bands from the literals `395`, `452`, `520` and bins rows at
`round(y0 / 3.0) * 3.0`. W3 §W7.2 already named that as the defect rather than
the fix: "geometry read as constants rather than as the page's own column
positions". `ocr/column_grid.py` derives every band from the header's own word
boxes, and `test_the_same_layout_at_another_scale_reads_identically` pins the
property that constants cannot have.

## GEOM1.3 The proof that flattening destroyed printed information

`analysis/woodforest.py`'s own docstring is the first witness: "Credits and
debits stand in two ADJACENT columns and the text layer destroys the column of
origin". The parser has been recovering direction from the running balance
instead, which works only while every balance reads.

Measured on `Royalty2`, page 1. What the flattened `_native_pages` emits:

```
POS CR CASH APP*RICHARD SMITH Oakland CA 000000000309404
120,237.77
03-04
1,000.00
```

— description, balance, date, amount; and the order is not even stable, later
rows arriving balance-first. What the word boxes carry on the same page:

```
y=341.2 | Date@47 Credits@112 Debits@185 Balance@253 Description@292
y=356.6 | 03-04@47 1,000.00@109 120,237.77@245 POS CR CASH APP*RICHARD SMITH ...
y=421.1 | 03-05@47 198.32@186 125,479.95@245 POS DB SAM'S CLUB #529 HOUSTON TX ...
```

The printed header is byte-identical on all seven documents sampled across the
family (`date[47-66] credits[112-140] debits[185-211] balance[253-284]
description[292-337]`) and money cells right-align to it: credits at right
edge 138-141, debits 207-211, balance 281-284, against column gaps of 71 and
73 points. Nothing here is close to ambiguous.

On `Royalty3` and `Royalty4` flattening destroys a second thing — the summary
row. The bank prints
`Second Chance Checking 1358422002 165,309.24 12,757.47 41,175.75 193,663.14`
as one line; the text layer emits the CLOSING BALANCE on a line of its own, so
`_SUMMARY_ROW_RE` matches nothing, `_accounts` returns zero, and the parser
declines a document whose oracle is printed perfectly well.

## GEOM1.4 Two measurement defects found while building, both in the tolerances

Recorded because both produced plausible-looking wrong answers rather than
errors, which is the failure mode this class is prone to.

1. **A page-median line tolerance read every balance one row late.** The
   balance cell sits ~0.8pt ABOVE its row's date on the same printed row. With
   the tolerance taken from the whole page's median type height — dragged down
   by the small print in the footer — that 0.8 exceeded it and each balance
   fell to the row above. Totals still looked plausible. Fixed by deriving the
   tolerance from the GRID's own type size and row pitch.
2. **Sorting a row's words by x interleaved wrapped descriptions.** A
   continuation line's words merged into the line above by x position
   (`ATM 000000000565054 WDL 2406 ...`). Fixed by reading line by line, then
   left to right.

A third, subtler one: bounding the last row at exactly one pitch dropped a
reference number printed exactly one pitch below (`000000000565054`). The row's
floor is now reached by chaining at the grid's own line spacing, so a
continuation survives and a block printed further down does not.

overstated the result and misdiagnosed one document; both corrections are kept

| document | before | after |
|---|---|---|
