**Net: +2 validated, 0 regressions.**

Both recovered documents reproduce the bank's own printed evidence
independently — nothing was padded to get there:

```
Royalty2  credits 49,025.50 (delta +0.00)  debits  2,954.03 (delta +0.00)
          chain breaks 0   119,237.77 - 2,954.03 + 49,025.50 = 165,309.24 = printed closing
Royalty4  credits 49,275.25 (delta +0.00)  debits 10,935.96 (delta +0.00)
          chain breaks 0   193,663.14 - 10,935.96 + 49,275.25 = 232,002.43 = printed closing
```

**`Royalty3` publishes nothing, and the rung now declines to read it at all.**
One of its printed debit cells is emitted as TWO word boxes — `1,` at
x[179.3, 185.7] and `682.89` — so the grid does not present a whole cell
there. The reader refuses the block on that evidence and the document falls
back to the text reader, which declines it exactly as before. Its outcome is
unchanged by this branch.

Measured separately, so the document's own state is on the record: reading
that cell whole, the debit cells sum to **12,821.85** against a stated TOTAL
DEBITS of **12,757.47** — a genuine defect of **64.38**, the same 64.38 by
which its printed summary identity fails to close (165,309.24 − 12,757.47 +
41,175.75 = 193,727.52 against a printed closing of 193,663.14). The document
is internally inconsistent and would withhold on that even if the split cell
were joined. Joining it is deliberately NOT implemented: this module's
contract is that it never repairs a row, and stitching two boxes into a number
the page did not print as one is a repair.

On the 17 documents that already read and still read the same: every scalar
field identical (bank, account number and name, period, both balances, both
stated totals, days, average), and every amount, direction and running balance
identical. **9 are byte-identical. 8 differ in exactly one transaction each**,
always the last, and always because the new read stops at the grid's printed
end instead of absorbing a trailing `Checks Cleared` or overdraft-fee table
into that row's description. Those eight descriptions are strictly cleaner; no
financial field moves.

### GEOM1.5a Two claims this section made that were wrong

Kept because the way they were wrong is the point.

1. **"the reader reads all 24 of 24" was false.** It read 24 rows and silently
   truncated one of them: `1,` was skipped as a non-matching token and
   `682.89` was booked as the whole cell, losing exactly 1,000.00. The ledger
   still had 24 rows, still had a balance on every one, and still looked like
   a ledger — which is why the row count read as completeness. A count of rows
   is not a count of cells.
2. **The 935.62 diagnosis was the sum of the reader's error and the
   document's.** 935.62 = 1,000.00 lost by the reader − 64.38 the document
   genuinely over-prints. Attributing all of it to "rows missing from the text
   objects" put this cell's own defect on the bank's side of the ledger. The
   document's real defect is 64.38 and it over-prints debits rather than
   under-printing them.

The reader-side cause is fixed (`cell_split_across_word_boxes`, GEOM1.7). The
lesson recorded: an instrument that agrees with the printed totals on two
documents can still be silently lossy on a third, and "totals match" is
evidence about the documents where they match and about nothing else.

## GEOM1.6 Why the printed column is better evidence, not just different

Worth stating because it is the argument for the whole class. Today direction
is derived from the movement between two printed balances, so the balance chain
is not an independent check of that ledger — it is its source. Read by column,
direction is what the bank printed and the chain becomes a second, separate
statement that either agrees or does not. On `Royalty2` and `Royalty4` it
agrees on every row.

It also closes, for this family, the row class J9.9 named on another template:
a $0.00 posting moves no balance, so a sign rule can only guess at it. Where
the bank printed a column there is nothing to guess, and the test is pinned.

## GEOM1.7 Fail-closed, and the refusal classes fixtured

The block is emitted only when EVERY posting placed unambiguously. One cell
that lands in no printed column, or a row printed in both money columns or in
neither, withdraws the whole block and the document reads exactly as it did
before — which for a defective page means failing closed on the existing
terms. A ledger half read by column and half by text order would be a reading
no instrument could check.

Fixtured refusals: a cell whose right edge matches no printed column; two
cells in one column; a page printing no header; a row the page never anchored;
a row in both money columns; a row with a balance and no amount; a whole
document withdrawn for one unplaceable cell.

Three more were added after adversarial review, and the first is the one that
mattered:

* **`cell_split_across_word_boxes`** — a money-SHAPED token standing inside a
  money column that is not a whole cell. The module's contract said it never
  drops anything silently and it had exactly one code path that did: a token
  failing the money pattern was skipped, so a printed `1,682.89` emitted as
  two boxes published as `682.89`. A right-edge test cannot see the fragment
  (it sits well left of the edge), so membership is now the column's REGION,
  bounded by whatever column the header prints before it. Live on `Royalty3`.
* **`columns_not_separated`** — two printed columns closer together than the
  distance a cell is allowed to miss its edge by. No per-cell rule can recover
  from that, so the grid is refused whole rather than read with a tie-break
  standing in for evidence.
* **`cell_admitted_by_two_columns`** — assignment was an ordered scan that
  booked a cell against whichever column was DECLARED first; on overlapping
  spans the reviewer got a Debits cell published as a CREDIT with zero
  refusals. Assignment is now by nearest edge, and a cell two columns both
  admit is refused.

Both of the last two are latent on Woodforest, whose columns are 45–71pt apart
against a ~7pt tolerance. They are not latent for GEOM1.10: that ranking aims
this module at six more families, and the Desjardins entry there already needs
the alignment work that makes overlap possible.

A fourth, at the parser rather than the grid: **a printed money cell whose
SIGN contradicts the column it stands in** is refused. This layout sets a
trailing minus on overdrawn figures, so a Credits cell can arrive saying both
"this increased the balance" and "this did not"; publishing it produced
`direction="credit"` with a negative amount, which breaks the platform's own
direction rule, and `abs`-ing it would pick a winner silently. J9.6 refuses
the same contradiction at the summary level for the same reason.

## GEOM1.8 Cost stated: `OCR_STAGE_VERSION` 2 -> 3 is global

The block is the only place the printed column survives, so a v2 cache entry
would keep serving the pre-fix markdown and the change would be invisible on a
warm cache rather than visibly wrong. The bump is one integer for the whole
ladder: it invalidates every cached OCR artifact in the archive and the next
full discovery run pays the wall clock again. Vendor cost stays $0.00 — the
native rung makes no model calls. `DESIGN_GEOMETRY_INTEGRATION.md` §5.1 raised
this as an open question for Ocean; this branch is the first to pay it.

**Correction after review: the corpus gate does NOT demonstrate that the
invalidation is safe.** The gate reads no artifact cache — it resolves the
pinned 109 from cold on every run, before and after this change alike — so its
874.4s runtime and its GREEN are evidence that the 109 still reproduce, and
say nothing whatever about cache invalidation. The first version of this
section claimed otherwise. What actually stands behind the bump is
`test_the_ocr_stage_version_bump_invalidates_pre_o3_entries`, which exercises
the version key directly, plus the module's own doctrine at
`artifact_cache.py:92-93`.

**Per-document extraction cost, stated rather than waved at.** This rung sits
in the ladder every native-text document passes through, and both it and the
`parse_native_pdf_text` rung below it start by calling `_native_pages`. Adding
a rung therefore added a whole second block-extraction to every native-text
document in the archive — ~3,300 of them, on every discovery run, for the sake
of 20. `_native_pages` is now memoised on the document's own bytes
(`lru_cache(maxsize=4)`, returning a tuple that each caller copies, because
two extractors in this file append their block to `pages[0]` and handing out
the cached object would let one caller's edit become the next caller's input).
The ladder works one document at a time, so four entries is enough, and the
extraction is paid once per document rather than once per rung.

**Composition note for Ocean at the train.** WOODFOREST-INIT owns
`c183e584_Feb.pdf` and `823DCE7FFCC9 fad3db75_document.PDF`, and both now
carry a geometry block, so their postings arrive through `_geometry_postings`
rather than `_postings`. Their outcome is unchanged on this branch (both still
withheld, by name, in GEOM1.5) — but the initialization-event mechanism that
cell is building has to compose with the geometry path, not only the
text-order one. Whichever lands second should re-measure those two documents
against both readers.

**Composition note for Ocean:** if another batch-4 cell also bumps
`OCR_STAGE_VERSION`, resolve to a single 2 -> 3 rather than 2 -> 4. The
integer's meaning is "the ladder's output changed since v2", not a count of
the cells that changed it.

## GEOM1.9 Proofs

Re-run in full after adversarial review, at `53ba736`. The one later commit is
a comment in `column_grid.py` and this section.

```

    3803 passed, 18 deselected, 1 warning in 352.15s          exit 0
    (3,769 at base + 34 new: 18 column-grid, 16 woodforest)

python -m pytest -m corpus -q
    14 passed, 3807 deselected, 1 warning in 1830.02s         exit 0

python -m pytest tests/test_no_statement_hardcodes.py tests/test_r1_hardcodes.py \
                 tests/test_parser_conformance.py -q
    730 passed in 3.97s                                       exit 0

python corpus_gate.py
    106 PASS / 3 WITHHELD   RESULT: GREEN   Runtime 514.7s    exit 0
```

The corpus-marked slice is GREEN this run, including
`test_detect_sweep_stays_affordable_for_the_discovery_run`, which had failed on
the pre-review run. That is the same test behaving both ways on the same
branch, which is the clearest available statement of what it measures.

### What the gate does and does not prove here

An earlier draft of this section claimed the gate demonstrated that the
`OCR_STAGE_VERSION` bump invalidates safely. **It does not, and the claim is
withdrawn.** `corpus_gate.py` reads no artifact cache — it resolves the pinned
109 from cold on every run, before and after this change alike. Its GREEN is
evidence that all 109 still reproduce every audited balance and ADB field, and
evidence of nothing whatever about cache invalidation. (The runtimes bear that
out: 874.4s on the first run and 514.7s here, on the same code, because the
number tracks machine load rather than anything about a cache.)

What actually stands behind the bump is
`test_the_ocr_stage_version_bump_invalidates_pre_o3_entries`, which exercises
the version key directly, plus the module's own doctrine at
`artifact_cache.py:92-93`.

### The one red on the pre-review run, A/B'd against base

`test_detect_sweep_stays_affordable_for_the_discovery_run` is a wall-clock
budget (`worst < 0.25s` for a full-registry detect sweep over one document).

| tree | measured | result |
|---|---|---|
| base `707ba9e` | **304.7 ms** | fail |
| branch `bc478ec` | **311.6 ms** | fail |
| branch `53ba736`, this run | under budget | **pass** |

6.9 ms apart between base and branch, and `len(pr.registrations())` is **68 on
both**. Pre-existing and load-dependent, matching Ocean's batch-wide notice; a
dedicated DETECT-BUDGET cell owns the structural fix and **the constant was not
raised**. The base measurement was taken from a `git archive` of `707ba9e` into
the scratchpad — no worktree added, no git metadata touched.

Independently of the timing, this branch cannot move that number: it adds no
registration, changes nothing in the detect path, and changes the markdown of
no pinned document — the test's input is the 109 corpus sources, and no
woodforest document is pinned.

### Non-interference over the whole archive, re-run after the review fixes

The new rung sits above `parse_native_desjardins` and `parse_native_pdf_text`,
so every native-text document in the archive passes through it. Swept over all
**3,615** archive PDFs by direct file path:

  ...all 19 woodforest

woodforest-marker documents the rung REFUSED                  1
  Unidentified/e96144ab_Royalty3.pdf

The claim set moved 20 -> 19 against the pre-review sweep, and the one document
that left is `Royalty3`: the refuse-not-drop change withdrew the block it

The sweep also runs 1,027s -> 210s, which is the `_native_pages` memoisation
(D4) measured rather than asserted: the ladder was extracting the same page

**4 documents raise `FzErrorFormat` out of `_native_pages`**
(`Unidentified/c3f27791_3 BUSINESS CHECKING X3774-*.PDF`). Confirmed identical
on base `707ba9e` — `_native_pages` guards `fitz.open` but not the
`page.get_text("blocks")` loop — so it is pre-existing and not this branch's.
Recorded as a finding rather than fixed: it is outside this cell's named
populations, the discovery runner catches it (all four appear as
`no_parser_matched`, not `ocr_failed`), and an unguarded crash class in the
intake ladder is worth a card of its own.

### The seams the design named, checked rather than assumed

`DESIGN_GEOMETRY_INTEGRATION.md` §3.2 property 1 — geometry must never reach
detection — holds structurally rather than by discipline: the block is appended
to the markdown AFTER the flattened text, detection reads markers that were
already present, and the claim set over 3,615 documents is the measured 19
above.

`admissible_text` strips only `<!-- SOURCE: ... -->`, so the block survives to
the parser (the `NFCU_NATIVE_TRANSACTIONS` precedent relies on the same thing)
AND sits inside the text `cached_analysis` hashes. The analysis cache therefore
partitions on it with no key change — which is why §4.3's mandatory cache-key
work was not needed on this branch. It remains needed for the `analysis/`-side
wiring card, where geometry would arrive as a parameter rather than inside the
markdown.

## GEOM1.10 The ranking, with the proof attached to each

Ranked by the card's own criteria: (a) proof that flattening destroyed printed
information, (b) volume, (c) reader risk. Every row below was measured at
`d5c75ff6` with `ocr/column_grid.find_columns`, not inferred from the earlier
logs — where a measurement contradicts a prior entry, it is said so.

**A structural note that applies to items 3-7.** The pinned 109 contains 5 PNC,
4 Wells Fargo, 4 RBC and 9 TD documents (`docs/adb-audit-results.csv`). No
woodforest document is pinned, which is why this cell's change could be proven
by the gate alone. **Every remaining item touches pinned corpus documents**, so
each needs the corpus-marked slice AND, if any pinned document moves,
Gustavo's ceremony. `DESIGN_GEOMETRY_INTEGRATION.md` §6.3 said this; the
composition above is the current confirmation of it.

### Rank 1 — DONE. Woodforest Royalty, 3 documents. +2 validated.

Recorded in GEOM1.2-GEOM1.8.

### Rank 2 — Desjardins inside a Java envelope, 16 documents. BLOCKED.

The fifth evidence item, from SCAN-SCOUT, and on proof quality it is the
strongest in the queue. Measured on the scout's 16 unwrapped payloads
(read-only, in its scratchpad; nothing written back to the archive):

* **Flattening does not merely lose the column, it detaches every amount from
  every row.** The whole page's money arrives as one run of tokens:
  `347.67 2.75 344.92 1.50 343.42 303.00 40.42 1.50 38.92 25.00 13.92 …`,
  with the descriptions in a separate blob. There is no rule over that text
  that recovers a ledger.
* **The word boxes are a clean four-money-column grid.** The printed header is
  `Date Code Description Frais Retrait Dépôt Solde`, found on nearly every page
  of all 16 documents, and at byte-identical positions across all of them
  (`frais[338-357] retrait[388-413] dépôt[461-484] solde[533-555]`) — one
  layout, not sixteen.
* **The cells cluster into three tight disjoint bands** on every document:
  right edges 434-437 (Retrait), 506 (Dépôt), 570-581 (Solde), with counts
  that add up as a ledger should (110 + 31 against 145 balances on the first).

Reader risk today: **zero**. These publish nothing — they are `invalid_pdf`.
And measured here: even once unwrapped they stay at zero, because all 16 fall
through `parse_native_desjardins` (its markers do not match) to
`native-pdf-text` and then to `no_parser_matched`. **So the intake unwrap card
recovers nothing by itself; it needs this reader, and this reader needs it.**
They should be scheduled as a pair or not at all.

**One primitive extension is required, and it is the same one items 6 and 7
need.** `read_rows` snaps a cell to the header LABEL's right edge, which is
correct for Woodforest and Wells (label and cells both right-aligned) and
wrong here: Desjardins left-aligns the label over a right-aligned number
column, so the cells' right edge sits ~20pt beyond the label's. The fix is to
infer each column's alignment edge by clustering the cells that fall within
the header's x-span, rather than assuming the label's own edge. Bounded, and
it generalises the module to every layout in the queue.

### Rank 3 — TD Canada T-F4, 6 withheld (+3 td_canada_french to measure).

§T6.1 measured geometry closing **all 24** underdetermined groups. Confirmed
independently here: `CHEQUE/DEBIT` at x[212,284] and `DEPOSIT/CREDIT` at
x[309,389] are printed on every page — exactly the bands §T6.1 named, still
there at `d5c75ff6`. `find_columns` misses them today only because the labels
are compound (`CHEQUE/DEBIT` is one word to PyMuPDF), which is an entry in a
label list, not an architecture change.

Best oracle set in the queue: the bank's own per-page `Credits <count> <total>`
and `Debits <count> <total>` blocks AND the running BALANCE — a count and a
total and a chain, three independent statements. §T6.1's ruling that the
balance solver should stay either way holds: it becomes the check rather than
the source, exactly as it did for Woodforest here.

Shape is identical to what this cell just built (a `parse_native_td_canada`
that appends a block). The 3 `td_canada_french` withhelds are worth measuring
first — if they share the layout the population is 9.

### Rank 4 — Wells Fargo W-F7, 5 withheld. Highest leverage, highest risk.

This is the only item that **deletes constants** rather than adding a reader.
`_wells_rows` reads bands from `395`, `452`, `520` and bins rows at
`round(y0 / 3.0) * 3.0`; §W7.2 already named that as the defect. Measured
here: the printed `credits/debits/balance` header IS found on all 5 documents,
and the money cells land on it — 37, 37, 39, 38, 39 on-column against 0, 0, 0,
2, 4 off. The layout is readable; the reader is what is wrong.

`test_the_same_layout_at_another_scale_reads_identically` already pins the
property the fix would deliver.

**Risk is real and larger than the others:** `wells_fargo` claims 219 archive
documents and 4 are pinned. The 18-document side-by-side discipline used here
would have to be run over all 219 before it could be believed.

### Rank 5 — community_section J-B, 2 documents. Needs its identities first.

J9.3's evidence is specific and good: the ledger prints `Debits Credits
Balance` and fills the balance column on no row, so direction survives only as
column position. It would also close J9.9 (the $0.00 row signed by convention)
for that template, exactly as this cell closed it for Woodforest.

**But the pair could not be located.** None of the 7 withheld or 2 review
`community_section` documents at `d5c75ff6` prints a `Debits Credits Balance`
header on one baseline. Either the pair moved in batch 3, or the header is
printed in a form the probe does not match. **This card cannot be costed until
the JHA cell names the two content_sha256 values.** Recorded as an open
question rather than an estimate.

### Rank 6 — PNC P-F5, 3 of 4 withheld.

`Additions Deductions Balance` header found on 3 of the 4, but only 4 cells
land on it — the same alignment-inference gap as Desjardins, so item 2's
extension is a prerequisite. §3.4's separate finding still stands on top of
that: the Date column is emitted as its own block (`04 04 04` on one line,
`/08 /10 /10` on the next), so rows need rebuilding, not just labelling. 5 PNC
documents are pinned.

### Rank 7 — RBC F11, 6 withheld. Lowest expected yield; do not promise 6.

Two measurements, both discouraging. The ledger header IS printed
(`Debits Deposits Credits Balance`) but **zero** money cells align to it on any
of the 6, and the header's own x position MOVES between pages of one document
(x=357 on page 1, x=331 on page 2) — so bands must be re-derived per page,
which the module already does but which removes the cross-page consistency
every other family here provides.

More decisively, §5.7 measured one document's 129 stated rows yielding at most
118 recoverable cells. A cell absent from the text objects has no box either —
which is precisely what `Royalty3` demonstrated in this cell, and it is why
that document is still withheld. **The target should be agreed as "close as
many as the text objects permit and prove the rest unrecoverable"** before any

### Rank 8 — fiserv F2, 4 review. Geometry is not what is holding these.

Named in the card, and the measurement does not support it. Two of the four
(`B1F649CC9396`, `83E4ACAE0CF1`) are geometrically pristine — `debit@387
credit@466 balance@544` printed, 81 and 80 of 82 rows carrying exactly two

### Carded but not schedulable this wave — the registration budget

Both are strong geometry customers and neither can be built while the
detect-sweep budget is held at 68 registrations, because each needs a new one:

* **American Savings Bank D2, 10 documents** (§C6.5) — the largest carded
  geometry population. The printed column ORDER differs between page 1 and

  money-cells-per-row runs 1/2/3/4/6/13. Per-page bands are exactly what the

* **First Carolina G5, 2 documents** (§G5) — small, but the argument is the
  sharpest statement of why this whole class matters: without the printed
  column, direction would have to be derived FROM the reconciliation, and the

### What this cell did not touch

`DESIGN_GEOMETRY_INTEGRATION.md` §4.4's disclosed defect is still open:

# §WFINIT — the two Woodforest account openings: what the documents print, and the one line of protected code that stands between them and publication

## WF0. Summary

The two withheld Woodforest statements (§UNID-A UA4.1, carried finding UA6.1)
are mid-cycle **account openings**. Both are fully readable — every figure the
bank prints matches the published ledger exactly — and both are withheld
because their single funding deposit is dated the day BEFORE the period the
bank prints, which `analysis/adb.py` refuses.

The narrow ruling's six evidence gates **can all be met generically**, from
each document's own print, with no per-document constant and no generic
out-of-period tolerance. What cannot be done inside this cell's ownership is
CONSUME that evidence: every admissible design requires `analysis/adb.py`,
which is protected (MASTER_PLAN §4). Per the handoff this cell therefore
**stopped after characterization**. Shipped: the evidence prover
(`analysis.woodforest.initialization_postings`, deliberately unwired), eighteen
fixtures, and the exact patch Ocean would apply, with its effect measured end
to end.

**This packet is the SECOND version.** Ocean's adversarial review blocked the
first as "code safe, evidence not accurate enough to rule on", and it was
right on every count. What changed, all of it verified here before being
acted on:

* **A real defect, not just a wording problem.** Nothing required the folded
  amount to be positive, so a `−50.00 NSF CHARGE` dated the day before a
  zero-forward statement passed both layers and published a NEGATIVE opening
  balance as an "account opening". Reproduced, then fixed in the prover (G3)
  and independently in the pinned diff, and fixtured at both. **WF4.1.**
* **The oracle meant something weaker than claimed.** The n+1 zero residual is
  Woodforest's divisor convention on zero-forward statements, not a signature
  of an opening: `E0A4A5DB` satisfies the complete identity with a phantom
  0.00 day and has no out-of-period row at all. The baseline was 12 of 15, not
  13, with two ongoing statements at exactly 0.00 over their own periods.
  **WF1.6.**
* **The fixtures were weaker than claimed.** "Thirteen fixtures killing one
  condition at a time" was false: mutation testing killed 3 of 14 guards.
  Rebuilt to 5 of 16 pinned with every survivor explained. **WF5.1.**
* **Two diff corrections and a merge-order hazard.** The boundary is now
  enforced at the consuming layer, and the hunks are NOT standalone-inert.
  **WF4.**
* **Two numbers that did not reproduce.** The census intermediates and the
  538375B8 gate count. **WF5.**

**Nothing moves on this branch. Both documents stay withheld.** All 20 claimed
Woodforest documents are byte-identical to the base: the base parser was loaded
out of git as a second module and its `parse_woodforest_statement` compared
field for field against this branch's over every claimed archive document —
**20 claimed, 20 identical, 0 differing** (base `707ba9e`, whose `analysis/`
and `tests/` are unchanged from `ea8d8e8`).

| | |
|---|---|
| Documents | `823DCE7F…` (`fad3db75_document.PDF`), `D9EF1A8C…` (`c183e584_Feb.pdf`) |
| Today | `withheld` / `withheld_adb` — both |
| If Ocean rules yes | `validated` — both, +2 |
| Family sweep | 20 claimed; 2 declared, 16 ADB-result bit-identical, 2 parser-declines unchanged |
| Corpus census | 3,315 readable shas / 2,468 claimed; **6** documents in the whole archive carry ANY out-of-period posting; the loosest form of the rule fires on exactly these 2 |

### `823DCE7F…` — `fad3db75_document.PDF`, FAITH REMODELING & LIGHTING LLC

    Statement Period: January 24  - January 31, 2026 Page 1 of 2
    ACCOUNT TYPE AND NUMBER BALANCE FORWARD TOTAL DEBITS TOTAL CREDITS CLOSING BALANCE
    Business Simple Checking 1168006326 0.00 7,247.60 10,085.01 2,837.41
    Transactions
    Date Credits Debits Balance Description
    01-23 1,000.00 1,000.00 01-24 15.00 985.00 DEBIT CARD SETUP FEE
    01-25 108.68 876.32 POS DB WAL-MART #4405 AURORA IL 000000000430807 …
    Account Summary
    Average Balance $2,602.01 Average Collected Balance $2,602.01 Minimum Balance on 01/26/2026 $745.14 Number of Days in Cycle 8
    Daily Closing Balance Summary
    Date Balance
    01-23 1,000.00 01-24 985.00 01-25 861.32
    …

### What that print does and does not give us

**There is no opening-deposit wording to key on.** `D9EF1A8C`'s row says
`DEPOSIT`; `823DCE7F`'s row prints **no description at all** — a date, an
amount and a balance, nothing else. Any rule keyed on wording would fail on one
of the two documents. This is the single most important characterization
finding: the evidence has to be the arithmetic the bank prints AROUND the row,
not the words it does not print.

Common to both, and each an identity rather than a heuristic:

1. **`BALANCE FORWARD` is `0.00`.** The account carried nothing into the
   period. The bank's own summary identity closes on that zero *including* the
   pre-period row: `0.00 − 10,322.27 + 30,000.00 = 19,677.73` and
   `0.00 − 7,247.60 + 10,085.01 = 2,837.41`. The bank counts the row.
2. **The row is dated the day IMMEDIATELY before `period_start`** — 02-10 for a
   Feb 11 start, 01-23 for a Jan 24 start. Not a window; the day before.
3. **It is the LEADING row and the balance history starts from zero:** its
   printed running balance equals its own amount (30,000.00 / 1,000.00).
4. **The bank's own `Daily Closing Balance Summary` prints a closing balance
   for that day** — `02-10 30,000.00`, `01-23 1,000.00` — a day the statement's
   own printed period excludes. (This is also why §UNID-A UA2 refused to
   publish the table as `stated_daily_balances`: `adb.py` treats an
   out-of-period snapshot as invalid.)
5. **`Number of Days in Cycle` equals the printed period's calendar length**
   (18 = Feb 11–28, 8 = Jan 24–31), so the cycle the bank names IS the period
   we read.
6. **The bank's own printed `Average Balance` is reproduced EXACTLY, to the
   cent, only over the window that starts on the opening day.** This is the
   oracle the design rests on, and it was found by measurement, not assumed:

   | doc | printed | mean over printed period | mean over [opening day .. period end] |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `D9EF1A8C` | **25,632.67** | −4,609.96 (18d) | **25,632.67** (19d) — residual 0.00 |
   | `823DCE7F` | **2,602.01** | 1,802.26 (8d) | **2,602.01** (9d) — residual 0.00 |

   **CORRECTED — what this identity actually means.** The first version of
   this packet called the n+1 identity the strongest and least forgeable
   evidence that the row opened the account. That was wrong, and Ocean's
   review was right to block on it. Re-measured over all 17 claimed documents
   that print an average, with the platform's own engine run twice per
   document:

   | | residual over the printed period | residual over `[start-1 .. end]` |
   |---|---|---|
   | `D9EF1A8C` (opening) | −30,242.63 | **0.00** |
   | `823DCE7F` (opening) | −799.75 | **0.00** |
   | **`E0A4A5DB` (zero forward, NO pre-period row)** | +60.08 | **0.00** |
   | 12 ongoing statements | −0.38 … −0.50 | −152.91 … +275.79 |
   | `38D42B6A`, `BA0B55C6` (ongoing) | **0.00** | −2.21, −33.44 |

   Three corrections fall out of that table. **(a)** The zero residual is not a
   signature of an opening: it is Woodforest's divisor convention on
   ZERO-FORWARD statements. `E0A4A5DB` prints a zero forward, has no
   out-of-period row at all, and satisfies the complete identity — probe
   reconciles, `agrees_with_bank_stated_average` true — over `[start-1 .. end]`
   with a **phantom 0.00 day**. It holds on all three zero-forward documents
   and on none of the other fourteen. **(b)** The baseline is **12** of 15
   validated documents in the 0.38–0.50 band, not 13; two ongoing statements
   (`38D42B6A`, `BA0B55C6`) sit at exactly 0.00 over their own printed periods,
   so "exactly zero" is not rare in this family either. **(c)** What the
   identity does establish is that the forward really is zero and that the
   ledger READ is right — every amount and date, the declared posting's
   included, reproducing a printed figure the parser never used to build it.
   That is why it remains the sharpest mutation check available (a 2,000.00
   opening with every other figure made consistent is still refused by it), and
   why it cannot carry the interpretation on its own.

   **The evidence that actually discriminates an opening** is therefore G1
   (forward is 0.00), G2 (the posting is dated the day immediately before, and
   nothing is dated after), G3 (every declared posting is a CREDIT leaving a
   positive balance) and G4 (the ledger closes with them and not without).
   G5–G8 confirm the read.
7. Corroboration, recorded but NOT required: both print account-opening
   furniture on the first in-period day — `ACCOUNT SETUP FEE` and
   `DEBIT CARD SETUP FEE` on `D9EF1A8C`, `DEBIT CARD SETUP FEE` on
   `823DCE7F` — and `D9EF1A8C` prints `Account Item Images Total of 1 /
   02/10/2026 Deposit $30,000.00`, the bank's own image index for that one
   deposit. Requiring the setup-fee wording would hold on both today; it is
   left as corroboration because it is wording, and wording is exactly what the
   other six conditions were chosen to avoid depending on.

**Corroboration from outside the documents:** the archive also holds each
account's NEXT statement, and both open where these close —
`F60EDE2E` (Mar 2026) prints `BALANCE FORWARD 19,677.73`, `1023E395` (Feb 2026)
prints `BALANCE FORWARD 2,837.41`. Not used as evidence (a single document must
stand alone), but it confirms the reading.

## WF2. What actually fails today — four checks, not one

UA6.1 named `transactions_within_period`. Measured on the real documents
through the real pipeline, **four** required ADB checks fail, and `reconcile`
passes cleanly:

```
D9EF1A8C  reconcile.ok=True  summary_ok=True  breaks=0  credit_cov=1.0  debit_cov=1.0
          adb.ok=False   adb=-4609.96  days=18  out_of_period=1
            FAIL transactions_within_period
            FAIL final_balance_matches_statement_closing
            FAIL ledger_reconciles_to_closing
            FAIL running_balances_support_daily_ledger
          OUTCOME withheld / withheld_adb
823DCE7F  reconcile.ok=True  summary_ok=True  breaks=0  credit_cov=1.0  debit_cov=1.0
          adb.ok=False   adb=1802.26   days=8   out_of_period=1
            (same four)
          OUTCOME withheld / withheld_adb
```

The cause is one thing seen four ways: `adb.py` computes the period total over
in-period rows only, so the deposit is dropped from the ledger while
`beginning_balance` stays at the printed `0.00`, and everything downstream is
off by exactly the deposit.

## WF3. Why no parser-only design is admissible — measured, not argued

The tension is structural. `reconcile` needs the deposit INSIDE
`stmt.transactions` (its coverage check compares captured credits against the
bank's `TOTAL CREDITS`, which includes it, and its summary identity is seeded
from the printed `0.00`). `adb.py` needs it OUTSIDE the period. Only a
component that can tell "in the ledger" from "in the period" can satisfy both,
and `adb.py` is the only such component.

Every lever a parser has was tried against the REAL `reconcile` and the REAL
`compute_average_daily_balance`:

| design | reconcile | adb | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| D0 today: forward 0.00, row in `transactions` | ok | fail | withheld |
| D1 forward := post-init, row dropped, printed totals kept | **fail** (summary off by the deposit; credit coverage 0% / 90%) | ok | withheld |
| D2 …and the printed totals SUPPRESSED | ok | ok | **publishes — inadmissible** |
| D3 forward omitted, row dropped | **fail** (sum check, continuity, coverage) | ok | withheld |
| D4 forward omitted, row kept | ok | fail | withheld |
| D5 row moved to `period_start` | ok | ok | **publishes — forbidden** |
| D6 period widened to the opening day | ok | ok | **publishes — forbidden** |

* **D2 is the only parser-only design that publishes, and it buys publication
  by DELETING the bank's two printed totals from the payload.** Gate 5 requires
  the stated totals to remain *independently satisfied*; suppressing the
  oracle so the check cannot run is the opposite of satisfying it, and it
  silently drops `TOTAL DEBITS` / `TOTAL CREDITS` from what we publish.
  Rejected.
* **D5** moves a row to a boundary day — the thing `adb.py`'s own warning text
  says it will not do, and §UNID-A already refused.
* **D6** invents a period the document does not state, and the ruling requires
  the ADB basis to remain the printed period. (Recorded because it is
  arithmetically seductive: D6 reproduces the bank's printed average exactly,
  25,632.67 and 2,602.01, residual 0.00. That is the same fact WF1.6 uses as
  EVIDENCE — the difference is that evidence informs a fold into the opening
  balance, while D6 would publish an ADB over a period the bank did not print.)

## WF4. The design, and what it does to published fields

Two halves, deliberately separated.

**Half A — the parser proves it (shipped, unwired).**
`analysis.woodforest.initialization_postings(markdown, stmt)` returns the
postings the document PROVES are account opening, or an empty list. Eight
conditions, each exact, none carrying a threshold or a tolerance, any one
failing returning `[]` — and they are NOT equal in what they establish.
**G1–G4 discriminate an opening** (forward is zero; dated the day immediately
before with nothing after; every declared posting a CREDIT leaving a positive
balance; the ledger closes with them and not without). **G5–G8 confirm the
read** (leading rows and the walk; the daily table prints that day; the cycle
length is the printed period; the n+1 average identity). G8 runs the platform's
OWN engine over a throwaway copy whose `period_start` is the opening day and
requires both `result.ok` (the full ledger reconciles over that window — the
ruling's gate 4) and the engine's own `agrees_with_bank_stated_average`
(residual exactly 0.00 — the ruling's gate 5). The extended window is EVIDENCE
ONLY: nothing is published from it, and per WF1.6 it evidences the READ rather
than the interpretation.

**Half B — the engine consumes it (NOT shipped; `analysis/adb.py`, protected).**
`Statement` gains `initialization_transaction_count: int = 0`
(`analysis/schema.py`, not protected), the parser sets it to
`len(initialization_postings(...))`, and `adb.py` folds exactly those postings
into the opening balance.

### Consequences for published fields — stated before implementing

* **`transactions`: the initialization posting IS published, with its true
  printed date.** It is a real row on a real ledger; hiding it would break
  `reconcile`'s coverage against the bank's own `TOTAL CREDITS` and would
  publish a ledger the bank did not print. It is initialization CONTEXT for the
  *period arithmetic*, not a row we pretend does not exist.
* **`period_start` / `period_end`: unchanged**, exactly as printed.
* **ADB day count: unchanged** — 18 and 8, the printed periods. The opening day
  never becomes a calendar day of the ADB, never appears in `daily_balances`,
  and contributes no `transaction_count` to any day.
* **`beginning_balance`: unchanged** — the printed `0.00`. What changes is the
  ADB engine's internal `opening`, which becomes `0.00 + the event`, reported
  as `opening_balance_source="initialization_event"` and disclosed in a
  warning. `opening_balance_matches_statement` still compares against the
  PRINTED figure (the patch subtracts what was folded in), so it stays a
  truthful check rather than being quietly satisfied.
* **`stated_*`: unchanged**, every printed figure published as printed.
* **The published ADB will differ from the bank's printed average by
  −242.63 and +200.25.** This is disclosed, not hidden: the two figures answer
  different questions. Ours is "the mean end-of-day balance over the statement
  period", which is what the platform defines and what the ruling requires;
  the bank's is the mean over the account's life to date, which begins a day
  earlier. Both are published side by side (`average_daily_balance` and
  `stated_average_balance`), and `adb.py`'s existing
  `agrees_with_bank_stated_average` warning fires. **Ocean should decide
  explicitly whether a gap of that size is acceptable to publish** — it is an
  order of magnitude larger than the family's usual 0.38–0.50, and the reason
  is fully understood rather than mysterious.

### The exact patch (`analysis/adb.py`, +55 / −1)

Five hunks. Reproduced in full at the end of this section; the substance is:

1. after `outside` is computed, a guarded branch that empties `outside` and
   zeroes `out_of_period_transaction_count` when — and only when — the parser
   declared exactly this many pre-period rows, nothing is dated after the
   period, `beginning_balance` is `0.00`, the event is non-zero, the whole
   printed ledger closes on the printed closing balance WITH it, and does not
   close without it. A warning names the folded dates.
2. `opening = _money(opening + seeded_total)` with
   `opening_source = "initialization_event"`.
3–4. `seeded_total` threaded into `_validate` as a keyword with a
   `Decimal("0")` default.
5. `opening_balance_matches_statement` compares the printed figure against
   `opening − seeded_total`.

**THE HUNKS ARE NOT STANDALONE-INERT — they must land in the SAME COMMIT as
the schema field.** Hunk 1 reads `stmt.initialization_transaction_count`
unconditionally. Applied to `analysis/adb.py` on its own, against today's
`Statement`, every call to `compute_average_daily_balance` raises
`AttributeError` — that is the whole platform, not this family. This is a
same-commit requirement on `analysis/schema.py`, not a footnote, and it is
stated here because the earlier draft's "inert by construction" invited exactly
the wrong merge order.

**Inert WHEN the field exists.** With the field present and
`initialization_transaction_count == 0`, every new line is behind
`if declared and …` and `seeded_total` is `Decimal("0")`, so hunk 5 reduces to
the original comparison and the patched function is the production function.
Measured, not just argued: over the 18 parsed Woodforest documents the patched
engine's `AverageDailyBalanceResult` is **bit-identical**
(`dataclasses.asdict` equality) on all 16 undeclared ones, and the two declared
ones move.

**Two corrections the review forced into the diff itself**, both now in the
text below. (1) The day-before boundary is re-enforced at the CONSUMING layer —
`all(day == start - timedelta(days=1) …)`, not `day < start`. The reviewer fed
a `start − 2` posting to the original hunk and it was accepted, because the
hunk trusted the declaring parser to have checked. A consuming layer that
trusts its caller has no check. (2) The folded amount must be POSITIVE
(`seeded > 0` and every declared posting `> 0`) — see WF4.1.

```diff
--- a/analysis/adb.py
+++ b/analysis/adb.py
@@ -221,6 +221,63 @@
     ordered = [(day, txn) for day, txn in all_ordered if start <= day <= end]
     outside = [(day, txn) for day, txn in all_ordered if not start <= day <= end]
     result.out_of_period_transaction_count = len(outside)
+
+    # ACCOUNT-OPENING INITIALIZATION EVENT — narrow, declared, fail-closed.
+    #
+    # An account opened mid-cycle can have its funding deposit posted the day
+    # before the period the statement prints, counted in the bank's own printed
+    # totals and printed in the bank's own daily balance history, while the
+    # printed period still begins the next day. That posting is not period
+    # activity: it is what day one opens WITH. It is folded into the opening
+    # balance, so it never becomes a period day, the ADB divisor stays the
+    # printed period's calendar length, and no row is moved to a boundary day.
+    #
+    # This is NOT a general tolerance for out-of-period transactions. It is
+    # reachable only when the parser has DECLARED, from the document's own
+    # printed evidence, exactly how many leading postings opened the account
+    # (`Statement.initialization_transaction_count`), and only when every
+    # condition below also holds of the ledger itself. Any row after the
+    # period, any pre-period row beyond the declared count, a non-zero stated
+    # opening balance, or a ledger that closes either without the event or not
+    # at all with it, leaves `out_of_period_transaction_count` intact and the
+    # document withheld.
+    initialization: list[tuple[date, Any]] = []
+    declared = stmt.initialization_transaction_count
+    # The boundary is re-enforced HERE, not inherited from the declaring
+    # parser: `day == start - 1`, not `day < start`. A consuming layer that
+    # trusts its caller to have checked is a consuming layer with no check.
+    if (
+        declared
+        and len(outside) == declared
+        and all(day == start - timedelta(days=1) for day, _ in outside)
+    ):
+        seeded = sum((_decimal(txn.amount) for _, txn in outside), Decimal("0"))
+        in_period = sum((_decimal(txn.amount) for _, txn in ordered), Decimal("0"))
+        if (
+            stmt.beginning_balance is not None
+            and _money(stmt.beginning_balance) == Decimal("0.00")
+            and stmt.ending_balance is not None
+            # An account is opened by money ARRIVING. Without this a debit
+            # dated the day before a zero-forward statement folds a NEGATIVE
+            # opening balance in and publishes it as an account opening.
+            and seeded > Decimal("0")
+            and all(txn.amount > 0 for _, txn in outside)
+            # The event is REQUIRED: the whole printed ledger closes on the
+            # printed closing balance with it, and does not close without it.
+            and _money(seeded + in_period) == _money(stmt.ending_balance)
+            and _money(in_period) != _money(stmt.ending_balance)
+        ):
+            initialization = outside
+            outside = []
+            result.out_of_period_transaction_count = 0
+            result.warnings.append(
+                f"{len(initialization)} account-opening posting(s) dated before the "
+                f"statement period ("
+                + ", ".join(day.isoformat() for day, _ in initialization)
+                + ") were folded into the opening balance as initialization "
+                "context; the ADB basis remains the printed period"
+            )
+
     if outside:
         shown = ", ".join(day.isoformat() for day, _ in outside[:6])
         more = f" (+{len(outside) - 6} more)" if len(outside) > 6 else ""
@@ -242,6 +299,10 @@
     result.total_debits = float(_money(debits))
 
     opening, opening_source = _resolve_opening(stmt, ordered, total)
+    seeded_total = sum((_decimal(txn.amount) for _, txn in initialization), Decimal("0"))
+    if initialization and opening is not None:
+        opening = _money(opening + seeded_total)
+        opening_source = "initialization_event"
     result.opening_balance = float(opening) if opening is not None else None
     result.opening_balance_source = opening_source
     result.closing_balance = (
@@ -322,6 +383,7 @@
         undated=undated,
         snapshot_dates_valid=snapshot_dates_valid,
         source_markdown=source_markdown,
+        seeded_total=seeded_total,
     )
     return result
 
@@ -339,6 +401,7 @@
     undated: int,
     snapshot_dates_valid: bool,
     source_markdown: str | None = None,
+    seeded_total: Decimal = Decimal("0"),
 ) -> None:
     daily = result.daily_balances
     checks: dict[str, bool] = {}
@@ -413,8 +476,10 @@
             )
 
     if stmt.beginning_balance is not None:
+        # `opening` carries any initialization event; the printed figure is the
+        # balance BEFORE it, so the comparison subtracts what was folded in.
         checks["opening_balance_matches_statement"] = (
-            _money(stmt.beginning_balance) == opening
+            _money(stmt.beginning_balance) == _money(opening - seeded_total)
         )
     else:
         checks["opening_balance_matches_statement"] = False
```

### WF4.1 The sign defect — the review's worst finding, and it was real

Nothing in the first version required the folded amount to be POSITIVE. The
reviewer constructed a `−50.00 NSF CHARGE` dated the day before a zero-forward
statement and it passed `initialization_postings` AND the patched engine,
publishing `opening = −50.00` and an ADB computed on top of it, described as an
account opening. I reproduced it before changing anything:

```
parsed rows: [('2026-01-23', -50.0, -50.0), ('2026-01-24', 1000.0, 950.0), ...]
initialization_postings -> [('2026-01-23', -50.0)]
*** PROVER ACCEPTS A NEGATIVE 'OPENING': True ***
```

It satisfied every other condition honestly: forward zero, dated the day
immediately before, leading row, walk reproducing the printed balance, the
bank's daily table printing that day, cycle length matching, the ledger closing
with it and not without it, and the n+1 average identity holding exactly. That
is a compact demonstration of why G8 could not be allowed to carry the
interpretation — the arithmetic was all correct; the READING was absurd.

The fix is one idea in two places, because the two layers must not depend on
each other for it: **an account is opened by money arriving.**
`initialization_postings` now requires every declared posting to be a credit
and the balance they leave to be positive (G3); the pinned diff independently
requires `seeded > 0` and every declared posting `> 0`. Fixtured at both
layers: `test_a_debit_dated_the_day_before_is_not_an_account_opening` (the
reviewer's exact construction) and simulation probe A7.

## WF5. The adversarial gate (ruling gate 6)

**In the archive, not only in fixtures.** A census over the whole D-3 OCR
artifact store — 6,773 `ocr` artifacts over **3,409 distinct content shas**, of
which **13** hold only a cached NEGATIVE preflight and **3,396 hold readable
markdown** — run through dispatch + parse + repairs on the deterministic path
only, $0 vendor. **2,477** of the 3,396 are claimed by a registration, and
among them **six** documents in the entire corpus carry any out-of-period
posting:

**CORRECTED accounting.** The first pass reported 94 negatives / 3,315 readable
/ 2,468 claimed. Those intermediates were wrong and the review caught it: each
PDF has TWO artifacts (two settings keys) and my pass took whichever sorted
first per sha, so 81 documents whose other artifact carried the markdown were
recorded as negatives. Preferring the artifact that carries a document — which
is what the sha means — reproduces the reviewer's 13 / 3,396 / 2,477 exactly.
The headline was unaffected (those 81 resolve through their readable artifact
either way), but an intermediate that does not reproduce is not evidence, and
the corrected pass is the one recorded here.

```
1B6768E8  atb          pre=0  post=514  2026-01-01..2026-01-31
7F2B71AF  atb          pre=0  post=444  2026-01-01..2026-01-31
538375B8  capital_one  pre=1  post=0    2026-05-01..2026-05-29
4D7CD4EB  relay        pre=0  post=1    2026-05-01..2026-05-31
823DCE7F  woodforest   pre=1  post=0    2026-01-24..2026-01-31
D9EF1A8C  woodforest   pre=1  post=0    2026-02-11..2026-02-28
```

`538375B8` is the real-world adversary the ruling asks for: a genuine
pre-period row — `2026-04-30 −35.00 'NSF charge DR AMT 1,976.21 …'` — on a
statement whose `BALANCE FORWARD` is 83.51. It stays withheld, and Woodforest's
prover returns `[]` on it and on all four foreign out-of-period documents.

**CORRECTED, and it matters for the recommendation.** The first version said it
"fails on three independent counts". It fails **one**. Of the undeclared rule's
conditions it satisfies "all out-of-period rows are pre-period", "the event is
non-zero" and "does not close without it"; it fails `forward == 0.00`; and its
apparent second failure — "does not close WITH it" — is a pure consequence of
the first, since that comparison omits the forward and
`83.51 + (−35.00) + 397.25 = 445.76` is exactly the printed closing balance.
So the undeclared form's real-world margin on the only natural adversary in
3,396 documents is **a single gate**, not three. Note also what it is NOT
excluded by: it is a −35.00 DEBIT, so under the corrected rule G3 excludes it
too — but G3 came from the review, not from this document. That thinness is
the strongest argument for the declared form, where the parser must prove
account-opening from printed evidence before the engine will look at all.

### WF5.1 Fixture strength, measured by mutation

The first version claimed "thirteen fixtures killing it one condition at a
time". That claim was false and the review was right to reject it. Every
fixture DID refuse — but mostly for the wrong reason: each mutated the ledger
without recomputing the printed average, so G8b refused first and the condition
under test was never reached.

Measured properly, by deleting each guard in turn and re-running
`tests/test_woodforest.py`: **3 of 14 guards were killed. Eleven survived** —
worse than the review's estimate of eight.

The fix was to make every discriminating fixture internally consistent. A
`consistent_document` helper computes the average Woodforest itself would print
for the document AS MUTATED (its n+1 convention), so the named condition is the
only one that can refuse. After that, plus the new G3 and a fixture built so
that G3's two halves cannot mask each other:

| guard | killed by its own fixture? |
|---|---|
| G1 `BALANCE FORWARD` is zero | **yes** |
| G3 every declared posting is a credit | **yes** |
| G6 the daily table prints that day | **yes** |
| G7 `Number of Days in Cycle` = printed period | **yes** |
| G8b the printed average is reproduced | **yes** |
| G2 day-immediately-before / nothing after | no — G8a also catches it |
| G4a the ledger closes WITH the event | no — it IS G8a's `ledger_reconciles_to_closing` |
| G4b the ledger does not close WITHOUT it | no — G3 already excludes the shape |
| G5 leading rows | no — G4a also catches it |
| G5 the walk reproduces printed balances | no — unfalsifiable from this parser |
| G3's `carry > 0` half | no — unreachable while every posting must be a credit |
| the four `None`-input guards | no — unreachable from this parser |

**5 killed / 11 surviving, and every survivor is now explained** in
`initialization_postings`'s docstring rather than counted as evidence: three

output cannot violate. Only the five pinned conditions are load-bearing for the

### WF7.1 The corpus-slice failure is pre-existing — §HUNT's prediction landing

`test_detect_sweep_stays_affordable_for_the_discovery_run` caps the worst
per-document full-registry detect sweep at 250 ms. It failed at 472.5 ms.
**It is not this branch.** Three independent lines say so, and the third
settles it.

**1. The detect path has a zero diff.** Parsed to AST and compared against
`707ba9e`, the six statements that constitute this registration's detection —
`_MONEY`, `_SUMMARY_HEADER_RE`, `_GRID_RE`, `_BANK_RE`, `DETECTION_MARKERS`,
`detect` — are **identical**, and `analysis/parser_registry_entries.py` is
byte-identical. The whole diff to `analysis/woodforest.py` is additive: one
import widened, two imports added, two module-level regexes compiled at import,
two new functions. `parse_woodforest_statement` is untouched and neither new
function is on the detect path.

**2. In-process A/B of this parser's own `detect`.** Base and branch modules
loaded into ONE interpreter and timed alternately, ten rounds each, over all
109 corpus documents — no cross-process or machine-drift noise. Verdicts
identical on all 109. Base median **141.9 ms** (129.0–171.3), branch median
**146.0 ms** (128.6–175.5): +0.038 ms per document, inside a ±20 ms spread.

**3. The base fails the same test by the same margin, on the same machine,
minutes apart.** Five rounds each of the test's exact loop:

| | min | median | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| branch | 275.5 | **306.4** | 322.3 ms |
| base `707ba9e` | 286.0 | **310.0** | 317.5 ms |

The base is if anything marginally SLOWER. Reverting this branch does not make
the test pass.

**What is actually going on — and §HUNT called it.** Best-of-three on the worst
pinned document (`Others/Altana/Altana june 26.pdf`, 62,702 chars, the largest)
is **259.8 ms**: over budget before any contention, with the machine only
moderately loaded. The 472.5 ms in the slice was that plus ~20 concurrent
python processes from other batch-4 cells saturating all 16 cores.

§HUNT-CELL item 11 measured **195.2 ms at 55 registrations** one batch ago and
wrote: *"at ~13 ms a cell the cap is four merges away … Worth deciding at the
batch level, before the merge train, rather than by whichever cell happens to
cross the line."* Batch 3 merged eleven cells and took the registry to 68. The
line has now been crossed: 195.2 → 259.8 ms for +13 registrations, about 5 ms
each, exactly the trajectory §HUNT projected. Batch 3's record that the test
"HELD at 68 registrations" is not contradicted — on a quiet machine it evidently
did — and that IS the finding: **the margin is now thin enough that the verdict
depends on who else is running.**

No single parser is the cause, which is why shaving one cannot fix it:

| registration | ms | share |
|---|---|---|
| community_section | 17.56 | 8.6% |
| rbc_french | 9.92 | 4.8% |
| square_checking | 9.83 | 4.8% |
| cibc | 9.55 | 4.7% |
| td_canada_french | 9.23 | 4.5% |
| … | | |
| **woodforest (9th)** | **5.76** | **2.8%** |
| the other 53 registrations | 96.2 | 47% |

The worst single registration is 8.6% of the sweep; the top fifteen are 53%.
**Deleting this registration outright would leave ~254 ms and the test would
still fail.**

**Nothing was done about it here, deliberately.** The budget constant is not
this cell's to move, and raising it to make a red test green is the one
response that would be wrong. Carried to Ocean as WF8.11.

## WF8. Carried findings and questions for Ocean

1. **THE RULING. `analysis/adb.py` is protected and the mechanism needs it.**
   The patch is WF4, +55/−1, five hunks, inert with `declared == 0` by
   construction and measured bit-identical on 16 documents. It also needs one
   new optional field on `Statement` (`analysis/schema.py`, not protected) and
   two lines in `parse_woodforest_statement`. **Two documents turn on it.**
2. **`initialization_postings` is shipped UNWIRED and is dead code until the
   ruling lands.** That is deliberate — it is the half this cell owns, it is
   fully fixture-covered, and it makes the ruling a wiring change rather than a
   new cell. If the ruling is NO, delete it: one function, one commit.
3. **Adding the schema field changes every payload.** `initialization_transaction_count`
   would serialize as `0` on all 3,380 documents, which invalidates every
   cached analysis payload and requires the `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` bump in
   the same commit (Ocean's at merge). If that blast radius is unwanted, the
   alternative in item 4 avoids it entirely.
4. **The alternative — no declaration at all — is now clearly the worse one,
   and the count-based declaration is the design to keep.** `adb.py` could
   infer the event from the Statement alone; measured over the whole corpus
   that undeclared form fires on **exactly the same two documents and nothing
   else**, and it needs no schema field, no version bump and no parser change.
   Against that: its real-world margin on the only natural adversary in 3,396
   documents is **one gate**, not the three the first packet claimed
   (WF5), its only printed evidence is `BALANCE FORWARD == 0.00`, it is
   reachable by every parser and by the LLM path rather than by one declaring
   parser, and the printed-average oracle goes unused. The declaration also
   carries its own check — the engine requires the pre-period row COUNT to
   equal what the parser declared, so a parser that proves one posting cannot
   have a second one folded in silently. **Recommended: the declared form,
   with the count.**
5. **The published ADB will disagree with the bank's printed average by
   −242.63 / +200.25.** WF4 explains why and both figures are published. Ocean
   should say explicitly that this is acceptable, because it is a much larger
   gap than the family's usual sub-dollar one.
6. **`Number of Days in Cycle` is not what the bank divides its own average
   by.** `D9EF1A8C` prints 18 and divides by 19; `823DCE7F` prints 8 and
   divides by 9. Recorded so it is not later rediscovered as an extraction
   defect: the printed cycle length is the printed period, and the printed
   average is over the account's life to date.
7. **`analysis/woodforest.py` now imports `analysis/adb.py`, and COUPLES to a
   named validation inside a protected module.** A parser calling the
   deterministic math layer read-only is new here; it is what makes G8 the
   platform's own answer rather than a second daily-balance walk inside a
   parser, and duplicating that walk is the worse option. No import cycle:
   `adb` imports only `dates` and `schema`. But the dependency is finer than
   "imports a module" and the review was right to ask for it in writing: the
   prover reads
   `probed.validations["agrees_with_bank_stated_average"]` — a KEY NAME and a
   SEMANTIC (printed average vs computed ADB, compared to the cent) that live
   in `analysis/adb.py`. Two failure modes, and they are not symmetric.
   **Renaming or removing that check fails CLOSED** (`.get` returns None, the
   prover declares nothing, the documents stay withheld). **Loosening its
   comparison to a tolerance fails OPEN** — G8b would stop pinning the amount
   and the mutation fixture would be the only thing standing. Anyone editing
   that check must know this reader exists; the coupling is commented at the
   call site as well as recorded here.
8. **The prover is O(one ADB run) and only on documents with a pre-period
   row** — 2 of 20 in this family, 6 in 3,396 corpus-wide. It is not on the
   detect-sweep path, so it costs the registry budget nothing.
9. **G8b will refuse a future opening whose printed average carries the
   family's usual offset, and that refusal will not be about its opening.**
   **Twelve** of the fifteen validated Woodforest statements miss their own
   printed average by 0.38–0.50 (two more sit at exactly 0.00 over their own
   printed periods); the two openings hit theirs at exactly 0.00 on the n+1
   window. If a third opening arrives carrying the offset, it stays withheld —
   fail-closed, correct, and for a reason that has nothing to do with whether
   it is an opening. That is the price of using the sharpest oracle the
   document prints, and it is the right price to pay first; loosening G8b to a
   tolerance would be a tuned constant and should not be done without new
   evidence. **Do not loosen it to make a future document pass** — and note
   from WF8.7 that loosening the check it reads inside `adb.py` would have the
   same effect from the other side.
10. **Why the residual is exactly zero on these two and 0.38–0.50 elsewhere is
    NOT explained by this cell.** UA6.8 established the difference is a
    convention in how Woodforest averages (its `Average Collected Balance` is
    printed equal to its `Average Balance`, and reproducing the figure from the
    bank's own complete daily table gives the platform's answer, not the
    bank's). This cell measured that the two openings sit at 0.00 and used it;
    it did not learn why. Recorded rather than dressed up in a story: a
    plausible reading is that a days-old account funded by one deposit has no
    uncollected float, but nothing here proves that.
11. **STOP-THE-LINE CANDIDATE, and it is not this branch's: the detect-sweep
    budget has been crossed on `main`.** `test_detect_sweep_stays_affordable_
    for_the_discovery_run` fails at 472.5 ms under batch-4 load and at

    Base `707ba9e` measures 310.0 ms median where this branch measures 306.4 ms;

    at 55 registrations, warned the cap was "four merges away", and asked for a

# §MG-C — the wrapped row the export dropped, and the refusal that became a zero

Two staged follow-ups from §MONEY-GRAMMAR: MG-C1 finishes the three
corrected-sign chase exports; MG-C2 closes the `or 0.0` fail-open class §MG8.2
catalogued. Base `ea8d8e8`, branch `wave4-mgc`.

## MGC1. The chase export's grid, and the cell that wraps

The export flattens five columns — Date | Description | Type | Amount |
Balance — into text, so a logical row ALREADY spans two physical lines: date
and description on the first, type and the amount pair on the second. The type
cell is what sits in front of the amounts, which is why this parser's published
"description" is `ACH debit`, `Card`, `Account transfer` and not the
descriptive text above it.

Three type cells in the archive are too long to fit beside the amounts and wrap
onto a line of their own — `Incoming wire transfer`, `Outgoing wire transfer`,
`ACH vendor payment`. The amount pair is then alone on its line, and
`if not description: continue` dropped the entire transaction.

Replaying the shipped loop over the three documents, with the base finder for
comparison, gives the exact population:

```
                 HEAD kept   HEAD dropped   BASE kept   BASE dropped
112431717DA1        145           11           153           3
5A29258D7626         29            1            29           1
5C93775BBA87         88            2            90           0
```

The §MG7 nuance is visible in that table and is worth stating plainly: on
7302/7501 HEAD drops rows BASE kept, and the money-grammar card is why. With
the ASCII-only finder a `−$702.32` matched from the `$`, leaving the U+2212 as
a one-character "description" — truthy, so the row survived with its sign
inverted. Widening the finder to the shared MINUS_CLASS made the description
empty, and an empty description is dropped. The sign fix did not cause the
defect; it exposed it.

**Every one of the 14 dropped lines is preceded by a type cell** — no
exceptions, no other shape. So the recovery is structural rather than a list of
three strings: the wrapped cell is the last physical line that carried text and
no amount at all. A line carrying an amount is a row in its own right —
complete, or pending with a `—` where the balance goes — so it CONSUMES the
carry instead of passing it on, and a pending row can never lend its type to
the row beneath it.

### MGC1.1 Outcomes — withheld to review, with the residual named

| doc | txns | credits/debits | ending | ADB | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `112431717DA1` | 145 to **156** | 31/125 | **3,714.06** | **9,101.16** | withheld_adb to **review** |
| `5A29258D7626` | 29 to **30** | 6/24 | **20,852.46** | **5,723.88** | withheld_adb to **review** |
| `5C93775BBA87` | 88 to **90** | 20/70 | **485.38** | **1,051.15** | withheld_adb to **review** |

`ledger_sum_mismatch` and `running_balance_breaks` are both gone on all three:
the walk is continuous and the sum closes to the printed ending balance
exactly. That is an independent oracle — it confirms every recovered row's
amount, sign and position at once, which no fixture can.

**They are not validated, and validated is not the honest terminal state.** The
residual is `not_a_formal_statement`, a REGISTRY declaration
(`registration.formal_statement is False`, `analysis/pipeline.py:307`): a Chase
online transaction export is not a complete bank statement, and saying so is
deliberate. `classify_outcome` therefore returns `review / integrity_flags`.
The brief asked for an honest terminal state or a named independent reason;
this is the named reason.

## MGC2. Absence is not a refusal — the distinction the whole card turns on

§MG8.2 catalogued ~12 sites in ~10 parsers. Re-derived on `ea8d8e8` by AST over
the whole analysis layer, the real census is four classes, and only one of them
is a defect:

| class | left of `or 0` | sites / files | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | a money-reading CALL | **39 / 15** | **fail-open — fixed** |
| C | a NAME bound to a money read | 22 / 6 | absence |
| C? | a NAME bound to something else | 18 / 5 | absence |
| B | an ATTRIBUTE (`stmt.stated_*`, `.running_balance`) | 44 / 19 | different class |

`None` out of a money reader means one of two opposite things. **Absence** — no
label matched, nothing printed — is legitimate, and `or 0.0` is the correct
arithmetic identity: a statement with no Checks line really does have zero
cheques. **Refusal** — a token was THERE and the grammar said no — is the
fail-open: a figure the bank printed, replaced by one it did not.

Two readers collapsed both into the same `None`, so their callers could not
possibly tell them apart: `bofa._native_money_after` and the `money_after`
closure inside `repair_bofa_summary`. Both now separate them, and they are the
two sites the archive actually exercises.

`analysis.money.read_money(token, reader)` is the generalized helper —
absence returns `None`, a refusal raises `ValueError`. The grammar stays
shared; the FORMAT stays local, because each caller hands over its own reader
rather than reimplementing the split. `ValueError` is not a new convention: it
is the raising family's documented contract (§MG4) and what
`chase._money_required` and `banco_popular` already do.

### MGC2.1 The blast radius, measured before the edit

`X or 0.0` differs from `X` only when X is None, so the documents that fire no
site are exactly the documents that are byte-identical under the fix. One
instrumented pass answers the whole question. Probing all 79 or-zero sites
(behaviour-preserving; the full suite passed 3,774 under the probe, the single
red being the helper-clone guard catching the probe's own import):

## MGC3. The left digit boundary (cross-cell answer to §UNKNOWN-ISSUER)

Asked whether the shared grammar admits the prefix-swallow class
UNKNOWN-ISSUER fixed locally. **It does not.** `_TOKEN_RE` opens with
`(?<![\d.])`, and measured on their fixture:

```
analysis/money.py      parse_money("D77100000001337 150.00")  -> 150.0      correct
cibc.py:41  _MONEY_RE  (?<![A-Za-z0-9]) ...                   -> 150,00     correct
bmo_ca_business.py:90  _MONEY_FR  (?<![\d.,-]) ...            -> 150,00     correct
cibc.py:62  _summary's local `money` fragment — NO boundary   -> 337 150,00 WRONG
```

**One parser-local site carries the class**: the `money` fragment inside
`cibc._summary` is the same pattern as `_MONEY_RE` with the left boundary
dropped, and it reproduces the fabricated amount exactly. Listed rather than
fixed, per the coordinator's instruction and because CIBC French overlaps
UNKNOWN-ISSUER's active territory. Its four uses are label-anchored with `.*?`,
which is non-greedy and therefore stops at the FIRST match — so a reference
number printed between the label and the amount is enough to fire it. Not
attested in today's archive; the sweep shows no cibc movement.

The boundary is now pinned in `tests/test_money.py` so the answer stays
answered. What it does NOT promise is unchanged and restated there:
`parse_money` searches, so a whole-LINE caller still gets the line's first
money-shaped token, reference numbers included (§MG8 finding 3, out of scope).

### MGC5.2 The carry anchoring, and one measured disagreement

Four rules now anchor the wrapped-cell carry, each fixtured:

| rule | what it forbids | bites? |
|---|---|---|
| ADJACENCY | anything between the type cell and the amount pair — a page separator, a `Pending` row, a line carrying its own amount | **yes** (3 of 3 fail pre-anchoring) |
| SINGLE | accumulating text lines into a description, or retaining an older one | pins |
| SAME DATE | a carry describing an amount pair posted under another date | **yes** |
| CONSUMED | a dangling carry at section end reaching the next row | pins |

Blank lines alone do not break adjacency; everything else does.

**One condition could not be implemented as written, and the measurement is
why.** Condition (b) asked that a SECOND text-only line refuse the pending
carry. Measured over the three documents, the run of consecutive text-only
lines before a genuine wrap is:

```
2 lines  x10      5 lines  x2      6 lines  x2      1 line  x0
```

never one — because the export prints the row's descriptive text above its
type cell, and across a page break its header furniture too. A rule that
refused the carry on sight of a second text-only line would therefore discard
**all 14** recoveries and revert MG-C1 entirely. What is implemented instead
is SINGLE (last-one-wins, no accumulation) plus ADJACENCY, which is the same
protection by a different route: the furniture is unreachable because only the
line immediately above the amount pair can ever be the carry. Also measured:
**0 of 14** genuine wraps cross a date boundary, so SAME DATE is free.

### MGC5.3 D2/D3 — `read_money` is not a probe

The review is right that the helper was applied past its own contract, and
the contract is now stated in its docstring: `read_money` is for a
REGEX-GUARANTEED token, where a `None` can only mean refusal.

* **D2, `regions.py:219`** fed it `cells[3]` — a RAW grid cell that can hold
  `N/A` or `--`. A non-money cell there is ABSENCE: the field stays unset,
  rather than raising (killing a document over an optional figure) or
  publishing a 0.00 average balance nobody printed.
* **D3, `regions._money`** is a column-finding PROBE: `_parse_section` walks a
  row's cells right-to-left asking "is this the amount column?", so it is
  handed dates, descriptions and `N/A` by design. It now returns `None` and
  never raises — and, importantly, still never returns `0.0` for a refusal,
  which is what the original `abs(parse_money(...) or 0.0)` did. Refusal still
  propagates; it propagates as `None`, which is the answer a probe needs.

Fixtured across `N/A`, `n/a`, `--`, `—`, empty, whitespace, `DEPOSIT`,
`Balance`, `1.5`, `1.2.3` and a 14-digit run. Four of these fail against the
reviewed tree, so the fixtures bite.

An audit of the other 37 class-A sites found **no second instance**: every one
is fed a regex capture or a group-unpacked variable. The one syntactic tell of
the D2 shape — a subscript argument — is now a guard
(`test_read_money_is_never_handed_a_raw_container_cell`).

### MGC5.6 The MG-D card, enriched and corrected

`money.py` is internally inconsistent about the em dash, measured on this tree:

```
MINUS_GLYPHS  (module scope)   '-−–—'     4 glyphs — the second definition
                                          at :521 SHADOWS the one at :102
MINUS_CLASS                    '[-−–]'    3 — no em dash
_MINUS_TABLE                   {U+2212, U+2013} -> '-'   2 — no em dash
SIGNED_MONEY_TOKEN             admits the em dash (built from MINUS_GLYPHS)

parse_money("—$500.00")          ->  +500.0
parse_signed_decimal("—$500.00") ->  -500.00
```

**The two exported parsers return OPPOSITE SIGNS for the same token today.**

**Correction to the card's premise: the archive attestation is 2, not 0.** A
direct scan of the cached text for an em dash welded to a money token found
two documents, and what they print is the argument FOR keeping the em dash out
of the sign class rather than a reason to admit it:

| doc | folder | outcome | printed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `88AAC06119FC` | Columbia Bank | failed | `03-16 — 39,692.35` — a placeholder in a daily-balance grid; the amount is a positive balance |
| `FFEBAF819F74` | TD Bank | failed | `—— $4812.39` inside mangled OCR (`TRANSFER "*56B ——— pet ee See eg`) — noise, not a sign |

Neither is a sign, and neither document is claimed by any parser, so neither
reaches a money reader today. Admitting the em dash to the sign class would
flip a printed positive balance on the first. §MG7 finding 7's ruling — em
dash is punctuation, and stays out permanently — is correct; what needs fixing
is the module agreeing with itself. Differential matrix required: the two
`MINUS_GLYPHS` definitions, `SIGNED_MONEY_TOKEN`, and every parser reading a
sign through either path.

## U2. Card 1 — five reconciling documents that name no bank

W3 §JHA J9.2. Characterized before any code changed, over every servable
document:

```
community_section detects            : 115
  names exactly one labelled domain  : 110
  names NO labelled domain           :   5
  names TWO OR MORE                  :   0
```

The 5 are exactly J9.2's five: all `failed` / `parser_declined` in the run of
record, all in the `Unidentified/` folder. The refusal was one branch —
`_issuer` returned `None` and the parser returned `None` with it.

**`_issuer` became `_masthead_domains`, returning the SET**, because the three
sizes of that set are three different findings and only two of them are the
same fact:

| size | finding | now |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the document names its issuer | published, unchanged — 110 documents |
| 0 | the document names no issuer | **published with `bank=None`** — 5 |
| 2+ | the document contradicts ITSELF about its issuer | still refused — 0 |

The 2+ case is deliberately NOT folded into the ruling. An unknown issuer is
a gap in the document; two labelled domains in the masthead is a gap in our
reading of it — the likeliest cause is `_MASTHEAD_END_RE` missing a layout's
first account so the scope runs on into the fine print, where these
statements cite their state regulator. Publishing `bank=None` there would
file our own defect as the document's honest silence. No archive document is
in the class, so there is nothing to prove a publication rule against either,
and an unproven class fails closed.

**No inference anywhere.** Four of the five really do print merchant domains
(`walmart.com` and the like) in transaction descriptions; "the first domain
in the document" would publish the shop the customer bought lunch at as the
bank. Pinned as its own assertion.

The five, by `content_sha256`, with the field that moved:

**A cross-document oracle nobody asked for.** Four of the five are the same

## U3. Does the platform tolerate `bank=None` end to end?

`Statement.bank` has always been `str | None` (`analysis/schema.py:30`). The
question is what every consumer does with the absence. Swept, and named:

| surface | reads | behaviour on `None` |
|---|---|---|
| `analysis/pipeline.py:545` | `stmt.bank` | `model_used` becomes `"bank-deterministic"` — the `or "bank"` fallback was already there |
| `analysis/pipeline.py:176` `_registration_for` | `by_bank_label(stmt.bank)` | never reached for these: the dispatch claimed, so the claiming registration is returned. `by_bank_label(None)` returns `None` anyway (`if not bank`) |
| `analysis/bank_repairs.py` (8 repairs) | `(stmt.bank or "").upper()` | none fire; each is None-safe already |
| `discovery/runner.py:494` | `statement.get("bank")` | field is `str \| None`; stored as null |
| `discovery/report.py:27` `folder_agreement` | `if row.statement_bank` | None-safe, but see D3 below — **6 of the 21 will surface as `label_unmatched`**, and the first version of this table said otherwise |
| `telemetry/record.py` | — | deliberately never carries the extracted bank label (H3_SCHEMA I1) |
| `webapp/app.py:831,:864` | `statement.get("bank")` | passed through as null |
| `webapp/static/app.js:269` | report field | renders **"Bank Name: N/A"** |
| `webapp/static/app.js:1448` | package doc row | renders **"Unknown bank"** |
| `webapp/static/app.js:1592` | report title | renders **"Bank Statement"** |
| `webapp/static/app.js:1721` | package summary sentence | opens **"Statement &lt;period&gt;: average daily balance …"** |
| `webapp/static/app.js:485` | flattened ledger row | falls back to the document name, then `"Statement"` |
| `analyze.py:19` | CLI header | `f"# {s.bank or 'Bank'}"` |

Every one of these fallbacks pre-dates this cell. Nothing was added to make
the absence displayable; the platform was already written for it. The one
consequence worth naming to Ocean is `model_used="bank-deterministic"`

`analysis/parser_registry.py:385` is the only unguarded `.bank` attribute

### U4.2 The 10 "chain-broken" documents were a missing digit boundary

The scout and UB5 both measured 6 reconciling / 10 chain-broken. Reproduced
