# §DETBUDGET — the sweep prepared every document sixty-eight times

Central triage of the batch-4 STOP-THE-LINE. Three cells read
`test_detect_sweep_stays_affordable_for_the_discovery_run` red on an
**unmodified base** while ten agents shared the machine, and each spent an hour
proving the red was not theirs. The unit of work is `analysis/parser_registry.py`
— the sweep path — and the affordability test's MEASUREMENT DESIGN. The
constant is not touched: the budget is still a quarter-second per document.

## DT0. Summary

The red was real, and it was two separate defects wearing one symptom.

| # | defect | fix | measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The sweep prepared each document's text once per registration.** `admissible_text` ran 68 times and 36 normalizations ran, per document, to produce five distinct strings. Four fifths of the sweep. | `PreparedDocument`: `admissible_text` once, each *distinct* normalizer once, results interned so a marker two registrations share over the same text runs once. | worst pinned sweep **267.7 → 128.6 ms** loaded, **118.1 → 50.4 ms** quiet; text preparations per document **104 → 33** |
| 2 | **The test timed a loop no caller runs, and read one sample of it.** It called `Registration.detect(markdown)` 68 times — which is the per-registration preparation, i.e. defect 1 measured deliberately — and took a single wall-clock sample on a shared machine. | Time the production seam (`_surviving_claimants`); take the **minimum** of five samples; assert against the cost **projected to 80 registrations**; and add a load-immune structural assertion in OPERATIONS. | the assertion is now **strictly harsher** than the one it replaces and passes with 30% margin |

`0` documents change behaviour. Full-archive claim-set equivalence over every
archive sha that has text offline — 3,367 of 3,380 — is byte-identical:
claimant sets, scores, matched marker ids and `excluded_by`, for all 68
registrations on every document, digest
`9A7DEAA1468033FA0966B429742660C2F9023EEAE4707ECEDEFF67C0C1672B15` on both
arms. The 13 documents with no offline text are the deferred visual-OCR set;
there is no text to sweep and they are excluded rather than assumed.

`analysis/parser_registry_entries.py` and all 59 parser modules carry a
**zero-line diff**. `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` is deliberately NOT bumped —
nothing published changes, and the bump is Ocean's at merge in any case.

## DT1. The instrument

Two checkouts, one markdown store, one process per arm.

* **base arm** — `git archive 229a3cd analysis ocr telemetry discovery`
  extracted to a directory outside the worktree. Production code is imported
  from the arm's own checkout and the harness asserts
  `Path(pr.__file__).is_relative_to(CHECKOUT)` before measuring anything; the
  first draft of this harness silently measured the branch twice and the
  assertion is what caught it.
* **the documents** — the run of record `d5c75ff6`'s 3,380 distinct shas,
  resolved out of the D-3 artifact store **by direct file path** under the
  run's OCR settings key. The sqlite index was never opened. 3,367 have text;
  62,715,801 characters in total. Both arms read one pickled store, so the two
  arms provably sweep identical bytes.
* **the pinned corpus** — the 109-path manifest, resolved exactly as
  `tests/test_parser_parity.py` resolves it.
* **the timing method** — best-of-N per document, paired, arms alternating in
  one command. Reported in both load regimes (DT6): *loaded* is roughly ten
  parallel cells, *quiet* is three processes. Neither is a claim about a
  dedicated machine; the train's numbers will be better than the quiet column.

## DT2. Where the cost was

Decomposed on the largest pinned document (`Others/Altana/Altana june 26.pdf`,
62,702 chars), base arm, best-of-5:

| stage | calls per document | cost | share |
|---|---|---|---|
| `admissible_text` | **68** — one per registration | 116 ms | 48% |
| parser normalization | **36** — one per registration that has one | 77 ms | 32% |
| markers | 68 registrations, 189 marker slots | 82 ms | 34% |
| *(measured whole sweep)* | | *242 ms* | |

The first two rows are the finding. `admissible_text` is a pure function of
the document; a parser's `normalize` is a pure function of the document and of
the parser's own preprocessing. Neither depends on which registration is
asking, and the sweep asks 68 times. The 104 preparations produced, on that
document, **five distinct strings**: 32 registrations have no normalizer, 30
normalizers agreed on `admissible.upper()`, and three more stood alone.

That is why HUNT-CELL's prediction landed at 55 registrations and why shaving
could not save it: the dominant term grew with the registry, and removing the
ninth-most-expensive registration entirely still left ~254 ms.

## DT3. The fix — prepare once per document, not once per registration

`PreparedDocument` in `analysis/parser_registry.py`. Three memos, each of them
exact rather than approximate:

1. **`admissible_text` once.** Whatever the registry's size.
2. **Each distinct normalizer once.** Keyed on the callable itself, so the two
   Chase entries, the two Found entries and the two scanned small banks share
   one output apiece. 36 calls → 32.
3. **Each distinct resulting text interned**, so two registrations whose
   normalizations happen to agree on *this* document hold the same string —
   and a marker they also share is then evaluated once. Worth 8.5 ms of a
   157 ms sweep.

**Interning trusts the value a normalizer returns, and that trust is now
guarded rather than assumed** (review finding, `text_for`). Two things go
wrong if the return is not an exact `str`. An unhashable one cannot be a dict
key, so the intern raises where the base merely handed the object to the
markers — fail-closed, but a `ParserFailure` that did not exist before, on a
registration that used to score. A `str` subclass carrying its own
`__eq__`/`__hash__` can compare equal to another normalizer's text, and
`setdefault` then hands this registration a *different* string to run its
markers over — silent. `type(produced) is str` is the guard: anything else
takes the base path, run per call and never interned, and the marker memo
carries the same guard one level on because it keys on the text too. The
purity contract this rests on is now written on `text_for` itself rather than
left to the module docstring. That is the fallback; the assertion that no
registered normalizer ever needs it is
`test_each_registrations_normalization_returns_an_exact_str`, which runs the
36 normalizations over five probe documents. It lives in the registry test and
not in `validate_registry` deliberately: the check needs a document to run on,
and `validate_registry` runs at import — putting every parser's normalization
on the import path of `analysis` to satisfy a type contract is the worse
trade.

Nothing here decides a registration cannot claim. Every registration still
runs every one of its markers over exactly the text it ran them over before,
in the same order, and still produces a `Detection` — including the near-miss
scores telemetry publishes for registrations that did not claim. The seam is
threaded through `_surviving_claimants`, `detection_report`, `safe_detect`
(which now accepts a `PreparedDocument` or a string), `Registration.detect`
(now `detect_prepared` over a prepared document of one) and `make_detector`.
Public behaviour of every one of them is unchanged.

**No global cache.** A prepared document lives exactly as long as the sweep
that asked for it. Caching the last document's prepared texts in a module
global would halve the discovery run's detection cost again — see DT9.1 — but
it would also leave five copies of a customer's statement in a module-level
variable for as long as the process lives, and this codebase does not do that
(`ParserFailure` refuses to keep an exception *message* for the same reason).

## DT4. The two candidates that were NOT taken, and why

**Candidate 1, the two-tier prescan, is incompatible with the binding
equivalence requirement.** A prescan is sound as a claim gate — a registration
whose required markers cannot all be present can never claim — but skipping a
registration does not merely withhold a claim. `detection_report` publishes a
`Detection` for **every** registration on every document, and telemetry's
near-miss vector (`telemetry/collect.score_vector`) records every non-zero
score. A skipped registration would lose its partial score and its `matched`
marker ids, which is a behaviour change outside sweep cost on documents that
nothing claims — 815 of the 3,367 swept here, which is exactly the population
whose near-miss vector the discovery run reads to rank the next parser cell.
To keep the vector intact the prescan would have to run the markers anyway, at
which point it has saved nothing.

This is where the cell diverges from the design package. A gated-vs-ungated
equivalence test of the kind SCAN-C pins would pass — it compares **claims**,
and a prescan built from strictly necessary conditions really does preserve
those — while the near-miss score and the `matched` marker ids of every gated-
out registration silently went to zero. The DT7 sweep is what would catch it,
because it compares the whole `Detection` for all 68 registrations and not only
the claimants. Recorded, not attempted; the headroom was taken out of the
normalization stage instead, where it costs no behaviour at all.

**Candidate 2, per-registration shaving, is real work but it is not this
cell's and it cannot close the gap alone.** The handoff's own arithmetic holds.
What the profile adds is *where* the remaining cost is, so the cards can be
written against evidence — DT9.2.

## DT5. The measurement was wrong in two ways, and only one of them was load

The shipped test read:

```python
for registration in registrations:
    registration.detect(markdown)
```

That is not a sweep. It is the per-registration preparation of defect 1,
performed deliberately, and **no caller has run detection that way since R-3**:
`resolve` goes through `_surviving_claimants` and telemetry goes through
`detection_report`, both of which sweep the registry once over one document.
The test was measuring a shape production does not have, and it was the most
expensive shape available.

Second, one wall-clock sample on a shared machine is the wrong instrument for
an absolute cost contract. Contention can only ever make a sample *slower*, so
the minimum of several samples is the reading least contaminated by load and
the one that converges on what a quiet machine pays.

The replacement keeps the constant and states three things:

| clause | what it asserts | instrument |
|---|---|---|
| `test_the_detect_sweep_prepares_each_document_once` | every pinned document costs exactly `1 + (distinct normalizers)` text preparations — 33 today | **operations. Deterministic; a busy machine and a quiet one cannot read it differently.** |
| `test_the_sweep_entry_points_strip_the_filename_comment_once` | `_surviving_claimants` and `detection_report` — the two real entry points — strip the filename comment once per document, not once per registration | operations |
| `test_detect_sweep_stays_affordable_for_the_discovery_run` | **every** pinned document read as the best of five sweeps through the production seam; the worst of those, **projected to 80 registrations**, is under **250 ms** | wall clock, absolute ceiling, load-robust estimator |

The projection is what turns "the budget holds today" into "the budget holds at
the size the coverage wave is heading for". At 68 registrations it requires the
sweep to come in under 212.5 ms, which is **stricter than the 250 ms the
shipped test asked for.**

**It is a floor on the cost at 80, not a bound, and the record should not read
otherwise.** `worst × 80/68` scales by the mean cost of today's registrations,
and that mean is diluted by the 32 that have no normalization at all. Review
measured projection ÷ actual at **1.00** for a growth shape resembling today's
mix and **0.79** for one where every new registration brings its own
normalizer — so the real cost at 80 can exceed the projection by a quarter.
The projection earns its place by being harsher than asserting at 68 and
honest about direction; it does not predict. Note also what the first clause
does and does not cover: it is the **exact** guard for the quadratic class
this cell removed — per-registration preparation cannot come back without
turning it red — while other superlinear shapes (a marker whose cost grows
with the registry, say) are caught by neither clause. Carried in DT9.

Selection is done the same way as the reading, for the same reason. The first
revision picked the worst document from a single sample and only then applied
best-of-five to it; review measured that selection finding the true worst
**0 times in 7** and understating the reading by up to **44%**, because a
document that draws one unlucky sample wins a selection it should not and then
has that very sample discarded. Both are now the minimum of five.

Be precise about what is red where, because it matters for reading the next
red. The wall-clock clause is red on base **under load** (267.7 ms → projects
to 315 ms) and green on base **on a quiet machine** (118.1 ms → 139 ms): the
production sweep really was affordable when nothing else was running, and the
old test only looked green there because 203 ms of loop-shape sat just inside
a 250 ms cap. That is the whole shape of the STOP-THE-LINE — a contract with
no margin, read through an instrument that doubled the number and a machine
that trebled it. The fix restores the margin; the structural clause is what
makes the margin permanent.

**The middle clause is red on base, and red without a stopwatch.** Run against
`229a3cd`'s `analysis` (same harness, same document, arms selected by
`DB_ARM`):

```
arm=base    registrations=68
  _surviving_claimants: admissible_text called 68x  -> FAIL
  detection_report    : admissible_text called 68x  -> FAIL
arm=branch  registrations=68
  _surviving_claimants: admissible_text called 1x   -> PASS
  detection_report    : admissible_text called 1x   -> PASS
```

That is the defect stated as a number a loaded machine cannot change. The
first clause cannot run against base at all — there is no `PreparedDocument`
to count preparations on — so this is the one that carries the red.

## DT6. Results

Paired, arms alternating in one command, production seam
(`_surviving_claimants`). **Two load regimes**, because the point of the
exercise is that a reading has to survive both. *Loaded* is best-of-5 with
roughly ten cells sharing the machine; *quiet* is the minimum over three
alternating rounds of best-of-7, taken later when the machine was down to
three processes.

| measurement | base loaded | branch loaded | base quiet | branch quiet |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| worst pinned document | 267.7 ms | **128.6 ms** | 118.1 ms | **50.4 ms** |
| largest pinned (62,702 chars) | 241.7 ms | **142.2 ms** | 110.2 ms | **50.6 ms** |
| one pass over the 109 pinned | 8.14 s | **4.57 s** | 5.96 s | **1.73 s** |
| 40 largest archive docs, worst (139,737 chars) | 591.4 ms | **318.9 ms** | 339.0 ms | **124.8 ms** |
| 40 largest archive docs, median | 320.4 ms | **170.6 ms** | 193.0 ms | **69.9 ms** |
| text preparations per document | 104 | **33** | 104 | **33** |
| full-archive equivalence pass (3,367 docs × 2 sweeps) | ~400 s | **~135 s** | | |

Speedup 1.7–2.1× loaded, 2.2–2.8× quiet; the whole-corpus pass 3.4× quiet.
Projected to 80 registrations from the worst pinned reading: base **315 ms
loaded / 139 ms quiet**, branch **151 ms loaded / 59 ms quiet** — a 40% margin
under the ceiling in the worst regime measured, and 4.2× in the best.

The gap between the two regimes is the whole argument for the estimator: the
same quantity has been read anywhere from 50 ms to 310 ms on this machine
depending on nothing but what else was running.

And the shipped assertion's own computation, run on both arms after the
selection pass was corrected — min-of-five for **every** pinned document, the
worst of those, projected to 80 — twice each, alternating, on a quiet machine:

```
base    worst=  87.4 ms  Others/Altana/Altana june 26.pdf   projected@80= 102.8 ms  PASS
branch  worst=  50.5 ms  Others/Altana/Altana june 26.pdf   projected@80=  59.4 ms  PASS
base    worst=  89.8 ms  BofA/eStmt_2026-03-31 (3) (1).pdf  projected@80= 105.7 ms  PASS
branch  worst=  51.1 ms  Others/Altana/Altana june 26.pdf   projected@80=  60.1 ms  PASS
```

Two things worth keeping. The branch picks the same document both times — the
largest one, which is what a correct selection should pick — while the base
wobbles between two of near-equal cost, which is the noise the old
single-sample selection used to amplify into a 44% understatement. And both
arms PASS quiet, which is the DT5 point restated: the wall-clock clause is not
the one that carries the red on base.

## DT7. The equivalence proof

For every archive sha with text offline, both arms recorded, per document:

* the surviving claimant set after `supersedes` pruning, with scores;
* the **complete** `detection_report` — all 68 registrations' `(score,
  matched marker ids, excluded_by)`.

3,367 documents, 3,367 identical records, one identical digest per arm:
`9A7DEAA1468033FA0966B429742660C2F9023EEAE4707ECEDEFF67C0C1672B15`.
Documents differing: **0**. Claim-set composition, unchanged on both arms:
2,552 single-claimant · 0 ambiguous · 815 unclaimed.

This is strictly more than the binding proof asked for — it pins the near-miss
vector telemetry publishes, not only the winner and the claimants.

### DT7.1 The crash arm — the W3-1 guard, exercised on purpose

Ocean's addendum is right that the sweep above proves equivalence only on the
non-raising path: not one of the 68 registrations raised on any of the 3,367
documents, so the `_guarded` seam was never entered. The proof was therefore
re-run with five synthetic registrations injected, covering every place a
registration's own code runs during detection:

| injected | raises in |
|---|---|
| `zz_boom_required` | a REQUIRED marker |
| `zz_boom_excluding` | an EXCLUDING marker — the first loop, before any other kind runs |
| `zz_boom_exclusive` | an EXCLUSIVE marker |
| `zz_boom_normalize` | the parser's own normalization — i.e. inside `PreparedDocument.text_for` |
| `zz_shares_a_marker` | nothing; it shares a marker test object with a crashing sibling, so the prepared-text memo runs alongside the guard |

73 registrations × 3,367 documents, both arms, recording the claimant set, the
full detection report **and** the `ParserFailure` list:

```
base   : 3367 docs  digest 0A8990FF80F8D648A79E2BCB5767797F79BE719B2F65BBD1EF90E75E88717256
branch : 3367 docs  digest 0A8990FF80F8D648A79E2BCB5767797F79BE719B2F65BBD1EF90E75E88717256
documents whose detection differs: 0

recorded ParserFailures, per arm:
   ('zz_boom_excluding', 'detect', 'KeyError')   3367
   ('zz_boom_exclusive', 'detect', 'IndexError') 3367
   ('zz_boom_normalize', 'detect', 'TypeError')  3367
   ('zz_boom_required',  'detect', 'ValueError') 3367
scores the four crashing registrations received: 0.0, on all 3,367
crashing registrations that ever claimed: 0
```

13,468 crash events, every one of them fail-closed to `Detection(0.0)`,
recorded as a `ParserFailure` carrying the exception CLASS NAME and nothing
else, and identical on both arms. The guard is preserved by evidence and not
only by construction: `safe_detect` still wraps `detect_prepared` in
`_guarded`, and a marker that raises is never memoized — the exception
propagates to the guard on every call, which
`test_a_marker_that_raises_is_not_memoized_and_still_reaches_the_guard` pins
at unit scale by asserting two consecutive `safe_detect` calls each record
their own `ParserFailure`.

## DT9. Carried findings and questions for Ocean

1. **The discovery run sweeps every document TWICE, and the second sweep can
   now be made free.** `analysis/pipeline.analyze_markdown` calls `resolve`,
   and `telemetry/collect.score_vector` then calls `detection_report` on the
   same markdown — a second full sweep, correctly justified in its own
   docstring as admissible because `detect` is pure. With this seam in place
   the first sweep's `PreparedDocument` could be handed to the second and the
   second would cost almost nothing, halving the discovery run's detection
   cost again. Not done here: it needs `analysis/pipeline.py` and
   `telemetry/collect.py`, both outside this cell's ownership, and both live
   in batch 4.
2. **Where the remaining 149 ms is, so the shaving cards can be written against
   evidence.** On the largest pinned document, after this cell:

   | | cost | owner |
   |---|---|---|
   | `community_section._clean` | 10.6 ms | `analysis/community_section.py` |
   | `td_canada_french.detection_text` | 10.5 ms | `analysis/td_canada_french.py` |
   | `chase_savings.detection_text` | 7.4 ms | `analysis/chase_savings.py` |
   | `square_checking.detection_text` | 6.6 ms | `analysis/square_checking.py` |
   | `regions.detection_text` | 3.7 ms | `analysis/regions.py` |
   | `glyph_damaged` markers (`rbc`, `rbc_french`, `cibc`) | 15.8 + 8.8 + 10.9 ms | `analysis/tables.py` |
   | `symitar` markers | 8.2 ms | `analysis/symitar.py` |

   Five normalizers are 39 ms of the 67 ms normalization stage; `glyph_damaged`
   is 35 ms of the 83 ms marker stage and is two `re.findall` over the whole
   document. Each is a small card in the owning module.
3. **`glyph_damaged` is wired to three registrations and the fourth
   over-threshold document is unprotected.** Not new — `analysis/tables.py`
   says so itself and W3 §RBCCIBC carded it as RC8.7 — but this cell is the
   first to price it: platform-wide wiring at today's cost would add ~12 ms per
   registration per document, which the budget cannot absorb 68 times. The memo
   in `PreparedDocument` makes it affordable *if* the registrations reading it
   share a normalized text; they do not today (`.upper()` vs
   `normalize_mojibake().upper()` vs CIBC's own). Wiring it platform-wide
   should be costed together with a shared normalizer.
4. **`PLANNED_REGISTRATIONS = 80` — ratified, and its limits recorded.** It is
   a floor on the cost at 80, not a bound (DT5): review measured
   projection ÷ actual at 1.00 and 0.79 for two growth shapes, the mean being
   diluted by the 32 registrations with no normalization. **Superlinear growth
   shapes other than the quadratic one this cell removed are caught by
   neither clause** — the load-independent clause is exact for
   per-registration preparation and silent about, say, a marker whose cost
   grows with the registry. If the registry passes ~80, the honest move is to
   re-measure rather than to trust the projection.
5. **`test_detect_sweep_stays_affordable_for_the_discovery_run` is still a
   wall-clock test, and wall-clock tests still flake.** Best-of-5 through the
   production seam with a 40% margin is a very different proposition from one
   sample with none, but if the batch sees another red the load-immune clause
   (`test_the_detect_sweep_prepares_each_document_once`) is the one to read
   first: if it is green, the structure is intact and the red is the machine.
6. **The pinned corpus under-represents the archive's document sizes.** The
   largest pinned document is 62,702 chars; the largest archive document is
   139,737, and the branch sweeps it in 319 ms loaded (124.8 ms quiet) — over
   the 250 ms ceiling in the loaded regime, for a document the budget test
   cannot see. The base sweeps it in 591 ms loaded / 339 ms quiet, so the fix
   moves it from over-budget in BOTH regimes to over-budget in one; the tail is
   improved and still uncovered. The ceiling is honest about the corpus it
   measures and silent about the tail. A per-character ceiling or a pinned
   large document would close it; both are decisions about the contract rather
   than fixes, so they are put here rather than taken.
7. **The archive markdown store and the A/B harness are reusable.** The
   session scratchpad `detbudget-5fb5b603/` holds `db_harness.py` (arm-selected
   production import with an assertion that catches measuring the wrong arm —
   it caught exactly that on the first draft), `archive_md.pkl` (all 3,367
   archive documents' markdown, one pickle, so two arms provably sweep
   identical bytes), `measure.py` (paired A/B, `DB_MODE=sweep|loop`),
   `equiv.py`, `equiv_crash.py` and `redcheck.py`. Any cell measuring a
   registry-wide cost or proving a detection-level equivalence can reuse them

## W2-1. Card C — the committed artifacts carry their page list

§WIRING W2 found half the approved ceremony inexecutable: `Regions/Regions.pdf`
is one of the six image-only pinned statements, every offline harness resolves
those from a committed markdown STRING, and the intake object's page list was
discarded when the artifact was committed. Offline, Regions could only ever be
analysed with `sheets=None`, and the check fail-closes — so the flag stood for
want of evidence rather than because a page was absent.

The remedy is the one §WIRING named: give the committed artifacts their page
list. **No OCR ran.** The D-3 archive store still holds one for all six, read by
direct file path (the sqlite index was never opened), and each was refused
unless it re-joins:

```
statement                              pages  D-3 model             re-joins byte-identical
Chase/Chase Business.pdf                   8  local-tesseract-ocr   True
Misc/Builder June 2026.pdf                 4  local-tesseract-ocr   True
Misc/Columbia May 26 complete.pdf          4  local-tesseract-ocr   True
Misc/First Farmers 2026 01-document.pdf    3  local-tesseract-ocr   True
Misc/KLR.May 31,2026 (1).pdf               7  local-tesseract-ocr   True
Regions/Regions.pdf                        3  local-tesseract-ocr   True
```

"Re-joins" means `StatementMarkdown(source_file, model, pages).to_markdown()`
equals the committed `.md` byte for byte, so the two halves provably come from
one intake run. `test_the_committed_page_list_rejoins_to_the_committed_markdown`
keeps that true, and `test_every_committed_artifact_carries_its_page_list`
asserts the presence of the list — necessary precisely because its ABSENCE is
fail-closed and would otherwise leave the gate green while the check stayed
blind.

The manifest is extended additively: existing fields untouched, each entry gains
`pages` and `pages_sha256`, and `build_corpus_cache.py` writes both halves so a
future rebuild cannot produce a one-sided artifact. `cached_pages` fail-closes on
absence and **raises** on alteration — silence weakens nothing, but a wrong page
list could clear a genuine finding. `.gitattributes` pins the new files against
CRLF rewriting for the same reason the markdown artifacts are pinned.

## W2-2. Card B — the count was not enough; the key carries the partition

§PIPEFIX P4b.5 prescribed adding "the sheet count" to the analysis key.
§WIRING W3 demonstrated that is quantitatively wrong, and this cell ships the
respecified form. `analysis_input_sha(markdown, sheets)` is now the stage's
input hash:

```python
def analysis_input_sha(markdown, sheets=None):
    return text_sha256(_canonical_json({
        "text": text_sha256(admissible_text(markdown)),
        "sheets": sheets_sha256(sheets),
    }))

def sheets_sha256(sheets):
    if sheets is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(sheets, str):
        raise TypeError(...)
    return text_sha256(_canonical_json([text_sha256(sheet) for sheet in sheets]))
```

Three properties, each deliberate:

* **Per-sheet digests, not the concatenation.** The whole point is the
  BOUNDARIES — `["ab", "c"]` and `["a", "bc"]` must not collide, and joining
  them makes them identical. §WIRING's own counterexample is now a test:
  two page lists of the same LENGTH rendering to the same admissible markdown
  with opposite answers on `missing_declared_statement_page`
  (`test_the_sheet_partition_is_analysis_key_material`).
* **`None` and `[]` hash differently.** No evidence of page structure is not
  the same fact as a document with no sheets, and only the first fail-closes.
* **`str` is refused.** The same footgun `assess_document_integrity` refuses:
  `sheets=markdown` type-checks and iterates one character per sheet. In the
  analysis it would clear a fraud-relevant flag; in the cache it would
  partition on nonsense while looking like evidence.

It lives in the INPUT hash, not in `analysis_settings_key`: the settings key is
a per-RUN constant and the telemetry observer's read-only artifact join indexes
the whole artifact table on one value of it, so a per-document value there
would blind that instrument while it reported nothing wrong.

**The second copy of the derivation is gone rather than updated.** The
observer's join used to recompose `text_sha256(admissible_text(markdown))`
itself — the copy the FILENAME-BOUNDARY lesson warned about, which had already
gone stale once. It now imports `analysis_input_sha` and supplies the page list
it was already reconstructing. Repo-wide grep for `admissible_text` /
`text_sha256` / `analysis_settings_key` finds no third copy in repo code; the
one outside the repo (WIRING-1's scratchpad `keys.py`, §WIRING W6.5) is now
stale as predicted.

**This invalidates the whole v12 analysis cache by construction** — every
document's input hash changes, whether or not its caller supplies a page list.
Expected and chosen; Ocean's composed stage bump covers the re-measurement.

**And here is the consequence, stated so nobody reads it as a defect.** On
merge, all ~23,598 analysis entries in the store resolve under the OLD
text-only key and **0** under the new one, so the stated-counts observer's
`_ArtifactJoin` resolves **nothing**: `observe_run` reports
`REASON_PAYLOAD_ABSENT` on every row, archive-wide, and its rollup is empty.
That is the cache invalidation showing through the instrument that reads the
cache — not a broken join. It fails safe (an unresolvable payload is never
guessed) and it **self-heals at the train's cold run**, when the archive is
re-analyzed at the bumped stage version and every key is written in the new
form. No action is needed, and none should be taken on the strength of an empty
rollup measured before that run.

Worth one more sentence because it is the reason this needs saying at all: the
join's own tests seed their fixture through `cached_analysis`, so they write
and read the same (new) key and **stay green straight through the blindness**.
Nothing in CI can warn about it; only an empty rollup over the real archive
shows it, and that is exactly what an unwarned reader would misdiagnose.

### The `sheets_sha256` contract, and why it is a guard rather than a note

Ocean's review asked for the real contract to be stated or enforced. It is
ENFORCED, because two of the three failure modes are silent:

* **`str`** — refused already, the `assess_document_integrity` footgun one
  layer down.
* **a one-shot iterable** (generator, `map`, a bare iterator) — now refused.
  Hashing CONSUMES it and the caller then hands the analysis an empty sequence:
  the analysis fail-closes, so the answer is conservative, but it is stored
  under the key of a partition that WAS proven, and a later caller supplying
  the same pages properly is served that fail-closed answer. Nothing in the
  payload looks wrong. A note would not have caught it; the guard does.
* **non-`str` members** — now refused *by index*, because the alternative is an
  `AttributeError` raised inside `text_sha256` that names neither the sheet nor
  the call site.

The accepted type is therefore a re-iterable `Sequence[str]`, checked with
`collections.abc.Sequence` rather than the typing alias so the check is real at
runtime. Every production caller already passes a list (`document.pages`,
`cached_pages`). Only a call site can reach any of these — no document's
content can — so raising costs nothing at runtime and fails a mis-wiring
loudly. Pinned by `test_a_one_shot_iterable_of_sheets_is_refused` and
`test_a_non_string_sheet_is_refused_by_name`.

**Order is key material, and that is deliberate conservatism.** `["a", "b"]`
and `["b", "a"]` hash differently, so three sheets have six permutations and
six keys for one answer — over-partitioning, which this module's contract has
always called the safe direction: it costs a recompute and never returns a
stale artifact. It is also unreachable in production, since the markdown is
rendered from the same ordered list that is hashed, so the cost is theoretical.
Recorded rather than removed, and pinned by
`test_sheet_order_is_key_material_and_that_is_deliberate`.

## CM0. Summary

`CountSemantics` had two states and the archive has three. A bank that
prints `N Checks/Debits` beside a separate `Service Charges` line is not
printing an unknowable figure — it is printing a **known figure about a
known subset**, and the difference between that subset and our rows is a row
class the bank named on the same page. COUNTS-P1 called that class
incomparable because equality would manufacture flags on it; COUNTS-P3
confirmed the evidence (22 of 22, 26/9) and **refused both promotions
anyway**, because flipping `comparable` installs the equality test the
mapping exists to avoid, and it measured the price: 11 and 9 documents
`validated` → `review` on ledgers that reconcile to the cent, four of the 11
being pinned corpus PASS documents the gate cannot see move.

This cell adds the third state and promotes the two entries on it. The
result is the one the design bar asked for: **0 outcome movers, 0 false
mismatch flags, and a constructed genuine mismatch that the mapping catches
and the equality test is blind to.**

## CM1. The schema — declarative, closed, and printed-evidence-only

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CountMapping:
    rule: str                  # one of RULES
    printed_field: str         # one of PRINTED_EVIDENCE_FIELDS
    excluded_row_class: str    # the sentence the mapping is making
```

`PRINTED_EVIDENCE_FIELDS = ("stated_service_charge",)`, and `RULES` is
**derived** from `_RULE_ADJUSTMENTS`, the `name -> arithmetic` dict
`adjustment` dispatches through. Both are checked in `__post_init__`, not at
the call site, so **an entry that could not be applied cannot be written**.
There is deliberately no callable ON THE ENTRY: a table whose behaviour is a
function object somewhere else is not a table a reviewer can audit, and the
whole value of `count_semantics.py` is that a reviewer can check it against a
printed page.

The derivation is a self-review finding closed before any proof ran. The
first draft had `RULES` as a literal tuple beside a hand-written `if`, so a
second rule could be NAMED without being IMPLEMENTED and `adjustment` would
silently keep applying the first one — the unenforced-enum shape. Deriving
the vocabulary from the implementations makes that unrepresentable, and
`test_a_rule_cannot_be_named_without_being_implemented` pins it.

Three properties carry the design, each asserted rather than promised:

1. **Printed evidence only.** `stated_service_charge` is a figure the parser
   lifted off the printed summary cell, so the expected side is still
   evidence off the page. A mapping able to read anything derived from
   `transactions` would let a parser satisfy the check with its own output —
   the one property the whole check exists to have.
   `test_a_mapping_may_read_bank_printed_evidence_only` pins the allowlist
   against `Statement.model_fields` and pins that `printed_evidence` refuses
   any other name.
2. **A mapping implies `comparable=True`.** An entry that declares an
   adjustment and then refuses to compare leaves the adjustment unreachable —
   a decision that has not been made, wearing the costume of one.
   `CountSemantics.__post_init__` raises.
3. **One function, two callers.** `expected_count(parser_id, direction,
   printed, source)` is called by `analysis/reconcile.py` (which decides what
   is published) and by the phase-1 count observer (which predicts it), and
   `source` may be a `Statement` **or** the serialized payload mapping,
   because those are the two shapes that exist. `test_the_observer_and_the_
   check_read_one_table` now asserts the identity of the function as well as
   of the table: one shared table with two different adjustments is the same
   defect wearing a different hat.

`expected_count` is the identity for 29 of the 31 parsers in the table and
for everything outside it, which is what
`test_expected_count_is_the_identity_wherever_there_is_no_mapping` says out
loud rather than leaving to the absence of a failing test.

**`> 0`, not truthiness.** `stated_service_charge` is documented as a POSITIVE
magnitude; a negative reading would be a refund, and a refund is never a DEBIT
row under either mapped parser — `first_citizens` emits **no row at all**
(`_service_charge_posting` returns None on `charge <= 0`,
`analysis/first_citizens.py:506-507`), and `capital_one` reads its detail rows
and would record the refund in the column the document printed it in. (The
first draft of both the entry and this paragraph said "a CREDIT row", which is
true of at most one of the two and false of the one whose parser declines to
post it at all — review D4.) Zero, `None`, a string, a bool and a negative all
adjust by nothing: fail-closed in every direction.

**And the threshold is `> 0`, not `>= 0.01`** — a printed sub-cent charge
would adjust by one. Stated rather than guarded, because no bank in the
archive prints one and rounding money to the cent belongs to
`analysis/reconcile.py`, which owns the tolerances, rather than to this table.
Immaterial today; on the record so it is a known limit and not a discovery.

## CM2. Why the naive promotion is the wrong tool, in numbers already measured

Not re-argued here; §COUNTSP3 CP3 ran it end to end and this cell's whole
premise is those two rows:

| counterfactual | flag movers | outcome movers |
|---|---|---|
| `capital_one:debit` → plain COMPARABLE | 12 | **11 `validated/approved` → `review/integrity_flags`** (the 12th is already withheld) |
| `first_citizens:debit` → plain COMPARABLE | 9 | **9 `validated/approved` → `review/integrity_flags`** |

Twenty manufactured review cases on ledgers that reconcile to the cent, and
`corpus_gate.py` GREEN over four pinned documents moving inside its PASS
bucket. That is what the mapping field is for.

## CM3. The two entries, measured fresh

Population identity was recovered the way §COUNTSP3 established, because the
run of record's `rows.csv` still leaves `parser_id` EMPTY on every
analysis-cache hit — **119 distinct documents** (110 `validated`, 6 `review`,
3 `withheld`), the same hole, unchanged at v12. Identity came from replaying
`parser_registry.resolve` over the reconstructed markdown, and its fidelity
was proven before its results were believed: on all 52 candidate-family
documents that DO carry a `parser_id`, the replay reproduced it, **52 of 52**.
Enriched, the families land on their historical figures — `capital_one` 22
(18 in `rows.csv`), `first_citizens` 35 (34), `texas_bank` 1 (0).

Cached OCR and analysis artifacts were addressed **arithmetically**
(`cache_key(stage, input_sha, settings_key)` →
`webapp_data/artifacts/<stage>/<key[:2]>/<key>.json`) across the three OCR
settings partitions. **The sqlite index was never opened.** Zero OCR, zero
model calls, **$0.00**.

| family | documents | zero charge | billed | raw debit delta | under the mapping | credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `capital_one` | 22 | 10 | 12 | `+0` on all 10, `+1` on all 12 | **22/22 agree** | 22/22 |
| `first_citizens` | 35 | 26 | 9 | `+0` on all 26, `+1` on all 9 | **35/35 agree** | 35/35 |
| `texas_bank` | 1 | 0 | 1 | `+1` | 1/1 (**not promoted** — CM11) | 1/1 |

This reproduces §DB8's 22, §FI14.3's 26/9 and §COUNTSP3's whole CP2 table on
the current archive, from a cold re-derivation.

**The control arm exists and is what makes the mapping falsifiable.** Ten
capital_one and twenty-six first_citizens documents bill a ZERO charge and
agree exactly, so `+1 always` and `+1 iff charged` are *distinguishable* on
this archive — the indistinguishability §DB8 warned about on the old
12-document population, and the reason the stale sentence in the
`capital_one:debit` entry (§COUNTSP3 CP4.1, left for Ocean) is corrected in
place by this cell, which owns the entry.

**Corroboration that the `+1` row IS the charge**, rather than a coincidence
of arithmetic: on every one of the 12 + 9 + 1 billed documents there is a
DEBIT row whose magnitude equals the printed service charge, and every such
row posts as an OUTFLOW — so the archive carries no refunded cycle, which is
the second falsifier's control. Two of the 12 capital_one documents carry a
second debit row of the same magnitude by coincidence, which the count
arithmetic does not depend on and which is recorded so nobody reads the
corroboration as tighter than it is. And the limit of that evidence is
written into the entry: `stated_service_charge` is a MAGNITUDE, so the field
the mapping reads cannot tell a charge from a refund at all — the bound comes
entirely from the two summary readers, one of which refuses a contradicting
sign and one of which does not.

**Money is silent throughout**, which is the entire point of a count check:
`debit_coverage` is 1.00 on all 22 capital_one and on 31 of 35
first_citizens (the other 4 print no debit total), `sum_delta` is 0.00 on all
57, and **not one of the 57 documents carries any integrity flag today.**

### CM3.0 The money-side sentence was wrong, and correcting it is the best argument in the cell

The `capital_one:debit` entry has carried this since COUNTS-P1: *"its money
is inside the printed debit TOTAL."* It was never measured. It is false.

On all 12 billed capital_one documents (and all 9 first_citizens, and the
one texas_bank), `beginning + credits - printed debits` misses `ending` by
exactly the charge and closes only with the charge subtracted SEPARATELY. The
charge is **outside** the printed debit total.

That matters twice.

1. **Count scope and money scope AGREE on this bank**, and both exclude the
   charge. BofA's defect — the one BOFA-COUNTS was spent removing — was
   precisely that they did NOT agree there, and the repair path read one off
   the other. Here there is nothing to read off anything: both figures
   exclude the same printed line.
2. **The platform already applies this exact mapping to the debit TOTAL.**
   `_debit_coverage_target` (`analysis/reconcile.py:63-84`) adds
   `stated_service_charge` back to the printed debit total whenever the
   summary's own arithmetic says the charge sits outside it — same printed
   field, same `+ charge`, shipping since before COUNTS-P1, and firing on
   every one of these 12 documents. The count mapping is that adjustment's
   twin, and the asymmetry this cell removes is that the money side has had
   it for a year while the count side was called "incomparable".

Both entries now carry the measurement, and
`test_the_capital_one_entry_records_the_money_side_and_its_correction` pins
the correction so it cannot quietly revert.

### CM3.1 The first_citizens debit direction is the informative one

Worth stating because the family's credit direction is not. `_matches`
refuses the document unless each of the four printed sections' parsed posting
count equals the count the bank printed for it, so the credit direction's
35/35 is a TAUTOLOGY (§COUNTSP3 recorded it as one). `billed` is appended
**outside all four gated sections**, so the mapped debit comparison tests
exactly one thing nothing else tests: **that the service-charge posting was
recovered iff the bank billed one.** It is the platform's only per-document
check on `_service_charge_posting`. The same is true of `capital_one`, which
gates on no count at all.

## CM4. The clause §FI14.3 asked for, and why it is deliberately absent

§FI14.3 proposed the mapping as `+1 where the billed service charge was
**RECOVERED AS A POSTING**`, because `_service_charge_posting` returns
nothing when the itemisation cannot be located, so a charged document whose
charge was not found is `+0` and a naive "+1 iff charged" would flag it.

That clause is **not in the mapping**, and the reason is independence: "was
it recovered as a posting" is a fact about OUR ROWS. An expected side that
reads the captured side is exactly what the phase-1 sign-off's independence
rule forbids, and it would let the parser satisfy the check with its own
output — the property `FORBIDDEN_EXPECTED_SOURCES` exists to protect.

So the mapping keys on the PRINTED charge, and the billed-but-not-recovered
case **flags**. That is correct rather than costly: a billed charge the
parser could not locate is a debit row the ledger is missing, which the
module docstring already names as the one path that can still fail
reconciliation. The count check becomes a second, independent witness to that
defect instead of being blinded to it by an exemption written in its own
favour.

**The arm is UNEXERCISED and the entry says so** — the disclosure standard
§COUNTSP3 D2 made binding. All 9 charged first_citizens documents in the
archive were located, so **0 documents exercise the path** and the claim that
flagging it is right rests on the argument above, not on a measurement.

## CM5. Application — one key, one arithmetic

`reconcile` had no way to know which parser claimed the document, so the
mapping could not be applied where the expected side is read. It now takes
`parser_id` as a keyword whose default is `None`:

```python
def reconcile(stmt: Statement, *, parser_id: str | None = None) -> ReconResult:
```

`reconcile(stmt)` — every caller outside the pipeline, and every test written
before mappings existed — is unchanged and fail-closed: no claim, no
adjustment, the raw printed figure.

The comparison hunk, verbatim:

```python
    if stmt.transactions and not aggregate_backed:
        if stmt.stated_credit_count is not None:
            captured_credit_count = sum(
                1 for t in stmt.transactions if t.direction == "credit"
            )
            expected_credit_count = expected_count(
                parser_id, "credit", stmt.stated_credit_count, stmt
            )
            credit_count_matches = captured_credit_count == expected_credit_count
        if stmt.stated_debit_count is not None:
            captured_debit_count = sum(
                1 for t in stmt.transactions if t.direction == "debit"
            )
            expected_debit_count = expected_count(
                parser_id, "debit", stmt.stated_debit_count, stmt
            )
            debit_count_matches = captured_debit_count == expected_debit_count
```

Still no `issues.append` in the block — `ok` gates the ADB, so a count may
never withhold a document, and
`test_a_mapped_direction_still_appends_no_reconciliation_issue` pins it on
the new arm as well.

**`expected_credit_count` / `expected_debit_count` are published** beside the
verdict. The alternative is a payload reading `stated_debit_count 12 /
captured_debit_count 13 / stated_debit_count_matches true`, which is only not
a contradiction if the reader knows the table — one field with two meanings,
the defect BOFA-COUNTS was spent removing. The cost is two keys on every
payload's reconciliation block, and the precedent is COUNTS-P2, which added
four.

**The pipeline change is three lines, and the drift hazard it closes is one
this cell CREATED.** Stated as what it is rather than as a free win: before
this cell `reconcile` had no parser key at all, so there was nothing to drift.
Keying it is what makes two derivations of "which parser claimed this"
possible — `reconcile` now APPLIES a table row's mapping and
`assess_document_integrity` decides whether the result may be flagged, and two
copies of that expression could send them to different rows (applying
capital_one's adjustment and judging it under nobody's semantics, or the
reverse). Single-sourcing the key through
`count_semantics.claiming_parser_id` closes the hazard the same commit opened,
which is a good outcome and not a virtue. What makes it stay closed is the
test, not the intention:
`test_the_reconciler_and_the_flag_gate_key_on_the_same_claim` asserts that the
pipeline derives BOTH keys from that one function and that every `reconcile(`
call site names one.

**The observer applies the same function.** `OBSERVER_VERSION` 3 → 4, its
contract being "bumped when the vocabulary, the evaluation order or the
semantics table changes"; `DirectionObservation` gained `expected` for the
same legibility reason as the payload; and the sign-keyed counterfactual now
runs against `expected` rather than `stated`, because that counterfactual
changes ONE thing — the key the captured side is counted on — and must not
silently change the expected side too.

**What a v4 rollup will actually print, which is not 57** (review D2). The
version note says 57 documents leave `semantics_incomparable` for `match`, and
that is the population WITH PARSER IDENTITY AVAILABLE — the number this cell
measured, using the dispatch replay. The SHIPPED runner reads `parser_id` off
`rows.csv`, so on a bare pre-projection run it reports **52**: the
analysis-cache-hit hole leaves the column empty on 4 billed `capital_one` and
1 `first_citizens` document, and an unknown parser is `unsurveyed_parser`,
never compared. The gap closes when DISCOVERY-OBS's projection lands in the
same train. Until then the instrument under-reports and **fails closed**,
which is the right direction for it to be wrong in, and the version note now
carries both numbers so a reader diffing two rollups is not left to discover
the difference.

## CM6. The constructed genuine mismatch — and what it says about the field

The design bar asked for a fixture whose captured count is off by two — one
charge and one genuinely missing row. Built exactly that way, and the point
is that **the two errors offset**, which is what makes it the sharpest
argument in the cell:

> The bank printed `Checks/Debits (2)` and billed a charge, so a complete
> ledger carries THREE debit rows. This one carries two — the charge row is
> present and one printed row was dropped.
>
> The **equality test compares 2 against the printed 2 and reports MATCH** —
> a ledger missing a posting, called clean. The **mapping compares 2 against
> 3 and flags.**

So the field is not only a false-positive suppressor: it is what makes this
class visible at all. `test_the_mapping_catches_a_dropped_row_the_equality_
test_is_blind_to` runs it on both promoted parsers, asserts the flag, asserts
`risk_level == "review"`, asserts `recon.ok is True` and
`possible_document_issue is False` (advisory, never a withholding), asserts
`classify_outcome` returns `("review", "integrity_flags")` — and then asserts
the counterfactual: `reconcile(stmt)` without the claim reports
`expected_debit_count == 2` and `matches is True`, seeing nothing.

# §DISCOBS — the row that forgot which parser answered it

Measurement infrastructure only. `analysis/`, `ocr/`, `telemetry/` and
`webapp/` carry a **zero-line diff**; no published payload changes; no document
moves. `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` is deliberately untouched — nothing this cell
does can change a cached artifact's contents, which is the property the whole
projection depends on.

Two blind spots in `rows.csv`, both named in the batch-2 and batch-4 logs and
both left open until now.

## DO0. Summary

| # | blind spot | what it cost | fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **A cache-served row carried no parser identity at all.** On a D-3 analysis cache hit `analyze_markdown` never runs, so no `Dispatch` exists and `parser_id` / `parser_score` / `dispatch_outcome` / `candidates` were all blank. `discovery/report.py` then dropped the document from the coverage denominator. | On a fully warm run this is not a rounding error — it is an inversion. The analysis cache stores **successes only** (a refusal raises and nothing is cached), so the rows that lose their verdict are exactly the CLAIMED ones, while every unclaimed document re-dispatches live and stays in the denominator. Coverage tends to **0%** as the cache warms. The −11.9% printed in batch 2 was this at partial warmth, and COUNTS-P3's counterfactual denominators were short by the same set. | Re-resolve the identity from the detection sweep the row already pays for, and **mark it** `parser_id_source=live_detect` so an observation and a reconstruction are never confused. |
| 2 | **The folder-agreement rollup filed template claims as label disagreements.** The honest-unknown-issuer registrations (§U) claim a document TEMPLATE and publish `Statement.bank = None`; the matcher then had only the registration's template name to compare against a folder's bank name. | Six documents printed as `Desjardins -> releve_facturation` in the one ranking a human works through — an invitation to rename the parser after the folder, which §U4.1's evidence forbids and `tests/test_parser_detection_markers.py` exists to prevent. | Its own rollup class, `template_claim`, with its own ranked pairs and the §U D3 warning in the code. |

## DO1. The survey: what a cached analysis payload actually holds

The card said "project parser identity into the row from the cached payload".
The payload cannot supply it. Surveyed field by field
(`analysis/serialization.py:report_to_dict`):

| field | holds | usable as parser identity? |
|---|---|---|
| `detection` | `analysis.detect.DetectionResult` — known funders, potential lenders, insurance providers, recurring debits, evidence lists | **No.** This is the FINANCIAL detection layer. The name collision with parser detection is the trap; there is not one parser fact in it. |
| `model_used` | `f"{bank_label}-deterministic"`, built from the extracted `Statement.bank` (`analysis/pipeline.py:545`) | **No.** A bank label, lower-cased and hyphenated — not a parser id, and not unique to one parser: several registrations share a bank label, and the §U registrations publish `bank=None`, which renders as the literal `bank-deterministic`. |
| `statement.bank` | the extracted issuer | **No**, and already on the row as `statement_bank`. |
| `quality`, `integrity` | flags, notes, risk level | **No.** A parser reaches them only as English inside a note. |
| `classifications`, `reconciliation`, `metrics`, `escalated` | financial output | No. |

So identity is **genuinely absent**, and the card's own fallback applies:
re-resolve detection live and mark the provenance. That is also the option
`H3_SCHEMA.md §5.3` pre-ranked — *"`detection_report()` alone, no seam …
insufficient [for telemetry] — but it is the right fallback for cache hits
(§5.4)"* — and it avoids the alternative §5.4 explicitly recommends against:
persisting the dispatch INTO the cached artifact, which changes the payload
shape and needs an `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` bump. This cell's binding
constraint was byte-identical payloads, so that door was closed anyway.

## DO2. Why one detection sweep names the parser exactly

The projection is not a guess dressed up as a measurement. In
`parse_mode="deterministic"` — the only mode discovery uses —
`analyze_markdown` produces a payload on **exactly one path**: a claiming
parser returned a statement. Every other `resolve` outcome raises before a
payload exists:

| `resolve` outcome | deterministic mode | payload? |
|---|---|---|
| `ambiguous` (>1 survivor after `supersedes`) | `AmbiguousParserError` | no |
| `parser_exception` | `ParserCrashError` | no |
| `unclaimed` (0 survivors, or the sole survivor declined) | `RuntimeError` | no |
| `claimed` | returns | **yes** |

And `resolve` decides `ambiguous` **before any parse runs**. So a cached
payload is itself the evidence that the sweep had exactly one survivor, that
its `parse` succeeded, that `attempted` was empty and that the outcome was
`claimed`. `_sole_surviving_claimant` reproduces that survivor from the score
vector: claimants are `score >= CLAIM_THRESHOLD`, `dominated` is computed over
all claimants before pruning (exactly as `_surviving_claimants` does), and one
survivor is required — never "the best of several".

Three properties make the reproduction exact rather than approximate:

1. `telemetry.score_vector` is `detection_report`, i.e. the same `safe_detect`
   sweep over the same `PreparedDocument` that `resolve` runs, and `detect` is
   pure and total by the R-3 protocol contract. This is `score_vector`'s own
   documented argument for why it may re-sweep where re-calling `resolve` was
   inadmissible.
2. `score_vector` rounds to six decimals, and every score the registry can
   produce is already six-decimal exact (`round(..., 6)`, or the literals `0.5`
   and `1.0`), so the rounding is the identity and cannot move a registration
   across the threshold. Zeros are dropped; a claimant is never a zero.
3. **The registry that answers today is the registry that produced the
   artifact — within one registry composition, and not across a mid-wave
   change.** The first draft of this property said the composition is
   guaranteed, "because a registry change bumps `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION`,
   which invalidates the artifact." That is `webapp/artifact_cache.py`'s
   stated rule and it is **false about this repository's process**, which
   composes the bump at wave end. Measured: the three commits that added
   `supersedes` edges — `6bcaf85` (SCANB), `c59f98a` (community_section),
   `50bd704` (chase_savings) — each touched
   `analysis/parser_registry_entries.py` and none of them touched
   `webapp/artifact_cache.py`. The window is real and it is the normal case
   mid-wave, not an accident.

   What that costs, stated precisely. Inside such a window a warm run can hold
   a payload authored by a parser that TODAY loses a `supersedes` contest.
   Today's sweep then names exactly one survivor — the new narrow winner —
   confidently and wrongly, and the row reads that parser with `live_detect`
   provenance while the financial content came from the superseded one.
   **One survivor is not a symptom, so DO3's fail-closed branch never fires
   for this shape**; it catches the zero-survivor and multi-survivor cases
   only. Saying otherwise would be exactly the kind of tidy-but-false
   invariant this log exists to catch.

   What it does NOT cost: this is a **stale-cache corruption the projection
   inherits, not one it creates.** Before this cell, that same warm run served
   that same stale payload and published that same outcome; the row simply
   carried no `parser_id`, which is blank rather than right. Naming today's
   winner and marking it a reconstruction is strictly more visible than naming
   nobody, and the outcome — the thing the wave measures — is identical either
   way.

   **REGFP, carried card, deliberately not implemented here.** The structural
   fix is to make the registry composition part of the analysis cache key: a
   registry fingerprint component in `analysis_settings_key` (ids + bands +
   `supersedes` edges), or, cheaper, a guard test that ties any change to the
   registry composition to an `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` change in the same
   commit. Cache-key material is WIRING/Ocean territory and outside this
   cell's ownership, so it is named and left. `dispatch_inconclusive` (DO6) is
   the instrument that would show the other half of it arriving.

**Measured, not argued.** All 109 pinned documents, projection vs `resolve`
itself: identical `parser_id` and identical score, **109/109, zero
mismatches**. The archive arm is DO5.

**No second sweep is paid for.** `score_vector` already ran on every row for
the near-miss vector; the call was hoisted three lines and read twice.

## DO3. Fail-closed, twice, and one thing deliberately not reconstructed

* **The generic structurer** (W3-3c, opt-in, off) is the one branch that
  publishes a payload with no parser behind it. A `model_used ==
  STRUCTURER_MODEL` payload projects nothing.
* **An inconclusive sweep** — zero survivors, or more than one, while a payload
  exists — means the DO2 invariant has been broken by a stale artifact. The
  projection names nobody and marks `unavailable`. A finding, not a blank, and
  never a pick.
* **`parser_exceptions` is NOT reconstructed.** A detect-stage crash in some
  other registration is part of the observed `Dispatch` and is unrecoverable
  from a score vector — a crashed detect scores 0.0 and 0.0 is dropped. The
  column stays empty and says nothing, rather than saying "no parser crashed".
  `attempted` is empty because DO2 proves it was.

The vocabulary, so the instrument can tell:

| `parser_id_source` | meaning |
|---|---|
| `live_dispatch` | `analyze_markdown` ran and the runner observed its `Dispatch`. The verdict is an observation — including `unclaimed`, where the observation is that nobody claimed. |
| `live_detect` | analysis served from the D-3 cache; identity re-derived from a live detection sweep. |
| `unavailable` | analysis served from cache and the sweep could not name one parser (or the structurer produced the payload). |
| `""` | the analysis stage never ran for this document (deferred, invalid PDF, OCR failure). Not a provenance, an absence. |

There is no `cache` value because DO1 found nothing in the payload to source
one from. An enum member that can never be emitted is worse than a documented
absence.

## DO4. The second hole: `template_claim`

`folder_agreement` compares the parser's claim against the analyst's folder
label. For a §U registration there is nothing on the claim side to compare:
the registration is named after a document TEMPLATE ("Releve de Compte
Statement Template", "Core Processor Sectioned Platform") and it publishes
`Statement.bank = None` **on purpose**, because the paper names no issuer.
Comparing a template name to a bank name is a category error, not a
disagreement.

Measured on the run of record `c924d751`, over its 3,291 dispatched rows:

| parser | no-issuer claims | where they landed before |
|---|---|---|
| `releve_facturation` | 16 | 10 `unlabelled_folder` (`Unidentified/`), **6 `label_unmatched` (`Desjardins/`)** |
| `balance_by_date` | 11 | 11 `unlabelled_folder` |
| `core_processor_sectioned` | 9 | 9 `unlabelled_folder` |
| `community_section` | 5 | 5 `unlabelled_folder` |
| **total** | **41** | 35 exempt already, 6 filed as disagreements |

All 41 come from those four template registrations, and no bank-specific
parser appears among them — **but that is a census of today's data, not a
structural guarantee, and the review was right to make me say so.** At least
**five** registrations can publish `bank=None` by design: the four above plus
`fiserv_premier`, which deliberately declines to publish a capitalized run in
front of an address as an identity ("a capitalized run in front of an address
is not an identity" — its own `_issuer` docstring). It is absent from the 41
only because **all ten documents it claimed happened to print a readable
issuer** — a fact about this archive, not about the registry. It is registered
under a platform name too ("Fiserv Premier"), so the class would still be
right for it; the point is that nothing here ENFORCES the coincidence, and a
bank-specific parser that simply failed to set `bank` would land in this
bucket and be described as a template claim.

Two things keep that honest rather than hidden, and neither is a name-sniffing
test on the registry label: the pairs are ranked and printed, so such a parser
is on the page instead of inside a bucket total; and the real fix is a
registry-side "this label is not an issuer claim" fact, carried as DO7#4.

Rollup movement, whole archive: `label_unmatched` **103 → 97**, new
`template_claim` **6**; `agree` 1,907, `no_claim` 915 and `unlabelled_folder`
366 all unchanged. The change is a strict split of one bucket.

Two ordering decisions, both load-bearing:

* `unlabelled_folder` is still tested **first**. It is a statement about the
  REFERENCE side and it already exempts the 35 `Unidentified/` documents; the
  card scoped this to the `label_unmatched` noise, and moving 35 rows between
  two "not comparable" buckets is churn, not information.
* `template_claim` is tested **before** the containment match. A template name
  that happened to be contained in a folder name would otherwise be reported
  as `agree` — manufacturing a detection-accuracy datum out of a coincidence,
  which is the same fiction the docstring opens with, running the other way.
  No archive row is affected today (all 41 fall outside `agree`), so the
  ordering is free and correct rather than free and convenient.

**And the warning is in the code, not only here.** The obvious way to make six
disagreements disappear is to name the registration after the folder it is
filed under. Never. §U D3 recorded why: the other ten documents of that same
template sit in `Unidentified/` and are not that bank's paper at all. The
rollup is reporting a true fact — statements filed under a bank name that
appears nowhere in them — and renaming a parser to silence a rollup writes the
folder's guess into the registry as if it were evidence.

The branch, over the frozen archive, through the run of record's own D-3
caches (`WEBAPP_DATA_DIR` pointed at the main checkout; OCR v3 and analysis
v12 unchanged, so every key matches and the run reads without writing an
artifact). Run `b7b40c73`, mode `scanned`, 3,506 documents.

| validated | 2,470 | **2,470** |
| review | 25 | **25** |
| withheld | 66 | **66** |
| failed | 932 | **932** |
| deferred | 13 | **13** |

Field-by-field over all 3,506 rows, keyed on `relative_path`: `outcome_class`,

**Rows that already had identity keep it byte-identical.** The 3,291 rows the

**Two of those six columns carry no information about the reconstruction, and

**The previously blank rows.** 215 rows carried no verdict in the run of
record. 185 of them — every single analysis-cache hit — are now populated,

# §PREPHAND — the second sweep prepared the whole document all over again

## PH0. Summary

Every document on the production path is swept TWICE. `analysis.pipeline.
analyze_markdown` sweeps the registry through `resolve` to route it, and
`telemetry/collect.score_vector` sweeps it again through `detection_report` to
record what nearly claimed it. The second sweep is honest — H3_SCHEMA §4
admits it because `detect` is pure and total, so re-running it reproduces the
run of record rather than re-enacting it — but purity is what made it
*correct*, not what made it *cheap*. DETECT-BUDGET reduced ONE sweep from 104
text preparations to 33 and carried the rest as DT9.1: the second sweep was
still paying the whole preparation again, recomputing character for character
the texts the first sweep had just produced.

It is fixed by publication, not by caching. `resolve` now returns the
`PreparedDocument` it swept on as `Dispatch.prepared`; the `DispatchCollector`
that already crosses the analysis/telemetry seam exposes it; and
`score_vector` takes it **only when its admissible text is this document's
admissible text**, which is exactly the condition under which the two sweeps
are the same computation. The pipeline's admissibility rebind is taken from
that same preparation, so one document now costs one preparation instead of
two plus a spare strip.

| | base | branch |
|---|---|---|
| text preparations per document, both sweeps (largest pinned and largest archive document alike) | **71** (3 strips + 68 normalizations) | **36** (2 strips + 34 normalizations) |
| worst pinned document, best of five, double sweep | 325.4 ms | **166.6 ms** |
| largest pinned document (62,702 chars) | 301.2 ms | **135.0 ms** |
| one pass over the 109 pinned | 10.44 s | **4.94 s** |
| 40 largest archive documents, worst (139,737 chars) | 758.8 ms | **366.5 ms** |
| 40 largest archive documents, median | 430.6 ms | **188.1 ms** |
| the same seven readings, arms measured in the opposite order an hour later | | **1.63x-2.62x, PH6** |
| full-archive equivalence pass (3,351 docs, sweep + parse + serialize) | 10 min 52 s | **7 min 3 s** |

Equivalence: 3,351 archive documents, every registration's `(score, matched
marker ids, excluded_by)`, the near-miss vector as `discovery/runner.py`
formats it, the dispatch of record, the SHA-256 of the text `parse` was handed
and of the parsed `Statement` — one digest per arm,
`75871FEEC01AC72E994C8D9D44C96D5C2E46BC092D6F501020FFFD3BD08EDC4F`, documents
differing **0**. Re-run with six crash injections: digest
`9B73F75DCF8698C3A3A93841A646E9DF00F03F6DAA97862537DB93C8D4DDC3F6`, documents
differing **0**, **27,544 raise events per arm** — each detect crasher raising
exactly twice per document, once per sweep, which is the number that would
have dropped if the reused preparation had served a cached score in place of
entering the guard.

## PH1. What the double sweep is, and why it is not removable

The two sweeps answer different questions and neither is redundant:

* `resolve` decides the outcome. It runs `detect` for every registration,
  prunes by `supersedes`, refuses on ambiguity, then parses the survivors.
* `detection_report` describes the field. It keeps every registration's
  `Detection` including the ones that scored zero-point-something — the
  near-miss vector, which is how a coverage wave learns that 164 documents sit
  at `bmo:0.166667` and which parser cell to write next.

`Dispatch` carries only the claimants; the near-misses are gone by the time it
is built, and `dispatch_section` cannot reconstruct them (H3_SCHEMA §4 states
exactly this, and rejected "recover them from `Dispatch`" for that reason). So
the second sweep stays. What was removable is that it re-derived the *inputs*
to detection, which are a property of the document, not of the sweep asking.

## PH2. The seam

Three facts make the reuse exact rather than approximate, and all three are
DETECT-BUDGET's, one consumer further on:

1. `PreparedDocument` holds `admissible_text(markdown)` and each distinct
   normalizer's output. Both are pure functions of the text (the module
   contract for `normalize`, and `tests/test_parser_registry_entries.py::
   test_each_registrations_normalization_returns_an_exact_str` keeps the
   interning path total over all 71 registrations).
2. It holds a memo of `(marker test, text) -> outcome`. `Marker.test` is pure,
   total and cheap by contract, so a memo hit is the value the call would have
   returned.
3. A marker that RAISES is never memoized (`_score`), and neither is a
   normalizer that raises (`text_for` stores nothing until it has a value), so
   the second sweep enters `_guarded` exactly as the first did.

Therefore: **two sweeps over prepared documents with equal admissible text
produce equal reports.**

**And say what that makes the second sweep, because "reuses the preparation"
undersells it (D5).** Fact 2 means the memo covers the MARKERS, not only the
texts, so the second sweep is not a cheaper sweep — it is a replay. Measured
on the largest pinned document, with one counting wrapper per distinct marker
test so the instrument shares exactly what the memo shares:

| | base | branch |
|---|---|---|
| `Marker.test` calls, sweep one | 190 | 190 |
| `Marker.test` calls, sweep two | 190 | **0** |
| memo entries retained | — | 190 |

Zero. Every `Detection` the near-miss vector publishes with a collector is
assembled from values the first sweep computed. H3_SCHEMA §4 admits this sweep
on the grounds that "re-running `detect` reproduces the run of record"; with a
collector the record is reproduced by **not** re-running it. That is the same
value for the same reason — `Marker.test` and the normalizers are pure by
contract, which is what §4's argument rests on too — but it is a different
mechanism from the one §4 describes, and it belongs in the record as such
rather than inside a sentence about preparation counts. The one thing that is
never replayed is a crash (fact 3), and the crash arm is the evidence that the
guard path stays live rather than the argument that it should: 2 raises per
crashing registration per document, 27,544 in all, identical on both arms
(PH5.1).

The seam is built so that "equal admissible text" is checked rather than
assumed:

* `resolve(document)` accepts a `str` or a `PreparedDocument` — `safe_detect`'s
  existing convention — and publishes what it swept as `Dispatch.prepared`
  (`compare=False`, so `Dispatch` equality is unchanged; `repr=False`, because
  a `PreparedDocument` has no readable repr).
* `DispatchCollector.prepared` reads it with `getattr`, because the collector's
  standing contract is that it keeps whatever object it was handed, including
  something that is not a `Dispatch`.
* `score_vector(markdown, collector)` takes the preparation only when it **is
  a `PreparedDocument`** (D4) and its admissible text is this document's:
  `prepared.admissible is markdown` or `prepared.admissible ==
  admissible_text(markdown)`. Anything else — a collector from another
  document, a D-3 analysis cache hit that never dispatched, a visual re-read
  that was not adopted, a duck-typed stand-in — is ignored and the sweep runs
  whole. Passing nothing is always correct; passing the wrong thing is
  ignored.

  The type half is not belt-and-braces: `detection_report` PREPARES whatever
  is not a `PreparedDocument`, so an object that only *compared* equal would
  reach `admissible_text` as a non-string and raise, out through
  `discovery/runner.py`'s one call site that is not inside a `try`. The
  identity half is not decoration either: `re.sub` returns the string it was
  handed when it substitutes nothing, so a document with no source comment IS
  its own admissible text and the guard is free on it. Production takes the
  other branch, because the OCR and native-text layers write a `<!-- SOURCE:
  … -->` header on every document they produce — which is the only reason the
  cost table below says one strip and not zero.

The guard costs one `admissible_text` (one of the 36 remaining preparations,
against the 34 it decides whether to skip). It is kept, at that price, because
the alternative is a near-miss vector that could describe a different
document, and near-miss vectors are what rank the next parser cells.

`webapp/worker.py` :134, `batch.py` :188, base numbering):

```python
-        scores, registration_count = score_vector(markdown)
+        scores, registration_count = score_vector(markdown, collector)
```

## PH4. Two designs not taken

**A module-level "last prepared document" slot in `telemetry/collect.py`,**
consumed by an unchanged `score_vector(markdown)`. It needs no call-site
change at all, which is why it was considered: the ownership line for this
cell names `analysis/pipeline.py` and `telemetry/collect.py`, and the three
emitters belong to WIRING-2 and DISCOVERY-OBS. It was rejected anyway. It
couples two call sites through hidden mutable state, it needs a thread-local
to be safe in the webapp's job thread, and it silently loses the optimization
in exactly the case the explicit version gets right (the discovery runner's
visual re-read that analysed and was NOT adopted, where the last dispatch and
the markdown being recorded are different documents). Four one-argument edits,
declared to Ocean with their line numbers, is the smaller price. **This is the
one place this cell went outside its named files; the diff there is one
argument per site and no logic.**

**Having the emitters build the `PreparedDocument` and pass it INTO
`analyze_markdown`.** Symmetric-looking, and strictly worse: a caller could
then hand the pipeline a preparation of a DIFFERENT document, and detection
would score document A while `parse` read document B. The direction chosen —
the preparation flows OUT of the analysis and never in — makes that
unrepresentable, and leaves the only mis-pairing risk on the telemetry side,
where the text guard closes it.

## PH5. The equivalence proof

`prephand-5fb5b603/` in the session scratchpad, descended from DETECT-BUDGET's
harness (DT9.7) and rebuilt for this wave's run of record: `ph_harness.py`
(arm-selected production import, with the assertion that catches measuring the
wrong arm; the OCR artifact index rebuilt by tail-reading every envelope, by
DIRECT file path, never the sqlite index), `archive_md_v3.pkl` (**3,351 of the
run of record's 3,380 shas**, 62.9 M chars, one pickle, so two arms provably
sweep identical bytes), `ph_equiv.py`, `ph_crash.py`, `ph_compare.py`,
`ph_measure.py`, `ph_ops.py`.

**The 29 shas not in the store are the 29 that have no text at all** — 16
`failed/invalid_pdf` and 13 `deferred/deferred_visual_ocr` in the run of
record's own `rows.csv`, each with a null document in the D-3 store. Detection
never runs on them, in either arm, so the corpus below is not a sample of the
archive: it is every archive document a detect sweep can be performed on.

Both arms run the production shape, per document:

```
BASE    dispatch = resolve(admissible_text(markdown))    # what the pipeline passes today
        vector   = score_vector(markdown)                # a second, whole sweep
BRANCH  prepared = prepare(markdown)                     # the pipeline's rebind
        dispatch = resolve(prepared)
        vector   = score_vector(markdown, collector)     # reuses the preparation
```

and record, per document: the outcome, parser id, winning score, candidates,
attempted, exceptions; the SHA-256 of the text handed to `parse`; the SHA-256
of the parsed `Statement` (`model_dump_json`); the whole score vector; the
near-miss field exactly as `discovery/runner.py` formats it; and the COMPLETE
detection report — all 71 registrations' score, matched marker ids and
`excluded_by`.

```

branch digest 75871FEEC01AC72E994C8D9D44C96D5C2E46BC092D6F501020FFFD3BD08EDC4F

outcomes (branch): {'claimed': 2495, 'unclaimed': 856}
claimed with a statement: 2495
