recorded parser failures: {}
```

The parsed `Statement` digest is in there deliberately: this is the
zero-payload-movement claim at archive scale, not only the detection claim,
and it is the same 2,495 statements byte for byte. `claimed` is not
`validated` — the run of record validates 2,405 of 3,380 — and no outcome
class is being asserted here, only that neither arm moved one.

### PH5.1 The crash arm — the guard exercised on purpose

`recorded parser failures: {}` is the whole reason this section exists. Not
one of the 71 registrations raised on any of the 3,351 documents, so the sweep
above never entered `_guarded` and proves nothing about it — DT7.1's caveat,
which applies with more force here, because the second sweep is now reading a
memo somebody else filled in. A memo that cached a crash as a score would be
invisible in a proof made of documents where nothing crashes.

Six synthetic registrations, covering every place a registration's own code
runs, and one that is healthy:

| injected | raises in |
|---|---|
| `zz_boom_required` | a REQUIRED marker |
| `zz_boom_excluding` | an EXCLUDING marker — the first loop, before any other kind runs |
| `zz_boom_exclusive` | an EXCLUSIVE marker |
| `zz_boom_normalize` | the parser's own normalization — i.e. inside `PreparedDocument.text_for`, the memo itself |
| `zz_boom_parse` | `parse`, claiming every document, so `resolve`'s parse loop is entered on all 3,351 |
| `zz_shares_a_marker` | nothing; it shares a marker TEST OBJECT with three crashing siblings, so the prepared-text memo runs alongside the guard, and it cannot claim, so it does not disturb the routing |

77 registrations × 3,351 documents, both arms, recording everything above plus
the `ParserFailure` list and **a per-document count of how many times each
injected registration actually raised, across both sweeps** — the number that
falls if reuse ever swallows a crash:

```
base   digest 9B73F75DCF8698C3A3A93841A646E9DF00F03F6DAA97862537DB93C8D4DDC3F6
branch digest 9B73F75DCF8698C3A3A93841A646E9DF00F03F6DAA97862537DB93C8D4DDC3F6
documents whose record differs: 0

raises, both arms, 27,544 each:
   zz_boom_excluding  6702   = 2 x 3351   (once per sweep, per document)
   zz_boom_exclusive  6702   = 2 x 3351
   zz_boom_normalize  6702   = 2 x 3351
   zz_boom_required   6702   = 2 x 3351
   zz_boom_parse       736               (the parse loop, where it was sole claimant)

recorded ParserFailures, both arms, 14,140 each:
   ('zz_boom_excluding', 'detect', 'KeyError')    3351
   ('zz_boom_exclusive', 'detect', 'IndexError')  3351
   ('zz_boom_normalize', 'detect', 'TypeError')   3351
   ('zz_boom_required',  'detect', 'ValueError')  3351
   ('zz_boom_parse',     'parse',  'RuntimeError') 736

`6702 = 2 × 3351` is the assertion in one number: the reused preparation
re-entered the guard on the second sweep for every crashing registration on

`test_a_crash_reaches_the_guard_on_the_second_sweep_as_well`.

## PH6. Cost

Paired, one arm per process, minimum of five samples per document (contention
can only make a sample slower, so the minimum is the reading least
contaminated by load — DETECT-BUDGET DT5), every document read the way the
winner is. The timed region is everything the two sweeps cost in text
preparation and detection, before any parse: the pipeline's rebind,
`_surviving_claimants`, and `score_vector`. Machine moderately loaded
throughout; the ratios are the durable part, the absolutes are this machine
today.

**Two rounds, with the arms in OPPOSITE ORDER**, because a single ordering
cannot tell a speedup from the machine getting busier between the two arms.
Round 1 ran base then branch on a moderately loaded machine; round 2 ran
branch then base an hour later, with roughly two dozen Python processes
sharing the box (the rest of batch 5 running its own proofs). The absolutes
move by a factor of one and a half between rounds. The ratios do not.

| measurement | round 1 base | round 1 branch | r1 | round 2 base | round 2 branch | r2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| worst pinned document, best of 5 | 325.39 ms | **166.62 ms** | 1.95x | 475.03 ms | **214.60 ms** | 2.21x |
| largest pinned document (62,702 chars) | 301.20 ms | **134.96 ms** | 2.23x | 434.45 ms | **210.37 ms** | 2.07x |
| one pass over the 109 pinned | 10.44 s | **4.94 s** | 2.11x | 17.96 s | **6.85 s** | 2.62x |
| the 109, summed best-of-five | 9.33 s | **4.25 s** | 2.19x | 14.10 s | **6.54 s** | 2.15x |
| 40 largest archive docs, worst (139,737 chars) | 758.80 ms | **366.46 ms** | 2.07x | 972.30 ms | **594.85 ms** | 1.63x |
| 40 largest archive docs, median | 430.60 ms | **188.14 ms** | 2.29x | 572.67 ms | **282.71 ms** | 2.03x |
| 40 largest archive docs, total | 18.30 s | **8.40 s** | 2.18x | 24.39 s | **12.27 s** | 1.99x |

The honest summary is **about 2x on the double sweep, in both load regimes and
in both orderings** — which is what halving the number of preparations should
buy, and the reason to state it in preparations as well.

And the load-independent reading, which a busy machine cannot move — measured
on the largest pinned document and the largest archive document, identical on
both because it counts operations and not characters:

| | base | branch |
|---|---|---|
| `admissible_text` calls per document | 3 | **2** |
| normalizer calls per document | 68 | **34** |
| `PreparedDocument`s built per document | 2 | **1** |
| total text preparations | **71** | **36** |

The remaining second strip is `score_vector`'s equality guard (PH2). The
detect-sweep affordability contract is untouched: it measures ONE sweep
through `_surviving_claimants`, which costs what it always did.

## PH9. Carried findings and questions for Ocean

1. **This cell touched four files it does not own, one argument each — and
   ONE of those lines is a merge landmine no test on either branch can catch.**
   *(Rewritten at Ocean's review: the first version of this item said the
   collision "resolves by keeping both changes on the one line", which is
   wrong, and wrong in the direction that ships a silent regression.)*

   The three emitters (`discovery/runner.py` :489 and :544,
   `webapp/worker.py` :134, `batch.py` :188, base numbering) belong to
   WIRING-2 and DISCOVERY-OBS, and `analysis/parser_registry.py` — where
   `Dispatch.prepared`, the two `str | PreparedDocument` widenings and
   `resolve`'s two-line preamble live — belongs to nobody in batch 5. PH4 says
   why the alternative (hidden module-level state, zero foreign edits) was
   refused. WIRING-2's three call sites are `_analyse` (runner :308-326),
   `_analyze_doc` and batch's `analyze_markdown` call: none of them a line
   this cell touches.

   **DISCOVERY-OBS is the landmine.** It does not edit runner :489 — it
   DELETES it and re-creates the call about thirteen lines earlier, hoisted
   above the dispatch projection because its cache-hit identity recovery
   (`_project_identity`) needs `scores` before the projection runs. On
   `wave5-discobs` the call is at :640, immediately after the visual-upgrade
   block and before `dispatch = collector.dispatch`, with `row.near_miss` left
   behind at :662. Against a base where PREPHAND MODIFIED the line it deleted,
   the three-way merge is a delete-vs-modify conflict, and **both plausible
   resolutions are silently wrong**:

   * *take DISCOVERY-OBS' side* — the hoisted call has no `collector`, so the
     reuse is gone at the ONLY site that sweeps the archive. Every test on
     both branches still passes, the gate is green, and the discovery run
     quietly pays two full sweeps per document again.
   * *keep both* — the hoisted call and PREPHAND's block both run, so the
     document is swept THREE times and `scores` is computed twice, the second
     assignment winning.

   **The resolution, verbatim:** delete PREPHAND's block at the old site
   entirely (comment included — `row.near_miss` keeps DISCOVERY-OBS's
   position), and add `, collector` to DISCOVERY-OBS's hoisted call:

   ```python
           # One detection sweep, read twice: for the near-miss vector (H-3) and,
           # on a cache-served row, for the parser identity the absent `Dispatch`
           # would otherwise have carried. Hoisted above the projection because
           # both consumers need it; `score_vector` is pure, so where it is called
           # changes nothing it returns.
   -       scores, registration_count = score_vector(markdown)
   +       scores, registration_count = score_vector(markdown, collector)
   ```

   That position is correct for the reuse as well as for DISCOVERY-OBS: it is
   after the visual-upgrade rebinding of `document, markdown, collector`, so
   the collector and the markdown are the adopted pair, which is exactly the
   pairing the guard checks. The post-merge assertion is
   `test_the_double_sweep_prepares_each_document_once` plus one live check
   that `discovery` still reuses: run the dry run and confirm the near-miss
   column is unchanged.

   **The fourth site is dead today, and should be recorded as dead rather than
   quietly kept.** Runner :544 (`_emit`'s `if scores is None:` fallback) cannot
   execute: of the four `self._emit(...)` call sites, the three early ones
   (:390, :409, :430) pass `markdown=None` positionally, so the `if markdown
   else ([], 0)` arm takes it, and the one site that does supply markdown
   (:519) always passes `scores=` explicitly. The argument added there is
   inert — correct if the site is ever reached, worth nothing until then.
2. **`Dispatch` now holds the document's prepared texts for as long as the
   `Dispatch` lives.** A deliberate widening of what the routing object
   carries, and the same class of thing `Dispatch.statement` already is —
   which is why `dispatch_section` projects named fields and never the object,
   and why nothing walks a `Dispatch` generically (checked repo-wide: there is
   no `asdict(dispatch)` anywhere, and `analysis/serialization.py` never sees
   one, because `Report` deliberately has no dispatch field). The lifetime is
   one document's analysis — the same window the caller's own `markdown`
   string is alive for — and the collector is rebuilt per document. If Ocean
   would rather the publication were opt-in (`resolve(document,
   publish=False)`), that is a one-line change that costs the whole
   optimization at the three emitters, so it is put here rather than taken.
3. **The guard costs one `admissible_text` per document and buys 34.** It
   could be made free by having `PreparedDocument` remember the string it was
   built from, so the guard could be an identity check — `re.sub` allocates
   even when it substitutes nothing, so today's identity fast path never fires
   on the production path. Not taken: that is a new slot on DETECT-BUDGET's
   class holding a second reference to the raw text, for ~1.7 ms on the
   largest pinned document against the ~150 ms the reuse saves there.
   Recorded so nobody re-derives it.
4. **A fourth strip is still out there, and it is not this cell's.**
   `webapp/artifact_cache.py:677` computes the analysis cache key as
   `text_sha256(admissible_text(markdown))` — a full pass over the document
   before the pipeline runs at all, on every cached path. WIRING-2 owns that
   region this batch (the input-hash digest hunk). Nothing to do today; the
   next cost card should know it exists.
5. **On a D-3 analysis cache hit nothing dispatches, so nothing is reused.**
   `dispatch_cached = 202` in the run of record: those documents pay the
   near-miss sweep whole, exactly as before, and pay no first sweep at all.
   The optimization applies to the ~3,289 documents that dispatch live.
6. **`score_vector` is `detection_report`'s only production caller, and now
   its only reusing one.** *(Corrected at review: the first version of this
   item said discovery adjudication calls `detection_report`. It does not —
   `discovery/adjudication.py` clusters and routes from the recorded rows, and
   `discovery/evidence.py` reads the near-miss straight out of the telemetry
   record's `dispatch.scores`. The only other callers are the conformance and
   registry tests, which pass strings and prepare their own text, correctly,
   because they run outside a dispatch. `detection_report`'s own docstring
   names adjudication as a consumer; that sentence predates this cell and is
   about the diagnostic, not about a call site.)* Noted so the next cell does
   not read the reuse as a rule about `detection_report`.
6b. **Three public signatures changed their parameter NAME**, which is an API
   change even though every in-repo caller is positional: `resolve(markdown)`
   → `resolve(document)`, `detection_report(markdown)` →
   `detection_report(document)`, and the private `_surviving_claimants`

   production or in tests, so nothing breaks today — but a `resolve(markdown=…)`

7. **`claimed` on the archive is 2,495 against the run of record's 2,405

## PH11. Closures from Ocean's adversarial review (verdict: SHIP conditional)

The review reproduced parity, the crash arm, the cost, the memory and the
serialization behaviour on its own arms (287 documents, both digests
identical, the 2x raise count reproduced). Six closures, all landed here. Two
of them are corrections to things this record ASSERTED and got wrong, which is
the part worth reading twice.

**PH9.1 — the merge landmine (required).** The collision characterization was
wrong: DISCOVERY-OBS does not edit runner :489, it deletes that line and
hoists the call thirteen lines up, so the merge is delete-vs-modify and both
obvious resolutions ship a silent defect — take-DISCOBS loses the reuse at the
only site that sweeps the archive, keep-both sweeps every document three
times. PH9.1 is rewritten with the resolution stated verbatim (delete
PREPHAND's block at the site; add `, collector` to the hoisted call, which
sits after the visual-upgrade rebinding and is therefore the correct pairing),
plus the observation that the fourth site — runner :544 — is **dead today**:
three of the four `_emit` call sites pass `markdown=None` and the fourth
always passes `scores=`, so the argument added there is inert.

**D1 — a protected-surface docstring this cell made false.** `PreparedDocument`
said the prepared texts "live exactly as long as the sweep that asked for
them". With `Dispatch.prepared` they live as long as the `Dispatch` — one
document's whole analysis and its telemetry record. The docstring now states
the real lifetime, the measured size (five distinct texts, 312,342 chars on a
62,702-char document — **5x**, plus a 190-entry memo) and the structural
reason it is safe: nothing retains a `Dispatch`. Two tests pin that rather
than asserting it —
`test_dispatch_section_never_carries_the_prepared_document` (no `prepared`
key, and a 100-character slice of the document is absent from the projected
section) and `test_the_report_never_carries_the_prepared_document` (no
`PreparedDocument` and no `Dispatch` among the `Report`'s fields). A weakref
no-retention assertion was considered and NOT added: `PreparedDocument`
declares `__slots__` without `__weakref__`, so it cannot be weakly referenced,
and adding the slot to make a test possible is a change to a protected class
for a test's convenience.

**D3 — a guard comment that asserted a falsehood.** The comment claimed the
identity branch never fires because "`re.sub` allocates even when it
substitutes nothing". It does not: on CPython 3.14 `re.sub` returns the object
it was given when nothing matched, so a document with no source comment IS its
own admissible text and the identity branch decides it for free. (The original
measurement that produced the wrong conclusion used a `str` SUBCLASS, which
does force a copy — the instrument, not the language.) The conclusion in the
cost table survives, but only for a stated reason: the OCR and native-text
layers write a `<!-- SOURCE: … -->` header on every document they produce, so
production always takes the equality branch and pays one strip.
`test_the_guard_is_free_when_the_document_carries_no_source_comment` now
covers both branches — 0 strips for the bare document, exactly 1 for the
header one.

**D4 — "cannot be wrong twice" was not true.** The guard read
`getattr(prepared, "admissible", None)` and compared it, so a duck-typed
object whose `.admissible` compared equal would be passed to
`detection_report`, which prepares anything that is not a `PreparedDocument`
— reaching `admissible_text` as a non-string and raising, out of
`score_vector`, through `discovery/runner.py`'s one un-`try`'d call site,
aborting a document over a telemetry detail. **Guarded rather than softened:**
the reuse now requires `isinstance(prepared, PreparedDocument)`.
`test_a_duck_typed_preparation_is_ignored_rather_than_swept` asserts both
halves — that the raise is real (`pytest.raises(TypeError)` on
`detection_report(duck)`) and that the guard makes it unreachable.

**D5 — disclosure: the second sweep is a total memo replay.** Not merely
"prepares nothing": `Marker.test` is called 190 times in sweep one and **0**
times in sweep two, so every published `Detection` is assembled from the first
sweep's values. H3_SCHEMA §4 admits the second sweep because re-running
`detect` reproduces the run of record; with a collector, the record is
reproduced by not re-running it. Same value, same purity argument, different
mechanism — stated in PH2 and in `score_vector`'s docstring, with the crash
arm as the evidence that the guard path stays live (a raising marker is never
memoized, so it re-raises on both sweeps: 2 per crashing registration per
document, 27,544 in all).

**D6 — a wrong sentence and an unrecorded API change.** `discovery/adjudication.py`
never calls `detection_report`; PH9.6 said it did. Corrected, with what the
discovery side actually reads (recorded rows, and `discovery/evidence.py`
taking the near-miss out of the telemetry record). And the
`markdown` → `document` parameter rename on `resolve`, `detection_report` and
`_surviving_claimants` is a public-signature change, now recorded as PH9.6b:
swept the repo, no caller passes them by keyword today, so nothing breaks —
but a keyword call written after this merge is a `TypeError`, not a rename.
# §PIPE5 — the repair seam, and an honest model label (batch 5)

Two pinned hunks in `analysis/pipeline.py`, one protected module, one cell.
Card 1 (REPAIR-GUARD) was drafted by MG-C at `docs/agent-handoffs/REPAIR-GUARD.md`
and is implemented as drafted. Card 2 (MODEL-LABEL) is the queued
`bank-deterministic` item.

## PIPE5.1 The repair seam was outside the promise

`analysis/parser_registry` states the law for the deterministic branch, in its
module docstring: *"The seam is total: no code path from `resolve` through
`parse` raises."* Every `detect` and every `parse` runs behind `_guarded`,
which reduces a crash to a `ParserFailure` — registration id, stage, and the
exception's CLASS NAME. `ParserFailure`'s docstring states why the message is
excluded: it *"routinely quotes the fragment of the document that provoked it
… The message is not stored anywhere, not even locally."*

`apply_statement_repairs` runs AFTER dispatch, at `:542`. It was the one line
in that branch standing outside the promise. A repair that raised propagated
out of `analyze_markdown` as a bare exception, and `webapp/worker.py:321` does
`store.set_error(job_id, str(e))` — so the quoted cell landed in the durable
job store and in front of a user. MG-C2 closed the loudest SOURCE
(`money.read_money` names the reader and the refusal class, never the token);
this closes the SEAM, which is the part that generalises to an `int()` on a
mangled cell or a `KeyError` on a mis-shaped grid.

**What the guard does.** The repair stage is discarded ATOMICALLY: the
UNREPAIRED statement stands, which is exactly what this branch published
before repairs existed, and the crash survives as a class name. Recovering
WHICH step raised would mean running the ten repairs, the year assignment and
the normalization independently — that changes what the stage DOES (today the
first raise stops the rest), which the card puts out of scope. For the same
reason the class is NOT attributed to `dispatch.registration`: only the keyed
summary repair belongs to the claiming parser, so naming it as the author of
one of the nine unconditional repairs' crashes would be exactly the
misattribution the seam exists to prevent.

**Scope boundary, stated rather than discovered.** The guard is NOT applied to
the two LLM-branch repair calls. `extract_statement` on those branches is
itself an unguarded call that raises out of `analyze_markdown`, so guarding
one line inside a branch that makes no totality promise buys nothing; the
escalation call already reduces any crash to `type(e).__name__` in its own
`except`. The deterministic branch is the one that promises totality, and it
now keeps it. Carried to Ocean as a question, not taken silently (§PIPE5.6).

**The flag.** A swallowed repair may not be silent: `repair_exception` is a
review cause with a named class, beside `parser_exception`. `classify_outcome`
already routes any integrity flag to `review`, so `telemetry/record.py` needed
no change. `telemetry/diagnostics.py` gains the flag and classes it
**`extraction_failure`** — a PRODUCTION stage that did not complete, which is
what that class already means for `recon:escalation_extraction_failed`. Not
`check_unavailable` (a repair yields no finding, so no diagnosis is partial)
and not advisory like `parser_exception` (a parser that crashed produced no
claim and its document never reached the checks; THIS document reached every
check with figures the platform knows are uncorrected). It ranks above the
financial classes on W3-2b's own argument: a repair rewrites published
balances and stated totals, so a `summary_identity` or `ledger_identity`
finding taken on unrepaired figures may be the crash's symptom.

## PIPE5.2 MODEL-LABEL — 41 documents, four parsers, one label

`(stmt.bank or "bank").lower()` published `bank-deterministic` for every
document whose parser publishes no issuer: the honest-unknown-issuer
registrations (UNKNOWN-ISSUER) and the issuer-agnostic core-processor
templates, which claim on a PLATFORM's paper and cannot name the bank without
inventing one. Four parsers' output aggregated under a label naming none of
them — in the field the coverage audits, the ADB forensic audit and the
balance forensic audit all carry as `parser`.

The claiming registration's id is the honest name. NARROW BY CONSTRUCTION:
`stmt.bank is None` is required, so a document carrying a bank label takes the
byte-identical old expression. `is None` and not falsiness — a parser
publishing an EMPTY label would be saying something different from "this paper
names no issuer", and this hunk does not adjudicate that; the live census
proves the question is currently vacant (all 41 are `None`). The
`-deterministic` suffix is unchanged, which is load-bearing:
`telemetry.record.model_calls_for` reads `endswith("-deterministic")` to mean
"no model call was made", so cost and call accounting are untouched.

## PIPE5.7 Ocean's BLOCK (narrow), and what it corrected

Verdict: behaviour clean (41 movers reproduced, census closed archive-wide,
inertness verified on 768 replays with four constructed firing shapes), both
design choices affirmed, five conditions. All five are closed here. Three of
them are findings about HONESTY OF DESCRIPTION rather than behaviour, which is
the class of defect a movement proof cannot catch.

**D1 — `DIAGNOSTICS_VERSION` 3 → 4 (the blocker).** This cell added
`integrity:repair_exception` to a closed vocabulary and left the version at 3.
`telemetry/diagnostics.py:37-38`'s own contract is "bumped when a code is
added, removed or re-classed", and COUNTS-P2 bumped 2 → 3 for the identical
shape one wave earlier. The version travels in every record so a rollup over
mixed runs can tell which vocabulary produced a row — and it matters MOST
here, because the new code fires on zero documents, so the version is the only
observable difference between a v3 rollup and a v4 one. Bumped, with the v4
entry inline and the full §11 v4 changelog in `W3_2_TAXONOMY.md`.

The instructive half is WHY it happened: nothing enforced the contract.
`test_the_diagnostics_version_moves_when_the_vocabulary_does` now pins
`(DIAGNOSTICS_VERSION, len(VOCABULARY), len(CLASS_OF), len(ADVISORY_CODES),
len(DIAGNOSABLE_CLASSES))` to `(4, 59, 53, 6, 2)`, mirroring the mechanism
COUNTS-P3 built for `OBSERVER_VERSION` after COUNTS-P2 made the same omission.
It earned its keep immediately: it caught a transcription error in its own
first pinned tuple. One consequential update followed —
`test_a_mixed_vocabulary_rollup_says_so` pins the current version literally
(now `{"1": 1, "4": 1}`), which is the intended behaviour of that test.

**D3 — the note misnamed the stage.** The note said *"a bank-summary repair
raised"*. `apply_statement_repairs` is TWELVE steps and exactly ONE is a
bank-summary repair; the other eleven are nine further bank-specific repairs,
`assign_transaction_years` and `normalize_statement`. The wording was wrong
twice: it misdescribes the eleven, and in the raise-after-success case the
bank-summary repair had already SUCCEEDED and was being discarded with the
rest. Now:

```
a statement-repair stage raised (<ExceptionClass>) and was discarded whole;
the unrepaired statement stands, including any date, sign or summary
correction the stage would have made, so the document is routed to review
rather than reported as clear
```

Reworded in all three places (the pipeline note, the `INTEGRITY_FLAGS` gloss,
`W3_2_TAXONOMY.md` §3.2) and pinned by
`test_the_note_names_the_STAGE_and_not_one_repair`, which asserts the note
says `statement-repair stage` and `discarded whole` and does NOT say
`bank-summary`.

**D2 — the `extraction_failure` gloss had one occupant.**
`W3_2_TAXONOMY.md` §4 read "the escalation extraction itself failed". The
class now has two occupants; the row reads "a stage that PRODUCES the
statement did not complete: the escalation extraction failed, or a
statement-repair stage raised and was discarded whole".

**D4 — what the discard actually costs, disclosed and measured.**
`assign_transaction_years` is inside the discarded stage. On a statement whose
period crosses a year boundary, parsers stamp one year on every `MM/DD` row and
that step is what re-derives it — so the discard path publishes **wrong
transaction DATES**, not merely uncorrected summary figures, and dates feed the
dated ledger, the daily-balance series and the ADB. That is a strictly larger
blast radius than the first write-up implied, and asserting it without
measuring it would have repeated the same error, so it is pinned:
`test_the_discard_publishes_uncorrected_dates_on_a_year_boundary` runs a
Dec→Jan statement twice and shows the January row moving `2026-01-09`
(stage runs) → `2025-01-09` (stage discarded), with the flag present and the
document routed to `review`.

Why it is still the right trade, stated at the seam rather than assumed: the
alternatives are a half-repaired statement nobody can characterise (an unknown
mixture of corrected and uncorrected figures) or an escaped exception carrying
the document's text into the durable job store. The discard is the only option
that is both fail-closed and honest, and it is never silent — the flag routes
the document to `review`, so a human reads it before the numbers are used.

**D5 — the label-collision hazard, guarded.** MODEL-LABEL publishes
`<registration.id>-deterministic` while every other document publishes
`<hyphenated bank label>-deterministic`. Eleven hyphenated labels in the live
registry are also parser ids (`chase`, `bmo`, `truist`, `cibc`, `bluevine`,
`brex`, `desjardins`, `linkbank`, `mercury`, `scotiabank`, `wealthsimple`), so
a bank=None publisher whose id landed on one would re-create exactly the
ambiguity this hunk removed. None of the four does today.
`test_the_new_label_cannot_collide_with_a_hyphenated_bank_label` forbids the
fifth. LIMITATION stated in the test rather than hidden: "publishes bank=None"
cannot be decided statically (`core_processor_sectioned` decides it per
document), so the four are pinned by name and the guard catches a RENAME, not
an unlisted newcomer.

**D6 — the fixtures were passing fields that do not exist.** Both wrote
`statement_period_start` / `statement_period_end`; the real fields are
`period_start` / `period_end`, and `Statement` does not forbid extras, so
pydantic silently DROPPED them and the fixtures carried no period at all —
while every test still passed. Fixed in both files with the reason recorded at
the call site. (Whether `Statement` should forbid extras is a schema question,
not this cell's: `analysis/schema.py` carries a zero-line diff.)

**Recorded, not changed:** `quality.corporate_use` is computed from
reconciliation, not from the integrity flags, so a document whose repair stage
crashed can read `approved` in `quality` while `integrity.risk_level` says
`review`. The asymmetry is PRE-EXISTING and symmetric — `parser_exception` and
`integrity_check_exception` behave identically — and the published outcome is
still `review`, because `classify_outcome` reads the flags. Pinned as a
recorded property by `test_the_flag_does_not_by_itself_block_corporate_approval`;
changing it would be a decision about every crash flag, not about this one.

**Claim 6 (the `str(e)` sink itself) is Ocean's WORKER-PRIVACY batch-6 card**
— `webapp/worker.py:81-82` and `:321` storing exception messages in the
durable job store, class names only — with this cell's guard as its cheap
first hunk. Not taken here.

**Re-proof after the five conditions.** Movement is unchanged by construction:
D1/D2/D3/D6 touch a version integer, prose and test fixtures; D4 and D5 add
tests only. The one behavioural surface that moved is the note STRING on a
flag that fires on zero archive documents.

## CM11. Carried findings and questions for Ocean

1. **`ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` needs its bump at merge, and the second reason
   is a decision you can reverse.** 21 documents' `stated_debit_count_matches`
   changes value — that alone forces the bump. But every payload's
   reconciliation block ALSO gains `expected_credit_count` /
   `expected_debit_count`, so the shape change is archive-wide rather than
   21 documents wide. I judged that worth it: without the published expected
   side, a capital_one payload reads `stated_debit_count 12 /
   captured_debit_count 13 / stated_debit_count_matches true`, which is only
   not a contradiction to a reader who knows the table — one field with two
   meanings, the defect BOFA-COUNTS was spent removing. COUNTS-P2 set the
   precedent by adding four such fields. If you would rather the payload not
   grow, dropping the two fields is a contained edit (the dataclass, two
   assignments, the return, and three test assertions) and the mapping still
   works; the cost is that the payload stops explaining itself.
   `webapp/` is untouched here either way; the brief reserves the bump to you.
2. **`texas_bank:debit` is the third member of the class and was NOT
   promoted.** It is outside this cell's named populations, and an entry is
   promoted by the cell that measured it — but the measurement is done and
   sits here so the decision is one line rather than a re-derivation: 1
   archive document, printed `Checks/Debits ( N )` beside a separate
   `Service Charge` line, `stated_service_charge` 10.00, raw `+1`, **1 of 1
   under the identical `plus_one_when_billed` mapping**. The document is
   pinned corpus PASS and already `review` on
   `missing_declared_statement_page`, so promoting it moves no outcome
   either. The parser's own acceptance gate is
   `debit_sum == debits + service_charge`, which is the same argument the
   entry already makes in prose. One caveat worth your eye: a
   one-document family is a mapping with no control arm at all — there is no
   zero-charge texas_bank statement in the archive, so `+1 always` and
   `+1 iff charged` are indistinguishable on it, exactly the §DB8 hazard. My
   recommendation is to promote it in a later cell that can say that out
   loud in the entry, not to fold it in here.
3. **Two corrections to the `capital_one:debit` entry, both in place, both
   named in the entry.** (a) §COUNTSP3 CP4.1's stale sentence — "12 of 12
   capital_one documents disagree by EXACTLY +1" — was true of the
   12-document population it was measured on and misleading about a family of
   22 with a 10-document zero-charge control arm. (b) A sentence nobody had
   ever measured: "its money is inside the printed debit TOTAL", which is
   FALSE on 12 of 12 (CM3.0). Both were rewritten as part of rewriting the
   entry this cell owns rather than left as somebody's future surprise. (b) is
   the one worth a second look from you: it is a claim COUNTS-P1 made, P2 and
   P3 both read past, and it argued the opposite of what the archive shows.
4. **The pipeline call-site change is outside the handoff's ownership list,
   and it is unavoidable.** The handoff names `reconcile.py` as the
   application point, and `reconcile` cannot apply a per-parser mapping
   without being told which parser claimed the document — `Statement` carries
   no parser identity. The change is three lines (an import, the two call
   sites, and one existing expression replaced by the shared helper it now
   has to agree with). The alternative designs are worse and are recorded so
   you can check the reasoning: applying the mapping in `pipeline` instead
   leaves `reconcile` publishing a `matches` field that disagrees with the
   flag (BOFA-COUNTS's exact defect), and deriving the mapping from the
   statement alone would make the expected side depend on the rows.
5. **The `rows.csv` `parser_id` hole is unchanged at v12** — still 119
   distinct documents (110 validated / 6 review / 3 withheld), and in this
   cell it hid 4 of the 22 `capital_one` documents and 1 of the 35
   `first_citizens`, five of the six pinned candidate-family documents among
   them. The DISCOVERY-OBS card in this batch is the fix; until it lands, any
   cell measuring a family from `rows.csv` alone is measuring a subset and
   will not know it.
6. **`PRINTED_EVIDENCE_FIELDS` is one field long, and the next entrant is the
   decision worth guarding.** Every name added there is a new way for the
   expected side to move, so the allowlist is asserted against
   `Statement.model_fields` and pins that nothing derived from `transactions`
   can appear — but the judgement of whether a given printed field is
   *independent enough* is not something a test can make. `stated_nsf_count`
   and `stated_interest_paid` are the plausible next candidates and neither
   has a measured need today.
7. **The movement harness is reusable and is the piece worth keeping.** The
   session scratchpad `countsmap/` holds `join.py` (the arithmetic
   artifact join — `cache_key` → path, sqlite never opened),
   `step1_identity.py` (the dispatch replay that closes the `parser_id` hole,
   with its own fidelity check), `step2_families.py` / `step2b_rowclass.py`
   (per-family counterfactuals and the row-class corroboration),
   `step3_movement.py` (whole-archive before/after under two tables loaded
   side by side, with the self-validation against the published flags),
   `step4_tablediff.py` (by-value table diff + the pinned-manifest join) and
   `step5_money.py` (the folded-vs-separate charge measurement). Any cell
   promoting a count direction can point `step3` at its table and get flag
   movers, outcome movers and the outcome split in one run. **One trap it
   already fell into and now guards:** `subprocess.run(..., text=True)`
   decodes `git show` with the system ANSI codepage on Windows, which mangles
   every em dash in the reasons and made the first by-value table diff report
   20 spurious drifted entries. `encoding="utf-8"` is mandatory, and a
   table-diff that reports drift in entries you did not touch is that bug
   until proven otherwise.
8. **What a mapping still cannot express, stated so the limit is a fact
   rather than a discovery.** `plus_one_when_billed` adds at most one row.
   A bank printing TWO separately-billed fee rows against one printed
   `Service Charges` total is `+2` and would flag a complete ledger; the tell
   is a captured count exceeding `printed + 1` by exactly the extra rows, and
   it is written into the `capital_one:debit` falsifier. No archive document
   of either family does this. The remedy, if one appears, is a new rule in
   `RULES` measured by the cell that finds it — not a callable.

## CM13. Adversarial review — the closures

Verdict: **SHIP**, with the pipeline exception ACCEPTED — the review proved
the alternatives worse and the `by_bank_label` hazard live. D5, the
`ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` bump, is Ocean's at the train as planned. The other
four findings and the framing correction are all documentation-grade, and all
are closed; none moved a line of executable code, so the proof floor of CM10
stands unchanged and the two owned test files plus the guards were re-run over
the closures.

**D1 — an off-by-one in the module's own prose.** `expected_count`'s docstring
said the mapping is the identity for "30 of the 31" parsers in the table. It
is 29 of 31: two are mapped. This log had it right and the module did not,
which is the wrong way round for a table whose whole value is that a reviewer
can read it. Corrected.

**D2 — "57 documents" is the number this CELL can see, not the number the
runner prints.** The `OBSERVER_VERSION = 4` note forecast the v3 → v4
population shift as 57 documents leaving `semantics_incomparable`. That is the
identity-complete figure, obtained here by replaying dispatch; the shipped
runner reads `parser_id` off `rows.csv` and reports **52**, because the
analysis-cache-hit hole hides 4 billed `capital_one` and 1 `first_citizens`.
A forecast that no run can reproduce is a forecast that will be read as a bug
in the runner. The note now carries both numbers, names DISCOVERY-OBS's
projection as what closes the gap, and says which way the instrument is wrong:
an unknown parser is never compared, so it under-reports and fails CLOSED.

**D3 — the falsifier named the hazard and not the discriminator. The one that
matters.** The `capital_one:debit` entry already disclosed that a billed cycle
whose charge row was never recorded reads `captured == printed` and flags, and
argued that this is a finding rather than a false positive. What it did not
say is that a FUTURE LAYOUT FOLDING THE CHARGE INTO THE PRINTED COUNT presents
the **identical observable** — same equality, same flag, complete ledger — so
the entry as written gave a reader no way to tell its true positive from its
false one.

The discriminator is measured and this cell had already measured it: the MONEY
scope. `_debit_coverage_target` (`analysis/reconcile.py:63-84`) fires only
where `beginning + credits - printed debits` misses `ending` by the charge —
only where the charge is OUTSIDE the printed total — and it fires on 12 of 12
today. So: **flag + that adjustment firing = a ledger missing a row; flag +
that adjustment silent = a folded layout, and this entry is wrong about the
document.** Written into the entry, where the next person to see the flag will
be reading.

**D4 — "a refund is a CREDIT row" is true of at most one of the two parsers.**
`_service_charge_posting` returns None on `charge <= 0`
(`analysis/first_citizens.py:506-507`), so first_citizens emits **no row at
all** for a refund; only `capital_one`, which reads detail rows, would post one
— in whichever column the document printed it. The conclusion the sentence was
supporting is unchanged (the DEBIT side gains nothing either way) and the
sentence is now accurate about how. Recorded with it, since the same paragraph
is where a reader checks the arithmetic: the test is `> 0`, not `>= 0.01`, so a
printed sub-cent charge would adjust by one — immaterial, no bank in the
archive prints one, and stated rather than guarded because the money
tolerances belong to `analysis/reconcile.py`.

**FRAMING — "closes a drift hazard rather than opening one" was self-serving.**
Before this cell `reconcile` had no parser key, so there was no key to drift.
Keying it is what creates the possibility of two derivations disagreeing;
single-sourcing through `claiming_parser_id` closes the hazard the same commit
opened. That is a good outcome and it is not a virtue, and CM5 now says so.
The property survives on the test that asserts it, not on the intention.
# §ADBSPLIT — the ratified ADB doctrine, implemented: one basis, stamped; five alternates, internal; two Woodforest openings, published

Base main `bbe5cf1` (v12, OCR v3, registry 71), branch `wave5-adbsplit`. Run of
record `discovery_reports/2026-08-15T111704.195314-0000-c924d751`.

## AS0. Summary

Gustavo's 2026-08-15 doctrine, in code. One statement yields ONE user-facing
Average Daily Balance and it is always the canonical calendar-day underwriting
figure over the printed period; the basis is a frozen literal stamped on every
result rather than a knob; five alternate denominators are computed for audit
and published nowhere; the bank's own printed average is preserved as evidence
with a signed variance and a named hypothesis for the gap.

| | |
|---|---|
| Suite | 4,240 to **4,264 passed**, 33 skipped, 29 deselected, exit 0 |
| Pinned corpus | 106 PASS / 3 WITHHELD, **every existing audit column byte-identical on all 109 rows of both CSVs** |
| Archive movers | **exactly 2**, both named, both Woodforest account openings |
| Archive non-movers | 2,492 of 2,494 analysed payloads byte-identical once the additive fields are stripped |
| H1 | **0 movers**, reproduced on the current tree, with the one near-miss named |
| Coverage | validated 2,403 to **2,405** (distinct shas); withheld 66 to 64; review 25 unchanged; failed 873 unchanged |

## AS1. Card 1 — the additive split

`analysis/adb.py`. `average_daily_balance` becomes `underwriting_adb`; the old
name survives as a read/write `@property`. That choice is load-bearing rather
than stylistic: `analysis/serialization.py` pops the ADB value out of the
nested `metrics.adb` object so the payload offers exactly one ADB number, and
`dataclasses.asdict` does not see properties — a second real field would have
leaked a second ADB into every payload. Both names are popped now, so a future
rename cannot reopen the hole.

`underwriting_adb_basis = "calendar_day_printed_period"` and
`underwriting_adb_policy = "canonical_v1"` are dataclass DEFAULTS, not
assignments. A result object therefore cannot exist without declaring its
basis, including on the two paths where `compute_average_daily_balance`
returns before building any ledger. Measured over the archive: **2,494 of
2,494** analysed documents publish the canonical basis, the three with no
ledger at all (`Ace Auto` Sept/Oct/Nov 2025) included.

`underwriting_adb_alternates` computes five denominators in one pass over the
ledger the canonical ADB already built — `banking_day`, `weekday_only`,
`posting_day`, `credit_only`, `beginning_of_day`. Internal only: no dashboard
card, no export row (`webapp/app.py::_adb_rows` keeps its whitelist, so the
nested stamps and alternates never reach CSV/XLSX), and every value is nulled
alongside the canonical figure at publication when the required checks fail —
an unvalidated ledger yields no valid figure on any basis. The basis and policy
STAMPS stay on a refused document, because an auditor needs to know which
methodology refused it.

`analysis/schema.py`. `stated_average_balance` becomes
`bank_reported_average_balance`, with the old name kept as a serialized
`@computed_field` alias plus a `validation_alias`, so constructor kwargs,
attribute assignment, and payload consumers of the old name all keep working.
**Four parsers had to change key, not just name**: `model_copy(update={...})`
bypasses both validation and the property setter, so pydantic silently drops an
alias key there. Reproduced before fixing, then fixed in `capital_one.py`,
`regions.py`, `bofa.py`, `td_us.py`.

`bank_reported_average_label` is captured at all 28 sites that already read a
printed average, across 26 parsers plus the structurer — the printed heading
verbatim, and captured from the live cell where the parser matches one
(`capital_one` table path, `regions` table path) or from the printed tokens
where the match runs on a folded copy (`td_canada_french`, which prints
`Solde créditeur mens moyen`). Sixteen distinct headings over the pinned 109.

`analysis/metrics.py` gains `bank_reported_average_variance` (signed,
ours minus theirs), `_variance_pct`, and `bank_reported_average_hypothesis`
over a closed seven-value vocabulary. Each discriminator is an exact identity
against the same ledger and each is stated in the code; `agrees` is tested
first so a coincidental alternate match can never be reported in place of the
plain fact, and a FLAT ledger suppresses the two alternate-equality tests
outright (AS10.3).

## AS2. Card 2 — the gate and the audit pins

Both CSVs gain the same four columns, APPENDED. The additive proof is the
identity of everything above them: **109 rows, 38 to 42 and 53 to 57 columns,
zero drift on any pre-existing column in either file**, and
`docs/adb-forensic-audit.md` regenerates byte-identical.

`adb-audit-results.csv` deliberately now carries TWO label columns.
`printed_adb_label` is the audit script's own after-the-fact guess from the
bank name and the markdown; `bank_reported_average_label` is what the parser
read off the page. Keeping both means the day they disagree is a finding
rather than a silent overwrite.

`corpus_gate.check_adb_doctrine` is new. `production_verdict` now returns its
payload so the check costs no third analysis pass. It holds the gate's OWN copy
of the doctrine literals — this file may not import `analysis.adb`, and a check
that borrowed the engine's constant could not detect the engine changing it.

The alternates are NOT pinned per document. What is pinned is the property that
makes them meaningful: `banking_day` must differ from the canonical figure
unless the period contains no non-banking day, or the daily series is flat —
two exemptions that make them equal by arithmetic rather than by substitution,
both checked from the published ledger rather than asserted. Both were written
in because a flat-balance statement is a real counterexample to the naive form
of the rule.

**Skips are not exemptions, and the count is now printed.** A document that
publishes no ADB has no canonical figure to be distinct from, so there is
nothing for this clause to assert and it is skipped - while still being held to
the basis stamp. On the pinned corpus that is the three withheld documents, and
the arithmetic reads `distinct 106 + skipped 3 + exemptions 0 = 109`. The
earlier phrasing of this record let "3" read as an exemption; it is not, and
`distinct + exemptions + skipped` is now in the summary line so the difference
cannot be inferred wrongly again. A second skip case exists and the corpus does
not contain one: a period holding no banking day at all - a weekend-only or
holiday-weekend statement - for which the engine reports None rather than a
mean over an empty day set. It is named in the check's docstring.

## AS4. Card 4 — H2, corrected against re-measurement

`benchmark/compare.py::_mt_activity_mean_note` claimed MoneyThumb averages
"activity days". That was wrong, and it stated undocumented vendor behaviour as
if it were a specification. Re-measured over `moneythumbResults/results` on
2026-08-15, reproduced here rather than carried over:

* **11 of 11** MT daily-balance series are exactly the BANKING days of their
  span — weekdays minus observed federal Reserve Bank holidays. Not activity
  days: those series carry days with no posting, and every weekday holiday in
  range is absent.
* **10 of 11** `avg_balance` figures equal the plain mean of that series to the
  cent; the eleventh (`chase_dec` account 9362) differs by 0.01.
* **6 of 6** benchmark documents where our ledger validates AND MT prints an
  average reproduce MT's figure EXACTLY from OUR ledger on the banking-day
  denominator — `chase_dec`, the three `chase_jan_feb_mar` months,
  `field_trucking_nov`, `wmb_may`. Under a weekday-only denominator only 1 of
  the 6 reproduces, so the federal-holiday calendar is load-bearing rather than
  incidental.
* **0 of 11** match a calendar-day mean over the same span.

PARITY_MATRIX rows 9 and 10 corrected: MT's average IS recomputable, from its
own published series. The verdict on row 9 stays, on defensibility — ours is
Decimal, validated, fail-closed and declares its basis — but the earlier reason
given for it was false. Every `adb` comparison row now carries an explicit
definition-relative qualification and, where our ledger validates, our own
banking-day figure beside it, so an `OUR_SYSTEM_CORRECT` verdict reads as "our
figure matches our audited expectation under our ratified definition" and not
as "MoneyThumb miscalculated".

## AS5. Card 5 — Woodforest under the doctrine

WF4's corrected diff applied, with the schema field, the parser declaration and
the engine hunks in ONE commit (WF4 is explicit that the hunks are not
standalone-inert). The consuming layer re-enforces the day-immediately-before
boundary itself and requires a positive fold; the divisor never changes.

Per-gate, on the real documents through the real pipeline:

| | `D9EF1A8C` (`c183e584_Feb.pdf`) | `823DCE7F` (`fad3db75_document.PDF`) |
|---|---|---|
| printed period | 2026-02-11 .. 2026-02-28 | 2026-01-24 .. 2026-01-31 |
| prover output | `[('2026-02-10', 30000.00, credit)]` | `[('2026-01-23', 1000.00, credit)]` |
| declared count | 1 | 1 |
| `beginning_balance` (published) | 0.00, unchanged | 0.00, unchanged |
| engine `opening` / source | 30,000.00 / `initialization_event` | 1,000.00 / `initialization_event` |
| ADB divisor | **18** — the printed period | **8** — the printed period |
| `out_of_period_transaction_count` | 1 to **0** | 1 to **0** |
| `opening_balance_matches_statement` | **True** (H1's promoted check) | **True** |
| `underwriting_adb` | 25,390.04 | 2,802.26 |
| bank's printed average | 25,632.67 (`Average Balance`) | 2,602.01 (`Average Balance`) |
| variance / pct | **-242.63** / -0.9466% | **+200.25** / +7.696% |
| hypothesis | `n_plus_1_zero_forward` | `n_plus_1_zero_forward` |
| outcome | withheld to **validated** | withheld to **validated** |

**What "every other gate passes" is worth, stated honestly.** Four of the
prover's eight gates - G1 (forward is zero), G2 (dated the day immediately
before, nothing after), G3 (every declared posting a positive credit) and G4
(the ledger closes with them and not without) - are re-checked by the engine as
the fold's own PRECONDITION. Citing them afterwards as independent corroboration
is double counting: the fold could not have happened had they failed. The
genuinely independent evidence that these two rows opened these two accounts is
**G6** (the bank's own `Daily Closing Balance Summary` prints a closing balance
for that day), **G7** (`Number of Days in Cycle` equals the printed period, so
the period the evidence is measured against is the one the bank printed) and
**G8** (the bank's printed average is reproduced to the cent over
`[period_start - 1 .. period_end]` by the platform's own engine). G5 sits
between the two groups - its leading-rows half is subsumed by G4, and its walk
became falsifiable only when GEOM-1 landed. Three independent gates, not seven.

The hypothesis is not decoration: it reproduces the (N+1)/N gap WF8.6 recorded
as unexplained-by-that-cell. On both documents
`(daily_sum + opening) / (days + 1)` equals the printed average to the cent —
the bank counted the day the account opened and the printed period does not.

Family sweep, all 22 archive documents whose text names WOODFOREST: 20 claimed

`initialization_postings`'s docstring is re-qualified for GEOM-1 per WF8.12(b):

   `metrics`), because `_analysis_rows` walks those sections generically. The
   nested `adb` whitelist is untouched, so no basis, policy or alternate
   reaches an export. No dashboard card was added: `webapp/` is untouched and
   contains none of the new field names.
5. **The Juneteenth limitation is deliberate and stated.** The banking-day
   calendar counts Juneteenth in every year rather than carrying an
   effective-date constant, because a literal year in the parser layer is what
   `test_no_statement_hardcodes.py` exists to refuse. The consequence is
   bounded to a pre-2021 period containing June 19, on an internal diagnostic.
6. **The frozen TD oracles in `tests/test_row_grouping.py` now compare a
   scoped statement.** `bank_reported_average_label` and
   `initialization_transaction_count` postdate them; back-filling the oracle
   bodies would have destroyed the "verbatim as of `8ce6abc`" property that is
   their whole value. Both fields are pinned by name elsewhere.
7. **`money_to_cents` is now public on `analysis/adb.py`.** `metrics.py` needs
   the same cent rounding for the variance, and
   `test_no_parser_helper_clones.py` forbids reaching for `_money` across
   modules. Promoting the name was the alternative to a second implementation
   of a financial decision.

## AS10. Ocean's adversarial review — closures

Verdict SHIP, with one code fix in a protected module and four hardenings.
Everything below was reproduced before it was changed.

### AS10.1 The `:466` clause — the engine tested the sign, not the column

The fold's comment said "all declared postings credits". The gate tested
`txn.amount > 0` and nothing else, so the reviewer folded a `+1000.00` row
carrying `direction="debit"` — a positive amount the producer described as
money LEAVING. The prover checks both halves; the engine did not, and the whole
reason this layer re-enforces the day-before boundary rather than inheriting it
is that it does not get to assume the declaring parser checked anything.

    -            and all(txn.amount > 0 for _, txn in outside)
    +            and all(
    +                txn.direction == "credit" and txn.amount > 0
    +                for _, txn in outside
    +            )

One term, and the invariant the comment already claimed. Fixtured at the engine
layer on the reviewer's exact construction
(`test_a_declared_posting_labelled_a_debit_is_refused_by_the_engine`), built on
the STATEMENT rather than the markdown so it pins the engine's refusal of any
producer, not the prover's refusal to declare. The same fixture asserts the
unmodified statement still publishes, so it pins the direction term rather than
incidental breakage. **Both movers re-verified unchanged** after the fix.

### AS10.2 The gate's skip line

The distinctness clause silently dropped documents with no canonical or no
banking-day figure. Three today, and the summary line's `106` against a
manifest of `109` invited exactly the misreading it produced. The count is now
printed — `distinct on 106, skipped 3 unpublished (0 all-banking-day periods,
0 flat ledgers)` — so `distinct + exemptions + skipped = 109` is visible rather
than inferred. The all-weekend / holiday-weekend skip case, which the pinned
corpus does not contain, is named in the check's docstring.

### AS10.3 The hypothesis flat guard

Reproduced first, on the TD NARROW shape — a ONE-DAY period, where the "balance
entering each day" is just the opening balance:

    period 2026-02-28 .. 2026-02-28, opening 100.00, closing 500.00
    daily            [('2026-02-28', 500.0)]        <- one distinct balance
    beginning_of_day 100.00
    bank printed     100.00
    HYPOTHESIS       beginning_of_day_alignment     <- from one coincidence

A bank that simply printed its opening balance was being reported as evidence
of an off-by-one-day averaging convention. The guard mirrors the gate's
`exempt_flat` test — one distinct end-of-day balance across the period — and
suppresses the two ALTERNATE-EQUALITY discriminators, `credit_only_floored` and
`beginning_of_day_alignment`. A new `indeterminate_flat` reading replaces
`unexplained` on a flat series, because "unexplained" implies evidence was
weighed and found wanting when in fact the evidence cannot exist.

**Deviation from the prescription, stated.** Ocean's note said a flat series
should report `agrees`/`indeterminate_flat` and nothing else. Two
discriminators are kept reachable there, because neither degenerates and
suppressing them would lose real answers:

* `collected_or_float` reads the bank's printed heading and never touches the
  series at all.
* `n_plus_1_zero_forward` is a different identity over different terms —
  `(daily_sum + opening) / (days + 1)`, reachable only on a printed zero
  balance forward. On a flat series it equals the constant only when the
  opening equals it too, in which case the variance is zero and `agrees` has
  already returned. Suppressing it would silence the mid-cycle
  account-opening class on exactly the shape that class produces: an account
  funded on day one and then static is FLAT, and `n_plus_1_zero_forward` is
  the true explanation of its printed average. Fixtured
  (`test_the_flat_guard_suppresses_only_the_two_degenerate_discriminators`).

### AS10.4 The export triple-print — the alias row is dropped, not relabelled

The flat exports printed the bank's figure three times: `statement`'s canonical
row, `statement`'s alias row, and the long-standing `metrics` echo. **Dropped**
rather than relabelled, and the reason is what the alias is FOR. It exists so a
JSON consumer of the old name does not break, and it stays in the payload where
that contract lives. A CSV or XLSX sheet is not that contract — it is a flat
sheet a human reads, and a relabelled duplicate ("stated_average_balance
(alias)") still asks the reader to work out which of three identical numbers is
authoritative. Suppression is one named entry, `_EXPORT_SUPPRESSED_KEYS` in
`webapp/app.py`, with the argument attached; the canonical row and the `metrics`
echo both remain, so nothing an analyst reads is lost. Fixtured
(`test_the_export_prints_the_bank_figure_once_per_section_not_three_times`),
which asserts the alias is still in the payload and no longer in the rows.

### AS10.5 Records

The four record corrections are applied in place above: the honest statement of
which prover gates are independent of the fold's own precondition (AS5 — three,

# §MGD — the minus-glyph canon: one class, and the two things that were not signs

## MGD0. Summary

`analysis/money.py` bound `MINUS_GLYPHS` **twice at module scope**. The
2-glyph canon at the top fed `_MINUS_TABLE`; a 4-glyph rebinding 500 lines
later, beside `parse_signed_decimal`, added ASCII hyphen and U+2014 EM DASH
and SHADOWED it for every importer — while `MINUS_CLASS` and `_MINUS_TABLE`,
already evaluated, kept the narrow value. The module answered one question two
ways, and two EXPORTED parsers read one token with opposite signs.

The cell surveyed every consumer's LIVE behaviour before unifying anything,
and the survey is where the real finding was: **two of the three external
consumers were not using the sign class as a sign class at all.** `brex` and
`mercury` built their statement PERIOD separator out of it — `Apr 1 - Apr 30,
2026` — because it was the only dash class the platform exported. That is how
the em dash reached a sign class: the period line legitimately needs a wide
dash, and the sign class inherited it.

Four cards. One canon (`MINUS_GLYPHS`, ASCII included, em dash out); one new
constant for the mark with the opposite risk profile
(`date_tokens.PERIOD_DASH`); one private fifth copy of the sign class removed
from `wealthsimple`; and one structural guard so a sixth cannot be written.

**Archive sweep: 3,367 of 3,367 payloads byte-identical, ZERO movers**, which
is the proof bar exactly. Suite 4,240 -> 4,253.

## MGD1. The instrument, checked before any production edit

Every figure below comes from replaying the archive markdown through the real
pipeline (`analyze_markdown(parse_mode="deterministic")` ->
`analysis.serialization.report_to_dict` -> `telemetry.record.classify_outcome`),
with the OCR text resolved from the D-3 artifact store **by direct file path**
— the `webapp_data` sqlite index was never opened, and neither the archive nor
either cache was ever written to.

The `content_sha256 -> markdown` index was built by reading every one of the
**10,246** OCR artifacts and taking the payload envelope's own `input_sha256`
as the document identity, so it does not depend on this process reproducing
the run's cache key. **3,396 distinct documents have offline text.**

Checked against the run of record
`discovery_reports/2026-08-15T111704.195314-0000-c924d751` before anything
changed:

```
documents in the run       : 3380
replayed with offline text : 3367
no offline text            : 13      (exactly the run's `deferred` set)
outcome_class  agree/dis   : 3367 / 0
parser_id      agree/dis   : 2376 / 0   (991 unrecorded — the cache-hit hole)
totals reproduced          : validated 2405 · review 25 · withheld 65 · failed 872
```

`parser_id` is compared only where the run recorded one: 991 rows were
analysis-cache hits and carry no dispatch at all (W3 §COUNTSP3's hole), so an
empty run-side parser is "not recorded" and never "no parser". Iterating rows
instead of shas would have given 3,493 — the two bases are not the same, which
§MGC5.5 had already had to correct once.

## MGD2. The consumer survey — what each one does TODAY

The shadow, measured on the base tree:

```
MINUS_GLYPHS   (:104, canon)      '−–'      2 glyphs
MINUS_GLYPHS   (:609, rebinding)  '-−–—'    4 — SHADOWS the above for importers
MINUS_CLASS    (:108)             '[-−–]'   3 — hand-spelled, no em dash
_MINUS_TABLE   (:110)             {U+2212, U+2013} -> '-'   2 — no em dash

parse_money("—$500.00")          ->  +500.0
parse_signed_decimal("—$500.00") ->  -500.00
```

Every consumer, in-module and out, with what it actually does:

| consumer | reads | uses it as | em dash today |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_MINUS_TABLE` :110 | canon (:104) | sign translation | no |
| `MINUS_CLASS` :108 | nothing — hand-spelled `[-−–]` | sign, in a finder | no |
| `SIGNED_MONEY_TOKEN` :619 | rebinding (:609) | sign, in a finder | **yes** |
| `parse_signed_decimal` :635 | rebinding, at CALL time | sign, in a parser | **yes** |
| `balance_by_date` (4 sites) | `MINUS_CLASS` | sign / a date range | no |
| `chase` :79 | `MINUS_CLASS` | sign, in a finder | no |
| `brex` :64 | `MINUS_GLYPHS` | **a DATE RANGE** | yes |
| `mercury` :73 | `MINUS_GLYPHS` | **a DATE RANGE** | yes |
| `brex`/`found_lead`/`mercury` | `SIGNED_MONEY_TOKEN` + `parse_signed_decimal` | sign | yes |
| `wealthsimple` :46 | **a private copy**, `"–−—-"` | sign AND a date range | yes |

The last two rows are the survey's whole value. Narrowing `MINUS_GLYPHS`
without noticing them would have quietly narrowed two PERIOD patterns, and
would have left the platform's fifth sign class still reading an em dash as a
minus.

What each family actually PRINTS. The populations are derived by LIVE
detection replay — the sweep's own `DispatchCollector` over every document —
and never from `rows.csv`'s `parser_id`, which is empty on the run's 991
analysis-cache hits (W3 #COUNTSP3). Both bases were computed and agree here,
6/31/12/16 either way, so the rule cost nothing this time and is recorded
because it is the rule:

```
                LIVE   rows.csv   money SIGN position                    period RANGE
brex               6          6   U+002D 135                             U+002D 6/6
mercury           31         31   U+2212 1,202 · U+2013 687 · U+002D 13  U+002D 31/31
found_lead        12         12   U+002D 1,611                           (no period class)
wealthsimple      16         16   U+2013 2,140                           U+002D 16/16
```

Stronger than "no em dash in a sign position": **not one of those 65 documents
contains U+2014 anywhere in its text at all.** The four families this cell
changes cannot be reached by the change, before any pipeline is run.

**Zero em dashes in a sign position in any of the four families**, and the
ASCII hyphen is load-bearing in two of them (brex 135, found_lead 1,611) —
which is why the canon had to be the WHOLE class rather than "the non-ASCII
part of it". A canon that omitted ASCII would have forced three of its four
consumers to add it back by hand, which is precisely how the second definition
came to exist.

## MGD3. The ruling, and the archive evidence for it

EM DASH STAYS OUT. Over all **3,396** documents with offline text, an em dash
stands in a sign position **twice**, both on documents that fail to parse:

| doc | folder | outcome | printed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `88AAC06119FC` | Columbia Bank | failed, no parser | `03-16 — 39,692.35` |
| `FFEBAF819F74` | TD Bank | failed, no parser | `S2 -—ps/25/2zet —— $4812.39]` |

The Columbia document is the decisive one, and its neighbours are the
argument. The line sits in a three-column Daily Balances grid:

```
02-28 59,347.32   03-11 47,180.73   03-23 34,559.09
03-04 56,767.53   03-16 —  39,692.35   03-26 34,167.30
03-09 71,669.52   03-19 31,435.22   03-31 32,358.65
```

39,692.35 is a POSITIVE running balance between 56,767.53 and 34,167.30; the
dash is the empty-column placeholder the grid prints. Admitting the glyph to
the sign class would flip a number the bank printed positive. It is also the
ONLY document in the archive where an em dash precedes a bare money figure at
all. The TD document is OCR wreckage.

Two attestations, both against. The em dash is punctuation.

## MGD4. Card 1 — one canon (`1179517`)

```
MINUS_GLYPHS = "-−–"                       # the WHOLE sign class, stated once
MINUS_CLASS  = "[" + MINUS_GLYPHS + "]"    # derived, not re-spelled
_MINUS_TABLE = str.maketrans({g: "-" for g in MINUS_GLYPHS})
SIGNED_MONEY_TOKEN = r"[" + MINUS_GLYPHS + r"+]?\s?\$[\d,]+\.\d{2}"
parse_signed_decimal:  text[0] in MINUS_GLYPHS   # unchanged code, one source
```

The second definition is gone. What each consumer's behaviour became,
line by line, verified against a `git archive` of the base tree:

| | base | now | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MINUS_CLASS` | `[-−–]` | `[-−–]` | **byte-identical string** |
| `_MINUS_TABLE` | 2 entries | 3 | gains only the identity `'-' -> '-'` |
| `normalize_sign_glyphs` | | | identical over the whole BMP |
| `SIGNED_MONEY_TOKEN` | `[-−–—+]?…` | `[-−–+]?…` | **U+2014 out** |
| `parse_signed_decimal("—$500")` | `-500.00` | **raises** | fail-closed |
| `parse_money("—$500")` | `+500.0` | `+500.0` | never read it |

The refusal is the point of the sign half. The em dash survives into
`parse_decimal`, which cannot convert it, so a document that genuinely prints
one **declines** rather than publishing a figure nobody printed. Both
alternatives publish: `+500.00` is a debit booked as a credit, and `-500.00`
is the reading that would have inverted the Columbia placeholder.

## MGD5. Card 2 — a date range is not a sign (`00727c8`)

`date_tokens.PERIOD_DASH = "[-−–—]"`, and the asymmetry with
`money.MINUS_CLASS` is deliberate in both directions:

* a glyph admitted to the SIGN class silently inverts the direction of every
  amount that carries it — so that class is narrowed to what documents attest;
* a glyph admitted to the RANGE class can only make a period line match. It
  carries no value and cannot change one. What it CAN do is fail to match, and
  the period is required, so an unrecognised range dash costs the whole
  document.

Membership is exactly what brex and mercury carried before the split, so their
compiled period patterns are **byte-identical** across the change — proven by
diffing the pattern strings against the base tree, not asserted. `wealthsimple`
joined them in card 3 (same member set, different source order; proven equal
by membership over the BMP rather than by string equality).

`square_checking:59` had already reached the same conclusion privately, with
an even wider class (`[-‐-―]`, a U+2010..U+2015 range). The platform now says
it once.

## MGD6. Card 3 — the fifth definition (`384d992`, SEPARABLE)

`wealthsimple._SIGN_GLYPHS = "–−—-"` was a private copy of the sign class,
used for BOTH the money sign and the period range. It never imported the
shadowed constant, so cards 1 and 2 left it untouched — and after them it was
the only sign class in the platform still reading an em dash as a minus. Its
own comment gave the reason it existed ("`analysis/money.py` is growing a
shared class for this in a parallel cell; this reader deliberately does not
depend on it"), and that reason had expired.

**FILE-OWNERSHIP DISCLOSURE, in full.** MG-D was scoped to
`analysis/money.py`, `tests/test_money.py` and the W3 log. What it actually
touches is wider, and the whole of it belongs here rather than only card 3's
half:

| file | card | forced by |
|---|---|---|
| `analysis/money.py` | 1 | in scope |
| `tests/test_money.py` | 1 | in scope |
| `analysis/date_tokens.py` | 2 | the new constant has to live somewhere, and the period line is a DATE token |
| `analysis/brex.py`, `analysis/mercury.py` | 2 | they import the constant being narrowed; leaving them would silently narrow two required period patterns |
| `tests/test_shared_parser_utils.py` | 2 | `date_tokens`' test home |
| `tests/test_fintech_layouts.py` | 2 | three em-dash pins had to be rewritten to the measured truth |
| `analysis/wealthsimple.py`, `tests/test_wealthsimple.py` | 3 | NOT forced — the judgement call below |
| `tests/test_no_parser_helper_clones.py` | 4 | the guard's home |

Cards 2 and 4 are forced footprint: card 2's four files are the direct
consequence of narrowing a constant those files import, and refusing to touch
them would have shipped the regression rather than avoided it. Card 3 is the
only genuine judgement call.

**Card 3 exceeds the scope on purpose and is isolated so it can be dropped —
but it must be dropped TOGETHER WITH card 4 (`f5d255c`).** Reverting it alone
restores `wealthsimple._SIGN_GLYPHS = "–−—-"`, which card 4's guard exists to
forbid: the suite would go red on a test that is doing its job. The pair is
the unit. It is offered because the ruling is "canonicalize to ONE definition
consumed by every consumer", and this was a consumer of the concept if not of
the constant.

**What it costs, stated exactly rather than optimistically.** Narrowing the
class does NOT make the row refuse: the sign group is optional, so an em dash
falls into the description and the amount publishes POSITIVE. That is a
mis-read, and a worse one than either sign. The honest defence is the backstop
the module docstring already names — "a row published with the wrong amount
breaks the balance walk the summary block is checked against". Measured:

```
wealthsimple  `Coop —$403.00 $94.27`
  -> amount +403.00, description "Coop —"
  -> recon.ok False, continuity_breaks 1, average_daily_balance None  → withheld

mercury       `Vendor Co ⟨mark⟩ACH Pull —$10.00 $130.00`
  -> the `type` group absorbs "ACH Pull —$10.00"; the BALANCE cell is read
     as the amount: +130.00 credit
  -> recon.ok False, average_daily_balance None                        → withheld
```

Both fail closed at the DOCUMENT, through the arithmetic rather than through
the grammar. Both are pinned as such — the tests say what actually happens,
including the mis-read, rather than claiming a refusal the parsers do not
make.

**And the backstop has a hole, which the claim above would otherwise paper
over.** It holds for NON-ZERO amounts only. At zero the sign collapses —
`-0.00` and `+0.00` are the same number — so the balance walk still reaches
the printed balance and the document **VALIDATES**, publishing the em dash the
bank set as a sign as DESCRIPTION TEXT:

```
wealthsimple  `Coop —$0.00 $497.27` (with a normal row after it)
  -> amount 0.00, description "Coop —", recon.ok True, ADB 484.27  → VALIDATED
```

Nothing financial is wrong on that document; the record of what the bank
printed is. A claim is worth what its narrowest case is worth, so it is pinned
as its own test rather than folded into the one above.

A THIRD shape exists and is a different mechanism again. `— $10.00` (spaced)
is not `—$10.00` (welded), because `SIGNED_MONEY_TOKEN` carries an optional
space: welded, the whole cell is swallowed by mercury's `type` group and the
BALANCE column becomes the amount (+130.00); spaced, only the dash is
swallowed and the amount cell is still read, unsigned (+10.00). Both are a
debit booked as a credit, both are caught, but by different arithmetic and at
different magnitudes. Pinned separately so the second is never assumed from
the first. All three carried as MGD-C2.

## MGD7. Card 4 — no parser may spell its own sign class (`f5d255c`)

Two copies removed in one cell, both drifted the same way, neither visible to
any test until a document printed the glyph they disagreed on. The existing
clone guards catch a copied FUNCTION; a sign class is a copied CONSTANT, so it
slipped past all of them.

The sentinel is **U+2212 MINUS SIGN alone**, and that is the whole precision of
the guard: U+2212 has no punctuation reading. It is not a range dash, not a
hyphen, not a bullet; Unicode names it MINUS SIGN. A module carrying it is
claiming to know what a minus is. The en and em dashes cannot serve — they have
legitimate non-sign readings and three modules print them as separators today
(`regions`, `scanned_small_bank`, `td_can`'s mojibake table), so a guard on
them would need an allowlist, and an allowlist is the thing that decays.

**SCOPE, corrected on review.** `_modules()` was `analysis/*.py` —
NON-RECURSIVE — so it had never seen `analysis/structurer/`'s six modules, and
neither had the three older guards in that file. It is `analysis/**/*.py` now:
83 modules become 89, there are no basename collisions (the allowlist's
`ANALYSIS_DIR / filename` lookups are unaffected), and all four guards pass
over the wider set with **no new exemptions**.

Ocean's prescription asked for an allowlist entry for `structurer/tokens.py`
alongside the recursion. Measurement says none is needed, and WHY is the
useful part: `tokens.py` carries no U+2212 at all. Its defect is the ABSENCE
of the glyph, not its presence — which is precisely what a presence-guard
cannot detect. The guard is blind to that whole class by construction, and the
test now says so rather than letting a passing run imply coverage it does not
have. `regions.py:40` is the same shape.

**The allowlist is empty and passes with no exemptions.** Prose is excluded
twice: the glyph is read from the AST's string CONSTANTS with docstrings
dropped by identity (four modules set a minus typographically in
documentation), and a constant longer than 60 characters is not a class either
— `count_semantics` stores paragraph-length provenance notes as string DATA,
two of which read "credit −n, debit +n".

The guard is proven to FIRE rather than merely to pass: a synthetic module
replays both real offender shapes alongside the three that must not trip it.

## MGD8. The differential matrix

The `INPUTS` matrix gains five rows — the em dash in every position the
existing sign-class rows occupy:

```
"—500.00", "—$1,234.56", "$1,234.56—", "1,234.56—", "— 500.00"
```

**They carry no divergence declaration anywhere, and that absence is the
finding.** `assert_equivalent` checks declarations in both directions, so a
stale one fails — these five are identical between every frozen pre-R-2 clone
and its replacement, across all 25 differential cases. To the whole strict
engine and to every tolerant parser the em dash was ALWAYS punctuation,
exactly as the clones read it. Only the shadowed rebinding disagreed, and it
reached just two consumers, neither of which has a pre-R-2 oracle to sit in
this matrix — so their em-dash pins are behavioural tests instead.

New behavioural pins, in `tests/test_money.py` §3b:

| test | what it makes unrepresentable |
|---|---|
| `..._binds_each_exported_name_exactly_once` | the HISTORICAL SHAPE of the defect, by AST (see the honesty note below) |
| `..._minus_class_is_derived_from_the_canon_and_not_re_spelled` | a re-spelled class, and an ASCII hyphen moved out of first position (where `[−-–]` becomes a codepoint RANGE) |
| `..._sign_table_and_the_class_cover_the_same_glyphs` | table/class disagreement, over the whole BMP |
| `..._finder_and_the_parser_read_the_same_sign_class` | a finder wider than its parser (hands over tokens the parser must decline) or narrower (drops rows silently) |
| `..._em_dash_is_not_a_sign_and_the_cell_declines` | the ruling |
| `..._two_exported_parsers_no_longer_answer_one_token_two_ways` | the measured symptom |

**Honesty note on the first of those, corrected on review.** It counts
`Assign` and `AnnAssign` nodes with a bare `Name` target in `Module.body`, so
it makes the shape this cell found unrepresentable — and no more than that.
Five rebinding forms escape it: an assignment nested in an `if`/`try`,
`globals()[...] = ...`, augmented assignment, a `for` target, and tuple
unpacking. None has ever occurred in this module and each is conspicuous on
sight, which is why the cheap check is the right one; the earlier wording
("for every module-scope name") claimed a guarantee it does not give.

`tests/test_balance_by_date.py`'s em-dash-bulleted statistic document already
pinned the exclusion from `MINUS_CLASS` independently, and is untouched —
`MINUS_CLASS` is byte-identical.
